🤖 The production hero — on the **pooled-wave** transport, not ragged — stalled silently for fifteen minutes today and then died of an NVLink fault, and it originated on one of the three racks the telemetry window flagged. This is the strongest evidence so far that #8870's root cause is a fabric fault on specific NVL72 domains rather than anything in the ragged kernel, which merely fails silently where NCCL's host path eventually fails loudly.

**Timeline (2026-09-05, UTC), `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k` on the same 176 nodes and the same rack map as both 09-02 hang attempts and the 09-04 window.** Last step 65069 completed at 17:19:31. Nothing was logged by any rank for the next fifteen minutes; Iris's py-spy dumps at 17:21 and 17:31 show every sampled rank's main thread inside `train_step` (`train.py:1176`), i.e. blocked on the device — the #8870 shape exactly. At **17:34:36.549 task 162 rank 1 on `s2grxs64` (rack 10, NVLink domain `dh1-r137`)** logged the first `CUDA_ERROR_CONTAINED: Invalid access of peer GPU memory over nvlink or a hardware error` (from `cudaFreeAsync`, `gpu_cudamallocasync_allocator.cc:414`); the other rack-10 nodes followed within 0.5 s, racks 2 and 6 by 17:34:37.8, and every rack by 17:34:43 — 88 of 176 tasks logged the fault, the rest were taken down by fate sharing. **Why this bears on the ragged hangs.** The pooled-wave transport moves data through NCCL's host-driven path, where a fabric fault eventually surfaces as a contained CUDA error and the driver tears the context down. The ragged device kernel spins in an LSA barrier with `abortFlag == nullptr` and, on the wheel that hung, no bounded wait, so the same fault produces fifteen minutes of silence followed by the 900 s progress watchdog — which is what both 09-02 attempts looked like. The fifteen-minute latency before the contained error is itself notable: the fault was in progress, invisible, for as long as the ragged hangs lasted before the watchdog fired.

**The three racks now line up with three independent fabric observations.** Rack 10 (`dh1-r137`): today's fault origin; and `s2grxs64` is the node that supplied the 22:40:30 straggler in the window (task 162, 124 ms). Rack 8 (`dh1-r129`): the 09-02 attempt-0 stall node set; a 5.009 s NVLS multicast bind at window startup (9-12× every other rack); the only repeat straggler node; and `s9jvxs64` GPU 0 link 14 is a flapping NVLink — 505 recovery events lifetime, +3 in a 21-minute sample last night and +1 more since, read-only from the running hero, the only counter that moved anywhere in a five-rack sweep. Rack 9 (`dh1-r136`): stragglers in the window, no counter evidence yet. Racks 0-7 show none of this. Rack 10's own GPU-side link counters did not move across today's fault, so the error is on the switch side or a non-link hardware error; node `dmesg`/XIDs are not visible from inside the containers.

**What this changes.** The 09-04 deep-dive (`scratch/8870/window/deepdive/`, eleven streams) had already falsified the cross-rack collective-stall mechanism and left "a per-GPU transient of 25-160 ms, ≥11× more frequent on racks 8-10, with nothing upstream of the GPU to blame." A fabric fault that stalls whatever is crossing a link, escalating occasionally to a contained error or a permanent stall, fits every measurement in this issue, including why attempt 0 hung on rack 8 and why one-rack reproductions on healthy racks never reproduced anything. It does not explain attempt 1 (rack 4, `dh1-r124`), which shows nothing in any sweep; that may be a fourth domain or a different event.

**Untested but now less likely as the cause:** the NCCL 2.29.7/2.30.7 compile skew (the ragged wheel that hung compiled its kernels against 2.29.7; every diagnostic wheel since used 2.30.7). It remains the one code difference between the hung configuration and every clean run, and an A/B wheel exists (`marin-xla-pjrt-candidate-355d8f15cc25`), but today's fault happened with no ragged kernel in the picture at all.

🤖 Offline decode of the [September 15 missing-peer dump](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/441) narrows the stall to a self-deadlocked CTA inside QuACK 0.6.4's SM100 grouped GEMM, and identifies the one code path that separates the warps that retired from the warps that did not. QuACK is not exonerated: the rank stops inside this kernel with no external dependency left, and the deadlock is structural to its CLC scheduler. The initiating condition is still unproved, and two reproduction attempts at production shape did not trigger it.

The stuck kernel is the `dh` backward GEMM (`quack_grouped_gemm(dy, w2, cu, b_major="k")`, tile 256x256, cluster 2x2x1, CLC on). Both resident clusters show the same state in every CTA: the MMA warp and all four epilogue warps have exited, the TMA load warp waits on an A/B empty barrier that the exited MMA warp will never release, and the scheduler warp is still inside its CLC loop. The scheduler ring holds three valid grants (work indices 3996/4032/4068 in one cluster, 4011/4047/4083 in the other), and the ring's barrier words show every warp released grants 1-4 while only the four scheduler warps released grant 5. So the MMA and epilogue warps decoded grant 4 as "no more work" and retired, while the load and scheduler warps decoded the same grant as a valid batch-1 tile and kept going. The load warp's registers hold the batch-1 window `[2214, 4182)` (369 and 328 M-clusters for the first two groups), inside which index 4032 is valid; the retired warps must have used a window ending in `(4011, 4032]`. No invalid CLC response was ever in the ring, so this is not the spurious-cancel failure fixed in 0.6.4.

Every warp role decodes its own tile from `cu_seqlens` in global memory (`VarlenMTileScheduler._delinearize_work_idx`, with a per-warp cached batch window). Only the load and scheduler warps execute `griddepcontrol.wait` first (SASS `ACQBULK` at kernel offsets +2272 and +10528); the MMA and epilogue warps' `cu_seqlens` loads (+15408, +21696) come before any wait, and upstream main still has the same placement (`336a5ca` "Enable PDL"). The kernel is launched with PDL (`use_pdl=True` default) and the XLA fusion after it was already resident at its `ACQBULK`, so the sequence is PDL-chained. Under the hero's `save_moe` remat, `cu` is recomputed in the backward by a small fusion, so a predecessor that writes `cu` is plausible. That is the only per-role difference in the decode path and the natural explanation for a role-consistent split, but a one-time stale read at kernel start does not by itself produce the observed state: the retired warps rescan the window at later grants, and a fresh rescan resynchronizes them. The observed state requires those warps to keep seeing stale group boundaries for the whole kernel, which I could not reproduce.

Two probes on `cw-us-east-08a` (2 nodes, production priority, both clean, `/mwittmann/8870-quack-pdl-repro-2` and `/mwittmann/8870-quack-moe-bwd-probe-1`): (1) `experiments/grug/recovery/quack_pdl_repro.py`, the production `dh` GEMM at 601,088 rows with the routing alternating every launch so a stale decode is visibly wrong, six arms (production config, PDL off, CLC off, QuACK patched to wait in the MMA/epilogue warps, constant routing, and the `cu` writer as the immediate predecessor), 600 launches per GPU per arm on 8 GPUs, 28,800 launches, zero hangs and zero output mismatches; (2) `experiments/grug/recovery/quack_moe_bwd_probe.py`, the full `_expert_mlp_quack_wgrad` forward plus backward with a fresh random routing every iteration, 1,500 iterations per GPU on 8 GPUs, 72,000 GEMM launches, zero hangs, zero non-finite values. The hero rate is roughly one hang per 1e6 GPU-steps, about 3e-9 per GEMM launch, so a clean 1e5 launches neither confirms nor excludes the PDL path. In probe (1) the PDL-off arm ran at the same speed as production (27 ms versus 27 ms per launch), so disabling PDL on these launchers costs nothing measurable at this shape.

What this changes: the pooled-wave backend runs dense einsums and never touches this kernel, which matches its clean record. CLC off alone removes the per-grant decode (the scheduler warp decodes once and broadcasts) but leaves the initial-tile decode per warp, so it converts most of this failure into wrong or missing tiles rather than a hang, at the 5-12% GEMM cost recorded in `sonic_cute.py`. The cheap, targeted mitigation for the next hero restart is `use_pdl=False` on the three `quack_moe_cute` launchers (or the two-line wait in the MMA and epilogue warps, arm `patched`, to propose upstream); its efficacy can only be judged by the hang recurrence interval, currently one to two thousand steps.

The retired warps' end of work therefore sits in `(4333, 4340]` in all six clusters, one value, 58-64 indices short of the real end of group 1. That is one stale set of group boundaries shared by 24 CTAs on 24 SMs, not per-CTA noise.

The seventh cluster (blocks 12-13, initial work index 6) is stuck on its very first tile. Its load warp holds the fresh group-0 window `[0, 2220)` and has filled six A/B stages of tile 6 that were never consumed (A/B full parity 1, empty parity 0 in every stage), its scheduler ring holds one grant (index 13, released by the four scheduler warps only), and its MMA and epilogue warps are gone. The MMA warp exited before issuing a single MMA, so it decoded the initial tile, `idx 6 < 2220`, as no work. That is a decode from `cu_seqlens` that says the kernel has fewer than seven clusters of work, taken in the first microseconds of the kernel, by exactly the warps that do not execute `griddepcontrol.wait`. This case needs no persistence argument at all, which was the gap in the previous comment: a stale read at kernel start deadlocks the CTA on its first tile directly. The six other clusters show the same read at a slightly later moment, with `cu_seqlens[1]` already current and the later boundaries not, which fits a buffer being written while the non-waiting warps read it.

One correction to the earlier reading of the scheduler warps: they are parked at the CLC throttle `bar.sync` (kernel offset +11968) waiting for a load-warp credit that never comes, and the reported PC is the following `TRYWAIT`. With that, every barrier count in both dumps reconciles (loads on the tile the MMA warp abandoned, scheduler one credit ahead).

Taken together with the SASS (only the load and scheduler warps wait before their first `cu_seqlens` load), I now put the PDL-stale-input mechanism well above the alternatives. The `cu_seqlens` read the monitoring agent added to the capture is the confirming measurement: on the next hang, the buffer should hold the boundaries the load warp used (`[0, 2220)` and `[2220, 4398)` in work-index units are 370 and 363 M-clusters of 256 rows) while the retired warps evidently used a set that ended around 723 clusters in total. Independently of that read, `use_pdl=False` on the three `quack_moe_cute` launchers, or the two-line wait in the MMA and epilogue warps, is the change to trial at the next relaunch.

🤖 The hero now runs as `hero-nopdl-step108k` (coordinator `/marin/hero-nopdl-step108k-coord-d446fca8`, trainer `/marin/hero-nopdl-step108k-coord-d446fca8/grug-train-hero-nopdl-step108k`, main `8f6f33bebe`), continuing `hero-mix-996f4891-step108k` from its checkpoint `step-108778` with the QuACK grouped GEMMs launched without PDL (#9183) and the PJRT `708c3a4` wheel (#9179). Capture tooling keyed to the previous trainer path needs re-pointing; a hang on this run tests the PDL mechanism directly, since the MMA and epilogue warps can no longer read `cu_seqlens` ahead of the preceding kernel. Trial report: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/hero-nopdl-step108k:-PDL-off-QuACK-launchers-+-PJRT-708c3a4-wheel,-200-step-trial--VmlldzoxNzk0MTE3NQ==

🤖 The latest no-progress alert was traced to a checkpoint error followed by shutdown; it does not establish another GPU-hang recurrence. Details and evidence are in [the incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/459).

🤖 The September 18 UTC stall at step 118837 followed an InfiniBand port failure. Its RAS signature differs from the earlier GPU hangs; no CUDA debugger was attached. The automatic retry restored checkpoint 118722 and resumed training. [Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/470). Monitoring continues with the two-minute threshold and the updated capture ready.

🤖 The September 18 stall after step 120206 was another permanent-checkpoint metadata deletion failure. Checkpoint 120000’s pending `DeleteObjects: AccessDenied` surfaced at the next checkpoint synchronization. The automatic retry restored 120000 and resumed training, rolling back 206 steps. [Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/473). The metadata commit incompatibility remains; this event provides no GPU-state evidence of an 8870 recurrence. Monitoring continues on attempt 3.

🤖 The September 19 interruption after step 124715 began with `CUDA_ERROR_CONTAINED` on task 14, local GPU 3, followed by GPU-reset-required and NVLink-mask node conditions. The error leaves invalid peer-memory access versus hardware/driver fault unresolved. No RAS or debugger capture is available, so this does not confirm another silent #8870 hang. Iris automatically retried from checkpoint 124642; attempt 1 resumed and later passed 127172. Evidence and recovery: [incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/488).

Permanent checkpoint 126000 subsequently logged successful completion with the deployed metadata fix, and later temporary checkpoints also completed. This verifies permanent publication; restoring 126000 has not been tested. [Checkpoint incident update](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/473). The 120-second no-progress monitor is rearmed on attempt 1 with the updated capture ready.

🤖 The September 23 stall on `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k` was traced to rank 0 waiting in an S3 `put_object` for checkpoint 146585’s `manifest.json`. Two host-thread captures showed the same stack. NCCL reported only rank 0 behind, unlike the previously captured rack-wide GPU hangs; no CUDA debugger was attached. Why the S3 call remained blocked is unresolved.

The existing watchdog terminated the stalled attempt, and Iris automatically started attempt 1. All 176 tasks were running by 00:00:27 UTC September 24. The retry restored temporary checkpoint 146355 at 00:01:55, rolling back 228 steps from the last observed metric, then resumed training through step 146366. The two-minute monitor is rearmed. [Incident and evidence](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/518).

topics.title: Replicate the Delphi K=0.20 mid-training sweep on the dense ladder (3e18, 9e18, 2e19)
topics.body:
## TL;DR

The `K=0.20` mid-training stage from #6279 was rebuilt from the original runs' own artifacts and re-run at `3e18`, `9e18`, and `2e19`. All three cells reproduce on `eval/paloma/macro_loss` to within 0.14% relative. Final checkpoints are published in native and HF form. Two things the original's artifacts can no longer supply are documented below — its endpoint selector metric is unreproducible, and HF export needs a gated tokenizer.

## Description

#6279 established that math capability arrives during mid-training, is elicited by SFT, and can be extended by RL. Its mid-training stage is a continued-pretraining phase of `K = 0.20` of the base model's pretraining tokens on a pretrain-replay / Nemotron-CC-math mixture. That sweep's launcher never landed in this repo, so the replication reconstructs it from what the completed runs left in GCS:

* `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/delphi-<scale>-p33m67-k0p20-lr83-a00N/midtrain_manifest.json` — base checkpoint, step count, batch size, token budget
* the sibling `train_lm_config.yaml` — model shape, AdamH values, mixture

Transcribing rather than re-deriving matters because the repo's scaling heuristics have moved since May 2026; re-deriving would silently reproduce a different cell. `K = 0.20` checks out against all nine original scales — the `3e18` manifest records `actual_tokens = 242,483,200` against a 1.2B-token base (`pretrain_fraction_actual: 0.199995`), and `1e22` records 32.07B against 160B.

Bases are published on HuggingFace, so nothing is pretrained: `initialize_from_hf` supplies the weights, and because an HF checkpoint carries no optimizer state the phase runs a fresh LR schedule from step 0 — the `model_only` init the original harness named.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Does #6279's mid-training stage reproduce from its recorded configuration, and are the resulting checkpoints usable for later evaluation?

## Status

Complete for the `p33m67` mix at three scales. `eval/paloma/macro_loss`, replication vs original:

```
3e18   3.6277 vs 3.6296   -0.0019
9e18   3.4308 vs 3.4263   +0.0045
2e19   3.3191 vs 3.3149   +0.0042
```

`eval/macro_loss` agrees to within 0.005 on all three. Endpoint `train/loss` is deliberately not the comparison: it is one batch's value and swings much wider than these gaps — the original's own curve moves 2.56 -> 2.91 -> 2.47 across consecutive logged points.

The mixture is reproduced exactly. Renormalizing the corpus proportions to a mix's replay share recovers the original config's ten component weights to float precision, including `starcoderdata` at 0.00749 and `proofpile_2` at 0.00165; a test pins this.

Checkpoints, native and HF, are at `gs://marin-us-east5/delphi/midtrain_replication/2026.07.30/<cell>-p33m67-k0p20/`. A fixed calendar version rather than a `dev` path, so they are not clobbered by a same-named step.

## Two limitations inherited from the original artifacts

**The endpoint selector cannot be reproduced.** #6279 selects on `eval/nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus/loss` (`3e18` 1.40467, `9e18` 1.24994, `2e19` 1.17311). Levanter resolves a component's validation data to `<cache_dir>/validation` with no fallback to train urls, and the `4plus` cache has only `train/` in every region today — so the split those numbers were measured on has been deleted since. A sampled `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus_val` component stands in for tracking math progress; it is not numerically comparable. Reproducing the original exactly would in any case reproduce a metric measured on data sitting in the training mixture at weight 0.67, which #6279 itself reports as fuzzy-contaminated.

**HF export needs a gated tokenizer.** The export resolves `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B`; training pods carry no HF token, so Levanter wrote `model.safetensors` alone and the four config/tokenizer descriptors were missing. Omitting the model's `reference_checkpoint` made this fatal — the 401 took the job's exit code with it, killing every cell after training had completed. Setting it to the original's ungated `NousResearch/Llama-2-7b-hf` stops the crash but not the missing metadata. The publish script fills those four files from each cell's original export, verified to match the architecture. A run with an HF token would export natively.

## Links

* Reference thread: #6279
* W&B: `marin-personal/delphi-midtraining`, runs `delphi-{3e18,9e18,2e19}-p33m67-k0p20-repl-a3`
* Originals: `marin-community/delphi-midtraining`, runs `delphi-<scale>-p33m67-k0p20-lr83-a00N`
* Code: `experiments/references/delphi_midtrain.py`, `experiments/references/publish_delphi_midtrain.py`, `tests/references/test_delphi_midtrain.py` — committed locally as `ea87ad229` on branch `midtraining-initial-test`, not pushed

## Decision Log

* Hyperparameters transcribed from the original runs rather than re-derived, so later heuristic drift cannot leak in.
* Component names rekeyed to drop the repo's `-llama3` handle suffix, so metrics land under the same names the originals logged.
* Checkpoint interval cut to 2 minutes: every v5p-8 group on this cluster is preemptible, and at the original's 10-minute cadence one cell lost 808 steps to a preemption that landed before its first checkpoint.
* Zone pin relaxed to region. Training must stay in us-east5 — the math cache is materialized there and the us-central copies are metadata stubs — but pinning a single zone left cells queued behind "Insufficient TPUs" while sibling zones had capacity.

## Conclusion

The mid-training stage reproduces from its recorded configuration, and the checkpoints are in a form later evaluation can consume. No benchmark evaluation has been run: every number here is validation loss. #6279's downstream results (MATH-500, AIME24, gsm8k) come after SFT, and its own finding is that SFT on a bare base is nearly inert for math while SFT on a midtrained base reaches MATH500 45.0 — so scoring these bases directly would say little. Remaining scales (`3e19` through `1e22`) and the `p50m50` / `p67m33` mixes are untouched.

topics.title: [grug][EP] Shard non-expert weights and optimizer state across the expert axis
topics.body:
## Problem

Grug defines `data = devices / (replica · expert)`. At EP64 this collapses `data` to 1, so non-expert weights—attention, shared MLP, LM head—and their optimizer state are replicated on every device.

## Reproduction scope

- GB200, 64-GPU expert axis
- Grug MoE: d5120, L48, E256, top-8
- `data=model=1`, `expert=64`
- Reproduction branch: [`rav-grug-moe-ep64`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/rav-grug-moe-ep64)
- Originating result: [#7201 EP64 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201#issuecomment-5048941489)

## Observed behavior

Non-expert parameters and optimizer state consume roughly 148 GiB/GPU and OOM before step 1.

## Expected behavior / fix boundary

Use the combined FSDP axis `("data", "expert")` for non-expert weights, e.g. `P(Pfsdp, "model")` / `P("model", Pfsdp)`. The expert axis is intra-rack, so the required all-gathers remain on NVLink. At EP1 this must be equivalent to the existing `P("data", ...)` layout.

## Done when

- The EP64 reproduction reaches training without replicated non-expert-state OOM.
- EP1 retains equivalent sharding and numerics.
- Tests cover parameter and optimizer-state partition specs.

topics.title: [experiment] Remove extra think segments from Grug SFT 10.05 with a short SFT
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Not started. This tests whether one short SFT pass over the 10.05 checkpoint's own samples, with each malformed reasoning span repaired, removes extra think segments without lowering pass rate. If it does, consumers get a patched 10.05 instead of a full SFT re-run, which took 126 hours on 1,024 TPU v4 chips.

## Description

`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` (revision `8c76b22`) sometimes writes more than one reasoning segment in one assistant message: a stray `<|end_think|>` after the first block, or back-to-back blocks (#10400). This happens in 0.6% of thinking messages on bixbench-pi and 3.2% on bfclparity-pi, and RL raises the rate to 9.1% (Smartie RL step 14). #10518, #10519 and #10520 stop new data and RL from teaching or rewarding the habit, but the 10.05 checkpoint keeps it.

A re-run of the 10.05 SFT would cost about 129k TPU v4 chip-hours. The W&B run `grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped` (project `marin_moe_sft`) took 125.9 h for 4,750 steps on 1,024 chips at 94.9 s/step, plus 5.2 h in two crashed starts.

The patch trains on the model's own samples. Off-policy rows change think behavior quickly: four updates at 1e-5 on GLM-written rows cut closed think blocks from 255 of 284 to 53 of 387 ([curriculum SFT README](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/README.md#L89-L101)). Training on clean samples alone gives a weak signal when only about 2% of samples are malformed. A repaired sample differs from the model's own output only at the malformed span, so its loss targets that decision.

## Hypothesis or Goal

One pass over at most 2,000 rows of repaired and clean samples, at a learning rate of at most 1e-5, cuts the held-out violation rate at least 10x and keeps held-out pass rate within 2 points of 10.05.

## Design

1. Baseline from stored samples (CPU only). #10000 sampled 10.05 8 times per SWE and terminal pivot prompt, with thinking on, temperature 1.0, special tokens kept and no reasoning parser ([runs.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/runs.py#L128-L139)). The raw messages are in `message_json` under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/dml/pivotrl/<candidates>/pass-rates/grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft-262k-20261005/2026.10.09/`. Classify each sample as well-formed (one `<|start_think|>` at the start and one `<|end_think|>`), stray end, back-to-back, or orphan close, and count `finish_reason=length` separately. If fewer than 0.5% of samples are malformed, switch to tool-use chat prompts like bfclparity-pi.
2. Rows (CPU only), from training candidates only. A repaired row takes a malformed sample that did not hit the token limit. Its reasoning is everything before the last `<|end_think|>`, with inner think tokens replaced by a blank line. Its reply and tool calls are unchanged. A clean row is a well-formed sample from the same prompts, unchanged. Use equal numbers of repaired and clean rows, keep samples whatever their task score, and put the loss on the final assistant turn only.
3. Train three arms from 10.05, one pass each, with an export at mid-pass and one at the end:

   | Arm | Rows | Learning rate |
   |---|---|---|
   | T-low | repaired + clean | 1e-6 |
   | T-high | repaired + clean | 1e-5 |
   | C-high | clean only, same row count | 1e-5 |

   Two trainers fit. The arm trainer in #10327 (prebuilt `input_ids` and `loss_weights`, batch 16 × 32k, constant learning rate, 4×8 H100) needs a 10.05 entry in its [`PARENTS`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/01d104874e0c3c20fc38a65645b466d3c02bde8b/experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py#L94-L107) table and rows in its manifest format. The PivotRL SFT path in #10000 already trains on the final turn of pivot prompts.
4. Measure on the held-out pivot rows, 4 samples per row, with the same settings for 10.05 and every arm (`heldout_baseline_step` and `heldout_eval_step` in #10000). The primary metric is the violation rate. The guards are pass rate, the share of samples that close their span, and the `finish_reason=length` rate. Sample enough rows for 10.05 to show at least 20 violations. Then run bfclparity-pi and bixbench-pi on the best arm and compare with the 10.05 runs from 2026-10-17.

Decision rule:
- Success: the violation rate falls at least 10x and its 95% interval excludes the 10.05 rate. Pass rate stays within 2 points, and the span-closing and length-stop rates do not get worse.
- If T-low succeeds, publish 10.05 with the patch as the base for consumers and add the patch to the post-training recipe.
- If T-high succeeds and C-high does not, the repair is what works. Adopt T-high if the guards hold.
- If C-high also succeeds, clean on-policy samples are enough and the repair step can go.
- If no arm succeeds, try a format reward in RL (#10520) before an SFT re-run.

If the patch works, repeat T-low on v0.1 (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14`, the base in #10213), which has extra segments in 9.1% of thinking messages.

Estimated cost: 100–150 H100-hours, about one day. Each arm takes 20–25 H100-hours, mostly model loading, compilation and export; its 65M padded tokens train in minutes. Held-out sampling takes about 8 H100-hours per checkpoint, and bfclparity-pi plus bixbench-pi take 20–40 H100-hours for one arm.

## Status

Not started.

## Links

* Logbook: this issue
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:
* Parent: #10400. Trainers: #10327, #10000. Related: #10428 (format SFT on Hero).

## Decision Log

- 2026-10-22: Patch the existing 10.05 checkpoint before considering an SFT re-run, which costs about 129k TPU v4 chip-hours. Train on repaired on-policy rows, for the reasons in the description.

## Conclusion

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The 10.05 checkpoint can emit extra reasoning delimiters, and the `grug` parser leaves later segments in reply content (#10400). The stored PivotRL samples retain special tokens and `message_json`, so the first measurement and row construction can use the existing artifacts without new inference. No open PR targets #10521; the relevant trainers, #10000 and #10327, are still draft PRs, and #10327 currently accepts only v0/v0.1 parents and its sweep-specific arm manifest.

**Relevant code**
- [`runs.py#L101-L139`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/runs.py#L101-L139) — pinned 10.05 model and thinking-on sampling.
- [`pass_rates.py#L73-L101`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/pass_rates.py#L73-L101) — stored message and stop-reason fields.
- [`sft_templates.py#L23-L35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/sft_templates.py#L23-L35) — final-turn loss mask.
- [`sft.py#L622-L667`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33f37f1c9a36368102d3c2d4c5d13beddb8a2263/experiments/post_training/pivotrl/sft.py#L622-L667) — matched held-out sampling.
- [`arms.py#L82-L121`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d23b8c9a94ea9c2c593f185287f28b86676f6a48/experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py#L82-L121) — current arm and parent restrictions.

# Proposed Fix

1. Audit the stored 10.05 SWE and terminal samples on CPU. Split by candidate row before selecting training examples; classify each assistant message by delimiter pattern and count `finish_reason=length` separately. Report counts by prompt family and sample ID. If violations are below 0.5%, sample tool-use prompts as the issue specifies. Size the held-out set to show at least 20 baseline violations.
2. Build a versioned manifest and at most 2,000 final-turn examples from training candidates only: equal repaired and unchanged clean rows, plus a clean-only comparator with the same row count. Exclude length stops, preserve reply text and tool calls, record source sample IDs and before/after delimiter counts, and test tokenized renderings for each malformed class and the loss mask.
3. Extend the Grug path in #10000 after its #9933 dependency is settled. It already pins 10.05, masks earlier turns, and measures held-out pass rates; configure one pass at 1e-6 and 1e-5 on repaired plus clean rows and one pass at 1e-5 on clean rows, with mid-pass and final exports. Check the actual GPU-hour estimate before launch because this path currently allocates 8×8 H100 rather than the 4×8 arm trainer cited in the issue. Coordinate changes with #10000 instead of opening a parallel trainer PR.
4. Evaluate 10.05 and every export on the same held-out rows with four samples per row and identical serving settings. Report violation classes, pass rate, closed-span share, and length-stop rate with 95% intervals clustered by prompt. Apply the issue's 10× reduction and 2-point pass-rate guards before running bfclparity-pi and bixbench-pi on the selected arm. Publish artifact paths, exact checkpoint revisions, and the adoption decision here.

topics.title: mini-swe-agent sandbox contains clean copies of SWE-smith task repositories
topics.body:
When Harbor runs the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter on a SWE-smith task, the agent's own Python environment is installed inside the task sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`). That environment contains clean, unbroken copies of three packages that are also SWE-smith task repositories: pygments, pandas and tenacity. The agent can read the fixed source directly. The same class exists at the image level, independent of the agent: conda's package cache ships boltons in every conda image, pip and setuptools vendor chardet, tomli and inflect, and one testbed environment holds an installed dataset egg.

Observed: in a GLM 5.3 trial on `swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity) with the mini-swe-agent adapter, the agent ran `sed -n 136,175p /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`, called it "the reference", copied the logic and passed. A pre-agent audit of the task packages cannot see this environment, because it appears only when the agent is installed.

Scope in the DCAgent SWE-smith packages (`DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`), measured with mini-swe-agent's dependencies pinned (identical 80 distributions across one image per repository): pygments 222 tasks, pandas 196, tenacity 30, boltons 21, chardet 10, tomli 23, inflect 27, dataset 13. In the 2,100-task shootout pool that was 542 tasks before replacement. A filename-only check produces false positives (pygments' `html.py` versus safety, IPython's `timing.py` versus alive-progress), so the check must compare module contents or names, not file suffixes.

Reproduce: start a trial with the mini-swe-agent adapter on any pygments, pandas or tenacity SWE-smith task, and in the agent phase list `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<package>/`. For the image-level copies, build the task's `environment/Dockerfile` and search outside `/testbed` for directories named after the task repository's import name (for example `find / -path /testbed -prune -o -type d -name tomli -print`).

Impact: pass rates on those tasks are inflated and the resulting traces teach reading a library copy instead of fixing the bug. Terminus-2 is not affected by the tool-environment copy, because the Terminus-2 agent runs outside the sandbox, but the image-level copies affect every agent. Existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ; they have not been audited for these paths.

Expected: during the agent phase, no readable copy of the task repository exists outside `/testbed`. Either the agent environment lives outside the sandbox (as Terminus-2 does), or the adapter installs it on a path the agent cannot read, or task packages whose repository is a dependency of the agent or of the base image are excluded from training pools and flagged in evaluation.

Done when: Harbor's mini-swe-agent adapter keeps its environment out of the agent's reach or documents the limitation; a content-based image check for repository copies outside `/testbed` is part of SWE-smith package validation; and existing SWE-smith trace sets are audited for reads under these paths. The shootout pool (#10213) already excludes the eight repositories above, pins the agent's dependencies, and drops traces that read a library copy of the task repository; the method and per-repository evidence are in the pool manifest at `open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10`. Related: #10212 (git history left in the same packages).

🤖

# Research

Harbor's Mini-SWE setup puts its Python tool environment inside the task container; a GLM 5.3 trial read the installed `tenacity/retry.py` and passed using that reference ([probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6227834962)). [Pool P v4](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6228022768) excludes the affected repositories, and its row builder drops known library-copy reads, but those controls apply to this shootout rather than to future SWE-smith packages or older traces. Marin delegates agent execution to the pinned Harbor runtime, so the adapter, package validator, and trace audit need separate changes.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L116) — Harbor agent selection.
- [`driver_config.py#L69-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L69-L80) — pinned external runtime.
- [`penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708) — one historical SWE-smith trace source.

# Proposal

Keep the v4 exclusions as the current safeguard. Add the following durable checks before treating other SWE-smith packages or historical traces as clean.

1. **Harbor adapter:** Move the Mini-SWE controller and its Python environment outside the task sandbox; send tool commands through Harbor's sandbox execution interface. Probe after agent setup, when the tool environment currently appears, and verify that the agent can edit `/testbed` but cannot read the controller's packages. If Harbor cannot support this boundary, document the limitation in the adapter and reject repository/agent pairs whose code ships in its pinned dependencies. The adapter change belongs in `marin-community/harbor`; Marin should pin the tested revision.
2. **Package validation:** Promote the [v4 image probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644) into the SWE-smith package build gate. Inspect agent-readable files outside `/testbed` in the built image and again after agent setup. Use repository import names and distribution metadata to find candidates, then confirm source overlap with content fingerprints; a matching filename alone must not reject a task. Record matched paths, files, image revision, and agent dependency pin in the manifest, and reject confirmed overlaps before publishing packages.
3. **Historical traces:** Inventory each existing SWE-smith trace source and its agent/setup revision, starting with the registered Penfever source and the Kimi traces noted in [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644). Join commands and observations to the task repository; flag reads from its copies in `site-packages`, `_vendor`, conda caches, eggs, Go module caches, and agent tool environments. Publish counts and example paths by dataset and repository, quarantine confirmed contaminated rows, and mark sources with missing command or environment provenance as unknown rather than clean. Run the audit where the traces are stored to avoid bulk cross-region transfer.

## Testing and rollout

Test the validator against the observed tenacity tool environment and vendored tomli, plus unrelated files such as Pygments' `html.py`; the latter must not trigger on its filename. Run one Mini-SWE task end to end with the new boundary and verify that setup, editing, and the verifier still work. Hand-check flagged and unflagged audit samples, publish the audit manifest and rejected counts, then require the validator result in future SWE-smith pool manifests.

## Costs and open question

Moving the controller changes Harbor's agent lifecycle and needs an integration test, while scanning built images adds package-build work. Can Harbor's current Mini-SWE adapter run outside the sandbox with its existing command transport? If not, the documented limitation plus enforced repository exclusions is the immediate adapter deliverable; the package gate and trace audit remain required.

🤖 **TL;DR:** in the existing SWE-smith trace sets, clean copies outside `/testbed` matter little for the testbed-format tasks, and mini-swe-agent's tool env never appears. They ran Terminus-2, not mini-swe-agent. The exception is AgentTrove's clone-format tasks: 1,142 of their traces read an installed release copy of the task's own package.

| Set (revision) | Traces | Agent command reads a library copy of the task's repo | Touches mini-swe-agent's tool env | Row-builder drop (copy or tool env anywhere in the trace) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-...-maxeps-32k` (`1b87a9cf78`) | 9,356 | 2 (1 of 5,237 passes) | 0 | 6 |
| `laion/calibforge-relay-traces` `kimi_swesmith` (`66feab4d24`) | 4,392 | 1 (0 passes) | 0 | 3 |
| `DCAgent2/GLM-4.7-swesmith-...-maxeps-131k` (`e209a88db1`) | 9,437 | 3 | 0 | 10 |
| `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` swesmith rows (`b395a4307a`) | 78,246 | 1,157 (1,142 in clone tasks) | 0 | 1,598 |

- **Clone tasks:** the instruction makes the agent clone `swesmith/<mirror>` into an image that already has the package installed. The agents then `ls` or `cat` the installed copy (`/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/<pkg>`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/<pkg>`, a venv's `site-packages`), and that copy is clean code. 106 repos are affected; cantools, pygments, oauthlib and python-docx lead. The same tasks also expose the full mirror history (see #10212).
- **Go module cache:** 2 traces read a Go repo's module-cache copy. The shootout lists no import names for Go repos, so this column is supplementary.

**Method:** the shootout row builder's own rules, used verbatim: `LIBRARY_LOCATION` plus the repo's import names, and `AGENT_TOOL_ENV`. They are applied to the agent's commands, and also to the whole trace, matching the builder's drop rule. Import names are the shootout's for its 38 repos and extended for the rest. Code and exact regexes: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215).

topics.title: [evaluation] Evalchemy c1d5c62c keeps a stale aggregate when rerun over a scored archive with transport-failure rows
topics.body:
Evalchemy at the policy pin `c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454` does not update an archive's results when a scored result already exists, even if that result contains transport-failure rows. A selective rerun that regenerates the failed rows therefore leaves the old aggregate and samples in place.

`write_finestore_output` returns before writing when `completed_finestore_output` is true ([`eval/contracts/finestore_output.py` L66](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L67)). A result counts as completed when it is marked scored, and a result with failure markers is still marked scored.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 a GSM8K record had 112 `model_transport` failure rows out of 1,319. A selective rerun regenerated exactly those 112 units (1,207 retained resume payloads byte-identical), but the aggregate and samples stayed stale. Recovery required dropping the `evalchemy_results` and `samples` tables from a copy of the archive and rerunning the evaluator over the 1,319 cached responses (job `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018`).

Reproduce:
1. Run Evalchemy GSM8K at `c1d5c62c` into a FineStore archive while the server drops some requests, so the stored result is scored but contains transport-failure rows.
2. Remove the failed resume units and rerun the same evaluator into the same archive.
3. The resume table gains the regenerated units; `evalchemy_results` and `samples` are unchanged.

Expected: the evaluator rescores when the stored result contains failure markers, or exposes a doc-id retry that regenerates the named rows and rewrites the aggregate and samples.

Status on main: Marin `main` now pins Evalchemy `09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5`, where `FineStoreOutput.finish` publishes results with `SUPERSEDE` and no longer has this early return. This has not been verified against a scored archive with failure rows; the policy branch still pins `c1d5c62c`.

Done when: a scored archive with transport-failure rows can be repaired by a rerun or doc-id retry under the pinned evaluator, with the aggregate and samples updated and retained rows unchanged, covered by a test.

Related FineStore defect, already fixed on the policy branch: the reader appended a derived `_gen` column to shards that already persisted one, so record assembly failed with `Field "_gen" exists 2 times in schema`. Fixed in `4d45932e39c15ddfbb7e5b679a9c4095b8408ff1` on `benfeuer/eval-campaign-09-25-v2`, which is not on `main`. `main`'s reader appends `_gen` only when it is missing (`_resolved_version_columns`, from #10216), which avoids the duplicate; not verified against the failing archives.

Evidence: selective rerun `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-selective112-20261018` (resume table gained exactly 112 successful units, 1,207 retained payloads byte-identical, aggregate and samples unchanged); cached regrade after dropping `evalchemy_results` and `samples` in the copy: `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018` (final 1,215/1,319). Retry archive: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task203-sweep/screens/gsm-ep2-selective-retry-20261018/results`; the original archive is untouched. The early return is shown by the code path and the archive state; the evaluator logs no explicit skip.

🤖
# Research

At the policy pin, Evalchemy restores saved `model_transport` failures as completed resume units; its writer then skips a rerun because the existing aggregate is marked scored. Thus replacing failed resume units alone leaves `evalchemy_results` and `samples` stale. Marin main pins a newer, divergent Evalchemy revision whose writer supersedes those tables, but its existing replacement test covers an unscored failure followed by success, not repair of a scored result with failed rows.

**Relevant code**
- [`finestore_resume.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_resume.py#L89-L142) — saved units are restored and existing keys skipped.
- [`finestore_output.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L92) — scored results trigger the early return.
- [`eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/eval.py#L1059-L1086) — evaluation passes new scores to that writer.
- [Policy Evalchemy lock](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36008e797f7e7cc65a00e70afd962eea0e8d54ca/config/external/evalchemy/uv.lock#L499) — still pins `c1d5c62c`.
- [Newer output writer](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L70-L124) — supersedes samples and results.

# Proposed Fix

`FineStoreResumeManager.restore()` → evaluation → `write_finestore_output()` preserves failed units and then declines to publish corrected scores. Repair both stages in the Evalchemy fork used by [the policy PR #9569](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9569):

1. Add a regression using one successful GSM8K unit and one saved `model_transport` failure in a scored FineStore archive. A rerun with the same fingerprint must regenerate only the failed unit, keep the successful resume payload byte-identical, update both aggregate and sample rows, and remain idempotent on a third run.
2. Make known transport-failure resume payloads eligible for replacement under their existing unit keys while preserving successful units and fingerprint checks. Backport the newer writer's supersede behavior for results and samples to the policy fork, with the result published after sample writes; cover the existing `_gen` reader issue against the same archive shape.
3. Pin the tested Evalchemy fork commit on #9569 and regenerate its lock and Marin dependency pin. Reconcile [PR #10169](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10169), which currently rejects archives containing saved transport failures, with the verified retry path. Validate against a copy of the 1,319-row archive: 112 regenerated units, 1,207 retained payloads unchanged, corrected samples and aggregate, and no duplicate `_gen` field.

This spans the Evalchemy fork and two open Marin PRs, so a separate Marin implementation PR would overlap active work. The original archive should remain untouched during validation.

topics.title: [vLLM] Snowball parity-test performance on real 8xH100 nodes
topics.body:
# Snowball parity-test performance on real 8×H100 nodes **Date:** 2026-07-17 · **Commit:** `4b32fcfb0747dbb83ef4c0e8a13ffa7d4863218d` · **Cluster:** `cw-us-east-02a` · **Attention:** `FLASH_ATTN` ## Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > **In this cold test path, vLLM cut end-to-end test-case time by 49% and prompt-scoring time by 8.4× relative to Levanter, while using about 10 GiB more HBM per GPU. Startup and setup—not scoring—dominated elapsed time for both backends.** | Measurement | Levanter | vLLM | Main takeaway | |---|---:|---:|---| | End-to-end test case | 535.05 s | 273.30 s | vLLM was 1.96× faster | | Model load / server startup | 334.39 s | 135.04 s | Largest phase for both backends | | Prompt scoring | 133.16 s | 15.85 s¹ | vLLM was 8.4× faster | | Peak HBM per GPU | 65,049 MiB | 75,425 MiB | vLLM used 10,376 MiB more | ¹ vLLM scoring includes an additional eight-request diagnostic. Its 64 representative requests alone took 13.05 seconds. ### Main learnings 1. **The 30-minute runtime limit has substantial observed headroom.** The slowest backend task took 8m55s, giving 3.6× headroom. The full paired pytest run passed in 13m28s. 2. **Improving cold-run latency means improving initialization.** Model loading consumed 62% of the Levanter test case. vLLM server startup consumed 49%, with another 80 seconds spent in environment setup and finalization. 3. **vLLM's performance advantage is concentrated in scoring.** The production-shaped requests took 15.85 seconds on vLLM versus 133.16 seconds on Levanter. Levanter's first batch at each shape includes JIT compilation, so these are cold test-path measurements—not a general serving benchmark. 4. **HBM is the clearest vLLM resource risk.** Its sampled peak was 92.5% of reported capacity, leaving about 6 GiB per GPU; Levanter peaked at 79.8%. ![Cold standing-cluster runtime breakdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/runtime-breakdown.png) ![Prompt scoring runtime by production-shaped batch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/batch-runtime.png) > [!NOTE] > **Correctness was stable on the representative set:** all 64 cases passed for both backends in the paired run, and all representative cases passed in five additional cold vLLM runs. A separate rank-consistency diagnostic was not reproducible; details are below.
Detailed performance evidence — phase timing, batching, latency, and timeout headroom The exact standing-cluster test passed for both backends on fresh 8×H100 jobs: ```text 2 passed in 808.65s (0:13:28) ``` | Backend | Pytest test case | Iris task | Remote function | Model load/startup | Prompt scoring | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Levanter | 535.05 s | 499.11 s | 485.99 s | 334.39 s | 133.16 s | | vLLM | 273.30 s | 255.38 s | 175.75 s | 135.04 s | 15.85 s¹ | ¹ vLLM scoring includes the eight-request rank diagnostic. The 64 representative requests took 13.05 seconds across eight concurrent waves; the diagnostic wave took 2.80 seconds. The 30-minute runtime limit is 3.6× the observed Levanter task duration and 7.0× the vLLM task duration. H100 assignment began 4–5 seconds after submission, so this experiment did not exercise the separate 30-minute pending limit. - The vLLM environment/setup layer took 79.63 seconds, largely from pinned CUDA 13 overlay installation and job finalization. - Levanter scored 329,514 real prompt tokens as 479,232 padded tokens (68.8% padding efficiency). - Levanter's first batch at each reused shape included JIT compilation: 15.21 vs 0.56 seconds at 256 tokens, 14.02 vs 1.39 seconds at 1,024, and 17.48 vs 4.75 seconds at 4,096. - vLLM's first short wave took 4.34 seconds and the second took 0.096 seconds, indicating first-request warmup. - Representative vLLM request latency was 0.47 seconds at the median and 4.29 seconds at the 95th percentile. ![vLLM request latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/vllm-request-latency.png)
GPU evidence — HBM, utilization, power, and temperature The monitor collected 209 complete eight-GPU samples for Levanter and 81 for vLLM at approximately two-second intervals. - Levanter peaked at 65,049 MiB per GPU, 100% utilization, 293 W, and 36°C. - vLLM peaked at 75,425 MiB per GPU, 100% utilization, 293 W, and 33°C. - Relative to the reported 81,559 MiB capacity, sampled HBM peaks were 79.8% for Levanter and 92.5% for vLLM. ![GPU resource timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/gpu-resource-timeline.png)
Correctness and reproducibility — representative parity and the rank diagnostic ### What is the rank sentinel? After scoring the normal 64 representative cases, the vLLM test selects one of those same cases—`knowledge-longbench-02`, a 15,025-token prompt—and sends it eight more times, with one request pinned to each vLLM serving-rank endpoint. These eight replays are the **rank sentinel**. In plain terms, it asks whether the same long prompt produces the same probabilities regardless of which rank serves it. It is not additional golden data and does not add workload coverage. ### Result | Check | Result | Maximum probability error | Interpretation | |---|---:|---:|---| | Levanter representative set, initial paired run | 64/64 passed | `0.068273` | Passed | | vLLM representative set, five cold runs | 5/5 runs passed | `0.053180–0.067022` | Reproducible in this sample | | vLLM eight-rank sentinel, five cold runs | **2/5 runs passed** | `0.055488–0.093050` | **Not reproducible at the `0.075` gate** | The sentinel is useful as a diagnostic, but these results do not support using it as a blocking gate in its current form. #### Initial paired run | Metric | Levanter | vLLM representative | vLLM rank sentinel | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Observations | 64 | 64 | 8 | | Maximum probability error | 0.068273 | 0.060728 | **0.073430** | | Median probability error | 0.012349 | 0.011156 | 0.036522 | | 95th percentile, representative set | 0.043770 | 0.045501 | — | | Observations above the old 0.008 bound | 43 | 41 | 8 | | Supported winner changes | 5 | 5 | 0 | The sentinel initially passed, but its maximum of `0.073430` left only `0.001570` headroom under the `0.075` gate. ![Representative-case error versus prompt length](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/accuracy-vs-prompt-length.png) ![Initial eight-rank sentinel results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/vllm-sentinel-by-rank.png) #### Five cold vLLM runs Five identical tests ran concurrently on fresh 8×H100 allocations with the same commit and configuration (`FLASH_ATTN`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, FlashInfer sampler disabled). | Run | Iris job suffix | Representative maximum | Sentinel maximum | Gate | |---:|---|---:|---:|---| | 1 | `7ff3af48` | 0.067022 | 0.074130 | pass | | 2 | `9af1f63f` | 0.053180 | 0.076045 | **fail** | | 3 | `c8ab3bb9` | 0.056067 | 0.055488 | pass | | 4 | `0373bc39` | 0.067022 | 0.093050 | **fail** | | 5 | `b3e2493b` | 0.055502 | 0.082465 | **fail** | The representative maximum stayed below the gate in every run. The high sentinel error moved between ranks rather than remaining on one consistently bad rank. ![Five-run representative and sentinel maxima](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/variance-5x8h100/run-maxima.png) ![Sentinel error by cold run and rank](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/variance-5x8h100/sentinel-error-heatmap.png) For the same sentinel rank-4/token-423 tuple, observed probability ranged from `0.475533` to `0.564618` (golden `0.557848`), a `0.089085` range. Across exact tuples, the 95th-percentile probability range was `0.010713` for representative requests and `0.043363` for sentinel requests. ![Sentinel top-token probability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/variance-5x8h100/sentinel-top-token-probability.png) ![Exact-token probability ranges across runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/34e9ae8ab90e1e0c6d875ead0139f79ed174f102/reports/snowball-parity-runtime-2026-07-17/variance-5x8h100/token-probability-range.png) The five concurrent jobs measure variation across fresh allocated nodes, not repeated execution on one fixed node. Five observations are too few for a precise failure-rate estimate, but three failures disprove reliable reproducibility at the current threshold. One original allocation (`f6b61bf9`) failed during vLLM worker initialization before scoring any request. It was replaced by run 5 and excluded from numerical analysis.
Method and limitations — commands, jobs, and telemetry effects The unmodified test contract was executed with temporary telemetry around it: ```sh uv run pytest tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_backend_parity.py \ -m cluster -o addopts= --import-mode=importlib -vv -s --durations=0 ``` Jobs: - Levanter: `/romain/snowball-representative-parity-levanter-8291831e` - vLLM: `/romain/snowball-representative-parity-vllm-673370df` The paired-run telemetry recorded phase, batch/wave, per-request, per-case parity, and per-GPU HBM/utilization/power/temperature. GPU polling and structured logging can perturb runtime, so timings are conservative cold-path measurements rather than a clean benchmark. Median time to emit an eight-GPU sample was below 0.3 ms for both backends; three Levanter samples had logging stalls above 0.1 seconds, with a 3.39-second maximum. The five-run follow-up used buffered per-request logprob capture and printed nothing during request serving. Records were emitted after the vLLM server stopped and before assertions, so telemetry did not change request scheduling or insert device synchronization between requests.

topics.title: [sft] Add an epoch-exact multi-parent arm trainer
topics.body:
Depends on #10324 (sweep runtime) and #10255 (plateau dropping), with main as the review base. This branch retains the earlier dependency snapshots inherited through `task/235` at `3b7f6c71f6`, not the current heads of those PRs. The overlapping library changes must be reconciled after the dependencies land and before this draft merges; this is not an independent replacement for either PR.

Train each agentic SFT arm from its ordered per-epoch row files, using one cache and mixture stage per epoch. Before requesting GPUs, verify row hashes, padding, token totals, the replay-row hash against plain's manifest, and that cached rows preserve the prepared order. Save native state each epoch and, by default, HF weights after epoch two and the final epoch. An opt-in final-only HF schedule removes the intermediate export without changing training, native checkpoint cadence or resume behavior.

Select pinned Snowball v0 or v0.1 weights separately from their shared v0 tokenizer. Reject a mismatched manifest parent, tokenizer or student used to collect relay traces, and refuse dry-run or incomplete production inputs. Parent, method, data-round label `v7` and launch date distinguish artifact names and W&B identities; artifact versions remain calendar dates. The wrapper takes production prefixes and hashes, defaults to plan-only and keeps plateau training on plain rows.

The data variant defaults to HIGH without changing those names. LOW adds `-low` to dataset, cache, checkpoint, tracker and coordinator identities, preventing collisions with HIGH for the same parent and date while keeping the manifest arm unchanged.

The arm-specific files are `experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py`, `launch_arms.sh`, `test_arm_parents.py` and `tests/experiment/test_arm_trainer.py`. The inherited branch also carries plateau probe/smoke tools and tests, context-token accounting, and a JaggedArray repeated-row-zero bounds fix needed by the arm loader. These are visible in the main-based diff alongside the dependency snapshots.

Part of #10213

topics.title: [harbor] mini-swe-agent trials exit before the first model call since litellm 1.106.0; SWE-bench scores read 0
topics.body:
Since 2026-10-18 05:49 UTC, every mini-swe-agent trial on Harbor main fails before its first model call, and SWE-bench Verified scores read 0. Marin main pins Harbor `18e71265`, so any SWE eval launched from marin main today is affected. Harbor `38742b0f` on `benfeuer/eval-campaign-09-25-runtime` has the fix, but Harbor main does not.

Harbor installs the agent inside each sandbox with `uv tool install mini-swe-agent==2.1.0` ([`mini_swe_agent.py` L456 on main](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/18e712655917ee1c5f82624809339daff3a26a9e/src/harbor/agents/installed/mini_swe_agent.py#L456)). mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 requires only `litellm>=1.75.5`. litellm 1.106.0, released at 05:49 UTC, raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'` on the first query.

Symptom: the vLLM server logs `/tokenize` requests but no `/v1/chat/completions`. Each trajectory has 2 steps and 0 prompt/completion tokens. The orchestrator log does not show the import error, because the captured agent stdout is cut off before it. The shootout's plain-arm SWE r100 screen read 0/99: 98 trials ended in `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError`, 1 in `VerifierRuntimeError`, 1 in `AgentTimeoutError`.

Local repro, against any OpenAI-compatible server set in `HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE`:

```python
# uv run --no-project --with mini-swe-agent==2.1.0 --with litellm==1.106.0 repro.py
from minisweagent.models.litellm_model import LitellmModel
LitellmModel(model_name="hosted_vllm/m", model_kwargs={"api_key": "EMPTY"}).query(
    [{"role": "system", "content": "s"}, {"role": "user", "content": "u"}]
)
```

It raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'` and sends no request. With `litellm==1.103.5` the request goes through. With Harbor 38742b0f's install (`uv tool install mini-swe-agent==2.1.0 --with mcp==2.3.0`) it also goes through: litellm 1.106.0 + mcp 2.3.0.

Who is affected: every mini-swe-agent eval and SWE-smith generation trial whose sandbox installed after 05:49 UTC on 2026-10-18, on Harbor `016dd78b` (the September campaign pin) or `18e71265` (marin main). Terminus-2 (TBLite, TB2), Evalchemy and BFCL do not install mini-swe-agent and are unaffected. The task204 LR-sweep SWE screens finished before 05:49 UTC and are valid.

Fix options:
1. Recommended: port 38742b0f's install change (`--with mcp==2.3.0` plus the setup-time import check) to Harbor main, then advance marin's Harbor pin. The setup check turns this kind of dependency drift into a setup failure, not a 0 score. Runs on the fix use litellm 1.106.0 instead of the earlier < 1.106 client, so comparisons should rerun their baseline under the same install.
2. Add `--exclude-newer 2026-10-18T05:00:00Z` to the install. This reproduces the pre-incident dependency set exactly, but the date must be bumped by hand later.
3. Pin `litellm<1.106` in the install. This is narrower, but leaves the other mini-swe-agent dependencies unpinned.

The shootout reruns its SWE screens (three arms plus v0) on 38742b0f. Shootout: #10213. Eval policy: #10197.


Incident note: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/789

topics.title: Track biology evals
topics.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 22, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **4.24/100**; 50/50 scored, 12/50 with any nonempty report (5/50 with both) | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-snowball-v01-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **71.14/100**; 50/50 scored, 45/50 with both reports | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-glm-5.3-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

Across benchmark rows, variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. The two BiomniBench-DA rows share the task/input preparation, Pi agent, rubric/judge and budget policy, with disclosed model-serving differences and reused early completions. BiomniBench-DA tasks with no nonempty report score zero; these scores are rubric-score means, not accuracy. Other GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

The completed BiomniBench-DA comparison scores **Snowball 4.24/100 versus GLM-5.3 71.14/100**, with all 50 outcomes per model verified against native rewards, sealed archives and EvalDash rows. Snowball produced no nonempty report on 38/50 tasks; GLM did so on 5/50. All 38 selected Snowball cases ended normally within 24 minutes, so the separately confirmed Pi timeout leak cannot explain them. This supports a file-delivery/tool-use gap under these model-serving configurations; checkpoint versus tool/serving integration remains unresolved, and this does not establish a general biology knowledge deficit.

The 60-minute protocol retained 83 unaffected outcomes from the earlier 30-minute budget and reran deadline-affected tasks from scratch. It uses five disclosed input variants and a replacement MiniMax judge/signed rubric scorer, remains supplementary, and does not change the release aggregate. The continuation used the [Harbor timeout repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/3bc27cbcffad1d92ad5d9bd4c83cd3f36bf89372); an unresolved `/tokenize` HTTP 502 diagnostic affects interpretation of one GLM timeout. [Full comparison, launch-source references, audit and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

- CLI adaptation, registry `bixbench-cli@1.5`, [task revision `711ff277`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-datasets/tree/711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73/datasets/bixbench-cli). One development task, `bix-1-q1`, excluded from the subsequent five-question pilot. The complete registry snapshot has 205 questions.
- GLM-5.3 with Terminus-2; Harbor [`7b18505a`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a) and its dependency lockfile. Use the [September evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): 32,768 input tokens, 8,192 output tokens, and the default enabled summarization.
- Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` verifier with BixBench's original grading prompt and Boolean response schema. Four basic live checks passed: exact and equivalent numeric answers accepted; wrong and empty answers rejected. This checks grader integration, not broad judge accuracy.

The run used [Marin a795b1d](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a795b1d4306c71b1f4fc52cdcac2b5b1f0ed70d4), [Harbor 21e0ea6](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a), and [task snapshot 674c37c](https://github.com/gonzalobenegas/harbor-datasets/tree/674c37ca8b2e537d36a1886f6cba99f2c6bdaa2f/datasets/bixbench-verified-50). There was one fresh attempt per question, up to 16 concurrent trials, Pi 0.87.0, 32,768 tokens of total context, an 8,192-token per-response limit, an 8,192-token compaction reserve, and setup/agent/verifier limits of 360/1,800/300 seconds. Pi was configured with `thinking=medium` and `thinking_format=chat-template`. This applies the Pi runtime/budget settings from [#9409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409) to Verified-50; it is a different benchmark from that policy's 205-task BixBench CLI corrections set. The earlier Terminus-2 result also used different agent and time budgets, so the aggregate difference is not a controlled model comparison.

The verifier explicitly reported that `/workspace/answer.txt` was absent. | Incomplete agent output under the response budget, combined with Pi/Harbor termination handling. No evidence of a judge service failure. |

Both subsequent verifiers timed out at 300 seconds. No answer or verifier-output artifact was recovered. | Agent time-budget exhaustion followed by verifier failures. Saved evidence does not establish why the computations took so long or where verification stalled. |

Source inspection and an offline replay on October 9 narrowed the harness behavior:

- [Pi 0.87.0's loop](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/16787ad5b2dc748047f314ca1bfe7708f30f54f3/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts#L244-L319) can end after a length-limited response with no tool calls and no continuation. Harbor's pinned Pi validator only rejects a final `error`. Feeding that exact validator a synthetic `length` event returned exit 0; an `error` control returned exit 1. Thus a truncated response can reach verification as a normal agent exit. This reproduces the validator behavior, not the biological computation or model generation.
- [Daytona cancellation cleanup](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/src/harbor/environments/daytona/environment.py#L1860-L1907) cancels local polling and runs `pkill -9 -f opencode`. Pi does not pass a remote execution timeout in its run command. That leaves a concrete gap in stopping Pi and its children before shared-sandbox verification. Continued processes could interfere with verification; this is a plausible contributor, not a demonstrated cause of these two verifier timeouts. Missing verifier logs alone do not prove the grader never started, because Harbor downloads those logs after the exec completes.
- [Trial exception recording](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L430-L452) deliberately lets the later exception replace the earlier one. A final `VerifierTimeoutError` therefore does not exclude an earlier agent timeout.
- The [Verified-50 grader](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/adapters/bixbench-verified-50/src/bixbench_verified50/template/tests/llm_judge.py#L76-L85) deliberately returns without reward when no answer exists. This is the pinned missing-submission convention, not a newly established grading bug. #9409 also does not automatically assign zero to Harbor agent errors. No grades were changed.

The saved launch configuration allowed up to 10 retries for an explicit infrastructure-exception list, but omitted `VerifierTimeoutError` and `RewardFileNotFoundError`. Consequently those failures were not automatically retried, despite #9409 classifying verifier timeouts as retryable infrastructure errors. This is a launch-policy mismatch for the two verifier timeouts.

The September 25 artifact inspection and sandbox inventory found no recoverable answer/workspace for verifier-only replay. No solver or judge calls were made during this diagnosis, and no verifier retry could be executed faithfully. On October 9 the old diagnostic job was no longer available through Iris and this VM lacked direct CoreWeave storage credentials; the new findings above come from the pinned source and offline validator replay, combined with the previously recorded artifact inspection.

Next: validate generic Pi process-tree cancellation and verifier isolation with a bounded harness reproduction, record response truncation explicitly, and decide the intended continuation behavior within the existing budget. Retain verifier logs and answer artifacts even on failure. Those checks should precede any fresh four-task solver retry. The biological causes of the long computations remain unresolved; [harbor#192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192) already tracks Verified-50 source/runtime concerns, including a separate earlier R failure.

The [earlier Verified-50 investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) documents the same Pi behavior with length-limited responses.

Examples distinguish execution from text that only describes execution. The links open in Hugging Face’s Agent Trace Viewer:

Those observations are assistant-generated text, as in BixBench [`bix-28-q6`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-28-q6.jsonl); they do not establish that the commands ran. This BiomniBench example does not simulate a successful report submission.
- [`da-10-1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-10-1.jsonl) received successful write confirmations for `/app/analysis/trace.md` and `/app/analysis/answer.txt`. The prompt and verifier require `/app/trace.md` and `/app/answer.txt`. Its 20 tool dispatches include those real writes; the final assistant response also contains a simulated terminal verification transcript, which is not another execution. Missing submission here does not mean no report was produced.
- [`da-17-5`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-17-5.jsonl) streamed malformed JSON for a report write. Replaying the saved argument deltas through Pi 0.87.0 and its exact `partial-json` 0.1.7 dependency reproduced the parsed `{ "path": "/app/trace.md" }` argument and missing-content validation failure. A valid multiline-JSON control parsed correctly. After the rejected write, the model left a report in chat and stopped. This resembles BFCL’s chat-only submission behavior, illustrated by [`bfcl-multiple-170`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-multiple-170.jsonl) and [`bfcl-parallel-147`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-parallel-147.jsonl), while adding a distinct write-argument failure.
