comments.body: @weaverbot run a wholistic review (include systems' diagram) pls

On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/43766yyk

- 🟢 `Oct 22 21:42Z` Reviewing PR #10297 and its loader integration
- 🟢 `Oct 22 21:48Z` Review drafted; verified memo-key blocker and two loader error paths; preparing PR comment
- 🟠 `Oct 22 21:48Z` **attention** — Holistic review posted; memo-key blocker needs author action: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10297#issuecomment-6352063182

🤖 Holistic review of `32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e`. The loader has a memo correctness blocker. I would hold this PR until the step digest issue in finding 1 is fixed.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  source["Authored Python source"] --> child["load_program_in_process: child + wall timeout"]
  child --> loader["load_program_source: AST checks + restricted imports"]
  source --> loader
  sdk["SdkExports from build SDK (#10298)"] --> loader
  loader --> manifest["ProgramManifest for author tools"]
  loader --> dag["RLEnvBuildProgram + step digests"]
  dag --> build["run_build"]
  build --> store["Step store: per-step memo keys"]
  build --> task["TaskSpec"]
```

The child returns only a manifest. `StageCoordinator` and the build path load the source again to get the executable DAG. The loader's AST pass limits the module top level, and the runtime pass limits imports and builtins. The build SDK supplies diagnostic names in #10298; [`test_pipeline_walkthrough.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/tests/test_pipeline_walkthrough.py) supplies an empty `SdkExports` and does not exercise #10298's standard template. A prior concern about eager imports for suggestions was fixed in `3741c6d`.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker — stale step memo after a later output class changes.** [`_check_module_level`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage30_author/loader.py#L334-L337) permits classes after decorated steps, while the decorator computes each source digest immediately. I loaded two accepted programs where `grader` reads `Later.FACT`, `Later` is an output model declared below `grader`, and only `FACT` changes. `later_step` returns the same JSON in both versions. Its digest changes, but `grader`'s digest does not. Because `grader`'s memo key uses its own digest and the unchanged upstream output digest, it can reuse a result computed under the old `FACT`. Require imports and output classes before the first step, or recompute all step digests after the module finishes loading. Add a regression that compares the actual grader memo key across this edit.

- **2. Should fix — class-body stdout corrupts the child response.** [`load_process.main`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage30_author/load_process.py#L99-L106) writes its JSON on the same stdout that authored code can use. An AST-accepted class body with `print("loader stdout noise")` caused `load_program_in_process` to raise a JSON `ValidationError` for an otherwise loadable program. Keep the child's stdout exclusively for its result, for example by redirecting program output to stderr during loading, and test that a printing class still yields a manifest.

- **3. Should fix — a partial SDK name catalog crashes a refusal.** [`_name_suggestion`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage30_author/loader.py#L192-L203) indexes `exports["grade_candidate"]` for the former name `try_grader`. With the empty `SdkExports` used by this PR's tests, an unbound `try_grader` raises `KeyError` instead of the documented `ValueError`. Return the replacement name without a module when that export is absent, or require and validate a complete catalog at the loader boundary.

The PR body says a step key covers only its own source and output type. The existing [`_source_digest`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage30_author/program.py#L120-L146) already follows reachable module helpers and constants, as its [regression test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/32ba189ef125d116b1d86e6c4b53c3c1ea20815e/lib/taskforge/tests/stage30_author/test_program.py#L192-L208) shows. Please correct that explanation; the declaration-time gap in finding 1 is the relevant remaining memo risk.

The two changed local test files passed (`22 passed`). Ad hoc loader reproductions confirmed all three findings. Loader-specific tests and the standard template are deferred to #10298; its current diff does not fix these findings.

topics.title: [storage] Remove legacy checkpoint discovery after the scratch TTL
topics.body:
Remove the temporary discovery of former scratch roots added by #10221 after the CoreWeave scratch cutover has drained. Normal resumes should search the run's permanent checkpoints and its configured scratch destination. Preserve explicit restore paths and the hero launcher's explicit destination.

Earliest review date: November 2, 2026. Merge only after 14 full days have elapsed since the last non-hero writer using an old scratch mapping stopped. Record that stop timestamp; a later stop moves the gate. Recheck active jobs and checkpoint expiration before merging. Removing discovery too early can prevent automatic resume from finding a checkpoint.

Done when:

- Controllers and downstream consumers use the new storage configuration, and non-hero jobs no longer write to the old scratch mappings.
- The last legacy non-hero writer stopped at least 14 days ago, lifecycle expiration has cleared its temporary checkpoints, and no non-hero resume depends on an old mapping.
- Remove `checkpoint_read_buckets` from backend configuration and parsing, and remove the migration-only `checkpoint_resume_paths` helper in favor of the trainer's checkpoint discovery.
- Update checkpoint discovery coverage for permanent plus configured scratch roots while preserving explicit restore paths and hero routing.
- Release the updated `marin-rigging` and `marin-core` packages and refresh the affected MarinSkyRL, Harbor, and Evalchemy dependency locks.

topics.title: [skyrl] Spread rollout workers across Ray nodes
topics.body:
SkyRL rollout workers are now spread round-robin over the live Ray nodes instead of hard-pinned to the node running the training entrypoint. Nodes are taken in address order, and each node takes only as many workers as its CPU count holds. The pool reserves one `{CPU: cpus_per_worker}` bundle per worker in a placement group, with each bundle bound to its planned node through the `ray.io/node-id` label. Startup raises `RolloutWorkerPlacementError` if the plan does not fit the nodes' CPU totals, or if Ray does not grant the reservation within `trainer.distributed.placement_group_timeout_seconds`. Before this change, a worker that could not be placed stayed pending. On a one-node cluster every worker still lands on that node.

Each worker runs its tasks' local bubblewrap sandboxes on its own host. In a six-node Megatron run (2 policy nodes, 4 inference nodes, 12 workers of 8 CPUs), all 12 workers ran on the entrypoint's node. During held-out evaluation, 1,668 concurrent rollouts saturated that host's namespace creation. Median eval completion rose from 250 s to 781 s, verifier timeouts per eval rose from 0 to 149, and median running vLLM requests fell from 19 to 2.4. With this change, the same run places 2 workers on each node.

Workers go on every node, including policy nodes. Inference-engine node IDs are not exposed uniformly across the hybrid, shared-group, per-engine and multiprocessing placements, and remote engines have no Ray node. On Iris, CPU is a request without a limit, so Ray advertises each host's full core count, and the GPU roles reserve about one CPU per GPU. The Iris task runtime already stages task data, the policy model and the tokenizer on every rank before Ray starts. Workers reach the rollout buffer, the trajectory sink and the engines through Ray actors, and `WorkerShard` only divides per-process limits. We have not measured whether sandbox load on policy nodes slows Megatron steps.

With workers on several hosts, a local `trainer.rollout_buffer.object_store_root` would hold payloads on disks the trainer cannot read, so a rollout worker pool with a local root on a multi-node cluster now raises at startup. The preference-pair runner writes from the trainer process and keeps accepting a local root. Object-store URIs and the default in-memory payloads are unchanged.

topics.title: taskforge: Agentic Taskforge flavor
topics.body:
Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1spGGRyLJAlA22SGKaRLLV3AFPZlPAq7OikT2P8NBWD8

<hr>

Add the Agentic Taskforge flavor, `taskforge.agentic`. `generate_tasks(idea, n, config)` runs one managed agent (#10264) for a `CapabilityIdea` (#10265). The agent produces up to `n` `TaskSpec`s and handles research, program building, and difficulty tuning.[^1] An example driver is `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/generate_tasks_agentic.py`.

The agent uses a bubblewrap `LocalMachineFactory` shell with Python, `taskcompendium`, and `verifyit`, without network access. It has six tools: `grade`, `rollout`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `submit`, and `finish`. Bubblewrap requires `--container-profile container_profile_privileged` on Iris. Shell output is capped at 32 KiB per command. The agent's shell uses `ShellHarness.output_limit_bytes` and `taskforge.capability` from #10442, which is merged.

`submit` enforces an evidence gate keyed by the `TaskSpec` digest, so the agent cannot accept its own task. A correct control must pass and a wrong control must fail. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, without thinking, must pass 0.1–0.8 of at least eight graded solver rollouts, with at most 25% format failures. The gate also requires at least four adversary rollouts with a graded answer. Finally, a GLM reviewer solves the task blind, reads the task, evidence, and its blind solution, then decides. `finish` refuses once if fewer than `n` tasks are accepted while more than half the solver rollouts remain. A session that stops before `finish` receives a report of the tools.

The tools refuse a task id that is not a file name of at most 128 characters, or that an accepted task already has, when they first read the task, so that no rollouts go to a task whose outputs the driver cannot write. `submit` also refuses files in `resources.all`, because the review reads only `resources.worker`. The driver's agent and solver models resolve the relay again after a connection error, so a relay that moved does not end the sessions. The tools also refuse a task that sets `environment_variables` or `setup_commands`: the engine resolves `${NAME}` from the host, which holds the driver's keys, and setup commands can rewrite the files that the review reads. The driver sets no tool-turn timeout, because one turn can hold several tool calls with their own deadlines, and the attempt timeout bounds the session. A solver that runs out of turns, budget or output length fails its run, and the driver sets the judge temperature (0.7). `grade` records a control only for a graded answer, so an answer that the answer format rejects does not satisfy the wrong-control rule. A review takes its two judge calls from the budget before its first call, so it never stops after the blind solve.

The solver's ShellSim shell has `python3` with the standard library when the task's package spec lists PyPI packages, even none. The prompt tells the agent how to give it, and `example_build.py` sets `package_spec=PackageSpec(pypi_packages=())`. With no package spec, `python3` is not found, and the solver is limited to awk and bc arithmetic. The 30-idea results below come from runs without solver Python.

Every accepted task runs in ShellSim: `submit` refuses a task with a shell or files unless its semantics are `shell_simulator`, and only ShellSim runs those. A task with no shell and no files would need no machine, but no agent made one in the runs (401 of 401 accepted tasks were ShellSim tasks). The solver's machine, harness and limits are fixed in `tools.py`, so these tasks do not train a policy on a real Linux machine with processes, network or git. Support for `linux_process` tasks can come later: the TaskSpec contract and RolloutEngine already run them on Docker, bubblewrap, Daytona, Iris and QEMU, and Taskforge would need a configurable solver machine factory, semantics that follow it, and a prompt for that machine.

Across 30 ideas, 20 from the catalog and 10 from `analyze_failed_runs`, with `n = 4`, the agentic generator accepted 59 tasks. Nine ideas reached 4/4 and 10 reached 0; each idea below four has a report.[^3] The staged generator using the same gate accepted 3 of 108 tasks; 77 were outside the pass-rate band, most of them too easy. Blind verifier agents rated 8 of the 59 agentic tasks blocking (14%) and found no wrong reference. GLM request tokens per accepted task were 3.9M for agentic and 0.9M for staged.[^4]

The full branch, including the staged comparison driver, is #10439. More `submit` checks and rollout-budget changes follow in #10445 and #10446. This PR alone was not run.[^2] Part of #10152.

[^1]: Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1spGGRyLJAlA22SGKaRLLV3AFPZlPAq7OikT2P8NBWD8
[^2]: In an earlier 30-idea run with the leak and tolerance checks but without the option rules, guess check, rollout cap, and last-line regrade, blind verifiers rated 22% of accepted tasks blocking.
[^3]: Outputs: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/user/rav/projects/taskforge-agentic/` (`l30`, `l30-d09`, `staged-30c`). Three agentic sessions stopped on model or tool deadlines during a `cw-us-east-02a` controller outage.
[^4]: The agentic figure sums request tokens across about 125 turns per session. About 98% are the same prefix sent again. `ChatModel` does not record cached tokens, so actual compute is lower.

```markdown
* part of #10152
* stacked on #10443; the agent's shell uses `ShellHarness.output_limit_bytes` from #10442
* add the Agentic Taskforge flavor, `taskforge.agentic`: `generate_tasks(idea, n, config)` runs one managed agent (#10264) for a `CapabilityIdea` (#10265), and the agent makes up to `n` `TaskSpec`s; research, build programs and difficulty tuning are the agent's work[^1]

  * a correct control passes and a wrong control fails

  * >= 4 adversary rollouts
```

🤖 Holistic review of 4c3d692b51.

This PR adds `taskforge.agentic`. For each `CapabilityIdea`, one GLM agent makes up to `n` `TaskSpec`s in a bubblewrap shell. Code decides which tasks to accept: a gate checks the evidence recorded under the hash of each task's content, and a blind GLM review runs last. The package fits the repository. It is a new `TOP` package beside `stage_coordinator`, it imports only the shared modules, and it runs every grade and model call through `RolloutEngine`, `ShellHarness` tool providers and ShellSim. Two findings change behavior: one `rollout` call can outlast the agent's tool-turn deadline, and an empty answer satisfies the "wrong control fails" rule.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  driver["generate_tasks_agentic.py"]:::added -->|"agent and solver models"| relay["RelayModel"]:::added
  driver --> gen["generate_tasks"]:::added
  subgraph agentic["taskforge.agentic"]
    gen -->|"run_task"| engine["RolloutEngine + ShellHarness"]
    engine -->|"shell"| bwrap["LocalMachineFactory (bwrap, no network)"]
    engine -->|"tool calls"| tools["TaskforgeTools"]:::added
    tools -->|"grade, rollout"| solver["solver RolloutEngine on ShellSim"]
    tools -->|"submit"| gate["missing_evidence + Gate"]:::added
    tools -->|"blind solve, review"| judge["GlmClient judge"]
    tools -->|"web_search, web_fetch"| web["ParallelWeb"]:::added
  end
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Before.** On main, `stage_coordinator` takes validation from the caller as a function. The staged driver, `generate_tasks.py`, writes the TaskSpec of each GLM-written program and runs no solver on it. No code on main measures the pass rate of a task before it is accepted.

**Design.** `submit` first refuses a task that the tools cannot run. Then `missing_evidence` (`gate.py:44`) checks four rules on the evidence of that exact content hash: controls, solver band, answer format and adversary runs. A changed file has a new hash and no evidence, so the agent cannot accept a task by editing it. The reviewer solves the task blind, then reads the task, the evidence and its blind answer, and decides. `_load` refuses an id that `FILE_SAFE_ID` rejects, an id longer than 128 characters, and a second task with an accepted id, so the driver can name output directories after task ids.

**Evidence and limits.** At 4c3d692b51, the agentic tests, `test_imports.py` and `test_generate_tasks_agentic.py` pass locally (11 tests). The code confirms these claims of the body: the workspace has no network (`NetworkPolicy.DENY` becomes `--unshare-net`), shell output stops at 32 KiB, `finish` refuses once, and a session that stops early gets a report from the tools. The gate values in the driver match the body. The yield and quality numbers come from the full branch, #10439; the body says that this PR alone was not run. The bubblewrap workspace has no memory limit, so a runaway build program uses the memory of the driver container. The new commit addresses the four Codex findings: `RelayModel` resolves the relay again after a connection error, `submit` refuses `resources.all`, and `_load` checks task ids.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/generate_tasks_agentic.py:81` The solver `attempt_timeout` is 3600 s, the same as the agent's `tool_turn_timeout` at line 102. `rollout` (`tools.py:339`) runs `n * len(paths)` rollouts in waves of `MAX_CONCURRENT_ROLLOUTS = 8`, and the agent's tool-turn deadline starts before the first solver deadline. When one solver runs to its own deadline, or two waves are slow, the agent's deadline expires first and ends the whole session with its remaining budget unused. In run L, three sessions stopped on model-turn or tool-turn deadlines while the relay was slow. `ShellHarness.check` refuses a `command_timeout` at or above `tool_turn_timeout` for the same reason. #10446 caps the rollouts of one task version, but nothing caps the time of one call. Check in `AgenticConfig` that `solver_limits.attempt_timeout` is below `agent_limits.tool_turn_timeout`, lower the driver's solver value (for example to 900 s), and make `rollout` refuse a call when `ceil(n * len(paths) / max_concurrent_rollouts) * attempt_timeout` reaches the agent's tool-turn timeout.

- **2. Should fix:** `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/agentic/tools.py:328` `grade` records every result that is not a pass as a failed control, because `_passed` returns `False` for `SUBMISSION_FAILURE`, `INFRA_ERROR`, `UNAVAILABLE` and `INVALID_TASK`. The prompt (`prompts.py:48-49`) tells the agent to grade "wrong or empty answers" with `expect "fail"`. A probe at this head: `grade(answer="", expect="fail")` returns `submission_failure` with `as_expected: true`, and `"the answer is unknown"` gives the same result. Each satisfies the "a wrong control fails" half of the controls rule (`gate.py:50-54`), although the grader rejected no wrong value. `_rollouts` (`tools.py:374`) already keeps format failures and ungraded results apart. The solver band still needs graded failures, so the gate still refuses a grader that rejects nothing. Record a control only for `Outcome.GRADED`, report a format failure to the agent without recording it, raise `ToolError` for the other statuses as `_rollouts` does, and change the prompt to "wrong answers in the answer format".

- **3. Should fix:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/generate_tasks_agentic.py:136` `Model = Callable[[ModelRequest], Awaitable[ModelTurn]]` copies `rolloutengine.models.Model`. Import `Model` from `rolloutengine.models` in the driver and in `test_generate_tasks_agentic.py:9`, and delete the alias.

No tests to drop. No other open PR needs action.

🤖 The three findings of the [holistic review](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10444#issuecomment-6327427643) are fixed in 5b4fcbbaa:

1. **Rollout calls inside the tool turn.** `AgenticConfig` now refuses a `solver_limits.attempt_timeout` that is not less than `agent_limits.tool_turn_timeout`. The driver's solver attempt timeout is 900 s (it was 3600 s). `rollout` refuses a call whose rollouts, run `max_concurrent_rollouts` at a time, can outlast the tool turn: `(ceil(tool_turn / attempt) - 1) * max_concurrent_rollouts` rollouts at most, which is 24 with the driver's values. The refusal uses no budget, and a test covers it.
2. **Only graded controls.** `grade` records a control only for `Outcome.GRADED`. A `SUBMISSION_FAILURE` returns `"control": false` with a note to the agent, and the other statuses raise `ToolError`. The prompt now asks for "wrong answers in the answer format". A test checks that `grade(answer="", expect="fail")` leaves `controls` missing at `submit`.
3. **`Model`.** The driver and `test_generate_tasks_agentic.py` import `Model` from `rolloutengine.models`, and the alias is gone.

I restacked #10445 and #10446 on this commit. At the top of the stack, 150 taskforge tests pass.

🤖 abc9f0fac (the stack is now rebased on main bf3bb61ac):

1. **Environment variables.** The tools refuse a task with `environment_variables` when they first read it, before any grade or rollout. `prepare_machine_spec` gets `dict(os.environ)`, so a `${PARALLEL_API_KEY}` value would resolve to the driver's key inside the solver machine. Plain values are refused too, because the review does not see them.
2. **Setup commands.** Refused in the same place. They run as root after the files are installed and can change what the solver sees, but `_public_task` shows the review only `resources.worker`.
3. **Tool-turn deadline.** One turn can hold several tool calls, so the per-call wave limit from 5b4fcbbaa did not protect the session. The driver now sets `tool_turn_timeout=None`, and `_check_waves`, `AgenticConfig.__post_init__` and their test are gone. Each tool call has its own deadline: the solver attempts (900 s), the judge client, the web client, and a new timeout on the file read. The 6 h attempt timeout bounds the session.
4. **Out-of-turns solvers.** A submission failure from a solver that stopped on `max_turns`, `budget_reached`, `length` or `total_turn_timeout` is a failed graded run, not a format failure. A test covers a solver that loops until `max_turns`.
5. **Judge temperature.** The driver sets `LLMPolicy(temperature=0.7)` explicitly.

#10445 and #10446 are restacked. 154 taskforge tests pass at the top.

topics.title: Add correctness-gated GDN-2 TPU kernels
topics.body:
Add experimental single-device Gated DeltaNet-2 kernels and a correctness-gated benchmark. Vendor only Atomic Ops' four compute files at a9bd7c5315907d23ccf1ce6b033d46a196566888 as the baseline, retaining the MIT license and original arithmetic. The modified candidate replaces off-diagonal pairwise exponentiation and reduction with matrix products, and masks noncausal pairs before exponentiation. It has no clipping, non-finite replacement, or solve damping.

Repeated matched sweeps show 3.05–3.27x faster forward+backward on v5e/v5p and 3.12–3.22x on v6e than each device's fastest tested baseline configuration, for batches 4/8, 4096 tokens, and six 128-dimensional heads in FP32/BF16. The v6e forward-only speedup is 5.36–5.62x. Outputs, final state, and gradients for q/k/v/w/b/g and the initial state pass an independent CPU recurrence before either timing mode is accepted. All four TPU generations select 128-token chunks; the solve microblock is 16 tokens on v4/v5e/v5p and 32 on v6e. Batches 5–7 are unmeasured interpolation.

The v4 candidate passes the same representative shapes; all four hardware types pass separate batch-1, 512-token stress tests with log-decays sampled down to -5. The baseline does not compile on v4; no baseline speedup is claimed there. The v4 256-token configuration exceeds VMEM. Its selected 128-token, batch-8 FP32 forward-only measurements include periodic outliers. v6e's selected tile repeats within 0.22%, but other tile configurations also show outliers. All timing samples are retained.

[Measurement artifacts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3df6efef5a0fb18928e72673e9fd5f769749ae15/docs/reports/data/gdn2-tpu-20260922/README.md) retain exact source snapshots, hardware settings, compilation costs, and caveats. The [kernel reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3df6efef5a0fb18928e72673e9fd5f769749ae15/docs/references/gdn2-kernels.md) documents reproduction and explicit tuning fallback. Affected unit tests, lint/type checks, and documentation-link checks pass. Model integration and training are outside this change.

topics.title: [harbor] Match Pi failure markers as complete stderr lines
topics.body:
After a process is killed, Bash can echo source code containing Pi’s authentication and context-limit markers to stderr. Substring matching then misclassifies the process termination. Match these markers only as complete lines so the original signal error is preserved.

[Investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/835).

topics.title: [belay] Record recipe control runs and cite them from trials
topics.body:
This PR adds a place in the Belay registry to record control runs once, and lets each trial point to the control it was compared against. Today a trial names its control only inside a free-text note. After this change, the control's W&B runs and losses can be looked up from any trial that used it, and a reference to a control that doesn't exist fails validation.

Some terms used below. A trial compares a variant against a control: baseline runs of the same setup without the change. A trial's delta is the variant's loss minus the control's loss, where loss is Paloma macro loss (the loss on the Paloma evaluation set, averaged with equal weight across its domains). A recipe is the training setup that variants are added to, such as Belay Ckpt 1. A rung is the model size a run uses, such as d512.

The problem: every trial copies its control into the free-text `baseline` field. The 25 X0217 and X0218 trials all carry the same text, `Belay Ckpt 1 belay-X0217-ctrl-s0/s1 (3.0269 / 3.0315)`. To recompute a delta, for example as measured bits per byte instead of the Belay page's placeholder value, you need the control's W&B runs, and today they can only be parsed out of that text.

The fix: a new file, `registry/recipes/ckpt1.yaml`, records the Belay Ckpt 1 recipe (its branch and commit) and its one control, `c001`: the runs `belay-X0217-ctrl-s0` and `-s1`, one loss per run, at d512 for 2,760 steps. Each of the 25 trials gains `baseline_control: ckpt1.c001` and keeps its free-text `baseline`, so nothing is lost. Loading the registry checks that every `baseline_control` names a control in a recipe file, run at the trial's rung and step count, so a typo or a reference to the wrong control fails instead of silently pointing at the wrong baseline. The commit check from #10447 is reused for the recipe and control commits.

Not covered here: about a thousand older trials name their control as "candidate N" with losses but no run names. Linking them needs W&B lookups and is left for later. The Belay page ignores the new field.

The recipe commit, `8415c3ce84`, is the current head of `marin_belay_v1_ckpt1`. That is a README commit made after Ckpt 1's code, so the commit that defines Ckpt 1 may be a better value.

The logic is in three files; the rest are the recipe file and the 25 one-line additions:

- [`experiments/belay/registry.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10452/files#diff-6c8e0d191e5380113f6c25c496d65023899fe81b0eae0dd09ea65d710e5c56b2): `Recipe`, `Control`, `Trial.baseline_control`, `load_recipes()`, `validate_recipes()` and `check_baseline_controls()`
- [`tests/belay/test_registry.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10452/files#diff-78802c1fa9acc99d3718576c45ff26568493a7cc54d53a391c7f7ee3e6b6273f): a missing control is rejected and an existing one loads
- [`experiments/belay/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10452/files#diff-13a5dbcc070bc8416c9bc33e2d51070d8370c15b71c069105d8aa0ae3e7404a8): the recipe and control format

🤖 Holistic review of dae791be2e0680545087b6f8f761f4db50817837.

This change declares the provenance fields that Evalchemy's custom benchmarks now emit (`source`, `reducers`, `prompt_length`, `requires_judge`) on `BenchmarkMetadataRef`. Records that previously failed validation and were written as `artifact_failed` will now publish their scores. The fix is correct for today's Evalchemy pin. However, the same drift can reach production again because the Evalchemy pin-advance gate cannot detect it. Readers in evaldash also need a release before the backfill.

Before this change, `BenchmarkMetadataRef` (`extra="forbid"`) listed only the core protocol fields. Evalchemy's `BenchmarkMetadata.to_dict()` (`eval/contracts/benchmark_metadata.py`, pin `28631c7`) adds the four provenance keys only when `source` is set, which happens only for custom chat benchmarks. `reducers` is `asdict(ReducerSpec)`, and `source` is `asdict(SourceRef)`. The new TypedDicts match those dataclasses field for field at the pinned commit. I checked locally that pydantic applies the parent's `extra="forbid"` to the nested TypedDicts and that `total=True` requires every key. As a result, any unknown or missing nested key rejects the whole benchmark entry. The PR intends this ("other unknown fields remain rejected"). The 164 tests in `test_eval_archive.py`, `test_evaluation.py`, `tests/evals/test_records.py`, and `test_harbor_runner.py` pass locally. The parametrized `provenance` case is a real regression test: it fails at the base commit.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py:87` `BenchmarkReducerRef` mirrors Evalchemy's `ReducerSpec` dataclass exactly, and Evalchemy serializes that dataclass with `asdict`. Adding one field to `ReducerSpec` or `SourceRef` upstream therefore brings back this incident: scored runs become `artifact_failed`. The pin-advance gate cannot catch it. `config/external/migration.toml` `[evalchemy]` runs `gsm8k-smoke.yaml` as its e2e, and `gsm8k` takes the lm-eval route (`_lm_eval_metadata`), which never sets `source`, so the smoke never emits these keys. #10235 advanced the pin past this change with the gate green. Either make the gate cover the strict shape by switching the e2e to, or adding, a custom-route benchmark such as `MATH500` or `AIME24`, or make only the nested provenance types tolerant with `@with_config(ConfigDict(extra="allow"))` on the three TypedDicts. The second option matches the sibling `BenchmarkMetricRef`, which already uses `extra="allow"`, while the top level stays forbid.
- **2. Should fix:** `infra/marina/apps/evaldash/app.py:55` evaldash validates records with this same `BenchmarkMetadataRef` (`read_records` → `RecordParseFailure`; `results_db.py` `EvalRunRecord.model_validate`). Once this merges, newly published Evalchemy records and the planned backfill of the 117 runs carry the new keys. A deployment built before this commit drops those records as parse failures, so they will not appear on the dashboard. Release evaldash from a commit that includes this change before running the backfill, and say so in the PR body next to the backfill note.

topics.title: [taskforge] Read every Clef question type through the decision client
topics.body:
Let the Clef decision client read any mix of choice, noul, and score questions. The adversary arbiter can then ask noul and choice questions through the same client, HTTP pool, and in-flight limit used for decision grading.

`ClefDecisionClient.read(state, questions, *, elastic, truncate_from, timeout)` builds the request, fits it to the window with Clef's tokenizer, sends it through the client's HTTP pool and in-flight limit, and returns Clef's whole response. It rejects responses that skip a question or answer one with the wrong type. The client satisfies `ClefReader`, a narrow protocol containing only `read`, and still retries nothing.

`decide` now makes one `read` call for a grader's score questions. Its signature, errors, and request bytes are unchanged; one test pins the request-body digest for both a fitting request and one cut to a 16k window. The graders' `DecisionClient` protocol is unchanged, so each grader still asks only its comparative score question.

Builds on #10302.

---

topics.title: [harbor] Exclude inline policy references from the Tau3 prompt
topics.body:
Tau³ tasks have two blocks: `<instructions>` tells a standalone coding agent how to start, advance, and end the conversation; `<policy>` contains the customer-service rules. Our relay is meant to control the conversation itself, so it should give the Pi coding agent relay-specific conversation instructions plus only the domain policy.

The parser includes `<instructions>` in the extracted policy, giving Pi conflicting directions about who controls the conversation. In the observed run, Pi ended the conversation, then the relay tried to send another message and failed.

Extract only the policy block.

Upstream Harbor's [task template](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/867801035118d1e75c0996821779b59238c7fb29/adapters/tau3-bench/src/tau3_bench/task-template/instruction.md#L1-L16) has the same structure. Its [reference-agent extractor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/867801035118d1e75c0996821779b59238c7fb29/adapters/tau3-bench/tau3_llm_agent.py#L28-L41) already avoids this bug by selecting the policy block immediately after `</instructions>`.

[Investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/810).

topics.title: [datakit] Require MMLU, HumanEval and GSM8K in the decontam corpus
topics.body:
Eval corpus preparation now stops before it seals the lm-eval manifest when gsm8k, humaneval or mmlu, or any of their leaf tasks, fails to load. The manifest records each required task's leaf tasks under `required_tasks`, and the eval Bloom build refuses a manifest that does not include all of them.

The aa-index-v4.1.1-v3 corpus treated these tasks as best effort. GSM8K failed in every region because the Hub no longer resolves the un-namespaced `gsm8k` ID, and MMLU failed on CoreWeave after a dropped connection. Preparation logged and skipped both, so the Hero's decontam marks (`_combined_fixed_8c17764d` Bloom, built from the CoreWeave corpus) never checked MMLU or GSM8K. HumanEval loaded in every region.

The loader patch now maps `gsm8k` to `openai/gsm8k`. A sealed corpus version is immutable, so `EVAL_CORPUS_VERSION` moves to aa-index-v4.1.1-v4. The v4 corpus is staged and sealed in `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin`, `gs://marin-us-west4`, `gs://marin-eu-west4` and `gs://marin-us-central2`, the four prefixes that held v3, so the Datakit canaries can build the Bloom after merge. Each regional lm-eval manifest includes 811 leaf tasks, among them gsm8k, humaneval and all 57 MMLU subjects. 116 other best-effort leaf tasks still fail, 40 of them on datasets that need a loading script and 20 on other un-namespaced Hub IDs.

The new `best_effort_required_tasks` hash attribute rekeys the reference pipeline and testbed Blooms. The Hero's pinned decontam paths do not change.

topics.title: [finelog] Increase forwarding throughput for dense log backlogs
topics.body:
Increase regional Finelog → hub forwarding throughput so dense log backlogs drain faster and delayed task logs reach Iris. Forward up to four namespaces concurrently and read up to one million log rows per read-and-send cycle. Requests retain their byte limit, and chunks remain serial within the log namespace. The saved source cursor records completed progress and cannot advance past a pending or retryable request.

Encode each candidate chunk once. If its payload exceeds 150 MiB, split it in half and process each half the same way. Process the left half first to preserve source order. Source scans keep separate row-count and segment bounds, and oversized single rows retain their existing handling. Release the decoded Arrow batch before waiting for acknowledgements. Slow-cycle diagnostics separate source reads, chunk encoding, and RPC compression/transport/durable acknowledgement from cursor persistence.

During the October 17 incident, RNO2A was roughly 395 million regional sequence positions behind. Forwarding counters showed about 24,000 accepted positions/sec before deployment and 87,000–107,000/sec over successive 71- and 65-second samples after deploying namespace concurrency and larger reads. A dense source sample contained about 77,000 rows per second of event time; this measures production density. Sequence positions can include gaps and filtered rows, so those counters are not exact row counts. By 17:56 UTC, backlog was down to 91 positions and all 417 rows for the affected task were present on the hub. The chunk-splitting follow-up remains undeployed.

A local benchmark on one million synthetic NCCL-shaped rows with six log columns and 294 MB of Arrow IPC output reduced serialization attempts from seven to three compared with the deployed sizing search. Bytes serialized, including discarded attempts, fell from 1,010 to 589 MB; both versions produced two requests. With 100,000 narrow rows followed by 100,000 wide rows, halving produced nine requests against eight with the packing search. Halving accepts underfilled requests to avoid the sizing search. These measurements describe serialization work; they do not establish an end-to-end throughput improvement.

A bounded million-row regional read took 1.32 seconds initially and 0.19 seconds on repeat. Later live scans took 5.4–8.2 seconds in 12–16-second cycles, including a 128-segment window returning only 424,000 rows. Read cost varies with segment geometry and cache state. An isolated local server capped at four CPUs acknowledged compressed 500,000-row writes in 0.70–0.78 seconds. Live hub samples showed about three active cores on a four-core VM, compaction/index work, and near-zero disk I/O wait. The largest resolved perf symbols involved copying, comparisons, and page faults; stripped Rust symbols limited attribution. These probes do not fully apportion live cycle time; the added stage timings expose the remaining waits.

[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/780).

topics.title: [levanter] resume into a root with uncommitted partial checkpoints fails the next save (TensorStore chunk-layout mismatch)
topics.body:
Resuming from a committed epoch checkpoint into a root containing later uncommitted checkpoints can fail on the next save. A 32-H100 Snowball SFT continuation restored step 320, completed the remaining 642 updates, then failed while finalizing an asynchronous save into the existing step-641 directory:

```text
ValueError: FAILED_PRECONDITION: Error opening "zarr3" driver:
Expected "chunk_shape" of [2560] but received: [80]
array: model/transformer/blocks/1/rms_attn/weight
checkpoint: checkpoints/step-641/
```

The checkpoint barrier subsequently timed out after 30 minutes, and the gang exited before producing its final HF export.

Reproduce:
1. Train with permanent epoch checkpoints at zero-based steps 320, 641 and 962. Interrupt the run while later checkpoint writes are incomplete, leaving `step-320/metadata.json` committed, a step-641 TensorStore payload without `metadata.json`, and a manifest-only step-962 directory.
2. Resume from the committed step-320 checkpoint with the same output root. Keep the incomplete later directories in place.
3. Continue through the remaining epoch boundaries. In the observed continuation, the save requested chunk shape `[2560]` for an array whose partial write stored `[80]`. TensorStore raised the error above; the asynchronous failure surfaced at the terminal checkpoint hook, after training had completed. The reason the requested chunk shape changed after restore has not yet been isolated, so this is an observed reproduction rather than a reduced deterministic test.

Observed on `cw-rno2a`, 2026-10-21, with four eight-H100 tasks, batch 16 × 32,768, eight-way expert parallelism, four-way context parallelism, and native checkpoints every 321 updates. Both the original run and continuation used `11d41241ec`, `experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py`, and `--parent v0.1 --arm relay --data-variant low --learning-rate 1e-6 --epochs 3 --hf-export-schedule final-only`. No mesh or optimizer change was requested on resume. The original coordinator `/karan/arm-train-relay-low-v0p1-v7-20261021-cw-rno2a` was killed at 18:47 UTC during the controller outage in #10433. Its root retained a committed step 320 (16:48 UTC), an uncommitted step-641 payload (17:49–17:54 UTC), and a manifest-only step 962 (18:30 UTC).

Continuation `/karan/arm-train-relay-low-v0p1-v7-20261021-cw-rno2a-r3`, at `11d41241ec`, selected step 320 at 19:20 UTC. It reached step 641 at 20:09 UTC and the last optimizer update, step 962, at 20:41 UTC. At 21:11 UTC the terminal hook surfaced the step-641 chunk-layout error and checkpoint barrier timeout. Fresh object reads found neither a step-641 nor a step-962 commit marker. The original partial directories are preserved under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/checkpoints/karan/relay-low-v0.1-v7-20261021-lr1e-06-3ep/2026.10.21/checkpoints/`.

Two plain SFT runs using the same batch size and mesh committed their epoch saves in clean roots; those runs exported HF after epoch 2 and at the final step. A third plain SFT run using final-only HF exports also committed its first epoch, step 205, in a clean root. These observations show that final-only HF exports alone do not prevent native saves; they do not isolate every condition needed for the chunk-layout mismatch.

Expected: On resume, identify later step directories lacking a commit marker and remove or version those incomplete writes before reusing their step numbers. A terminal checkpoint write should start in an empty directory when a stale incomplete directory exists, without reopening its incompatible arrays. Preserve committed checkpoints, and report asynchronous save failures before allowing an entire additional epoch to run.

Related: #9380 reports a chunk-layout mismatch when rewriting an already committed final checkpoint after a resume with no new optimizer updates. This case concerns uncommitted later checkpoints encountered while continuing from an earlier committed epoch. Part of #10213.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Checkpoint discovery requires `metadata.json`, so the continuation correctly restored step 320 while leaving the uncommitted step 641 payload in place. `Checkpointer` then reused the fixed `step-641` destination; TensorStore opened arrays already carrying a different chunk grid. The previous asynchronous save is checked at the next save or during trainer exit, which can delay the error until another epoch has run.

**Relevant code**
- [`checkpoint.py#L638-L667`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L638-L667) — fixed step destination
- [`checkpoint.py#L840-L915`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L840-L915) — completion marker follows writes
- [`checkpoint.py#L1217-L1243`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L1217-L1243) — committed-directory discovery
- [`tensorstore_serialization.py#L678-L820`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py#L678-L820) — prior-save wait and array open
- [`trainer.py#L412-L430`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L412-L430) — final asynchronous wait

# Proposed Fix

Give each save invocation a fresh checkpoint directory, such as `step-641-<save-id>`, with one ID chosen on process 0 and shared across the gang. Keep `metadata.json` as the completion marker and numeric step as its source of truth. Existing `step-N` checkpoints remain readable; a resumed save never reopens a prior attempt's arrays, including an uncommitted attempt or a committed final-step save (#9380). This avoids deleting an old writer's payload while it may still be active.

Audit readers and operational scripts that assume an exact `step-N` directory name. Discovery already reads the step from metadata, but direct path construction may need updating. Add a nonblocking check of completed asynchronous saves to each training checkpoint hook and before final hooks/export. Raise the original failure as soon as the background commit finishes while preserving asynchronous training when it is still running.

Test with local TensorStore data: leave a step 641 payload with incompatible chunk metadata and no commit marker, restore step 320, save step 641, and verify that the new checkpoint loads while the old payload and committed step 320 are untouched. Cover a repeated committed final step, cross-process agreement on the save path, and a real failed asynchronous write reported before the next scheduled save. Keep orphan cleanup separate from the save path; it needs an age threshold and an inactive-writer check before deleting object-store data.

The path change reaches checkpoint producers, direct-path consumers, and asynchronous trainer error handling, so this needs a design and regression pass rather than a one-line overwrite fix. No open PR matched #10453 or the chunk-layout failure. The remaining decision is the retention window for abandoned attempt directories; it does not block save isolation.

🤖 Control evidence: a sibling run on the same trainer head and the same final-only HF export setting, started in a clean root, committed both of its epoch-boundary native checkpoints (step-205 marker at 20:35 UTC, step-411 marker at 22:02 UTC, both `is_temporary=false`). So the epoch-2 save path itself works; the failure above is specific to resuming into a root that already holds uncommitted partial step directories.

🤖 Closing evidence: the second resume (r4) of the same run, restored from the committed step-320 checkpoint into a clean output version with the old partial directories left untouched in the original version, committed both its epoch-2 native save (step 641, 22:40 UTC) and its terminal save (step 962, 23:43 UTC) and produced a verified HF export. Same trainer head, same data, same settings as the failed same-root resume; only the output root differs. So the failure is entirely the collision with uncommitted partial step directories in the resume root.

🤖 Reproduction inputs and a correction to the clean-root comparison:

The failed same-root continuation used `11d41241ec`; the successful clean-version continuation used `519568ab74`. The intervening change removed the launch wrapper's production-priority override, not the trainer save path. The failed continuation was interactive and the successful continuation production, on different nodes. Thus “only the output root differs” in the previous comment was too strong. The TensorStore error identifies a collision with existing incompatible array metadata; the clean-root success supports the workaround but is not a fully controlled experiment.

At `11d41241ec`, the failed continuation's training entrypoint was:

```bash
python -m experiments.post_training.agentic_sweep.arms \
  --parent v0.1 --arm relay --data-variant low --run-date 20261021 \
  --context-length 32768 --hf-export-schedule final-only \
  --arm-data s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/rows/v7-low-20261020/relay \
  --manifest-sha256 0de958b10a567b4e67d4bcfba34f7339731c2044d94b55c36720779407a4e70a \
  --plain-data s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/rows/v7-low-20261020/plain \
  --learning-rate 1e-6 --epochs 3 --only train --preemption-retries 2 \
  --resume-checkpoint s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/checkpoints/karan/relay-low-v0.1-v7-20261021-lr1e-06-3ep/2026.10.21/checkpoints/step-320 \
  --run
```

This is the training-stage invocation inside the Iris coordinator, not a complete outer submission; its verified epoch caches must already exist. It requests 963 total updates and restores 321 completed updates, leaving 642. No mesh change was requested. The old root's later partial directories remain evidence, not valid restore points.

For the successful control, the training artifact alone was assigned version `2026.10.21.4`; cache versions stayed `2026.10.21`, and restore still explicitly named the original step 320. The new step-641 commit timestamp was `2026-10-21T22:40:35.373458Z`, and step 962 committed at `2026-10-21T23:43:12.051183Z`. Both commits preceded the verified HF export. Do not retry this reproduction against the preserved root without first copying its partial state to an isolated test destination.

The remaining unresolved detail is why the resumed writer requested chunk shape `[2560]` where the old partial array stored `[80]`. The observations establish the failure and the successful isolated-output workaround, not a reduced deterministic reproducer or a tested upstream fix.

topics.title: [iris] Reproducible job spec via secret and bundle references
topics.body:
## Problem

The `spec` verb (#7560) should render the definition a job was submitted with, sufficient to resubmit. It cannot be faithful today, for two structural reasons in the submission model.

**Secrets are inline literals.** Per-job env — `HF_TOKEN`, `WANDB_API_KEY`, every `-e KEY VALUE` — is carried as literal values end to end: the client injects them from its shell into `EnvironmentConfig.env_vars` (a `map<string,string>`, `rpc/job.proto:427`; `cluster/types.py:744`), the controller persists them verbatim in `job_config.environment_json` (`controller/schema.py`), and the k8s backend writes them straight into each pod's container env (`backends/k8s/tasks.py:619`). The only redaction is a cosmetic read-side copy in `get_job_status` (`cluster/redaction.py:40`, `controller/service.py:1789`). So a rendered spec must either leak the secrets or redact them into something that will not re-run. Separately, the plaintext already sits at rest in the controller DB and in every pod manifest (`kubectl get pod -o yaml`).

**Bundles render by id only.** `reconstruct_launch_job_request` rebuilds the request from normalized columns and drops `bundle_blob` (only `bundle_id` survives), along with `container_profile`, `client_revision_date`, and `federation` (`controller/codec.py:148`). A spec is a reference to a bundle, so its reproducibility depends on that bundle still existing.

## Proposal

Move secrets and bundles from inline values to named references that iris resolves, so a spec becomes a manifest of references with no secret material to redact.

### Secrets: reference, delegate the store

Submit `env_vars` values as references (`iris-secret://…`, or the existing `gcp-secret://…`) and resolve them at run time. iris already has the resolver: `rigging.secrets` resolves `env:` / `file:` / `gcp-secret://` (`secrets.py:33`), used today for cluster-config fields (`oauth_client_secret`, `signing_key`) behind an `assert_no_inlined_secrets` deploy guard (`cluster/config.py:113,1123`). Extending that resolver to per-job env is the natural step.

Two constraints:
- **Delegate the store.** iris resolves references; GCP Secret Manager and k8s Secrets hold the material. iris does not become a vault (encryption at rest, rotation, ACLs, audit) — that surface already exists in the cloud providers.
- **Resolve at the workload.** The pod resolves its own references (workload identity → Secret Manager, or a projected k8s Secret, as the `iris-task-env` envFrom already does — `backends/k8s/tasks.py:684`), so the literal never lands in the DB or the manifest. Controller-side resolution would restore reproducibility but keep the plaintext-in-manifest exposure.

This ties into per-tenant authorization (a cross-cutting item on #7560): a job may resolve only the references its tenant is cleared for.

### Bundles: formalize the reference, fix the lifetime

A bundle is already a SHA-256 content address (`cluster/bundle.py:33`): the controller stores it at `gs://…/bundles/{sha256}`, persists the id durably in `job_config.bundle_id` (`controller/schema.py:301`), and re-fetches it at dispatch via `{controller}/bundles/{id}.zip` (`backends/k8s/bundle_fetch.py:52`). An `iris-bundle://<hash>` scheme would formalize that content id into a self-describing URI — useful for spec portability, cosmetic on its own.

The substantive gap is lifetime, and it is the direct cause of the #7542 job loss. Nothing pins the bytes to a referencing job: the DB keeps the hash indefinitely, but the GCS object is TTL-expired (smoke/CI state roots under `tmp/ttl=7d/…`, `cli/cluster.py:548`) or wiped by `--clear-state` (`cli/cluster.py:562`), after which the `stage-workdir` init container 404s against a live id (`controller/dashboard.py:597`). **This half is independently shippable and does not depend on the rest of this design:** pin bundle bytes to referencing job records (ref-count, or exempt the `bundles/` prefix from TTL while a job references it). It should be pulled into its own PR as the concrete fix for the incident.

## Reproducibility semantics

A spec of references reproduces only where the references resolve: same secret project, a live bundle object, the correct controller. That matches every CI and Kubernetes manifest. `spec` should present as a manifest of references and surface per-reference resolvability, so an old spec whose bundle was collected fails loudly.

## Resolution seam

Custom schemes register through fsspec (`register_implementation` plus an `AbstractFileSystem` subclass, the `mirror://` pattern — `rigging/filesystem/mirror.py`), and iris already does I/O through raw `fsspec.core` (`cluster/bundle.py:52`), so a bundle scheme is reachable there. Secret resolution is a name→value lookup; `rigging.secrets` already handles it, so a scheme string can front it.

## Sequencing

1. Ship `spec` now over the reconstructed request with an explicit caveat (env redacted, bundle by id, not guaranteed re-runnable).
2. Pin bundle bytes to referencing jobs — standalone, closes the #7542 root cause.
3. Per-job secret references resolved at the workload; retire the redaction and the plaintext-at-rest exposure; `spec` drops its caveat.
4. Optional `iris-bundle://` / `iris-secret://` URI formalization and per-reference resolvability in `spec`.

## Open questions

- Scheme surface: reuse `gcp-secret://` directly, or front it with `iris-secret://` for backend independence?
- Bundle lifetime mechanism: DB ref-count versus a TTL exemption on referenced objects; who decrements on job GC?
- Resolution failure semantics: hard-fail the task on an unresolvable reference (as bundle fetch does today) with a typed reason surfaced through `describe`.
- Migration: env values that look secret keep working via the inline path until submitters move to references; a deploy-time guard rejects new inline secrets once references exist.

Follow-on to #7560 (the `spec` verb) and the closed #7543. The bundle-lifetime item is the root-cause fix for #7542. Design note for review; no code yet.

The `env:` / `file:` / `gcp-secret://` resolver already exists in `rigging.secrets` ([`secrets.py:33-35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/secrets.py#L33-L35), dispatch at [`secrets.py:126-131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/secrets.py#L126-L131)) but is wired only to cluster-config fields, not per-job env.

One structural suggestion: **split step 2 (pin bundle bytes to referencing jobs) into its own issue now.** It is the standalone root-cause fix for the job-loss incident, does not depend on the secret-reference redesign, and shouldn't wait behind it. The rest (per-job secret references resolved at the workload, retiring the redaction, optional `iris-bundle://` / `iris-secret://` URIs) is the larger design and belongs to #7560's arc.

On the open questions, where code gives a lean:
- **Scheme surface** — front with `iris-secret://`. Resolution moves to the pod, and the backing store differs by backend (Secret Manager via workload identity vs. a projected k8s Secret / the existing `iris-task-env` envFrom). A single iris-owned scheme keeps the submit-side reference backend-independent; `rigging.secrets` already dispatches by scheme, so adding one is cheap.

That is the real work of step 3, and it's what ties into per-tenant authorization on #7560.

topics.title: taskforge: test agentic graders with wrong answers made from the controls
topics.body:
After the evidence rules, `submit` now grades wrong answers that it makes from the agent's two controls. They are the right answer with one unit more or less in its last digit, the right and the wrong answer as a list in the two orders, and an empty answer. If the grader accepts one of them, `submit` refuses the task. The check uses only the task's own grader, so it does not read the grader spec. In a replay on 373 accepted tasks, these wrong answers found the same 16 loose tolerances and substring graders as rules that read the spec, and no other task. When a version has more than one right control, the one with the fewest decimals sets the precision: in three runs, 7 of 950 right controls had more decimals than the reference.

`submit` also refuses CSV files whose rows have different field counts, invalid JSON files and keyword graders. It refuses a task whose answer a solver with the prompt alone and no files guesses in at least three of four attempts, and these guesses use no rollout budget. In a replay on labeled tasks, the guess check refused 7 of 50 blocking, 2 of 46 ok and 4 of 145 minor tasks.

A review that finds a list of options from which the answer selects one refuses the task, and the agent prompt states this rule. On 313 labeled tasks, 27% of the option tasks that a review accepted had a blocking flaw, against 8% of the other tasks. Rules on the option length and place were active in that replay and did not close the gap, so they are not in this PR.

`submit` does not search the prompt and the files for the reference answer. In seven runs, such a search refused 61 task versions. In about 58 of them, the answer was an ID, a date or a label that the task asks the solver to find in the data. Among the accepted tasks, it found one real leak, a format example equal to the answer, and the guess check refuses that task in 8 of 8 replays.

Part of #10152. Follows #10444.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add triage: structural checks and a surface for expansion
topics.body:
Add triage as a deterministic preflight. `stage20_triage.checks` holds the proposal checks that read what `parse` leaves open, each reporting PASS, FAIL or SKIP: the required sections have content (fatal), and the grader section matches the declared verification, every research item states a purpose and the build plan names every declared resource (advisory). `stage20_triage.preflight.preflight(proposal)` runs them and rejects a fatal failure or a null proposal with the reason, accepts anything else, and makes no model call. Header validity is `parse`'s job: it also refuses a resource path outside the build root and a repeated build name. Whether the host can provide the machine is the build's check. `verdict.py` holds the `Verdict` record and `TriageDecision`, whose REPAIR value and `author_state` field are the surface a consumer's triage may use.

The preflight is the default, and the package has no model review: the README describes a panel with repair and a bounded review with obligations as designs a consumer could add, which experiments found not to be meaningful predictors of downstream quality. `StageCoordinator` still triages with `verdict.accept` here; #10298 moves it onto the preflight's verdict.

Builds on #10295; #10297 builds on it.

comments.body:
🤖 Holistic review of 650d667b7f.

This change replaces triage's accept-all stub with a deterministic preflight. `preflight` runs eight checks and rejects a proposal when a fatal check fails or when the proposal is null. Three of the checks cannot change a decision, a fourth holds two header rules that belong in `parse`, and `Verdict` gains two fields that nothing in the stack writes. Moving two header rules into `parse` and deleting the unused surface leaves a preflight of one fatal check and three advisory checks.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph stage10["stage10_proposal"]
    source["CapabilitySource (#10301)"] -->|"reply text"| parse["parse"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph stage20["stage20_triage"]
    preflight["preflight"]:::added -->|"runs"| checks["CHECKS: 8 checks"]:::added
    preflight -->|"returns"| verdict["Verdict"]:::added
  end
  parse -->|"TaskProposal"| preflight
  checks -.->|"solver_machine_violation"| parse
  verdict -->|"decision, reasons"| coord["StageCoordinator (#10298)"]
  verdict -->|"to_json"| file["slot-NN.verdict.json (#10301)"]
  coord -->|"REPAIR: repaired/k.md, read back with parse"| parse
  coord -->|"ACCEPT, author_state"| author["Author"]
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

Green boxes are new in this PR, and the orange box changes. A PR number marks where a later PR in the stack uses the triage. At this head the coordinator still triages with `accept`.

Before this change, `stage20_triage.verdict.accept` admitted every proposal. The coordinator still uses `accept` at this head; #10298 switches it to `preflight`. The #10301 driver (`propose_tasks.py`) calls `preflight` and writes each verdict, advisory results included, to `slot-NN.verdict.json`. Every proposal that reaches triage in the stack has passed `parse`: `CapabilitySource` parses each reply (`proposal_source.py:405` and `:436` in #10301), and the coordinator reads a repaired proposal back with `parse` before triage judges it (`coordinator.py:217` in #10298). The PR also deletes `llm.store.CallStore`, which only the removed model review used.

The 82 tests in `tests/stage20_triage` and `tests/stage10_proposal` pass locally at this head.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage20_triage/checks.py:139` `header_schema_valid` and `checks.py:174` `solver_machine_fits` cannot fail for a proposal that came from `parse`. Their own comments say so, and every proposal that reaches triage came from `parse`. They contain two new rules: resource paths stay inside the build root, and build names are unique. Enforce those in `stage10_proposal.model._header`, so every reader of a proposal gets them, and move their tests to the stage10 tests. A proposal that breaks them then gets the one repair request `CapabilitySource` makes for a parse failure, where today triage rejects it. Delete both checks and revert the `solver_machine_violation` split in `model.py:372-401`.

- **2. Should fix:** `checks.py:86` `CheckContext` holds only `allowed_combinations`, and no caller narrows it. `preflight` defaults to `EVERY_COMBINATION`, and both the coordinator and the #10301 driver call it with the proposal alone, so `combination_allowed` cannot fail outside tests. Delete `CheckContext`, `ALL_COMBINATIONS`, `EVERY_COMBINATION`, `combination_allowed` and the `ctx` argument on `preflight` and on every rule. The `Check` protocol (`checks.py:96`) then has one implementation; type `CHECKS` as `tuple[RuleCheck, ...]` and delete the protocol. Tests can call the rule functions directly, which removes `CHECKS_BY_NAME`. With findings 1 to 3 applied, the table is:

  ```python
  # lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage20_triage/checks.py
  CHECKS: tuple[RuleCheck, ...] = (
      RuleCheck("required_sections", Severity.FATAL, required_sections),
      RuleCheck("grader_matches_verification", Severity.ADVISORY, grader_matches_verification),
      RuleCheck("research_has_purpose", Severity.ADVISORY, research_has_purpose),
      RuleCheck("resources_in_build_plan", Severity.ADVISORY, resources_in_build_plan),
  )
  ```

- **3. Should fix:** `checks.py:293` `null_reason_only` is fatal, but `preflight.py:28` rejects every null proposal anyway. The check changes only the text of the reason. If a null proposal must declare empty `research`, `build` and `resources` lists, enforce that in `parse`. Otherwise delete the check.

- **4. Should fix:** `verdict.py:27` `REPAIR` and `verdict.py:47` `author_state` have no producer in the stack. At this head, `TRIAGE_EXITS` (`stage_coordinator/coordinator.py:109`) has no `REPAIR` entry, so a triage that returns it raises `KeyError` at `coordinator.py:258`. The owner chose the repair edge in the review thread, and #10298 adds it. No triage returns `REPAIR`, and every `StageFunctions` caller passes a placeholder `repair` (`no_call`, `no_repair`). #10298 also adds `author_state` as a third argument of the `Author` protocol. `glm_author` ignores it, and the coordinator docstring says nothing in the package writes one. Add `REPAIR` in #10298 together with the edge that handles it. Drop `author_state` and its `Author` argument until a triage writes one.

- **5. Related PR:** `lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/llm/store.py` (`CallStore`) and `tests/llm/test_store.py` come from #10291, and this PR deletes them. No PR between the two uses them. Remove both files and the README paragraph from #10291, so the stack does not add and then delete 231 lines. This PR then changes nothing under `llm/` except the docstring in `test_live.py`.

- **6. Should fix:** `lib/taskforge/README.md:80-89` describes two triage designs that the package does not implement. It says experiments found that neither predicts downstream quality, and it links no experiment. Commit `40a489966e` states the result more precisely: no review feature predicted build defects better than the base rate. Link the experiment in one sentence or delete the subsection.

topics.title: Unify GRPO learner APIs across SPMD and pipeline execution
topics.body:
Provide one synchronous GRPO score/update interface for ordinary sharded training and JaxPP pipeline execution. Both adapters consume `GrpoExample` batches and call the same objective; each keeps its native model, optimizer, and checkpoint state.

Average pipeline gradients after temporal accumulation, matching Trainer's accumulation convention. Scale microbatch losses using the execution microbatch count to preserve globally precomputed objective weights; keep metric sum/max reductions and global clipping.

Share trajectory packing and explicit attention segments so packed batches can also use the generic model scorer. CPU parity checks cover packed scoring and gradients, Trainer updates across microbatch counts, FP32/BF16 accumulation, and explicit PP/data score reshaping. Accelerator JaxPP execution and distributed FSDP/EP validation remain separate acceptance checks.

topics.title: [data] Sequence-level shuffled v16384 cache removes 128-step loss sawtooth and improves eval
topics.body:
Sequence shuffling reduces the 128-step train-loss sawtooth seen with flat-cache training on `hero_tok/v16384_shuf` at batch 1024. In a single-seed S7 d512 comparison, it improves Paloma macro loss by 0.0135 and reduces train-loss autocorrelation at lag 128 from 0.226 to 0.026. A second seed and a batch-256 rung are still needed to confirm the gain size.

The default block shuffle (`BlockShuffleConfig(io_block_size=256, window_blocks=512)`, [datasets.py:574](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L574)) gives a 128-step train-loss sawtooth on [s7l-d1280L16](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/s7l-d1280L16), for example +0.11 at step 5504 = 43×128. A window contains 131,072 sequences. Long documents (56.5% of tokens are in documents >4096 tokens, 16.3% in >256k, up to 1.6M) occupy consecutive sequences inside one 256-sequence block. Every slice of a document therefore lands in the same window, and the model sees the same file for 128 steps.

The old cache, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/hero_tok/v16384_shuf/train`, contains 124,408,413,939 tokens. Hero store `store_4d2e363d` was decoded to text and sampled by `harrier_mix_2026_08_18.json` (`hero_text`), documents were capped (`hero_text_capped`), tokenized with `hero-bpe-v16384` (`v16384_617680a7`), then shuffled at the document level by `experiments/grug/fast_track/shuffle_cache.py`.

The sequence-shuffled cache, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/hero_tok/v16384_seqshuf/train`, packs the old cache into 4096-token sequences exactly as `TokenSeqDataset` reads it, then permutes them with `numpy.random.default_rng(20261020).permutation(30373147)`, one sequence per row ([seq_shuffle_cache.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin_belay_v1_fp8quality/experiments/grug/fast_track/seq_shuffle_cache.py), e53d6b0620). Sequence contents are unchanged; only their order changes. Validation found the same sequence and token counts, with 514 sampled sequences byte-identical.

S7 d512, batch 1024, 1346 steps, seed 0, and the default block shuffle were held fixed; only `--train-cache` differs (a5a8647840). [saw5-ctl](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/saw5-ctl) uses the old cache; [saw5-seq](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/saw5-seq) uses the sequence-shuffled cache:

- Paloma macro loss: 2.9322 → 2.9187 (−0.0135)
- Paloma micro loss: 2.6586 → 2.6460 (−0.0126)
- Uncheatable macro loss: 2.3959 → 2.3817 (−0.0142)
- Eval loss: 2.6232 → 2.6103 (−0.0128)
- Paloma macro BPB: 1.2139 → 1.2077 (−0.0062)
- Uncheatable macro BPB: 0.9136 → 0.9075 (−0.0061)
- Eval BPB: 1.0429 → 1.0378 (−0.0051)
- Train-loss autocorrelation at lag 128: 0.226 → 0.026

d512 seed noise is ~0.007 in macro loss. BPB uses the current token-weighted levanter computation, which has a known batching dependence; losses are the primary metric.

Done when ladder and large-batch fast_track runs default to `v16384_seqshuf`, and a second seed and batch-256 rung confirm the gain size.

Current `main` still selects `v16384_shuf`; the experimental branch has the sequence-shuffled cache builder and a `--train-cache` override, but the second-seed and batch-256 comparisons in the definition of done have not been reported.

**Relevant code**
- [`datasets.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L599-L611) — block-shuffle default
- [`launch.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/df2a8d9883ba5c2b6b9b35ce5c127d763706ebb2/experiments/grug/fast_track/launch.py#L107-L108) — current training-cache default
- [`launch.py` on the experimental branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin_belay_v1_fp8quality/experiments/grug/fast_track/launch.py#L1084-L1088) — cache override
- [`seq_shuffle_cache.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e53d6b0620/experiments/grug/fast_track/seq_shuffle_cache.py) — cache permutation and validation

# Proposed Fix

1. Reuse the `saw5-ctl` / `saw5-seq` recipe for a matched seed-1 pair at batch 1024 and 1346 steps. Change only `--train-cache` within each pair; retain the same model, data seed, evaluation sets, and block shuffle. Publish both run links, cache paths, code revision, Paloma and Uncheatable macro losses, eval loss, and train-loss autocorrelation at lag 128.
2. Run a matched batch-256 pair at seed 0 for 5384 steps, holding the 4096-token sequence length and total training tokens equal to the batch-1024 comparison. Report the same held-out losses and autocorrelation at lag 512, the window period at batch 256.
3. Compare paired loss deltas across the existing and new runs. If Paloma, Uncheatable, and eval losses improve consistently, change the fast_track and large-batch defaults to `v16384_seqshuf`; if deltas are near the reported ~0.007 seed noise or losses regress, add matched seeds before changing the default. Keep an explicit old-cache override for reproducing prior runs, update the fast_track README with the cache identity, and check the constructed training data config in a local test.
4. Coordinate the launcher edit with [#10108](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10108) and [#9371](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9371), which both change `fast_track/launch.py`, then use the normal lint, test, PR, and CI workflow. No open PR covers the sequence-shuffled default.
Purpose of this issue is just to log the experiment showing the impact. Closing.

topics.title: [evaldash] Display retained SOTOPIA trial summaries
topics.body:
Display SOTOPIA-hard conversations, evaluator reasoning, dimension scores, and context-budget data from retained Harbor trial summaries when Harbor archives no ATIF trajectory.

Sample responses add `summary_uri` from the archived trial ID. Artifact lookup reads Harbor's selected `trial_relpath` from the trial-root result and displays only that attempt's summary. A missing summary stays unavailable even if a superseded attempt retained one. Archived `trajectory_uri`, rewards, and correctness fields stay unchanged.

The reported sealed run could not be read from this workspace because CoreWeave credentials are unavailable. A local FineStore archive fixture covers a missing-trajectory row and a selected attempt without a summary. Continuous-reward outcome labels remain for follow-up.

Part of #10161
topics.head: cdd040cfb82ed9e098a116a1b33130f6eecacc15

comments.body: Working on this in loom: https://loom.oa.dev/s/4u7440y9

🤖 Holistic review of de90adf951e1f2cc5195ba21794dd31a75112113.

The PR adds a `sotopia-summary://<trial>` reference for SOTOPIA-hard samples that have no archived ATIF trajectory, resolves it from the Harbor job tree, and renders the episode in a new viewer. The overall shape works, but the server picks the wrong attempt: it takes the lexically latest one, while Harbor scored and archived the selected one.

**Blockers**
1. `infra/marina/apps/evaldash/samples.py:520` `_sotopia_summary_path` returns `sorted(...)[-1]`, the lexically latest `attempts/*/agent/sotopia-summary.json`. The archived sample comes from a different directory. Harbor's queue records the attempt it selected as `trial_relpath` in the trial-root `result.json` (`harbor/trial/attempt.py:persist_selected_result`), and `TrialArchive._write_result` reads the trajectory and reward from `result.resolve_trial_path(...)`. These diverge whenever the selected attempt wrote no summary. For example, retry `001` crashes before the agent writes the file, or a timeout result is published for an attempt that left no summary. The glob then returns `000`'s summary, and the viewer shows its transcript and evaluator scores under the sample's archived reward with no indication that they come from a superseded attempt. The added test fixes the "latest wins" rule in place but has no case where the selected attempt lacks a summary. Replacement: read `harbor_jobs/<job>/<trial>/result.json`, take `trial_relpath`, and fetch exactly `<job>/<trial_relpath>/agent/sotopia-summary.json`, reporting "not present" when that file is missing. This matches Harbor's archive and removes the `attempts/*` glob and the sort. Update the test so the selected attempt has no summary and assert the endpoint reports it unavailable instead of falling back to `000`.

**Related PRs**
2. #10151 and #9897 also touch `tests/test_samples.py`, `README.md`, and `web/src/types/api.ts`. Neither depends on or deletes this change, so any merge order works. The only expected conflict is textual.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:de90adf951e1f2cc5195ba21794dd31a75112113 -->

🤖 Removed the superseded-attempt fixture that encoded lexical selection and four redundant SOTOPIA comments. The selected-attempt blocker in the holistic review remains open. Affected tests passed (17 Python, 3 frontend), as did changed-files lint.

<!-- marin-deslop:de90adf951e1f2cc5195ba21794dd31a75112113 -->

🤖 Fixed in [6afacf2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/6afacf27b5). Summary lookup now reads the selected `trial_relpath` from the trial-root `result.json`; when that attempt has no summary, the artifact is unavailable even if an older attempt retained one. The regression test covers that case. The PR description and issue result now reflect this behavior.
