topics.title: [zephyr] Cap native thread pools at the worker's and task's CPU share
topics.body:
Native thread pools (Polars, OpenMP for faiss/torch/numba/Arrow, OpenBLAS,
MKL, numba, rayon for HF tokenizers) size themselves from the node's core
count and read their cap once, at import or first pool use. An Iris task pod
on CoreWeave carries only a CPU request, so a 2-CPU Zephyr worker starts
pools sized for the whole node. The four InlineRunner stages (embed, quality
score, centroid sample, domain assign) run inside the worker actor process,
where polars/pyarrow/numpy are imported before any task runs, so nothing
inside a task can lower the cap. Today only SubprocessRunner children are
capped, and only for Polars.

`memory_budget.native_thread_env(cpu)` returns `POLARS_MAX_THREADS`,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`,
`NUMBA_NUM_THREADS` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`, each `max(1, ceil(cpu))`. It is
applied at the two boundaries that are pre-import by construction:

- the Iris environment of the coordinator and worker actor-group jobs, via a
  new optional `environment` keyword on fray `create_actor_group` (forwarded
  by the Iris backend, ignored by `LocalClient`, whose actors are threads);
- the SubprocessRunner child env, which now carries the full map at task cpu
  instead of `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` alone. Arrow in shard children stays
  API-pinned to 1.

No process writes `os.environ`, and no threads or buffers are added, so
memory can only fall. `thread_cap_environment` passes `workspace=os.getcwd()`
only because `EnvironmentConfig` requires a workspace or an image;
`convert_environment` reads only `env_vars`. Narrowing the fray keyword to
`env_vars: dict[str, str]` would drop that placeholder at the cost of
diverging from `JobRequest.environment`; happy to switch if preferred.

## Measurements

Proxy kernels standing in for each stage, on a 16-CPU VM with no CPU quota:
8 fresh 2-CPU-shaped processes at once, 3 repeats, median, clean environment
vs `native_thread_env(2)`:

| kernel | wall p50 | CPU-s per repeat | max RSS | involuntary ctx switches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| assign (faiss) | 68.8 -> 11.8 s | 1082 -> 181 | flat | 10.7M -> 10k |
| embed (numba + OpenBLAS) | 21.7 -> 21.0 s | 303 -> 274 | -300 MB | -65% |
| reader (Arrow) | 7.7 -> 7.65 s | 73 -> 68 | -57 MB | -83% |
| shuffle (Polars) | 8.6 -> 7.9 s | 124 -> 110 | -840 MB | -94% |

The capped version lands within noise of pinning each process to 2 cores
with `taskset` on every kernel. Under a `CPUQuota=200%` cgroup (GCP
preemptible shape) assign and embed gain the same; shuffle is flat because
Polars already sizes from the quota. One process alone on an idle 16-core
box is slower (2 threads instead of 16), a shape no production worker has;
the same process under a 2-CPU quota is 63% (assign) and 57% (embed) faster.
Result hashes are identical in every arm.

A local datakit pipeline under SubprocessRunner (task cpu 1 and 2.5, main vs
branch) is byte-identical with worker mem_peak ratio 1.004 and 1.001.
Fresh-interpreter probes under `native_thread_env(2)` show every covered
library reporting 2 threads.

Not measured: the CoreWeave pod shape (CPU request only, no `limits.cpu` or
cpuset) is read from the Iris k8s backend
(`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py`), not observed on a
cluster, and the stage-level production gain is extrapolated from the
kernels.

Out of scope: quality score (XLA's CPU pool ignores all six variables and
needs sched affinity), tokenizer parallelism in shard children
(`TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` stays), the store worker's
partition-process Arrow pin, and `pa.io_thread_count`.

## Tests

- SubprocessRunner map returns `pl.thread_pool_size() == ceil(task cpu)` on
  a cpu=4 worker (1 -> 1, 2.5 -> 3).
- A fresh interpreter under `native_thread_env(1.5)` reports Polars and Arrow
  pools of 2.
- The fray Iris backend submits explicit env vars merged over device
  defaults.
- A `requires_cluster` test observes (2, 2) from an inline stage on a cpu=2
  Iris worker.

topics.title: grug: inverse-variance knowledge weights in the quality judge
topics.body:
Stacked on #10108. `quality_judge` now weights knowledge tasks by the inverse of their relative seed variance. `GROUP_WEIGHTS["K"]` is frozen from the 12 d512 web-arena random runs in #10108. Of the relative knowledge gain, ARC-Easy contributes 11.6%, ARC-Challenge 21.9%, MMLU 45.7%, SciQ 3.7%, and OpenBookQA 17.2%.[^1] The other groups retain equal weights. Under equal weights, SciQ, whose seed SD is 4.6% for one run, set much of the knowledge interval.

A plan fixed before the runs called for 48 new d512 web-arena runs: 24 `web_only`, 12 `dclm_web`, and 12 `fineweb_edu_web`, using seeds 12–35. The weights were to be adopted only if H2, H3, and H4 passed. All three passed:

- H2: Knowledge seed SD on the 24 new random runs fell from 1.63% to 1.27%, a ratio of 0.78 [0.71, 0.85].
- H3: A/A on the new random runs returned `better` for 2.9% of 12-seed pairs, against 2.0% with equal weights and a 5% limit. The rates were 1.4% for 6-seed pairs and 0.1% for 3-seed pairs. These splits reuse the 24 runs.
- H4: Neither low-weight task, ARC-Easy or SciQ, had an upper bound below −2% while knowledge passed. This means no harm was detected; it does not prove no harm. The DCLM SciQ interval remains [−4.0, +1.7], so the knowledge limit offers little protection for SciQ alone.

For DCLM, 12 new seeds against 12 new random runs returned `better`, with knowledge at +0.5% [−0.8, +1.8]. Equal weights returned `inconclusive`, with knowledge at +0.2% [−1.5, +1.8]. FineWeb-Edu remained `worse`, with commonsense at −1.9% [−2.7, −1.1].

The README seed count uses `s` = 1.7% for knowledge on the runs that set the weights, versus 2.3% with equal weights. This gives about 13 seeds per arm for a 0.9% knowledge gain and 48 for no gain, versus 24 and 86 before. A simulation of the complete judge with the real seed covariance gives 79% power at the two counts. The decisions of the 43 three-seed rung comparisons against random are unchanged. The median knowledge interval is 22% narrower at d512, 7% wider at d768, and 1% narrower at d1280; fewer seeds are expected only at d512.[^2]

These weights apply to the d512 web arena. A different arena needs weights estimated from separate random runs and frozen before the judge runs. The [report](https://claude.ai/artifact/46KvN5W9qp7rMnMPCdcNc9) contains the results and plan.

[^1]: `GROUP_WEIGHTS` stores weights on the BPB scale: each relative weight is divided by that task's mean BPB in those runs. Knowledge therefore remains a weighted mean of task BPBs, and the judge reproduces the planned test's gains to 0.01 points. At other rungs, the effective relative weights shift slightly with the control means.
[^2]: The rung check was outside the plan. Comparisons at a rung share random runs and are therefore dependent. The same frozen weights apply at every rung, giving knowledge one meaning across the ladder.

---
[Original description](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10424#issuecomment-6317113096) <!-- marin-prose-cleanup -->

topics.title: [marina] Add the public Snowball model family tree
topics.body:
Add a public Marina applet for the Snowball 67B A2B checkpoint family, with 130 model/run nodes, 138 parent edges, experiment evidence and scoped compute estimates. The tree supports expansion, zoom, search and branch filtering. Merge checkpoints show every pinned parent; the cooldown-family timeline records date provenance separately from weight ancestry.

The graph includes the campaign-1 serial merges, campaign-2 and campaign-3 DARE merges, BFCL recovery and protocol FTPO checkpoints, and the Smartie RL continuation. The Smartie chain is campaign-2 DARE-TIES-02 → .32 step 14 → .45 step 2 → .47 step 8 → .49 step 12. The .32 and .45 runs start fresh optimizers; .47 and .49 resume optimizer state. The displayed continuation step counts start at .45 update 1 and exclude .32's 14 updates. Internal checkpoints are distinguished from public releases. The .32 export is the best surviving checkpoint by pass@1 on its repeatedly inspected native development panel; the .49 export is user-selected with incomplete evaluation coverage. Pinned model cards, configs and W&B records support those distinctions.

The package declares its stable applet UUID and documents `marina release` from clean current main. Builds reject duplicate IDs, absent parents, cycles and cross-cooldown parent links before producing frontend output. Release tests exercise all four invalid graph cases and verify that failed builds preserve previous local output. Frontend assets use relative URLs and external scripts for Marina's content security policy. No private task payloads or traces are published.

The [public tree](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3/) currently serves [revision 6](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3/v/6/), published October 19. The source release safeguards and maintenance instructions apply to subsequent releases; merging alone does not change the live applet selection.

🤖 Holistic review of 32e0989e6474a83bfbe08f1e170dee0307c973be.

This PR adds a static, public Marina applet (`infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree/`) that renders the Snowball 67B A2B checkpoint lineage from one curated `graph-data.json`. It has 130 nodes, 138 parent edges, and a cooldown-family timeline. It also adds a maintenance guide under `docs/references/` and a mkdocs nav entry. Nothing outside the applet directory and docs changes, and no open PR touches these paths. The applet itself is sound. The release instructions predate Marina's move to `marina release` (36390183aa, October 15), and the manifest lacks the stable UUID that release relies on. Fix both before merging so the next maintainer can publish revision 7 from main.

**Design.** `build.py` recreates `dist/`, inlines the graph JSON into `index.html` (the `__DATA__` placeholder, with `</` escaped), and copies the classic-script JS/CSS and two token-count evidence extracts. Because the package has no Python entrypoint, Marina serves it as static files under the public CSP. `verify_layout.js` runs the three scripts against a stub DOM and checks that every node is placed once and every parent arrow reaches its child.

**Evidence.** I checked these locally at this head. `uv run marina release infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree --dry-run --json` passes the package and inline-script checks (9 files, 332 KB). `node verify_layout.js` reports 130/130 placed with 138/138 arrows, and every family passes. In `graph-data.json`, the 130 IDs are unique and every parent exists. I did not check the live public revision or the browser rendering.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree/README.md:58` and `docs/references/snowball-family-tree.md:69,78` tell maintainers to run `uv run marina publish ... --local --mode public` and `marina publish --update <uuid> --base-version N`. That command no longer exists on the merge base (`Error: No such command 'publish'`), so following the published guide fails at the first step. Use the current commands: `uv run marina release infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree --local --json` (or `--dry-run --json`) for previews, and `uv run marina applets versions d3b5517a-… --json` followed by `uv run marina release infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree --base-version CURRENT_VERSION --json` for public updates. Release preserves the existing public mode.
- **2. Should fix:** `infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree/applet.toml:1` declares no `applet_id`, but the applet's public UUID `d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3` is pinned in the docs. The `marina-applet` skill requires maintained sources under `infra/marina/applets/` to declare their stable UUID, as `filer`, `python_playground` and `rl_data_catalog` do. Without it, `marina release` needs `--id` on every update, and `release-status` raises `release-status requires applet_id in applet.toml`. Releases also skip the guarded path (`cli.py:316`: `require_current_main`, tracked-file check, `marina-release.json` provenance), so each public revision is unrecorded. Add `applet_id = "d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3"`, then remove `--update`/`--id` from the guide.
- **3. Should fix:** `infra/marina/applets/snowball_family_tree/README.md:49` asks contributors to check by hand that new IDs are unique, every parent exists, the chain is acyclic, and `lane` agrees with cooldown ancestry. The PR body says these checks pass, but no committed code runs them. `build.py` already loads `graph-data.json` (line 16), so assert the four invariants there. A bad graph would then fail `marina validate`/`release` before publication, and that README paragraph could be deleted.

topics.title: Prevent host credential and configuration leaks into sandboxes
topics.body:
Apply task variables inside bubblewrap after isolation, keeping loader settings such as `LD_PRELOAD` out of the host launcher. Pass environment options through a private inherited descriptor so their values stay out of host process command lines. Replace broad host configuration mounts with private allowlisted runtime files and keep host `/opt` contents and sysfs hidden. Make the local backend's file-download API read private system paths from inside the sandbox.

Limit the Harbor Docker Compose process environment to required client connection and login paths plus declared task variables. Remove Modal's implicit host lookup for Compose references and disable service links in Iris sandbox pods. Document the environment boundary for each backend; image contents, explicit mounts and provider-side settings remain trusted inputs.

comments.body:
🤖 Fixed in [0fdf40a](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/0fdf40aadc0e528a970d90b910ef469936f3513b). Environment options now travel as NUL-separated arguments through a private inherited descriptor (`bwrap --args`); the host launcher still receives only the fixed control environment. New regressions inspect the host launcher's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and assert that task and command environment values are absent while still reaching the guest unchanged. Embedded NULs that could introduce extra arguments are rejected. The existing `LD_PRELOAD` regression still verifies that task loader options cannot execute code on the host before isolation.

The Shellbox and local caller tests passed (173 passed, 12 skipped), as did lint and type checks. A disposable application check with symlinked private resolver and CA files resolved `example.com` and completed HTTPS certificate verification (HTTP 200).

topics.body:
Stage vLLM 0.30 source `47b411d5785d1c3dee0328334472d70310c53feb` with tpu-inference 0.30 source `66c5d8952eec0c263361915cb4613d8f30737955`. GPU and TPU use the same vLLM source and separate dependency environments. Stack this adoption on the [GPU candidate adoption](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10022).

Two fresh source and native build environments produced byte-identical complete TPU wheels with the pinned Debian GCC 12.2 recipe. The [normal GitHub producer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/38083919768) atomically published the [exact pair](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-47b411d5785d-66c5d8952eec-aa04b4969cf2-309096c4b1e9). Independently downloaded archives match the agreed vLLM SHA256 `c45de5c1322343b7b6953ae791aa56029c8254ce60e90c1ef4866dc670249bae` and backend SHA256 `dedad6b56c6fd01716bfa148b72cc2e32080eccf68b403d810748569408ab2e6`. topics.title: taskforge: require three agentic reviews
topics.body:
`submit` now runs `Gate.reviews` independent reviews concurrently. Each review includes a blind solve and a review. Any refusal rejects the task and reports the problems from each refusal. The driver sets `Gate.reviews` to 3. A version refused by one review remains refused, so later reviews of the same version cannot accept it.

In a replay of 313 labeled tasks with three reviews each, all three reviews refused 30 of 63 blocking tasks, all three accepted 20, and the remaining 13 had mixed verdicts. The blocking share of accepted tasks fell from 11.9% to 8.7%; about one in ten good tasks received a refusal.

The refusal of option tasks is now in #10445. With three reviews, 25% of the accepted option tasks still had a blocking flaw, against 4.3% of the other tasks, and the reviews agreed on whether a task had options for 290 of 313 tasks.

Judge spend now includes tokens from replies truncated by the output limit, about 131k output tokens.

`submit` refuses a task version after three submits whose review the judge did not finish, and tells the agent to change the task. In run Q, four versions got 3 to 7 truncated judge replies and no finished review, at about 13 minutes each; the two versions that got a finished review got it after 2 and 3 truncated replies. The rule removes 10 of Q's 27 truncated submits. A lower judge output limit is not the fix: with 32k output tokens, 7.3% of 313 replayed reviews were truncated, compared with 1.9% at 131k.

Run Q ran the earlier checks of #10445 (an answer search and rules that read the grader spec), and the option refusal. It used the 30 ideas from run L with n = 4 and produced 52 tasks: four ideas produced four tasks each, and six produced none. Run L produced 55 tasks, with eight ideas producing four tasks and 11 producing none, excluding the d09 rerun; including that rerun, L produced 59 tasks. Blind verifiers rated 0 of Q's 52 tasks blocking, 17 ok, and 35 minor, and found all 52 references correct. L had 8 of 59 blocking tasks.

A second blind pass, treating “a contradiction that changes the answer” as blocking, found 3 of Q's 52 tasks blocking: a count over judgment calls (d33), a false note in a prompt (d45), and a task whose usual command gives the wrong answer in ShellSim because `tr -d '\0'` removes the digit 0 rather than NUL bytes. The passes agreed on 37 of 52 verdicts.

GLM used 6.4M tokens per accepted Q task, including 0.27M judge tokens, compared with 4.0M for L. Staged Taskforge accepted 3 of 108 tasks on the same ideas at 0.9M tokens. Of 216 submits, 27 failed on a truncated judge reply; idea d20 accounted for eight of these failures and ran for 293 minutes without producing a task.

Part of #10152. Stacked on #10446.

---

topics.title: [taskforge] Add the staged capability driver and cluster probes
topics.body:
Add the staged capability driver and cluster probes. In `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs`, `proposal_source.CapabilitySource` plans slots for a catalog capability and writes a proposal for each slot under the document regex. `propose_tasks` proposes tasks for the selected capabilities, triages them with `stage20_triage.preflight.preflight`, and writes every request, completion, proposal and verdict under its output directory. A capability whose plan stays invalid, or whose planning call runs out of retries or is rejected, fails alone, so one capability cannot abort the run; a slot whose own model call fails is a slot failure, and the capability keeps its plan and its other slots. The driver stops at the verdicts, since building belongs to the stage coordinator. `CapabilitySource` implements the two-phase `ProposalSource` of #10295: `plan` makes the portfolio in one structured call and `write` writes one slot's document, or a null slot's proposal with no model call. Tests exercise both components with a scripted model, and live with GLM-5.3.

`scripts/cluster_rollout_probe.py` runs validation trials inside an Iris task using GLM resolved from a relay job through `llm.glm_client.RelayEndpoint`, and keeps its results in the Iris attempt archive. `lib/shellbox/benchmarks/iris_machine_probe.py` measures shellbox's Iris backend from inside an Iris task. The README and package description cover the full pipeline.

Builds on #10300; #10302 builds on it. The coordinator adaptation originally planned for this PR landed in #10298, which changes `run_build`'s signature.

---

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
Add the staged capability driver and the cluster probes. In `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs`, `proposal_source.CapabilitySource` plans slots for a catalog capability and writes a proposal per slot under the document regex, and `propose_tasks` proposes the selected capabilities' tasks and reviews them with `stage20_triage`, writing every request, completion, proposal and verdict under its output directory. The tests drive both with a scripted model, and live with GLM-5.3. `scripts/cluster_rollout_probe.py` runs validation trials inside an Iris task with GLM resolved from a relay job, and `scripts/iris_machine_probe.py` measures shellbox's Iris backend from inside an Iris task. The README and the package description cover the whole pipeline.

With this PR the stack's tree under `lib/taskforge` and the experiment equals the restack's tree before the decision-model commits. The taskforge suite passes 707 tests here (21 more than #10300).

```

</details>

🤖 Holistic review of 05732a525f.

This PR adds `propose_tasks`, the staged path from a catalog capability to triaged proposals, and two scripts that run inside Iris tasks. When one slot's model calls run out of retries, the driver discards the capability's plan and every sibling proposal. The PR body says the capability keeps them. The cluster rollout probe copies GLM relay code that already exists in `experiments` and keeps its results in three places where Iris already archives them. The Iris machine probe measures shellbox and does not use taskforge.

**System**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph exp["experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs"]
    driver["propose_tasks"]:::added -->|"idea, slots, environments"| source["CapabilitySource: plan_slots, author_proposal"]:::added
    driver -->|"files and summary.json"| out["OUTPUT_DIR"]:::added
  end
  source -->|"document_regex, parse"| stage10["stage10_proposal.model"]
  driver -->|"each SlotProposal"| triage["stage20_triage.preflight"]
  source -->|"generate_tasks.RelayEndpoint"| glm["GLM-5.3 behind an Iris relay job"]
  subgraph scripts["lib/taskforge/scripts, run inside Iris tasks"]
    rollout["cluster_rollout_probe.py"]:::added -->|"run_trials"| stage50["stage50_validate"]
    machine["iris_machine_probe.py"]:::added -->|"IrisMachineFactory"| shellbox["shellbox Iris backend"]
  end
  rollout -->|"its own RelayEndpoint copy"| glm
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

Green boxes are new in this PR. Unstyled boxes existed before it.

**Before.** `generate_tasks` (#10068) was the only capability driver. GLM writes a program for each catalog entry, and the program writes a TaskSpec. Stage 10 defines the `TaskProposal` document, its regex and the `ProposalSource` protocol, and nothing implemented the protocol.

**Design.** `CapabilitySource.propose(idea, n)` makes one structured call that plans `n` slots. It then writes the document of each proposed slot concurrently under `document_regex`. A reply that the output limit cuts off becomes a `SlotFailure`, and a parse error gets one repair request. `propose_tasks` runs the selected capabilities concurrently and triages each proposal with `preflight`. It writes the requests, completions, documents and verdicts of each capability, and `summary.json`. A plan that is still invalid after its repair fails only its own capability.

**Evidence and limits.** The 22 tests in `test_proposal_source.py` and `test_propose_tasks.py` pass locally at this head. The two `live_glm` cases did not run here. The PR links no live GLM run and no probe output.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/proposal_source.py:529` One slot whose model calls run out of retries discards its whole capability. `propose` raises the slot's `ModelUnavailable` out of the `TaskGroup`, and the group cancels the other slots. `propose_tasks.py:96-98` then records the capability with no batch, so `write_outputs` writes nothing for it. A scratch run with a two-slot plan, where slot 1 succeeds and slot 2 raises `ModelUnavailable`, makes 3 model calls and leaves the capability's directory empty. `test_a_slot_whose_model_runs_out_of_retries_fails_only_its_capability` (`test_propose_tasks.py:100`) asserts that the directory is empty. The PR body says such a capability "fails alone, keeping whatever it proposed". In `author_proposal` (`proposal_source.py:458`), return a `SlotFailure` for `ModelUnavailable` and `ModelRequestRejected`, as for a reply that is cut off. The batch then keeps the plan and the finished slots, and `propose_capability` catches only plan errors. The `ExceptionGroup` unwrapping at `proposal_source.py:529-533` can then go, because only programming errors still leave the group.

- **2. Should fix:** `proposal_source.py:134-142` `SlotPlan.consistent` repeats the solver-machine rule that #10296 put in `stage10_proposal.model.solver_machine_violation` (`model.py:372`). A container slot declares no machine, every other slot declares one, and only a reasoning slot may declare `none`. Call `solver_machine_violation(s.environment, s.solver_machine)` and raise its message with the slot number, so the plan, `parse` and triage apply one rule. Update the message that `test_slot_plan_declares_a_solver_machine_exactly_for_an_imageless_slot` matches. This makes the plan a second caller of the function, so #10296 should keep it.

- **3. Should fix:** `lib/taskforge/scripts/cluster_rollout_probe.py:166` `RelayEndpoint` copies `generate_tasks.RelayEndpoint` and `experiments/post_training/glm.resolve_glm_base_url`. The script lives under `lib/`, so it cannot import them from `experiments`. Move one `RelayEndpoint` into `taskforge.llm.glm_client` next to `FixedEndpoint`, since taskforge already depends on `marin-iris`. Import it in `generate_tasks` and in the probe, and delete both copies.

- **4. Should fix:** `cluster_rollout_probe.py:429-531` The probe keeps its results in three places. It writes them to `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR`, and Iris archives that directory for each attempt (`lib/iris/docs/task-outputs.md`; `iris attempt describe` names the archive). It also prints every file as `RESULT_FILE` log chunks that a `--reassemble` mode rebuilds, and copies the files to `--upload-prefix` when the task holds credentials. Keep the archive and the `RESULT_SUMMARY` line. Delete `print_results`, `reassemble`, `upload` and their options, which is about 60 lines.

- **5. Should fix:** `lib/taskforge/scripts/iris_machine_probe.py` measures shellbox's Iris backend and imports nothing from taskforge. It sets `iris_backend.TRANSFER_CHUNK_BYTES` at run time and pins a private CoreWeave image digest. Move it to `lib/shellbox/benchmarks/`, where shellbox keeps its backend measurement scripts with a README entry. Otherwise delete it and record its measurements in the issue that uses them. In both cases, remove it from the taskforge README.

- **6. Should fix:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/tests/test_live.py:50` The live test writes the plan, the slot requests, completions, documents and failures with its own `completion_record` and `write_json`. This repeats `propose_tasks.write_outputs` with one change: it drops the raw stream events. Call `propose_tasks` and `write_outputs` into the evidence directory, and keep the summary and the assertion. If the raw events are too large, drop them in `write_outputs`. Then the live evidence and the driver output have the same layout, and the live test also covers the driver.

- **7. Drop test:** `test_proposal_source.py:169` and `:178` assert prompt text, such as "This host can run these environments: reasoning, shellsim." and the absence of "JSON" in the plan prompt. They fail when the wording changes, and `TESTING.md` rejects copied prose. `test_proposal_source.py:222` `test_null_slot_is_not_needed` checks that the null proposal copies the fields of the planned slot. `test_propose_returns_one_outcome_per_slot_in_order_without_calling_the_model_for_null_slots` already covers a null slot from end to end.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:05732a525fd38dc4c050a10b04019efa5918c511 -->

🤖 On the holistic review, all seven are in 305b0112dd (head 55d68aa0e6 after the sync).

1. A slot whose model call runs out of retries or is rejected comes back as a `SlotFailure` carrying the error's text, so the batch keeps the plan and every finished slot; the `ExceptionGroup` unwrapping is gone and `propose_capability` catches planning errors only. The driver test now plans two slots and checks slot 1 is written and accepted while slot 2 is recorded as a failure with the plan kept.
2. `SlotPlan.consistent` raises `solver_machine_violation`'s message with the slot number; the test builds its expectation from the function.
3. One `RelayEndpoint` in `taskforge.llm.glm_client` beside `FixedEndpoint`, with its own test; `generate_tasks` and the probe import it. `resolve_glm_base_url` stays in `experiments/post_training/glm.py` because five other experiments call it.
4. The probe keeps results in `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR` only, which Iris archives per attempt; the log chunks, `--reassemble` and `--upload-prefix` are gone, and so is `--results-dir`, so results cannot land outside the archive.
5. `iris_machine_probe.py` is `lib/shellbox/benchmarks/iris_machine_probe.py`, with a README entry beside the tasktrove benchmark and no mention left in taskforge.
6. The live test writes through `propose_tasks` and `write_outputs`.
7. The two wording assertions and `test_null_slot_is_not_needed` are deleted.

🤖 Holistic review of 55d68aa0e6.

This PR adds `propose_tasks`, the staged path from a catalog capability to triaged proposals, and two scripts that run inside Iris tasks. The seven findings of the review at 05732a525f are resolved. One new problem remains: when a capability's plan stays invalid, the driver discards the plan request and both invalid replies, and writes only the error text.

**System**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph exp["experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs"]
    driver["propose_tasks"]:::added -->|"idea, slots, environments"| source["CapabilitySource: plan_slots, author_proposal"]:::added
    driver -->|"plan, slot files, verdicts, summary.json"| out["OUTPUT_DIR"]:::added
    driver -->|"endpoint_source"| gen["generate_tasks"]:::changed
  end
  source -->|"document_regex, parse, solver_machine_violation"| stage10["stage10_proposal.model"]
  driver -->|"each SlotProposal"| triage["stage20_triage.preflight"]
  subgraph tf["lib/taskforge"]
    relay["llm.glm_client.RelayEndpoint"]:::added
    rollout["scripts/cluster_rollout_probe.py"]:::added
  end
  gen -->|"--relay-job"| relay
  rollout --> relay
  relay -->|"Iris endpoint lookup"| glm["GLM-5.3 relay job"]
  rollout -->|"run_trials evidence, summary.json"| archive["$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR attempt archive"]
  machine["lib/shellbox/benchmarks/iris_machine_probe.py: IrisMachineFactory checks"]:::added
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
```

Green boxes are new in this PR. The orange box changed. Unstyled boxes existed before it.

**Before.** `generate_tasks` (#10068) was the only capability driver. GLM writes a program for each catalog entry, and the program writes a TaskSpec. Stage 10 defined the `TaskProposal` document, its regex and the `ProposalSource` protocol, and nothing implemented the protocol. `RelayEndpoint` was a private class of `generate_tasks`.

**Design.** `CapabilitySource.propose(idea, n)` makes one structured call that plans `n` slots. It then writes the document of each proposed slot concurrently under `document_regex`. A slot fails alone, as a `SlotFailure`, in four cases: the output limit cuts its reply off, its repair still fails `parse`, its model call runs out of retries, or the server rejects the call:

```python
# experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/proposal_source.py:474-479
try:
    first = await model.complete(messages, single, fields)
except SLOT_MODEL_ERRORS as error:
    return SlotFailure(slot.slot, str(error), request, ())
if first.finish_reason is FinishReason.LENGTH:
    return SlotFailure(slot.slot, CUT_OFF, request, (first,))
```

Only a failed planning call fails the whole capability (`PLAN_ERRORS`, `propose_tasks.py:74`). `propose_tasks` runs the selected capabilities concurrently, triages each proposal with `preflight` and stops at the verdicts, because `taskforge.stage_coordinator` owns the build. The rollout probe resolves GLM through `RelayEndpoint` and keeps its results only in `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR`, which Iris archives for each attempt.

**Evidence and limits.** At this head, 47 tests pass locally in `capability_driven_envs/tests` and `tests/llm/test_relay_endpoint.py`. The two `live_glm` cases did not run. The PR links no live GLM run and no probe output. In CI, `shellbox-unit` fails in `lib/shellbox/tests/test_local_machine.py` because an offline `uv pip compile` cannot resolve `six==1.17.0`. That test is on main and this stack does not change it. The lane runs only because this PR adds files under `lib/shellbox`.

**Findings**

- **8. Should fix:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/propose_tasks.py:100` A capability whose plan stays invalid keeps only its error text. `StructuredOutputError` carries both invalid plan replies in `error.completions`. `propose_capability` drops them, and the planning request too, so `write_outputs` leaves an empty capability directory (`test_propose_tasks.py:97` asserts that). These replies show why the planning prompt failed. The module docstring (`propose_tasks.py:19-25`) says the driver writes `plan.request.json` and `plan.completions.json` "either way", and the PR body says the driver writes every request and completion. `generate_tasks.generate_task` keeps `error.completions` for the same error (`generate_tasks.py:185-186`, tested by `test_workpiece_without_a_valid_submission_keeps_its_completions_and_no_program`). Build the planning messages in a `plan_request(idea, n, environments)` function that `plan_slots` also calls. On a plan error, `propose_capability` then keeps `ProposalBatch(plan_request(...), error.completions, ())` with the failure, with no completions for `ModelUnavailable` or `ModelRequestRejected`, and `write_outputs` writes both plan files. Change the test to expect two plan completions.

- **9. Drop test:** `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/tests/test_proposal_source.py:167` `test_the_plan_instruction_states_the_slot_count_and_the_status_values` asserts the text of a field description ("Exactly 3 slots, numbered 1 through 3 in order.") and the library's instruction format. It fails when that wording changes, and `TESTING.md` rejects copied prose. `test_slot_plan_requires_n_slots_and_rejects_using_an_excluded_pairing` already checks that the plan type refuses a wrong slot count. `lib/taskforge/tests/llm/test_relay_endpoint.py:43` `test_relay_endpoint_without_an_iris_client_raises` only mirrors the `client is None` guard at `glm_client.py:181`.

Earlier findings: 1–7 resolved. A slot's `ModelUnavailable` or `ModelRequestRejected` is now a `SlotFailure`, and the driver test checks that the plan and the sibling slot are written (1). `SlotPlan` calls `solver_machine_violation` (2). One `RelayEndpoint` is in `taskforge.llm.glm_client`. `experiments/post_training/glm.resolve_glm_base_url` stays for its callers in other experiments, so the Iris lookup exists in both places (3). The rollout probe keeps its results only in `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR` (4). The machine probe is in `lib/shellbox/benchmarks` (5). The live test writes through `write_outputs` (6). The prose and null-slot tests are deleted (7).

<!-- marin-holistic-review:55d68aa0e65f7bc4a1f54b2310dc0dfd3648e872 -->

🤖 Findings 8 and 9 are in a9a33f1810 (head c829dd516d after merging main up the stack). A capability whose plan stays invalid now keeps its planning request and the invalid replies: `plan_request(idea, n, environments)` builds the request that `plan_slots` sends, and `propose_capability` keeps `ProposalBatch(plan_request(...), error.completions, ())` with the failure, with no completions when the planning call itself is unavailable or rejected, so `write_outputs` writes both plan files; `ProposedCapability.batch` is no longer optional and the test expects the two plan completions. The plan-instruction wording test and the no-client guard test are deleted.

🤖 Heads-up since your approval: this PR changed underneath it. `CapabilitySource` now implements the two-phase `ProposalSource` that #10295 gained (`plan(idea, n)` once, then `write(idea, portfolio, slot)` per slot, so each workpiece can start as soon as its own proposal exists), and `propose_tasks` assembles the batch with `propose_all`. The diff for that is in 9876fa8e91; everything else came from merging the lower PRs.

topics.title: Unify HF release export defaults across Levanter and MarinSkyRL
topics.body:
Unify the HF release defaults and validation used by Levanter and vendored MarinSkyRL. The training backend should not silently determine the release precision, config field names, tokenizer metadata, or generation settings. Keep native training/recovery checkpoints separate from inference releases.

The published Snowball artifacts show the difference:

| Artifact | Tensor storage | Index total_size | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [v0.1 at adc0078](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1/tree/adc0078a19a4383bc998fcdb43867b3360baf5f3) | 67,078,876,160 BF16 values; 6,656 FP32 values | 134,157,778,944 bytes | `dtype=bfloat16`; several names for the same architecture fields |
| [v0.1.1 at 59852d6](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1.1/tree/59852d6f07261722bbec1edb6ab148317156b58e) | 67,078,882,816 FP32 values | 268,315,531,264 bytes | `dtype=null`; canonical architecture field names |

Both indexes contain the same 502 tensor names, but use 39 and 79 shards respectively. The tokenizer.json and standalone chat_template.jinja file hashes match across these revisions. Both generation configs specify EOS IDs `[128001, 128009]` and BOS ID `128000`; the Transformers version annotation differs. v0.1.1 also embeds its chat template in tokenizer_config.json and adds `begin_suppress_tokens` to config.json. These are different trained models: this metadata comparison does not establish numerical equivalence or attribute output-quality differences to export. No weight payloads were downloaded for this investigation.

Code inspected at Marin `d9d49f2c65` shows export paths with different defaults:

- [Levanter's converter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L488) preserves tensor dtype when `dtype=None`. An explicit dtype casts every floating tensor. Config construction is separate, so a weight cast alone does not establish matching dtype metadata. [The standalone export CLI](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/main/export_lm_to_hf.py#L39) does not expose an export dtype; training hooks have a separate `hf_save_dtype` option. The published v0.1.1 export configuration does not specify a dtype.
- [SkyRL's Megatron export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py#L518) saves the materialized model through Bridge and then saves its HF config. Its Grug provider uses BF16 parameters and persistent FP32 router biases. [GrugMoeConfig](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/models/grug_moe.py#L310) stores duplicate aliases; Levanter already has a [single-name export contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L80). Do not adopt SkyRL's duplicate-field output as the common format.
- Generation and publication policies also differ. Levanter writes generation_config.json when explicitly supplied. [SkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/strategy.py#L125) tries to load it from the source model and continues after failure. SkyRL has tokenizer normalization and ordered manifest publication in [hf_model_io.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/hf_model_io.py); its export verification checks shard presence, not agreement between tensor headers and config semantics.

Use a small framework-neutral policy and validation layer that both exporters can import. Keep JAX conversion, distributed gathers, and Megatron Bridge conversion in their existing backends. Reuse the existing canonical-config, generation-config, tokenizer, and manifest helpers where appropriate; do not add a Levanter dependency on Marin or SkyRL. Persist the resolved policy in each export request so retries cannot change its meaning.

Done when:

- Public inference exports resolve one versioned policy: a BF16 release mode with architecture-declared FP32 exceptions, an FP32 mode, and a preserve-source-dtype mode. Architecture schemas declare required tensors and minimum precision; every mode must satisfy them. Preserve router biases and other required high-precision state. Do not apply a blanket BF16 cast or change native resume checkpoints. Invalid policies fail before export.
- Levanter standalone, training-hook and merged-adapter HF exports, plus SkyRL checkpoint-export jobs, use the same policy. Inventory additional supported entry points and migrate their callers in the same change; adapter-only PEFT artifacts retain their own format. Write canonical architecture fields once; reject conflicting aliases and unsupported conversions. Preserve behavior-critical fields, including context length, RoPE, attention layout, expert layout/schema, and effective router bias. Keep full Grug/Hero variants distinct from the narrower Snowball architecture.
- Tokenizer vocabulary, special-token IDs, chat templates, EOS lists, and generation controls have validated precedence: explicit export-request values, checkpoint metadata, pinned source-HF metadata, then documented defaults for optional fields. Reject missing behavior-critical values. Required metadata cannot disappear after a failed source lookup. Do not introduce suppression or stopping changes as a side effect of serialization.
- A shared validator checks actual safetensors names, shapes, dtypes, index coverage and byte totals against the declared policy and model schema. Record source checkpoint/step, source-model HF commit and checkpoint identity, exporter code revision, policy version, and file hashes. Publish a completion manifest only after weights and metadata validate; preserve current bounded-memory export and retry behavior.
- Tests export the same tiny Snowball/Grug model state through Levanter and the distributed Megatron export path and compare effective config, tensor layout/dtypes, tokenizer rendering, stop behavior, and logits within justified precision tolerances. Include nonzero FP32 router bias, explicit FP32 export, invalid aliases, missing metadata, interrupted publication, and retry. Before enabling the shared release defaults, load a representative Snowball export in the supported Marin vLLM runtime and verify fixed-prompt logits within declared tolerances plus termination on each configured EOS token. Keep existing published revisions immutable; assess any replacement release separately.

Related prior work: #7366 requested HF config/serialization standardization; #9039 tracks the separate Grug import round-trip gap; #7954 concerns chat-template consistency. This issue defines the shared export contract across trainers.

# Research

Levanter’s HF writer preserves source dtype when `dtype` is omitted, and its config builder derives `begin_suppress_tokens` from tokenizer IDs. Marin’s pinned external MarinSkyRL revision writes Bridge weights and config separately, tolerates a failed source generation-config lookup, and lacks the former vendored `hf_model_io.py` validator/manifest helper. [PR #10112](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10112) changes the same Levanter export files; no open PR covers this shared release contract.

**Relevant code**
- [`hf_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L988-L1248) — dtype, config, shard upload
- [`snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L75-L130) — canonical Snowball field names
- [`external_dependencies.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py#L70-L82) — pinned external SkyRL revision
- [`megatron_strategy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/a906145aaf2bee56e3d8062830ef463f67722ea2/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/megatron/megatron_strategy.py#L317-L333) — Bridge weight conversion and config write
- [`strategy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/a906145aaf2bee56e3d8062830ef463f67722ea2/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/distributed/strategy.py#L114-L141) — optional generation-config lookup

# Shared HF release contract

## Background

The two Snowball revisions in the issue demonstrate different release representations, but their training runs differ. The new contract must specify a release independently of the trainer and reject an export that cannot satisfy it. Native recovery checkpoints and existing published revisions remain separate artifacts.

## Design

1. Add a small `marin-hf-release` distribution under `lib/hf_release/`, importable by Levanter and MarinSkyRL without importing JAX, Torch, or Marin. A frozen, versioned `ExportRequest` records `schema_id`, precision mode (`bf16`, `fp32`, or `preserve`), source checkpoint URI/step/identity, pinned source-HF commit, resolved tokenizer and generation metadata, destination, and exporter revision. Resolve and validate it before loading or gathering weights; persist its canonical JSON and digest so a retry uses the same request. An unknown mode, unpinned source lookup, or missing required metadata fails before export.

2. Register separate Snowball and full Grug/Hero schemas. Each declares required tensor names/shapes, minimum dtype per tensor, canonical config keys, allowed aliases on input, and required architectural fields (context/RoPE, attention, experts, effective router bias). Normalize equal aliases to one canonical key and reject conflicting aliases or unsupported schema conversions. In `bf16`, cast eligible floating weights to BF16 but keep schema-declared FP32 state, including nonzero router bias; reject a source that has already lost required precision. In `fp32`, write all floating weights as FP32; in `preserve`, keep source dtypes if they satisfy the schema. Nonfloating state is never cast. Set config `dtype` to `bfloat16` or `float32` for the corresponding mode; preserve mode retains a single source dtype only when homogeneous, otherwise omits the scalar and records per-tensor dtypes in the manifest.

3. Resolve tokenizer vocabulary, IDs, chat template, EOS list, and generation controls field by field in this order: explicit request, checkpoint metadata, pinned source-HF metadata, documented optional defaults. Reject absent behavior-critical fields and disagreement between resolved tokenizer, config, and generation config. Preserve explicit stopping and suppression settings; do not synthesize `begin_suppress_tokens` from BOS/EOS/PAD. Validate the rendered template and all token IDs against the saved tokenizer.

4. Validate safetensors headers and index against the schema before publication: exact tensor coverage, names, shapes, dtypes, shard references, and `total_size` computed from tensor byte sizes. Hash each file while processing one shard at a time; put hashes, source identities, code revision, policy version, and request digest in a completion manifest. Upload weights and metadata first, verify destination objects using upload checksums and sizes, then publish the manifest last. A retry returns an already validated matching release, invalidates a partial completion marker, and refuses a different request digest at the same destination. Keep the current bounded-memory shard writer and Bridge collectives.

5. Route Levanter’s standalone CLI, LM/DPO hooks, merged LoRA export, `lora_lm`, ASR, and Marin’s `ConvertCheckpointStepConfig` through the resolved request at the common `HFCheckpointConverter.save_pretrained` boundary. Adapter-only PEFT saves keep their own format. Update MarinSkyRL’s `save_hf_model` and export-only job to use the same package and validator; release a pinned dependency, then update `config/external/MarinSkyRL/uv.lock` and regenerate Marin’s external dependency metadata. Coordinate Levanter changes with #10112. Do not change native checkpoint writers.

## Costs / risks

- The contract spans two repositories and an isolated SkyRL launcher. The shared distribution must be available to both runtimes before Marin advances its SkyRL pin.
- Hashing reads every completed shard once; validation should run beside the writer and avoid cross-region reads. Publication remains incomplete until the final manifest is visible.

## Testing and rollout

- Unit tests cover all three modes, a nonzero FP32 router bias, alias conflicts, missing metadata, EOS and chat-template precedence, bad index totals, missing/extra tensors, interrupted upload, and retry with the same versus different request digest.
- Export one identical tiny Snowball/Grug state through Levanter and a distributed Megatron Bridge job. Compare effective config, tensor names/shapes/dtypes, tokenizer rendering, stopping on each EOS ID, and logits with tolerances measured and declared for BF16 and FP32.
- Before making BF16 the default for public releases, load a representative staged Snowball artifact in the current pinned Marin vLLM runtime and check fixed-prompt logits and termination on every configured EOS token. Record the runtime revision, checkpoint identity, prompts, and tolerances with the gate result; publish a replacement only as a new revision.

## Open question

Which source checkpoint should serve as the representative promotion gate? The contract and local tests can land before that gate; the shared release default should wait for its result.

topics.title: Agentic SFT shootout on Snowball v0: plain, RS-multi, relay, recovery, plateau dropping
topics.body:
## STATUS
Sorry guys this is currently all AI-generated. Will clean up as we get further in the experiment.

## TL;DR

Design stage, 2026-10-16. We compare five supervised fine-tuning (SFT) mechanisms for agentic coding on one base, one task pool, one teacher and one supervised-token budget: plain SFT (one accepted demonstration per task), rejection-sampled SFT with resampling across epochs, relay SFT (#10027), recovery SFT, and plateau dropping (#10028). The earlier transfer experiments (#9920, #9984) compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT, on-policy distillation and weight merging on non-agentic tasks; this experiment moves to agentic tasks under the eval policy (#10197) and drops merging and distillation. Nothing has trained yet except a learning-rate sweep of the control, which is in progress.

## Question

Which mechanism, if any, improves Snowball v0 on SWE-bench Verified and the terminal benchmarks over plain SFT at equal supervised tokens, without losing retention on GSM8K, BFCL-Parity and GPQA-Diamond.

## Fixed choices

- Base: Snowball v0 = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12` @ `4eeb756b`. v0 carries a diluted DARE graft of the allkimi relay SFT, so relay's lift reads smaller than it would on a pre-graft checkpoint; this is accepted because the question is what improves the release.
- Task pool: about 2,200 TMax environments (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K`, tasks.zip) and about 2,100 SWE-smith tasks sampled from the Harbor packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`, stratified by repository, SWE-bench Verified repositories removed, decontaminated through DataKit against SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite 2.0. Selection is outcome-blind. SWE-smith packages receive a git-history strip before the agent phase (#10212).
- Harness per task family, matching the policy's scoring agent: TMax under Terminus-2, SWE-smith under mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, both in Harbor under the policy pins.
- Teacher: GLM 5.3 through the internal inference service, 8 attempts per task, verified by each task's tests. v0 is never sampled except in relay, where it starts each task and GLM continues after a trigger (format error, context budget, completion claim).
- Recipe, shared by every arm: the #9984 comparison-arm settings (AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip 1.0, router bias frozen, batch 16 at 32k context, constant learning rate, loss averaged over supervised tokens), 3 epochs, replay of general SFT data (`nemotron_sft_v3`, reasoning kept) at one quarter of the agentic budget. The learning rate comes from the sweep below.

## Arms and token matching

B is the supervised-token count of the plain arm: the first passing attempt per task with at least one pass, one trajectory per task. Every arm trains on B agentic tokens plus the same replay slice for the same number of optimizer steps.

- Plain SFT (control): as above.
- RS-multi: identical task slots to plain; when a task recurs in a later epoch, a different passing attempt is used. Measures demonstration diversity at a fixed budget.
- Relay (#10027): v0's own turns stay in context with no loss; GLM's turns are trained; passing episodes subsampled to B. Episodes with no teacher turn are dropped.
- Recovery (phase 2): the plain trajectories; 20% receive one or two synthetic failed turns re-rendered in v0's measured error styles plus the real harness error, inserted through the parser; injections carry no loss, so the budget equals B by construction. Waits on a validated injection generator.
- Plateau dropping (#10028, phase 2): the plain trajectories; tokens whose loss has plateaued lose gradient; matched on optimizer steps, with gradient-carrying tokens reported. Waits on the trainer.

Phase 1 is plain, RS-multi and relay.

## Evaluation

Every arm, including plain, runs the retention gate (GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, GPQA-Diamond) and the agentic endpoint (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, TBLite 2.0) under the policy's trial counts and pins. An arm passes when it has no decisive loss against plain on the gate and a decisive win over plain on at least one agentic benchmark with no decisive loss on the others, where decisive is the policy's rule (gap above 1.96 times the combined task-level standard error, each scaled by 1/sqrt(0.9)). One policy run resolves gaps of roughly 4 to 5 points on SWE-bench Verified and 8 to 10 on the terminal benchmarks; unresolved arms are reported with intervals and not promoted. Passing arms, plain and v0 go to the 23-benchmark tournament.

## Learning-rate sweep of the control

Running now, on pilot data (existing Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, history-reading trials removed), four runs from v0 at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5, 3 epochs, recipe otherwise fixed. Screens per run: held-out validation loss on 5% of tasks, GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified random-100 and a 100-task TBLite subset. Decision rule, fixed in advance: among rates with no decisive retention loss against v0, the best equal-weight mean of the two agentic screens; ties to the smaller rate. The chosen rate is confirmed once on the real plain-arm data and then frozen for all arms.

## Budget

Core (sweep, generation, phase 1, tournament) about 3,700 to 4,000 H100-hours; phase 2 adds about 2,400, of which 1,700 is an optional 20-epoch plateau comparison. GLM generation runs on the internal service and sandbox CPU and is outside the GPU budget.

## Status and next steps

- Pilot dataset and learning-rate sweep: in progress.
- Task pool, decontamination and package fix: in progress.
- Harness bring-up, one-task dry runs, a 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilot and a relay dry run: in progress. The full 8-attempt generation waits on their results.
- Then: phase-1 training, first-stage evaluation, tournament for passers; phase 2 when its code exists.

Design notes and diagrams are kept in the maintainer's notes and will be attached as results land.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-15: scope cut to SFT only; merging and on-policy distillation dropped. Base set to Snowball v0.
- 2026-10-16: one harness per task family following the policy's scoring agents; GLM 5.3 as the single teacher with regenerated traces instead of reusing Kimi and Qwen traces; RS arm redefined as resampling across epochs after the token-budgeted variant was found to re-weight tasks; task eligibility defined by teacher success only; unfiltered-SFT control dropped; primary endpoint set to the agentic benchmarks with the tournament secondary; git-history leak found in the SWE-smith packages and a strip added to the pool build.

## Effective generation settings

Both clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so GLM runs on the service defaults. GLM 5.3's template then renders `Reasoning Effort: Max`.

Every request is logged by an in-cluster proxy. The log records the settings as sent and the full reply, reasoning included. The proxy also serves `/tokenize` with the `zai-org/GLM-5.3` tokenizer, because the mini-swe-agent context limiter needs it and the relay does not provide it. Its token counts matched the service on every request.

## Transcripts

Both harnesses write Harbor ATIF trajectories:
- **Terminus-2:** each step's message is the JSON action, and the reasoning is in `reasoning_content`.
- **mini-swe-agent:** native `bash` tool calls with `{returncode, output}` observations, but the trajectory **drops GLM's reasoning**. Training rows are therefore rebuilt from the proxy log, which keeps it. That rebuild checks clean on both dry runs.

**Cause.** In relay mode, the v0 student runs as a child inference job. When that job was preempted, Iris rescheduled it on another host. The relay proxy kept calling the address resolved once at startup (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:682`). Every student call then failed with `httpx.ConnectError`, the agents got HTTP 500, and Harbor still exited 0.

**Fix** (`task/212` @ [`174906474a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/174906474a8039d1ff8989e8f6d53103242cfec1)):
- On a connection error, the proxy looks up the student's current address and retries for up to 20 minutes.
- The proxy logs its own failures, which used to go unlogged.
- A run fails, with no `_SUCCESS`, when more than 20% of its trials raise without a reply.

The relay lanes are being resubmitted on this commit.

## Results on the GLM 5.3 traces

Screens are SWE-bench Verified random-100 and the TBLite 100-task subset (solved out of 100; TBLite timeouts count as failures), GSM8K and BFCL-Parity for retention. "Composite" is our screening mean (SWE + TBLite)/2, shown as a range when trials were unscored for infrastructure reasons; it is a bound, not a confidence interval. HIGH and LOW are the GLM reasoning-effort settings used to generate the traces; rows are token-matched per arm.

| model | parent | rows | SWE-bench r100 (submits) | TBLite-100 | GSM8K | BFCL | composite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent v0.1 | – | – | 26 (36) | 23 | 91.1 | 32/123 | 24.5-25.0 |
| plain | v0.1 | HIGH | 13 (4) | 8 | 92.3 | 67/123 | 10.5-11.5 |

| plain | v0 | HIGH | 17 (3) | 9 | 87.7 | 44/122 | 13.0-17.5 |
| plain, cut to the relay arm's token count | v0 | HIGH | 13 (6) | 11 | 91.1 | 54/123 | 12.0-12.5 |
| RS-multi | v0 | HIGH | 11 (6) | 10 | 89.9 | 41/123 | 10.5-11.0 |

What the data say:
- Every arm is below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite and above it on GSM8K and BFCL. The regression is specific to the agentic tasks.
- Paired per-task differences on the frozen task lists (task bootstrap, 95%): no HIGH-row method differs from plain on either screen (SWE-bench -3 to -6 [about -13, +4]; TBLite 0 to +3 [about -6, +9]). Relay on the LOW rows beats plain on the LOW rows on SWE-bench by +8 [+1, +16], the only method-versus-twin interval that excludes zero; on TBLite +1 [-6, +7]. Every student is below its parent on SWE-bench (HIGH-row arms -13 to -22, intervals exclude zero; LOW relay -1 [-10, +8]) and most are below on TBLite.

Submitting is where the score comes from.
- The two parents are not distinguishable on the frozen task lists: paired SWE-bench difference v0 minus v0.1 = +7 [-2, +16], TBLite -3 [-12, +6] (task bootstrap). Of the 49 TBLite tasks where v0.1 timed out, v0 solved 3, so v0.1's timeouts are mostly hard tasks, not lost score (#10338: tripling the limit changed its score by one task).

Limits: one run per arm, 100 tasks per screen (about 4 points of standard error), TBLite timeout-bound for every student.

## Next step 1: the same cheap arms on the contributor traces

The one run of this recipe that beat its parent was the learning-rate sweep's 1e-6 run on the pilot traces (Qwen3.6-27B TMax episodes and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith episodes, the data the contributors' original experiments used): composite 31.0-32.0 against v0's 26.5-27.0, TBLite 29 vs 20. The pilot rows also look different from the GLM rows: 14 steps per episode at 246 tokens per step with 28% reasoning tokens (HIGH: 25 steps, 120 tokens, 39%), and they are in Terminus-2 format, which never contains the mini-swe-agent submit command, yet that student kept 40% submits.

Plan: convert the pilot traces to the arm row format and train plain, RS-multi and recovery from v0.1 at 1e-6 under the arm recipe, plus plain from v0 as the bridge to the sweep. v0.1 is the base because it carries no relay graft and v0 was trained on about half of the pilot SWE tasks through the relay data grafted into it. Known limits: the Kimi SWE set has one trajectory per task, so RS-multi runs on TMax only; recovery needs an error style for Qwen's native tool calls; about 1,500 pilot SWE tasks have only the pilot's own decontamination check. Target: plain results within a day of the rows, the other two a day later.

## Next step 2: learning rate on the real rows

The sweep tied 3e-7, 1e-6 and 3e-6 on the pilot rows and 1e-6 was frozen without the planned confirmation on real plain rows. Two checks are running: plain SFT on the LOW v0 rows at 3e-7, paired against the 1e-6 twin (same rows, parent and schedule), to test whether gentler updates preserve more of the parent; and a screen of the HIGH plain v0.1 epoch-2 checkpoint against its final, as an update-dose check. A higher rate is not excluded but is the less likely direction given the sweep.

Also in flight: plain, relay and plateau on the LOW rows from v0, and RS-multi and recovery on the LOW rows from v0.1, to complete the LOW comparison on both parents. Models so far are on the Hub under `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` (private). topics.title: [RL] Add async Megatron launcher and score-centering study
topics.body:
Add a fully asynchronous Megatron/vLLM launcher for Snowball and Qwen, pinned to [MarinSkyRL #700](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/700). The launcher makes training, generation, evaluation, topology, context budget, checkpoint source, and artifact settings explicit. Score centering remains disabled by default.

The [study](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/goal/score-centering-launcher-01a0bb6f/experiments/post_training/score_centering_study.md) retains exact rendered configs, response-level scores, repeated evaluations, W&B histories, consumed-prompt trackers, Iris task costs, runtime failures, and quality curves against updates, loss tokens, elapsed time, and H100-hours. A matched-token A/B/C probe separates inference-versus-trainer engine mismatch from stale-weight drift. The signed terms partly cancel, so a stable aggregate magnitude does not show that stale-weight drift is negligible.

At the measured Qwen incumbent (TIS cap 1.05, top-k 32, token-weighted mean consumed age about 4.7 updates), the three exploratory seed pairs favored score centering by +36.5, +43.5, and +9 answers out of 756. Three prespecified confirmation pairs gave +28.5, -23.5, and -5.5. The confirmation mean is -0.2 answers with a paired 95% Student-t interval of -65.8 to +65.4; the six-seed descriptive mean is +14.8 (-12.6 to +42.1). The initial signal did not replicate consistently. Matched exposure, loss tokens, elapsed time, and cost show no compute saving at this setting. Because no acceptable quality-loss margin was selected, the result does not establish non-inferiority.

The format-fixed Snowball pair completed nine updates per arm with active TIS and finite score centering. Six evaluations of the same step-five weights varied more than the small arm difference: completed-answer endpoint differences ranged from -33 to +11 out of 756, while baseline-adjusted differences ranged from -20 to +24. The original 4,096-token run completed updates six through nine, then failed during update ten. Five matched continuations restored the arm-specific step-five checkpoints with response caps from 3,840 down to 1,536 tokens, but each failed before completing resumed update six in TransformerEngine's unfused attention path. The configs requested FlashAttention; retained runtime logs show that installed FlashAttention 2.8.4 was outside the supported range through 2.8.3, so the runtime fell back to unfused attention. This report therefore makes no Snowball quality claim past step five.

Round-two diagnostics, Qwen confirmation, Snowball qualification, retries, generation, evaluation, and discarded work consumed 1,072.548303 reserved H100 task-hours. The measured evidence supports keeping score centering off by default in the tested Qwen range. Further Snowball training requires a runtime or backend change, or a severe response-length reduction that would materially change the experiment. A compatible FlashAttention attempt must first verify that the fused backend is active.

The final High-tier goal review found no implementation correctness defect. Its two completion blockers, omitted diagnostic task costs and missing clean-pair YAMLs, are fixed in `928887f72d`. Targeted launcher and cost tests pass. CI is running on that final review-fix commit.
