topics.title: [gpu] Persist NCCL RAS snapshots before stalled-job recovery
topics.body:
#7692 detects distributed training stalls from missing optimizer progress, and Iris enables NCCL RAS and targeted NCCL logging for GPU tasks. Recent hang investigation #7344 still had no NCCL RAS output to identify the failed rank, link, or collective. Passive stall detection needs a durable RAS snapshot before an operator or controller terminates the task.

Done when:

- A monitor queries NCCL RAS at a documented cadence and on a training-stall signal.
- Each snapshot records timestamp, root job, task, node, worker, rank, restart attempt, query status, and the returned RAS state.
- Snapshots are available after task termination through Finelog or another durable job artifact and are linked from the stall alert.
- A failed or unsupported RAS query is recorded explicitly instead of being indistinguishable from a healthy empty response.
- A multi-node GPU validation demonstrates periodic capture and capture during an induced or naturally observed stall.
- Any recovery action runs only after capture succeeds or records why capture failed. Automated recovery acts on the whole coscheduled task; restarting one distributed rank is out of scope.

Part of #6938. Related to #5198 and #7344.

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and assess actionability
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Research RAS client, stall detection, recovery path, Finelog
- [x] Post Research + Proposed approach for human review

Scope: large, multi-module, and **blocked on open PR #7699**. Not opening a PR; analysis below for review.

# Research

The RAS capture primitive this task needs does not exist on `main` yet — it lands in open PR **#7699** (`agent/nccl-ras-diagnostics`), which adds `capture_nccl_ras()` and its capture envelope, and explicitly **defers recovery integration and periodic capture as follow-up**. So #7796 is the recovery-gating + durable-persistence follow-up to #7699, and shares its `.agents/projects/distributed_training_diagnostics/` design.

Two of this issue's "Done when" bullets directly contradict #7699's stated design — a decision is required before implementation (see Open questions):
- Issue wants a monitor that **queries RAS at a cadence**; #7699's design lists "Periodic NCCL RAS polling from every process" as **out of scope** and states the client "does not poll in the background."
- Issue wants capture **gating recovery** ("recovery runs only after capture succeeds or records why"); #7699's design lists "Automatic task kick, cluster restart, or job termination" and "Grafana calling an Iris mutation RPC" as **out of scope**, keeping capture a warning-only runbook step.

What already exists on `main` and is reusable:

**Relevant code**
- [`types.py#L762-L768`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L762) — GPU tasks already set `NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=1` + RAS debug subsys, so the RAS service is reachable.
- [`reconcile/task.py#L139`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L139) `merge_task_termination()` / [`task_state.py#L61`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/task_state.py#L61) `task_is_finished()` — the terminal/retry decision the capture must precede.
- [`task_state_stats.py#L27-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/task_state_stats.py#L27) + [`stats/emitter.py#L13`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/stats/emitter.py#L13) `PeriodicEmitter` — existing 30s periodic-emitter → Finelog pattern to model a cadence monitor on.
- [`log_stack.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/log_stack.py) + [`stats/tables.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/stats/tables.py) — where a durable namespace/row schema is registered (PR #7699 already routes captures into `iris.profile`, 7-day retention).
- PR #7699: `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/nccl_ras.py` — `capture_nccl_ras()` already records failed/unsupported queries explicitly (`NcclRasFormatError` → text fallback; per-section `status` of `ok|unavailable|timeout|error`), satisfying the "failed query is not a healthy empty response" bullet.

Stall signal to trigger on: `levanter_progress_time_seconds` / `levanter_phase` (from merged #7692), surfaced by the Grafana bridge in [`infra/grafana/src/training_stalls.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/grafana/src/training_stalls.py). Grafana is read-only by design and holds no Iris write credential, so it cannot itself drive capture-then-recover.

# Proposed approach (design task — needs human sign-off)

Land after #7699 merges. Reuse its `capture_nccl_ras()` envelope; do not reimplement RAS access.

1. **Persist before recovery (the core ask).** In the controller terminal path around `merge_task_termination()`, for GPU coscheduled tasks reaching a terminal/retry transition due to a stall, dispatch an authenticated distributed capture across the task's live pods *before* the transition commits, and gate the retry on it: proceed only after capture succeeds or a structured `capture_failed` record is written. Capture and gating belong in the controller/`ProfileTask` path, not in Grafana. Automated recovery acts on the whole coscheduled task (per issue; single-rank restart is out of scope).
2. **Snapshot identity fields.** Extend the #7699 envelope / a Finelog row with the issue's required columns: timestamp, root job, task, node, worker, rank, restart attempt, query status, RAS state. `attempt_id`/`worker`/`node`/`hostname` already exist in the envelope and `TaskEventRow`; add `root_job_id`, `rank`, `restart_attempt`.
3. **Cadence + on-signal monitor.** A controller-side `PeriodicEmitter` at a documented interval, plus a trigger keyed off the stall signal. This is the direct conflict with #7699's "no background polling" — resolve scope first (see below). A controller-driven, bounded, on-stall capture (not per-rank self-polling) likely reconciles both.
4. **Linkage.** Emit a `TaskEventRow` (`reason="nccl_ras_snapshot_captured"`, source `iris/controller`) referencing the snapshot row so the stall alert links to durable evidence.
5. **Validation.** Multi-node GPU smoke showing periodic capture and capture during an induced stall (kill one rank's collective) — an integration/live-cluster job, not a unit test.

Estimated size: multiple hundred LOC across controller reconcile, `stats/tables.py`, `log_stack.py`, CLI, and a live-cluster validation — well beyond the auto-PR threshold and dependent on unmerged work.

## Open questions (block implementation)
1. **Cadence vs. #7699 scope.** #7699 forbids background RAS polling. Does #7796 override this to require a real periodic monitor, or is "on stall signal only, controller-driven" sufficient? (Recommend the latter to avoid per-rank fan-out.)
2. **Recovery gating vs. warning-only.** #7699 keeps automated recovery out of scope. #7796 assumes an automated recovery path exists to gate. Is there an approved auto-recovery action for stalled GPU gangs to hook, or is this "capture on operator kick via `iris process ... --skip-diagnostics` opt-out"? This determines whether the work is a controller feature or a runbook + CLI change.
3. **Merge order.** Confirm this waits on #7699.

Assigning a human to resolve 1–2 before implementation.

topics.title: iris - detect stalled gpu processes
topics.body:
We should have a monitor which can detect if a GPU process is stalled: look for indicative NCCL log lines or tracebacks. The monitor could activate every N minutes and probe logs etc. For likely stalled processes - no progress made after N minutes - inject a FAILURE into the task with the appropriate message.

examples:

```

topics.title: iris: expose actor methods over HTTP
topics.body:
Each `ActorServer` now has a built-in HTTP router. `@web_endpoint(path, method=...)` exposes actor methods, maps path, query, and JSON object fields to keyword arguments, injects Starlette `Request` parameters, and passes through `Response` values. Decorated public methods remain available through Connect RPC; HTTP and RPC calls use the same actor instance and executor.

Shared HTTP paths route to the selected actor using the proxy prefix and internal endpoint name. The native proxy replaces `X-Iris-Endpoint-Name` with the registered endpoint name, and the endpoint name stays local during federation decision handoff. Duplicate actor routes and routes under the Connect RPC mount are rejected.

The counter demo and Iris actor documentation are updated. Native gRPC still needs an HTTP/2 listener with trailer support.

topics.title: Propose a metadata-only Hero dataset
topics.body:
Specify a metadata-only release of Hero's 292-source document pool so users can download the sources and reconstruct selected text without repeating global corpus curation. Require upstream row coordinates, preserve repeated document occurrences, and distinguish provider-file offsets from Hugging Face Viewer offsets. Include draft exporters and bounded provenance, selection, and reconstruction tools.

Include stored 1,024-dimensional int8 Harrier embeddings through a sparse ID join, preserving quantized values and reporting nulls and budget-limited lookups separately. Frozen model and quantization metadata were recovered for 291 sources; Common Crawl Focus still has a provenance gap. Selected-document embedding coverage remains unmeasured.

The trials checked selection and staged normalization across all 292 sources, then reconstructed raw-provider samples from six source families. FineTranslations also reproduced production normalized IDs through Hugging Face `/rows` at the pinned revision. These samples do not establish full provider-to-selected-document coverage or final token-stream parity.

Complete ordered source manifests, upstream locator backfill, historical transform provenance, and full-store count reconciliation remain unfinished. The public exporter rejects selected rows with missing or inconsistent recorded coordinates; those checks alone do not prove complete transform lineage. The affected safe test suite passed 90 tests, and the strict documentation build passed.

topics.title: [inference] Add matched native and vLLM checkpoint fixtures
topics.body:
Export small Snowball and Hero BF16 checkpoints and benchmark the same weights and token workload in Levanter and the promoted Marin vLLM fork. Verify every exported tensor through native loading. Retain checkpoint identity, configuration, runtime topology, effective execution modes, and generated-token hashes. A separate non-unit normalization fixture changes only norm weights and records its seed and affected tensors.

Use packed expert banks, isolate Triton caches, and bound Ninja/nvcc concurrency. Expose expert parallelism, bounded KV memory, and eager or compiled execution. An optional hashed FlashInfer cache wheel loads and hashes precompiled MoE libraries with JIT disabled, preserving backend selection and autotuning. Setup and warmup remain outside measured samples.

The compare command verifies checkpoint, architecture, dtype, exact workload, and accelerator allocation, including native EP versus vLLM DP/EP or TPU SPMD data parallelism. Validate Grug aliases and derived defaults while retaining raw configuration differences. An untimed validation batch identifies the first divergent token; mismatched outputs suppress throughput ratios.

Bounded Snowball diagnostics compare shared-prefix logits, router precision, actual layer activations, and independent FP64 head reprojections. Native tracing records its effect on logits; named worker RPC captures every vLLM DP rank. Ordinary-engine generation independently varies embedding-gate SiLU and sigmoid precision without activation tracing. On H100, sigmoid-only FP32 matches all 32 vLLM tokens for both all-one and non-unit norm fixtures; promoting both functions still fails the non-unit fixture. Shared training and serving defaults are unchanged. An exhaustive standalone diagnostic evaluates all 65,280 finite BF16 sigmoid inputs against an independent FP64 reference, separating normal, subnormal, and saturated outputs. Both CPU runtimes execute successfully; fourteen focused tests and the delta affected-test run pass. Accelerator unary validation remains pending.

H100 EP2 tiny eager Hero produces identical 32 tokens using marin-community/vllm#83. On v5p, the combined short-convolution/cache stack passes twelve cases, then both runtimes produce identical 32 tokens for the same tiny Hero checkpoint with data parallelism four and tensor/expert parallelism one. Native measures 790.72 output tokens/second and eager vLLM 358.54 (2.205× for this workload only). The two-layer fixture exercises local and global attention because the final layer is always global. The measured pins, workload, and production Hero memory accounting are in the inference design docs.

GB200 Snowball starts with precompiled FlashInfer kernels and JIT disabled: 54.64 seconds of model/cache setup and a 12.01 GiB sampled cgroup peak under the unchanged 48 GiB limit. Unmodified Snowball outputs still disagree across runtimes, so its ratios remain withheld. Production checkpoints and Hero CUDA graphs remain unvalidated. Stacked on #9661. Part of #7219.

topics.title: Snowball 67B: vLLM DP-rank sentinel logprob variance — findings + data
topics.body:
Investigation of `test_snowball_export_matches_representative_goldens[vllm-gpu]` failing on the rank sentinel (`knowledge-longbench-02`, 15,025 tokens). Follow-up to the descriptive pass in #7354. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The gate is flaky because it asserts a quantity the stack does not hold stable.** Serving Snowball under data parallelism (8) + expert parallelism, the same prompt gets a different next-token distribution depending on which rank serves it. The divergence is created by the expert-parallel combine's **destination-dependent reduce-scatter** (~1 bf16 ulp), amplified into 0.03–0.29 probability swings by **expert-routing flips**. A deterministic combine removes it at short prompts but not long ones, and a **separate launch-scoped effect** shifts per-rank values between a few discrete states across restarts. Of three states observed, **two fail** the 0.075 bound and one passes. **How to read this.** *Findings* are our current interpretation, each with a confidence tag — `[replicated]` (holds across ≥2 launches/nodes), `[single observation]` (measured once cleanly), `[hypothesis]` (consistent with the data, not isolated by an experiment). *Evidence* (O1–O7) is the measured data, each row tied to a job you can re-pull; it is collapsed below — expand what you want to check. ## Findings 1. **At a single-chunk prompt, divergence is caused entirely by destination-dependent reduce-scatter.** `[replicated]` — The production collective returns 8 different results for one identical sum, reproducibly and across nodes (O4); at 128 tokens the first MoE combine is where 8 identical inputs become 8 different outputs (O5); making the combine deterministic removes that divergence entirely (O6, O7). Ring reduce-scatter sums each destination's chunk in a rank-rotated order and rounds on the bf16 store. 2. **The amplifier is expert routing.** `[single observation]` — A ~1 ulp perturbation flips the router's top-4 by layer 14 and reaches 5 distinct expert sets by layer 25 (O5). A rounding difference cannot move a probability by 0.1; a change in *which experts run* can. Seen at 128 and 2,048, characterised in full only at 128. 3. **A deterministic combine is necessary but not sufficient.** `[replicated]` — It removes the first-layer divergence and 85% of the 128-token spread, but as little as 5% at 15,025 (O6), because multi-chunk prefills also diverge *upstream* of the combine. 4. **A second, chunk/position-dependent divergence sits in the local path, upstream of the combine.** `[single observation]` — Two single-job signatures: at 2,048 the pre-dispatch hidden is already split across ranks before any combine (O5), and with the combine made deterministic the terminal gathered-batch position is the only rank that still differs (O7). The responsible kernel is not identified. 5. **Launch-to-launch movement is a separate, discrete mechanism.** `[replicated]` fact / `[hypothesis]` cause — Per-rank values recur to six decimals across jobs, nodes, and days (O3): discrete, not drift, and not the collective (whose per-rank output is launch-invariant). *What* varies at launch is unidentified; cold-vs-warm compile/autotune is the obvious guess but does not fit cleanly. 6. **The gate samples an unstable quantity.** `[replicated]` — Identical config yields ≥3 states, 2 failing (O2). The 64-case wave scores each case on one rank and is stable; the sentinel replays across all 8 ranks, so its verdict depends on the draw. This is the flakiness in #7354. > [!NOTE] > **Proposed direction (not yet filed).** A deterministic combine alone will not make the gate reliable (finding 3), and both GPU backends already sit ~0.055 below the TPU golden here for unrelated reasons, leaving ~0.02 of headroom — smaller than the launch movement. The change that lands in this repo is a **test-contract change**: keep the 64-case golden assertion, replace the sentinel's cross-rank golden assertion with a same-rank determinism check (which held 5/5, O1), and log rank spread rather than asserting it. Separately, the collective and kernel behaviours (O4, O7) are candidate upstream vLLM issues. ## Evidence (measured)
O1 — Per-rank output is deterministic and context-invariant Fresh recomputes (caching off, cache reset between) are **bitwise identical**: 8/8 repeats at 15,025 and 8,192 tokens in the full session, 4/4 in each other session. Per-rank values are also bit-identical across isolated replay, concurrent waves (2 rounds), a staggered wave (~200 ms offsets), reverse and random service order, and a wave-realistic composition (sentinel on one rank, seven different long prompts on the others; Δ = 0.000000 for the sentinel-carrying rank in all 4 rounds).
O2 — Rank spread and gate verdict, by launch (2 of 3 states fail) Five launches produced three distinct states (S2/S3/S4 are one state; S2 and S3 are bit-identical): | session | S @ 15,025 | S @ 8,192 | worst-vs-golden @ 15,025 | vs 0.075 | |---|---|---|---|---| | S1 (first launch in job) | 0.111884 | 0.234087 | 0.098835 | **fail** | | S2 | 0.071126 | 0.286958 | 0.070121 | pass | | S3 (bit-identical to S2) | 0.071126 | 0.286958 | 0.070121 | pass | | S4 (caching on, gate-exact order) | 0.071126 | — | 0.070121 | pass | | XJ (second job, second node) | 0.099165 | 0.221011 | 0.078494 | **fail** | At 8,192 the greedy token itself differs across ranks in every session (ranks return 423 or 426). Three additional long prompts (23,113 / 14,734 / 11,291 tokens) also show cross-rank disagreement, two with the greedy token differing — so this is not specific to the sentinel. Spread is not monotone in length, and the sentinel's length is not the worst case. S1, left-truncated sentinel: | tokens | 128 | 2,048 | 8,192 | 15,025 | |---|---|---|---|---| | S1 spread | 0.041857 | 0.039831 | **0.234087** | 0.111884 | It peaks at 8,192 (16 prefill chunks) and 2,048 is as low as 128. The session ranking also flips with length: at 8,192, S2/S3 (0.286958) > S1 (0.234087) > XJ (0.221011), the reverse of their order at 15,025.
O3 — Launch movement recurs bit-exactly across jobs, nodes, days Per-rank |Δp|: S2→S3 (same job/node) = **0.000000**; S1→S2 = 0.046777 @ 15,025 (0.301409 @ 8,192); S2→XJ (different job/node) = 0.026833 @ 15,025 (0.278763 @ 8,192). The per-rank values are not drifting — they recur exactly. Rank 0 at 8,192 tokens: | launch | p(423) | |---|---| | XJ (`crossjob-d7c849b9`) | 0.621766 | | earlier job `snowball-experiment-b-vllm-bd7f6354` (day before) | 0.621766 | | S2 / S3 (`main-b20426d2`) | 0.343003 | | earlier job `snowball-experiment-b-vllm-de845a00` | 0.343003 | XJ also matched `bd7f6354` on ranks 1, 3 and 6.
O4 — The collective returns 8 different results for one identical sum Model-free reproducer on the production expert-parallel communicator; all 8 destinations receive the same mathematical sum. Equal-sizes dense mode, all sessions: | operand scale | distinct checksums (8 dest) | bit-stable over 16 iters | max \|out − fixed-order fp32 ref\| | mismatched elements | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 8 | yes | 1.25e-01 | 684,812 / 1,310,720 (52%) | | 8 | 8 | yes | 1.0 | 684,812 | | 32 | 8 | yes | 4.0 | 684,812 | Max deviation scales exactly with operand magnitude (1× → 8× → 32×), i.e. ≤1 bf16 ulp per element. The 4-of-8-sparse and uneven-sizes modes give the same picture (sparse: 431,924 mismatched). The eight per-rank checksums are **identical in S1, S2, S3, and XJ (different node)**, and all three fixed-order fp32 reference orderings (rank order, reversed, ring-rotated) agree bitwise with each other — so a fixed-order fp32 combine is destination-independent by construction.
O5 — Boundary trace: where the ranks first diverge Each serving rank's own prefill is compared across the 8 serving ranks; distinct values, 1 = all agree. The gathered-batch boundary (`b2`) differs by construction — each rank's real tokens sit at a different offset — so the informative boundaries are `b1` (input to the MoE) and `b5` (output of the combine). **128 tokens (single prefill chunk, 26 MoE calls):** | MoE call | b1 pre-dispatch | b5 post-combine | distinct top-4 expert sets | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | **1** | **8** | 1 | | 2–13 | 8 | 8 | 1 | | 14 | 8 | 8 | **3** | | 25 | 8 | 8 | **5** | At 128, everything before the first MoE is bitwise identical on all 8 ranks (b1 call 1 = 1); the first combine turns 8 identical inputs into 8 different outputs. **2,048 tokens (4 prefill chunks, 104 MoE calls):** | MoE call | b1 pre-dispatch | b5 post-combine | |---|---|---| | 1 | **2** | 8 | | 2+ | 8 | 8 | At 2,048 the pre-dispatch hidden is **already 2-distinct at the first MoE** — ranks 3,4 versus the other six — *before any combine*. A multi-chunk prefill therefore carries a rank-dependent difference upstream of the combine, on top of the combine's own 8-way split. The 3,4 grouping does not match the 4+4 PCI-socket split, and it is absent at 128.
O6 — Intervention: a destination-independent combine (−85% at 128, −5…−57% long) All-gather every rank's partial, sum in rank order in fp32, slice this rank's chunk. Measured B–A–A–B in one server, two launches. `baseline_pre` reproduces `baseline_post` bit-exactly; the two treatment sweeps reproduce each other bit-exactly. | length | F1 baseline → treatment | F2 baseline → treatment | |---|---|---| | 128 | 0.042688 → 0.006272 (−85%) | 0.042688 → 0.006272 (−85%) | | 8,192 | 0.200678 → 0.171888 (−14%) | 0.270564 → 0.157229 (−42%) | | 15,025 | 0.066786 → 0.063381 (−5%) | 0.080416 → 0.034474 (−57%) | At 15,025 in F1 the treatment moved the sentinel *further* from the golden (worst-vs-golden 0.066453 → 0.085918): better-conditioned arithmetic is not the same as agreement with a cross-hardware golden.
O7 — Trace with the intervention installed (residual is one rank) Same per-rank trace at 128 tokens, fixed combine active: | MoE layer | post-combine distinct | grouping | |---|---|---| | 1 | **1** | all 8 ranks identical | | 2 | **2** | ranks 0–6 identical, rank 7 alone differs | | 3+ | 2 | ranks 0–6 identical, rank 7 alone differs | Rank 7 is the terminal position in the gathered batch. The GPUs split 4+4 by PCI bus id, which does not match the 7-vs-1 grouping — pointing to a tile/padding boundary in the local kernel, not the collective.
Setup — exact serving config and instrumentation 67B-A2B MoE, 256 experts, top-4, 32 experts/rank, 26 layers, bf16. Served exactly as the gate does: `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 512`, FlashAttention, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`. Prefix caching off in all arms except the gate-exact session S4. Fork `afb2671946`. Per-rank internals were read from live servers via vLLM's `--worker-extension-cls` mixed into the Worker and called through `POST /collective_rpc` (`VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`); bulk data went to a node-local dir, not the RPC response. Metrics: **S** = spread (max−min) across the 8 ranks of the probability of a fixed token; **worst-vs-golden** = the gate's own statistic, max over the golden's 25 tokens of |p_observed − p_golden|, bound 0.075.
Corrections to earlier claims in this investigation (negative results) Recorded so they don't mislead future work. We first reported position sensitivity as *falsified*, because isolated/concurrent/staggered modes gave bit-identical outputs (O1). The trace (O5) showed why that inference was wrong: **vLLM serialises these requests** — the DP size vector during a "concurrent" wave is `[1,…,128,…,1]`, one real chunk and seven dummy tokens — so none of those modes varied gathered-batch position. O1 establishes that timing/peer-content/service-order are irrelevant *given* that scheduling; it says nothing about position. Our first boundary-trace design was invalid for the same reason and was discarded (job `trace-4e8f82aa`).
Data, reproduction & audit — jobs, R2 archive, audit recipe Full raw blocks are in finelog (per-task stdout), retrievable with `iris job logs /romain/`: | job | role | |---|---| | `snowball-experiment-c-main-b20426d2` | O1–O5 (4 sessions + gate-exact) | | `snowball-experiment-c-crossjob-d7c849b9` | O2–O4 cross-job/node band | | `snowball-experiment-c-trace-e15f0c4e` | O5 boundary trace | | `snowball-experiment-c-fixedcombine-2b0db3ad` | O6 intervention | | `snowball-experiment-c-tracefixed-5d61f23f` | O7 residual trace | Those logs are archived to Cloudflare R2 at `s3://marin-na/finelog/cw-us-east-02a` (the `iris job logs` path reads from that archive; the cluster's 250 GB local disk is only the ingest buffer), so the raw data outlives any single node. To audit any table above, pull a job's blocks and recompute from source: ``` iris job logs /romain/snowball-experiment-c-main-b20426d2 > main.log uv run python tests/cluster/vllm/_experiment_c_analyze.py main.log ``` `_experiment_c_analyze.py` recomputes every table from the raw `EXPERIMENT_C_JSON` blocks, so the raw → table step is inspectable code, not a hand-transcription. The reduced fixture that regenerates the tables offline (`_experiment_c_reduce_fixture.py`) is measurement data and is not committed; regenerate it from the logs on demand. The probe, harness, analyzer, and reducers are on branch [`rank-variance-g1-harness`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/rank-variance-g1-harness/tests/cluster/vllm), with the fuller root-cause report and gated plan under `docs/reports/` and `.agents/projects/` on the same branch. Two earlier jobs (`main-c13d5d45`, `crossjob-2f72ea73`) failed at startup on a probe defect and produced no data. The earlier descriptive pass (Experiments A/B: the length ladder, the Levanter-GPU head-to-head, and the golden-token deltas that O3's recurrence values come from) is summarized in the report `docs/reports/snowball-gpu-golden-logprob-parity.md`; its raw blocks are in jobs `snowball-experiment-b-{vllm-bd7f6354,vllm-de845a00,levanter-9f283c4b}`.
Related: #7354 (flaky gate, 5 cold runs), #7183 (two TPU execution paths on June-67B), the golden-provenance offset (unverified, out of scope here).

topics.title: Hero Run: Sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval
topics.body: Issue to track the investigation into the sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval PTB is in general OOD data due to token, 'N' token, and all lowercase. Among other quirks. Initial hypothesises: 1. Some in-context learning capacity turned on for a checkpoint. 2. Data contam/very similar article in training data around then. 3. Some very rare tokens in PTB happened to get upweighted on a checkpoint that under normal checkpoints are heavily penalized. 4. Other/Unk Artifact comparing first 4k tokens: https://claude.ai/artifact/W82uDiQuQygwAaqfX3hEiR Most noteworthy drop is: "los angeles financier marvin" " mar" for marvin is predicted with 80% confidence on the overperforming checkpoint- seems likely that the exact phrase los angeles financier marvin appeared in the training data. It then dropped back down to its usual 0.2% on the following checkpoint. Completions API with prompt for every checkpoint: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/hero-completions/latest/index.html#a=1ed4a3edd3645961c051e72c8b85a9ec7b6fbea0f2c5b3a27960cc1c806b237d&b=dde26b9fe079446f0c76ecc1b7f469d59815aca5f3f3c84f50a3993df7a26978&prompt=biocorpus-protein-design-heldout

comments.body: 'mar' was at 15% on checkpoint 198k. And the model always knows mar ->vin ->d ->avis. So the person marvin davis is cleanly in the training data for a while. Google search-> "Marvin Davis was a prominent Beverly Hills billionaire, oil tycoon, and corporate buyout artist who made massive waves as Wall Street's highest-paid financier in 1989." Any docs related to news ongoings in Los Angeles may be spiking the eval.

PTB is '1989 Wall Street Journal (WSJ) articles'. We want our model to understand what happened in the 1980s in general.. so having the facts of this eval in the training data is intentional. Will see what comes up from scanning our data in this 6k step range.

🤖 **Data scan result: PTB's own text was in the training stream ~500 steps before the 210k checkpoint (hypothesis 2, contamination).**

**Method.** I rebuilt the hero's exact training stream from the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 mix stages, and the block shuffle. Then I read every sequence trained in steps **204,000–216,000**: 12,000 steps × 11,264 sequences × 4,096 tokens, about 554B tokens over 48 CPU jobs on cw-us-east-02a. The scan searched for PTB-specific lowercase phrases, their normal-cased counterparts, and runs of ` <unk>`.

**Result.** A block of about **231 sequences (~1M tokens)** in source **`c13q3`** at **steps 209,272–209,669** contains Penn Treebank text expanded into sliding n-gram windows (`<s> <s> … <word>` per line). It reads like an NLP exercise repository: it also has NMT training notes and scraped request headers. It includes the exact sentences in our PTB eval, e.g. `los angeles financier marvin`, `in london british airways chairman lord king`, `the stock of ual corp. continued`, `the dow industrials were off N points`. A related source, `c28q1`, has n-gram log-probability tables over the same text around step 206.3k (`lg P(corp. | acquire ual)`).

| Lowercase PTB-format hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `los angeles financier` | 3 | 0 |
| `british airways chairman` | 3 | 0 |
| `ual corp` | 26 | 0 |

Normal-cased news about the same entities appears about equally in both ranges:

| Normal-cased hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `Marvin Davis` | 331 | 332 |
| `UAL Corp` | 226 | 230 |
| `British Airways chairman` | 25 | 27 |

So general knowledge of the 1989 story is steady. What changed before 210k is exposure to the PTB text itself, which the checkpoint partly retained and which had faded by 216k. "Lord King" alone produced thousands of false positives ("Sovereign Lord King James…"), so those hits are excluded.

**300-character chunks: PTB eval text vs. the training document**

PTB (Paloma `ptb` val):
```
this is a total <unk> for takeover-stock traders one investment banker said 
 los angeles financier marvin davis who put united in play with a $ N billion bid two months ago last night <unk> both a ray of hope and an extra element of uncertainty by saying he remains interested in acquiring ual 
 but
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,550):
```
 traders one investment
for takeover-stock traders one investment banker
takeover-stock traders one investment banker said
<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> los
<s> <s> <s> <s> los angeles
<s> <s> <s> los angeles financier
<s> <s> los angeles financier marvin
<s> los angeles financier <NAME>
los angeles financier
```

PTB:
```
in london british airways chairman lord king was quoted in the times as declaring he is not prepared to take my shareholders into a <unk> deal 
 observers said it appeared that british air was angered at the way the bid has <unk> into confusion as well as by the banks ' effort to round up financing 
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,665):
```
<s> <s> <s> <s> in london
<s> <s> <s> in london british
<s> <s> in london british airways
<s> in london british airways chairman
in london british airways chairman lord
london british airways chairman lord king
british airways chairman lord king was
airways chairman lord king was quoted
chairman lor
```

The training copy has "marvin davis" replaced with `<NAME>` in most windows, presumably by PII scrubbing. One window, `los angeles financier marvin`, kept the first name because the scrubber only caught "marvin davis" as a pair. That is the token the 210k checkpoint predicted at 0.80. It also explains why every checkpoint already completes `marvin → davis`: that part is general knowledge, not this document.

**Takeaways**
- The 210k drop in PTB loss (about −0.2 nats, spread across almost every line) comes from verbatim exposure to the eval text in an n-gram layout roughly 330–730 steps earlier. It is not a capability change. 210k still misses PTB's genuinely surprising words ("declaring", "my"), which fits brief, partial exposure.
- Paloma PTB is contaminated in the hero mix, at least in `c13q3` and `c28q1`. Its curve will spike whenever those windows come up in the data order, so it shouldn't be read as a quality signal. Wikitext-103 and the other public eval sets may warrant the same scan.

Raw hits: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/full/*.jsonl`. Scanner: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/scan_training_data.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`, not pushed.

🤖 **The contaminated document, and every step that reads it**

**What it is.** One GitHub repository dump in source `c13q3`, **`quanpn90/torch-nplm`**: a Torch implementation of Bengio et al. (2003), with the name scrubbed to `<NAME>` in the README. It is **1,385,899 tokens** (4.83M characters), a single BOS…EOS document that spans 340 training sequences of 4,096 tokens.

| File | Characters |
|---|---|
| README.md | 260 |
| extract_ngrams.py | 2,308 |
| train.lua | 12,261 |
| **data/ptb/test.6grams** | **2,543,118** |
| **data/ptb/valid.6grams** | **2,262,165** |
| util/BatchLoader.lua | 4,901 |
| util/IdentityLinear.lua | 985 |

About 99.6% of the document is the **full PTB test and validation sets as sliding 6-gram windows**. `valid.6grams` starts `<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> consumers / … / consumers may want to move their / may want to move their telephones …`, which is exactly the start of Paloma's `ptb` eval document. So the whole Paloma PTB eval set is in the training data, with each word appearing in 6 overlapping windows.

First 500 characters:
```
Repository: quanpn90/torch-nplm

File: README.md
# torch-nplm

Neural probabilistic language model (<NAME>, 2003) implemented in Torch.

GPU supported for fast training.

Hierarchical supported for fast softmax-ing on a large vocabulary. 

HSM borrowed from https://github.com/yoonkim/lstm-char-cnn


File: extract_ngrams.py
#!/usr/bin/python
import sys

# This script extracts n-grams from a set of PREPROCESSED text files (train, set, valid)

data_dir = sys.argv[1]
ngram_order = int(sys.argv[2])

tra
```

**Every step that reads it over the full 390,251-step schedule.** I inverted the mixture and block shuffle using the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 stages, and `c13q3` at 69.8M sequences per epoch. The document straddles two 256-sequence shuffle blocks, which land in different shuffle windows, so each epoch reads it in two bursts:

| Epoch | Document part | Sequences | Steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | **176,080–176,355** |
| 0 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams` (Paloma PTB)** | 228 | **209,390–209,669** |
| 1 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | 327,205–327,493 *(future)* |
| 1 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams`** | 228 | **362,280–362,578** *(future)* |

**Implications**
- The 210k checkpoint was saved about 330–610 steps after the hero trained on the entire Paloma PTB eval set. That explains the drop, and its fading by 216k.
- **The PTB eval should drop again right after step ~362.3k**, when epoch 1 reaches the same block; that's in the cooldown stage. It's a useful sanity check that this explanation is right. The ~176k and ~327k bursts carry only PTB test-split text, not the Paloma eval text.
- Other copies of PTB in the mix, for example the n-gram probability tables in `c28q1` around step 206.3k, aren't covered by this mapping. A dedup or decontamination pass against Paloma would find them.

Files: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/docs/` holds the full document text (`doc_209550_4116.txt`), `summary.json`, and `torch_nplm_steps.json`, which maps every read to its step and row. Scripts: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/{scan_training_data,find_training_doc,find_doc_steps}.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`.
Its https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/, specifically https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/blob/master/data/ptb/valid.6grams. The sort of doc that could induce very weird repetition behavior.

@ClassicLarry, I went through the public W&B evals: all 16 Paloma and 7 Uncheatable subsets, every eval from step 2,999 to 227,999. I also ran the decon matcher on the torch-nplm files. Here are four results that may help the scan. **1. PTB has drops the torch-nplm reads don't explain** | Evals | PTB loss | Note | |---|---|---| | 101,999 → **104,999** → 107,999 | 2.143 → **1.961** → 2.109 | A one-eval drop with no mapped read nearby | | 188,999 → **191,999** | 2.115 → **2.015** | Drops 0.10 and stays below 2.08 through 227,999 | | 173,999 → **176,999** → 179,999 | 2.141 → **2.099** → 2.114 | Just after the 176,080–176,355 read, which has only the PTB *test* split | | 203,999 → **206,999** → 209,999 | 2.079 → **1.903** → 1.712 | The first half comes before the 209,390 read; it fits the `c28q1` tables at ~206.3k | The 176,999 row is a natural control. That read had PTB test text but none of the eval sentences. It moved the eval 0.029 below the average of its two neighbours, while the curve otherwise stays between 2.113 and 2.141 from 155,999 to 188,999. By the same measure, 104,999 is 0.165 below its neighbours, close to 209,999's 0.187. So I'd guess another copy of the validation text was read in steps **102,000–104,999**. If your scanner can run on that range, and on **189,000–191,999**, that would test it. **2. WikiText-103 shows the same pattern; general Wikipedia doesn't** At steps 125,999 / 128,999 / 131,999 / 134,999, `wikitext_103` reads 1.707 / **1.558** / 1.638 / 1.684. Over the same evals, `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` reads 1.828 / 1.827 / 1.823 / 1.824. Smaller one-sided drops recur at 137,999, 152,999, 203,999 and 212,999–215,999. None of them shows up in m2d2_wikipedia. A 0.15 drop on the WikiText eval with flat general Wikipedia looks like a document containing the eval text itself, not a Wikipedia-heavy stretch. Candidate windows: - **126,000–128,999**; - **210,000–212,999**, which your 204k–216k scan already covers. Re-running it with a few WikiText eval sentences may be the cheapest first check. **3. Decon would have missed torch-nplm even with Paloma indexed** Paloma isn't in the decon eval corpus, and `wikitext` is excluded on purpose (`DECON_EXCLUDED_EVAL_TASKS`, #6852 cluster A). I indexed the PTB validation text (Paloma's `ptb`) anyway to test the matcher. I ran the matching functions in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/decon.py` unchanged, using the `reference_pipeline.py` settings: 13-grams, overlap ≥ 0.5, ≥ 2 matched features, paragraphs split on `\n\n`. The repo was rendered the way `stack_v3.row_to_doc` renders it. | Training document | Max overlap | Flagged | |---|---|---| | torch-nplm as trained (6-gram windows) | 0.000 | no | | the same repo plus the raw `data/ptb/valid.txt` | 1.000 | yes | | the validation set as windows of any width from 3 to 30 | ≤ 0.14 | no | A small pre-pass recovers it. When most lines of a paragraph are windows that shift by one token, stitch them back into running text, drop ``, and score the result as an extra paragraph. Overlap goes back to 1.000. In 5,724 ordinary code and text files (the Marin repo and the CPython 3.12 standard library), the pass triggered on none of 241,449 paragraphs. Details are on #6852, the issue about this matcher's recall. So one store-wide pass may be cheaper than scanning step ranges. Run decon in flag-only mode against Paloma `ptb` and `wikitext_103`, with the stitching pass, and then run `find_doc_steps.py` on what it flags. Raw copies would score about 1.0. **4. For alerts and for comparisons with the pre-registered prediction** After the 108k mix swap, PTB accounts for 50–68% of the variance in the Paloma macro's eval-to-eval movement, and WikiText-103 for 19–27%. The ranges cover three detrending methods; the block-bootstrap 95% CI for PTB is 0.33–0.85. Dropping both subsets cuts the macro's noise SD to 43–61% of its current value. The 7 Uncheatable subsets show no drops at any threshold I tried, which fits #9729. For the Paloma chart and the #8435 comparison, a 14-subset macro without `ptb` and `wikitext_103`, shown next to the official one, would keep these exposures out of the trend. Scripts and outputs: [eval-audit/](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/main/eval-audit). Everything uses the public W&B project and public GitHub files.

A follow-up on the store-wide pass from (3). I ran a narrower check: a 13-gram scan of the public Stack v3, the source of the torch-nplm document, limited to files whose path or size looks like PTB or WikiText data. Apart from torch-nplm, none of them holds either validation text. So the other drops, at 104,999 and 191,999 for PTB and the WikiText ones, still need your scanner or a store-wide pass.

**Scope**
- All 8,192 parquet files of `HuggingFaceCode/stack-v3-train`, 172.8M repos.
- The parquet files at your pinned `bb2fa950` (`stack_v3.py`) now return 403; HF squashed the dataset history on 2026-09-25. I used the current `1f61b735` (v3.1). It differs from v3.0 by opted-out repos and by the duplicated file entries that `deduplicate_files` already drops (#7788).
- 529 files passed the path/size filter. Each was scored by 13-gram overlap with PTB and WikiText-103 valid/test, as written and de-windowed.

| Eval text | Best file in Stack v3 | Share of the eval's 13-grams |
|---|---|---|
| PTB valid (Paloma `ptb` val) | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/valid.6grams` | 0.988, de-windowed |
| PTB test | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/test.6grams` | 0.987, de-windowed |
| WikiText-103 valid (Paloma `wikitext_103` val) | `DavidFanzz/llm_decoding` `data/wikitext/test.jsonl` | 0.024, as written |
| WikiText-103 test (raw) | `shaochenze/PatchTrain` `wikitext_document_level-test.json` | 0.699, as written (JSON-escaped) |

- **PTB.** torch-nplm is the only copy the scan found. None of the standard `ptb.*.txt` files is in stack-v3-train, and no selected file outside torch-nplm shares a single 13-gram with the validation text, as written or de-windowed. So the other copy I guessed at in (1) isn't in a Stack v3 file that looks like PTB data.
- **WikiText validation.** No selected file holds more than 2.4% of it. I also checked that Paloma's `wikitext_103` val is the WikiText-103 validation split: it contains 98% of validation's 13-grams and none of test's.
- **WikiText test.** The PatchTrain file is the full test set, all 62 articles, stored as JSON lines: the GitHub original decodes to it, identical up to whitespace, and the Stack v3 copy is 0.9% shorter, which fits the dataset's PII redaction (names become `<NAME>`). It doesn't touch Paloma, but it is the test set of lm-eval's `wikitext` task, since WikiText-2 raw test is the same text. `wikitext` is in `DECON_EXCLUDED_EVAL_TASKS` because "every web/book corpus overlaps it" (#6852 cluster A). Here, though, a code repo carries nearly the whole test set, so if the hero read this repo (`find_doc_steps.py` would show), its lm-eval `wikitext` score would be contaminated.
- **Limits.** The filter misses copies under unrelated names, PTB/WikiText-named files under 50 KB, and copies inside code or markup files (`.py`, `.md`, `.html`, …). The scoring only recognizes running text and shift-by-one windows, so it would also miss tables like the `c28q1` n-gram ones. Repos that opted out before v3.1 can't be checked. A flag-only decon pass over the whole store, with the stitching pass from (3), would close the name, size and opt-out gaps. It wouldn't catch tables, and it has low recall on copies embedded in code (#6852).

**New since my first comment.** The drops continue on `hero-mfu30-step231k`, and the latest one reaches a new low:
- `wikitext_103` fell from 1.584 at 230,999 to 1.491 at 233,999, held at 1.500, and fell to 1.301 at 239,999. Over the next four evals it rose to 1.427–1.455, still below its 1.52–1.59 range from 212,999 to 230,999. At 254,999 it fell again, by 0.168 in one eval, to 1.271, its lowest so far. Over the same evals `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` fell steadily from 1.732 to 1.705.
- PTB, from 230,999 to 254,999: 1.957 → 2.003 → 1.882 → 2.017 → 1.877 → 1.942 → 1.996 → 2.030 → 2.029. It dipped at 236,999 and 242,999, by 0.12 and 0.14 from the eval before, and then rose.
- Together, `wikitext_103` and PTB account for about 65% of the Paloma macro's drop from 2.140 at 230,999 to 2.118 at 242,999; the other 14 subsets fell 0.009 on average. As PTB rose, the macro rose back to 2.126 at 248,999. At 254,999 it fell 0.012 in one eval, to 2.111, and 88% of that came from `wikitext_103`: the other 14 subsets fell 0.0016 on average, and the Uncheatable macro moved from 1.583 to 1.582.

Neither the torch-nplm reads nor the Stack v3 pass explains these drops, so they give new windows for your scanner: 231,000–233,999, 237,000–239,999 and 252,000–254,999 for WikiText, and 234,000–236,999 and 240,000–242,999 for PTB, whose dips sit 0.13 and 0.10 below the average of their two neighbours (the 176,999 control in (1) was 0.029).

From 257,999 the evals pack at 16K (#10101), so their values can't be compared with those above. Between the first two 16K evals, `wikitext_103` rose from 1.372 to 1.419 while `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` stayed at 1.672. That fits the 254,999 drop fading.

Script and outputs: [stackv3_eval_copy_scan.py](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/blob/main/eval-audit/code/stackv3_eval_copy_scan.py), [results/stackv3/](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/main/eval-audit/results/stackv3).

topics.title: [levanter] Shift eval targets across context shards
topics.body:
Use the sharding-aware next-token shift from the training loss in tagged and labeled LM evaluation. An explicitly sharded context axis previously made JAX reject the evaluator's position roll before held-out metrics were emitted.

Preserve the explicit token layout for byte lookup when context is sharded. On a two-device CPU mesh, tagged evaluation matches unsharded loss and bits-per-byte metrics, and labeled evaluation returns the reference next-token IDs.

Fixes #10232

topics.title: [skyrl] Add PivotRL pivot-state training support
topics.body:
tl;dr

PivotRL (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383) is a flavor of RL that was used extensively in Nemotron-Ultra post-training. It operates on existing SFT trajectories to combine the compute efficiency of SFT with the OOD accuracy of E2E RL. PivotRL first executes local, on-policy rollouts and filters for pivots: informative intermediate turns where sampled actions exhibit high variance in outcomes; then it utilizes rewards for functional-equivalent actions rather than demanding strict string matching with the SFT data demonstration.

MarinSkyRL training data resolves to two kinds, a plain directory (`ArtifactDataSource`) and a TaskTrove parquet cohort (`TaskTroveDataSource`). Neither carries per-step annotations.

Scope: a Marin data source that resolves per-step pivot annotations with artifact identity, request plumbing for them, and a `MARIN_SKYRL` pin bump (`lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py:73`) to a MarinSkyRL revision that consumes the annotations and applies step weights in the training loop.

Open questions:

- Compute pivot scores (teacher-forced NLL under the student) as a Marin
  artifact step, or accept only precomputed annotations?
- Carry detection parameters (spike threshold, pivot weight) as named
  `SkyRLSpec` fields or leave them to `config_yaml` and `overrides`?

Done when:

- A pivot-annotated source resolves to a `ResolvedDataSource` whose
  identity covers the annotations, so the step fingerprint changes when
  annotations change.
- `SkyRLLaunchRequest` carries the annotations, and the pinned MarinSkyRL
  commit applies non-uniform step weights end to end.
- Annotation-free specs keep today's fingerprints and training behavior.
- `tests/rl/test_skyrl.py` covers the new source kind and request fields.
- We can reproduce this result from the paper E2E in MarinSkyRL -> 'On GSM8K (200 problems, 182 Kimi K2.5 competition-math traces, Gemma 4 E4B student), pivot-weighted SFT at 2.5x loss scored 80.0% vs 74.5% for uniform SFT against an 85.5% base."

comments.body:
Two released NVIDIA datasets are good candidate targets for the first Snowball PivotRL experiment:

- [`nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1), pinned at `4947a3c8ea803413a65f9eca14a96ef521b2ddf5`. The current release has 50,308 pivot rows with `trajectory_id`, prefix position, `expected_action`, and profiling counts/pass rate (`pass_rate_total` is 8 in the inspected rows).
- [`nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1), pinned at `eaef26944643644c8a3dbbf361ce6128142f5976`. It has 31,111 pivot rows with `expected_answer`, `source_trajectory_uid`, and `pivot_agent_turn_index` from GLM-5.1/Terminus-2 trajectories.

These releases correct the assumption in the issue that no training data is public. They are sufficient for a method-level reproduction, but not an exact reproduction of the paper: the SWE release is not the paper's reported 87,718-example filtered set, and the Terminal release uses a later teacher/task mixture.

Prepare separate SWE and Terminal artifacts first. Split SWE by `trajectory_id` and Terminal by `metadata.source_trajectory_uid`, not by row, so neighboring prefixes from one trajectory cannot cross train/validation. The adapter should map `responses_create_params.input` to `prompt`, preserve tools and request options, carry the expected action/answer and source identity in `extra_info`, and emit a single-turn local functional-verifier environment. SWE can reuse the existing `nemotron_ultra` action comparator after normalizing the released agent name; Terminal needs an `expected_answer` verifier case. The raw Hugging Face rows are not yet SkyRL-shaped and should not be passed directly to `PromptDataset`.

For iteration, use the two Harbor evals already implemented in Marin:

- SWE-bench Verified random-100: `swebench`
- Terminal-Bench 2.1: `tb2`

Both are in-distribution for this experiment and are safe to inspect and hill climb. Keep the policy's OOD suite untouched until the checkpoint and hyperparameters are frozen. The current launcher command is:

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model <registered-snowball-pivot-checkpoint> \
  --evals swebench,tb2 \
  --priority interactive \
  --no-wait
```

The checked-in Harbor policies use Terminus-2 + Daytona; `swebench` points at the fixed random-100 set and `tb2` points at Marin's Terminal-Bench 2 dataset. This also gives us a direct comparison with the Snowball R2E-Gym result in #9225.

Proposed training overlay below. Apply it to `cloud/iris/configs/snowball_ultra_rlvr1_split64.yaml` so the tested Megatron/vLLM placement and model geometry remain unchanged. `<...>` values are immutable prepared artifacts produced from one of the pinned releases above. Run SWE and Terminal as separate primary arms; a balanced mixture is a follow-up experiment.

```yaml
# snowball_pivotrl_split64.yaml: overlay on snowball_ultra_rlvr1_split64.yaml
entrypoint: standard

context_budget:
  request_window_tokens: 65536
  max_turns: 1
  max_new_tokens_per_turn: null  # proposed: use all context remaining after this row's prefix

trainer:
  strategy: megatron
  seed: 42
  algorithm:
    advantage_estimator: grpo
    grpo_norm_by_std: true
    advantage_batch_normalize: false
    eps_clip_low: 0.2
    eps_clip_high: 0.2
    use_entropy_loss: false
    use_kl_in_reward: false
    use_kl_loss: true
    kl_loss_coef: 0.001
    loss_reduction: token_mean
    dynamic_sampling:
      type: null                 # frozen released pivots: closest paper-like arm
      max_sample_batches: 30
      min_replace_ratio: 0.3
      informative_on: unshaped
      min_reward_std: 0.0
  epochs: 1
  max_steps: 130                # paper's disclosed SWE run length
  update_epochs_per_batch: 1
  train_batch_size: 64          # 64 unique pivot prefixes
  policy_mini_batch_size: 1024  # 64 prefixes x 16 responses
  eval_batch_size: 100
  micro_forward_batch_size_per_gpu: 1
  micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu: 1
  use_sample_packing: true
  eval_before_train: true
  eval_interval: 10
  ckpt_interval: 10
  max_ckpts_to_keep: 3
  resume_mode: none
  logger: wandb
  project_name: snowball-pivotrl
  # Keep policy/ref Megatron configs and split64 placement unchanged.

generator:
  backend: vllm
  n_samples_per_prompt: 16
  eval_n_samples_per_prompt: 1
  sampling_params:
    temperature: 1.0
    top_p: 1.0
    top_k: -1
  # Keep the tested split64 engine topology and Hermes tool parser unchanged.

data:
  kind: parquet
  train_data:
    - <s3://immutable-artifact/nemotron-{swe|terminal}-pivot/<hf-revision>/train.parquet>
  val_data:
    - <s3://immutable-artifact/nemotron-{swe|terminal}-pivot/<hf-revision>/validation.parquet>
  shuffle: true
```

The prepared rows should use `env_class: nemotron_ultra`; retain the existing `environment.skyrl_gym.nemotron_ultra` block. Each pivot rollout must terminate after one sampled action and use the local functional verifier.

`max_new_tokens_per_turn: null` is proposed syntax, not accepted by the current launcher. For a single-turn pivot there should be no separate generation budget: set each request's `max_tokens` to `request_window_tokens - tokenized_prefix_length` and let the model use the remaining context. `ContextBudget` currently requires a positive fixed output allowance and subtracts it from every row's prompt allowance; #9176 should make that field nullable for `max_turns: 1` (or add an equivalent remaining-context mode). Reusing the end-to-end RLVR config's 6,528-token cap would truncate valid pivot actions for no methodological reason.

The `64 x 16` geometry yields 1,024 rollout trajectories per trainer step. Confirm that count in the first rollout manifest before a full run. Start with a bounded startup/memory smoke, then run the static arm above. A Marin-specific follow-up can set `dynamic_sampling.type: filter` with `informative_on: unshaped` to replace stale all-pass/all-fail groups online; that is useful, but it is no longer the paper's frozen-pivot method.

The paper does not disclose the KL coefficient. Pre-register `0`, `0.001`, and `0.01` and report all three instead of selecting one retrospectively from SWE-bench/TB2.1. Keep reward shaping disabled so group informativeness is computed from the binary functional outcome.

open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21

Ok, I took a look at the two linked datasets, to get a flavor for them: * [nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1) * [nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1) **Some observations:** * no task difficulty bias by pivot position in trajectory * no task difficulty bias by tool category * lower variance than I'd expect between task difficulty when slicing by tool category More plots and explorations [here](https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/7828f3393f342a7df177cf5fb7b9a011#file-readme-md). #### position vs. difficulty #### task vs. difficulty

So [nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-SWE-Pivot-v1) appears to have duplicate rows. Of the ~51k rows, there are slightly under ~4k unique `prompt, target action` pairs. E.g., there are 400+ `(prompt, action)` pairs with exactly 12 dupes. Here's the full histogram. Code and example dupes at [this gist](https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/1ffedc3c5fc8dd5b6730a21d84c6e07c). N.b., [nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot-v1) seems fine and is clean (de-duping is [explicitly mentioned](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.21383v1#A1) in the paper).

Using baby qwen, I did a [small comparison of SFT to PivotRL](https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/8a77d03bc2c89e33364d0b51183bdd1d) on the SWE dataset. PivotRL seemed to be learning something over SFT--the results were promising enough to kick off a larger run.

I quickly compared (verified?) [Snowball](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92) and [Grug](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) with various verifiers. * Grug and Snowball both roughly match the published nvidia pass rates on `SWE`. * Terminal doesn't have published pass rates, but Snowball seems to suffer on schema correctness. * I also compared to using [jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev)-as-the-judge on the `terminal` data. But didn't observe any changes in the initial accuracy. Code [here](https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/d2a5a273dfc0abb525a69e6bdf0521e0). #### SWE #### Terminal #### Jev-as-a-Judge on Terminal

topics.title: [levanter] LM evaluation fails with explicitly context-sharded tokens
topics.body:
Held-out LM evaluation fails when token positions are explicitly sharded across a context mesh. Training updates succeed; the first evaluation raises:

```text
lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py:238, _default_lm_eval_loss_fn
per_pos_token_id = jnp.roll(named_batch.tokens.array, -1, axis=-1)
ShardingTypeError: `a` cannot be sharded on the axis being rolled over.
Got arr type=i32[16@(replica_dcn,data,expert),32768@context] and axis=(1,)
```

Reproduce:
1. Use an explicit mesh with local axes `data=1, replica=1, model=1, expert=8` and inter-node axes `replica_dcn=1, context=4` (32 GPUs).
2. Map `batch` to `(replica_dcn,data,expert)` and `position` to `context`, with global batch 16 and sequence length 32,768.
3. Run `cb_tagged_lm_evaluate` on a model and batch with that layout. Its default loss callback reaches the failing roll.

Expected: target-token shifting and token-weighted evaluation agree with an unsharded reference. The training loss path in `models/loss.py` already gathers the token IDs along the sharded position axis before shifting and restores their layout afterward.

Observed in the #10213 sweep at completed update 548, its first held-out evaluation, on base commit `753bbb163c78f0e7ea50059522f42156708162c8` plus experiment-local changes. Iris job: `/karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft`. Retrieve the error with `uv run iris --cluster=marin task logs /karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft/1 --substring ShardingTypeError`.

The labeled callback contains the same roll at `eval.py:277`; that path was not exercised in this run. This issue tracks the shared evaluator fix separately from moving the sweep's validation offline.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Both default LM evaluation callbacks call `jnp.roll` on token arrays whose position axis may be explicitly sharded. JAX rejects that roll before the evaluator can aggregate loss or byte counts. The evaluator already receives the mesh mapping needed to restore the token layout after shifting.

**Relevant code**
- [`eval.py#L223-L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L223-L237) — tagged callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L259-L276`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L259-L276) — labeled callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L531-L577`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L531-L577) — token IDs feed byte aggregation

# Proposed Fix

`TaggedEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` or `LabeledEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` → default loss callback → `jnp.roll` on context-sharded positions → `ShardingTypeError`. Replicate the position axis for the shift, then restore its mapped sharding in both default callbacks; verify token IDs and token-weighted metrics against an unsharded reference on a small context mesh.

🤖 Fix is open in #10233. Both default callbacks use the training loss's sharding-safe token shift, and byte lookup keeps an explicit output layout for context shards. Two-device CPU regressions match unsharded tagged loss and bits-per-byte metrics and labeled next-token IDs; the focused evaluator and loss suite passed 23 tests. The full Levanter run hit an unrelated Grug MoE test that uses `ragged-all-to-all`, which XLA:CPU does not support; all-files Pyrefly reported missing optional imports outside the changed files.
🤖 PR #10233 passed CI, including the Levanter unit and repository lint jobs. It remains open and mergeable, with review required and no submitted reviews after the 12-hour monitor timeout.

Run a version-pinned Snowball initializer for configurable training iterations, defaulting to 25 optimizer updates over the full training pool with 8,192-token replies and a 24,576-token context.

Cache the initializer baseline by model manifest, tokenizer and template, panel, grading and decoding protocol, source identity and frozen dependency lock. Training commits its checkpoint and HF export before independent scoring. Iterate on a fixed 100-task subset of the 910-task panel: 20 each from calendar, competitive coding, reasoning gym, STEM and structural tasks. Select the full panel for broader checks.

Persist answers before grading. A scoring retry reloads the saved launch configuration and completed inference, then allows one replay per admitted saved answer after a grading or infrastructure failure, bounded by per-answer and total recovery timeouts, without another model request. Incomplete coverage fails scoring while leaving completed training and export reusable.

CPU checks cover artifact cache reuse, export preservation after scoring failure and recovery across two independently built scoring attempts. Fresh qualification of the assembled GPU path is still required; the two-to-four-hour loop remains a target to measure.

topics.title: [iris] Capability proxy returns 502 while a preempted serve task is being replaced
topics.body:
When a served model's Iris task is preempted and replaced, the native capability proxy answers requests that arrive during the replacement with HTTP 502 `upstream transport error: client error (Connect)`. Clients see a hard failure for a gap Iris is already recovering from.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 an Evalchemy GSM8K screen on H100 lost 112 of 1,319 rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 00:14:07 UTC; Iris rescheduled it and the replacement was initializing from 00:14:55. At 00:19 the proxy returned 502 to the queued requests, the client exhausted its retries, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR` (`model_transport`). Recovery needed a manual selective rerun of the 112 doc ids and a cached regrade before the record could be merged (1,215/1,319 after recovery).

A second instance on 2026-10-19 lost 960 of 1,319 GSM8K rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 03:42:04 UTC. Requests in flight at that moment got 502 `client error (SendRequest)` (15 responses at 03:42). Requests sent afterwards got 502 `client error (Connect)` (985 responses from 03:42 to 03:47) until the client gave up, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR`. The same serve task was preempted six more times over the next 11 hours (attempts 1 to 6) at interactive priority. That record needed a full GSM8K rerun.

The 502 comes from the native proxy's upstream error path ([`lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs` L1243-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1243-L1246)), which maps any connect failure to `BAD_GATEWAY`. [`lib/iris/docs/federation.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/docs/federation.md) documents this message as "cannot connect to its upstream".

Reproduce:
1. Serve a model through a capability URL (for example the eval launcher with Harbor or a capability-routed Evalchemy run).
2. Send a steady stream of requests through the capability URL.
3. Preempt or cancel the serving task and let Iris start a replacement under the same endpoint name.
4. Requests sent before the replacement registers return 502 with the message above.

Expected: while the endpoint's job is still live and a replacement task is pending or initializing, the proxy holds the request until the endpoint registers again (bounded by the request timeout), or returns 503 with `Retry-After`. Clients retry connect errors and 503s with backoff for at least the documented serve replacement time. A replacement can take much longer than a request timeout: in the second instance the serve stayed unavailable for the rest of the GSM8K client's retry budget. Holding requests therefore covers short gaps only. Long gaps need the 503 signal so that the client can pause instead of recording failures.

Done when: a serve-replacement test through the capability proxy completes requests sent during the gap, or receives 503 with `Retry-After`, and no 502 is returned while the job is live.

Related: #10237 covers the direct-route client (`remote_inference`) keeping a stale address after rescheduling.

Evidence (Iris task events and the Evalchemy client log, URLs omitted):

```
2026-10-18T00:14:07.473Z attempt 0  k8s/kueue        WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted  Preempted to accommodate a workload (UID: 3fc9af02-…)
2026-10-18T00:14:50.525Z attempt 0  iris/controller  TaskRetryScheduled             Backend reported PREEMPTED; controller returned the task to PENDING.
2026-10-18T00:14:55.578Z attempt 1  k8s/container    PodInitializing
[00:19:08] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
[00:19:09] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
```

Second instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/inference-177d09d0c73a4f048310e082db087746/0` (Kueue `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted` at 03:42:04, 05:19:02, 07:12:39, 10:56:25, 11:04:59, 14:19:01 and 14:24:54 UTC), evaluator task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/eval-gsm8k-0shot-4ac3cd86/0`, record `20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-gsm8k-0shot-6554` (`infra_failed`, 359/1,319 scored).

First instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/inference-a54b7942d3b34ffba92e5f0d4192aa69/0`. Evaluator task: `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0`. Record: `20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-gsm8k-0shot-77c1`.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Iris keeps a serving endpoint's last address until its lease expires (at most 10 minutes). The native proxy can therefore route a request to a preempted task; its upstream transport error path returns 502. Once the lease expires, the registry omits the endpoint and the same live job can instead return 404. The registry has no replacement state, so changing 502 to 503 alone would leave that later gap unresolved. [PR #10033](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033) handles Evalchemy's direct-route relay and does not change this capability path.

**Relevant code**
- [`endpoint_service.py#L40-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L40-L49) — ten-minute registration lease.
- [`endpoint_service.py#L165-L177`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L165-L177) — live mappings enter the proxy snapshot.
- [`lib.rs#L230-L264`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L230-L264) — expired mappings are skipped.
- [`lib.rs#L1190-L1240`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1190-L1240) — transport failures become 502.
- [`client.py#L79-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L79-L93) — Evalchemy allows eight request retries.

# Proposed Fix

The failure chain is task preemption → old endpoint address remains routable → connect/send fails → proxy returns 502; after lease expiry, lookup returns 404. This needs a controller/proxy availability contract and a capability-client retry budget, so it is larger than a local status-code patch.

1. Preserve an authenticated endpoint name while its owning task is being retried. Publish `ready` versus `replacing` in the controller's proxy snapshot/deltas; preemption and lease expiry make the old address unavailable, replacement registration restores `ready`, and terminal job/task state removes the route. Reconstruct the same state after controller restart.
2. Return 503 with `Retry-After` for `replacing` and for connect/send failures to task-owned endpoints, including a race before the registry update. Keep ordinary 404 for unknown names and 502 for unrelated upstream/protocol failures. Do not replay an in-flight POST inside the proxy.
3. Verify the pinned Evalchemy and Harbor capability clients retry 503 according to `Retry-After` with a time budget tied to the evaluation deadline and stop on terminal serve state. Extend their policy where needed; leave the direct-route relay in #10033 alone.
4. Add a real HTTP capability-proxy test that sends requests before preemption, during replacement, after the old lease expires, and after a new address registers. Assert no 502/404 during the recoverable gap, 503 plus `Retry-After` until recovery, successful forwarding afterwards, and terminal/unknown routes ending promptly. Cover an in-flight send failure and the federated capability relay as separate cases.

Open decision: the repository documents a 10-minute endpoint lease but no upper bound on serve replacement. Use the evaluation's overall deadline as the retry cap unless a shorter serve-replacement contract is established; eight immediate request retries are insufficient for the observed multi-minute gaps.

topics.title: [vLLM] Diagnose Snowball TPU long-context logprob divergence
topics.body:
Snowball 67B served through TPU-vLLM differs from native Levanter TPU at long
context. Three clean v6e-8 processes produced bitwise-identical observations
for all 64 representative prompts, with complete selected-token coverage and no
nonfinite values or router overflows. Maximum probability errors against the
native TPU golden were:

| Context bucket | Maximum error | Greedy agreement |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | 0.030292 | 16/16 |
| 1K | 0.044239 | 14/16 |
| 4K | 0.082621 | 16/16 |
| 16K | 0.586413 | 3/8 |
| 32K | 0.436956 | 4/8 |

The qualified path used vLLM
`b66e4159789e09a87ce0b9e8bf679c46bb78ffe8`, tpu-inference
`88674e89b2fa120622448fe06ed00ae5e9b1faef`, TP8/DP1, and a top-4096
diagnostic response.

#7554 records related GPU long-context sensitivity, but the measured mechanisms
are different. Its GPU path uses DP8/expert parallelism and varies by rank and
launch. This TPU path uses DP1 and repeated bitwise across processes and slices.
MoE routing may amplify low-level numerical differences in both paths; a common
root cause has not been established.

The TPU parity PR will retain all 64 prompts under compatibility-smoke bounds of
0.04/0.05/0.10/0.70/0.50. These bounds prevent regression but do not claim
strong 16K/32K numerical parity.

Done when: identify the first material TPU-vLLM/native-TPU divergence at 16K and
32K, determine whether it shares a mechanism with #7554, and either reduce the
long-context envelope or document why the remaining difference is expected.

topics.title: [iris] Follow re-registered serve endpoints from Evalchemy evals
topics.body:
## tl;dr

While doing evals for another experiment ( https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9984), agent found that serve endpoints that got pre-empted permanently lost their connection. This should fix that.


## Full Explanation (agent)
Evalchemy children now reach their serve through a loopback relay that looks
the endpoint name up in the Iris registry, instead of a host:port resolved once
at launch. When Kueue preempts the serve and its retry registers on another
host, the old address refuses connections, hangs, or answers 404. The eval used
to retry that address until the group timed out: nine groups on cw-rno2a were
lost this way on 2026-10-09/10, some after 16-20 h.

The relay (iris.cluster.client.endpoint_relay) looks the name up every 30 s and
after each connection failure or 404. It aborts requests still waiting on a
replaced address and replays requests that have no response yet once the
endpoint is registered again (for up to 1 h, then 503). A response that has
started is never replayed; the relay drops the client connection so lm-eval's
own retries apply. Each relay thread keeps a pooled direct connection, so evals
keep the direct routing that #9480 chose over the hub proxy.

The fix sits in an Iris client module so any in-cluster client can use it. A
stable cluster-level address (a per-endpoint Kubernetes Service, or
controller-side forwarding) would cover every client without a helper process,
but it needs a controller deploy and work in each backend. The hub proxy
already follows re-registrations, and it is the path #9480 moved away from. The
relay ships in the job bundle and takes effect on the next eval launch.

While the Evalchemy job runs, the parent now reads the serve job states every
60 s. When one is terminal, it cancels the Evalchemy job and the record becomes
infra_failed with the serve job ID and state. A failed status read does not end
the eval. Before, the parent waited with no bound.

Tests drive the relay with real HTTP servers and a fake registry whose endpoint
moves mid-run. On a local in-process Iris cluster, the relay CLI in a client
task followed a serve job that was cancelled and replaced under the same
endpoint name; the request in flight during the gap waited about 4 s and was
answered by the replacement. A [CoreWeave smoke test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033#issuecomment-6136856836)
also passed task-token registry lookup and failover to a replacement port through
the `$IRIS_VENV` relay subprocess. Both serve tasks ran on the same node, and
the helper ran in a plain Iris task. Cross-host relocation and the actual
Evalchemy child's isolated uvx environment remain untested by that smoke.

Fixes #10030

🤖 CoreWeave smoke at 38bcc8b65a (cw-us-east-08a, CPU only, job `/karan/smoke-relay-10033-d`): passed.

A coordinator task started a fake serve job that registered `/serve/smoke-relay-<id>`, then opened the relay through the Evalchemy child's `endpoint_relay()` helper, which launches `$IRIS_VENV/bin/python -m iris.cluster.client.endpoint_relay`. The relay's registry lookup used the task token. It then cancelled the serve, waited until the old address stopped answering, started a replacement under the same name, and sent a request through the relay.

```
02:23:33 relay up; request 1 answered by first (http://10.186.213.131:10241)
02:24:03 relay: Endpoint moved: http://10.186.213.131:10241 -> None   (periodic refresh)
02:24:07 old address is down; request 2 sent
02:24:20 relay: Endpoint moved: None -> http://10.186.213.131:10243
02:24:20 request 2 answered by second after 13s
```

Limits: both serve tasks landed on the same node, so the move changed only the port, not the host. The relay ran in a plain Iris task, not under the uvx environment of a real Evalchemy child; the helper and `$IRIS_VENV` are the same. Earlier runs showed a cancelled serve pod keeps answering for about 30 s while Kubernetes stops it; the relay correctly kept using it while it answered.

Kept `_in_flight` cancellation: the relay and lm-eval both allow 1800-second responses, so relying only on timeout retries can leave a request blocked for 30 minutes after its endpoint has moved. The regressions for a stalled pre-header request and a stalled response body still pass; started responses are closed, never replayed. Kept the resolver/server structure and the focused 404 policy rather than expanding this fix into a proxy redesign or replaying arbitrary HTTP errors.

The six findings from the required lint-catalog review were addressed: log socket-shutdown errors during cleanup; move interpreter selection to the entry point; replace implementation narration with a boundary comment; remove three assertions tied to human-readable messages. topics.title: [grug] Add GB200 launch and H100 validation support
topics.body:
Add a GB200 launcher, tracked JAXPP runtime overlay and fresh Harrier data support to the H100 pipeline foundation merged in #9279. The launcher requests one NVLink domain in the opportunistic batch queue, separates admission and execution deadlines, and disables failure and preemption retries. Fresh-data trials explicitly disable simulated epoching, preserving full datasets even when the mixture schedule exceeds the simulated-token budget. The diagnostic fetches one batch at a time on demand, closes its iterators, and uses the same batch-placement policy for compilation and training. Checkpoint metadata includes the data source, seed, schedule horizon and router-bias adaptation mode.

The runtime pins JAXPP `328f75a80cecf22c7cc030a82d8941d3c1e220b6` plus `runtime/jaxpp_host_startup.patch` (SHA256 `d987c16ece399fe5eeb69d413703d549135635f19a57dc4b6c60cc0d1ea4b1a7`), which keeps activation copies in forward tasks, preserves pinned-host output placement and warms tasks with disposable inputs.
