| 16K | stack | 13.15 s | 319.0k | 32.03% | 123.4 GiB | 3.14e-3 |

* The stack saves about 1.27 s per step at every length (+10.0%, +10.0%, +9.6% tokens/s), and the extra time for long context is unchanged: 16K adds 0.449 s over 4K with the stack and 0.446 s without. As a fraction of the shorter step, 16K costs 3.4% of 4K throughput with the stack against 3.1% without.

@mcwitt @ClassicLarry Short version: the qk arms will probably tie, so it may help to write down a tie rule before the 11-rack runs. The rule: keep the formula value (1.48 at 16K) unless another arm beats it, on both Uncheatable and the Paloma macro without PTB and WikiText, by more than the noise the rehearsal measures. The details below build on Larry's 100-step test and the agent's one-rack rehearsal plan (2–3 seeds × 200 steps per arm).

**1. On the 67B, the qk arms were nearly tied, and the two metrics disagreed.**
- In the [67B qk test](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k_yarn_mscale01_test20) (five arms, 20 steps from step 39k at 65K packing), the arms spanned 0.009 on Paloma and 0.003 on Uncheatable at the last eval. The best two were 0.0002 apart on Paloma and 0.00002 on Uncheatable.
- All-layer 1.570, which the 67B cooldown then used, was first on Paloma and fourth of five on Uncheatable.
- The arms were still converging. Over the 19 steps after the first eval, their spread shrank from 0.013 to 0.009 on Paloma and from 0.015 to 0.003 on Uncheatable.

**2. PTB and WikiText make the full Paloma macro a noisy judge for this trial.**
- On the hero, the two carry 77% of the 16-subset macro's eval-to-eval variance. Over the last 30 evals, the SD of the change is 0.0049 for the full macro, 0.0026 for the other 14 subsets and 0.0012 for Uncheatable.
- Both look like exposures to copies in the training data (#9874). Over those evals, PTB or WikiText moved by up to 0.2 between consecutive evals, which is up to 0.012 on the macro.
- Arms that share batches see the same exposures, but they need not memorize them equally, and any difference lands in the comparison.
- In Belay, where paired arms also share batches, PTB's differences between configs barely reproduce across seeds (r = 0.10 near the frontier). Dropping PTB and WikiText there cuts the noise SD by about 20% ([analysis](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/main/belay-noise)).
- On the 67B test, dropping them didn't change the ranking; the disagreement there was between Paloma and Uncheatable.

**3. The rehearsal can set the bar.**
- Its seeds give the seed-to-seed SD of each arm's difference from the 1.48 arm on these two metrics. With 2–3 seeds per arm, pool that SD across arms.
- The pooled SD will be rough, and probably conservative for 11 racks, since one rack runs 11× fewer tokens per step. Matching the trial's length helps.
- A rule written down in advance could be: keep 1.48 unless another arm beats it on both metrics by more than twice that SD. If the metrics disagree, it's a tie.
- Applied to the 67B test, this rule keeps the formula arm, which is what the 67B used.
- For selection, score the arms on the 16K-packed evals that the agent's plan adds, and use the 4K-packed evals as a retention check. qk_mult changes the model at every length, so a 4K score alone could favour a smaller qk for reasons unrelated to 16K quality.

Happy to compute the bar from the rehearsal runs once they're on W&B.

> 23\. Short version: the qk arms will probably tie, so it may help to write down a tie rule before the 11-rack runs. The rule: keep the formula value (1.48 at 16K) unless another arm beats it, on both Uncheatable and the Paloma macro without PTB and WikiText, by more than the noise the rehearsal measures.

I like the idea of excluding PTB and WikiText! I agree that the default will be 1.48. (Also noting that the 67B started at 8k seqlen with 1.3 and not 4k seqlen, so it ended up with a lower qk_mult at each higher seqlen). Though I don't think we gain from fully automating the decision process up front. If the tests provide no differentiation we will go with 1.48 on all layers- but we may see signal in unexpected ways such as in gradient behavior on certain parameters, or stability of loss during its 200 steps.

Thanks! Agreed on 1.48 as the default. And yes, the 1.570 arm is the same formula from the 67B's 8K start, 1.3 × (0.1 ln 8 + 1); from the hero's 4K, the same X = 0.1 gives 1.48 at 16K.

On reading loss and gradient behavior, the existing step-180k restores show how noisy each one is:

- **Loss: compare arms step by step on the same seed.** Runs with the same seed and packing read the same batches: at 16K, the three seed-0 restores differ by an SD of 3–5e-4 per step, against 0.06 across seeds. On the 67B, whose arms also shared batches, the per-step gaps to 1.3 varied by an SD of 0.0005–0.002 after the first 5 steps, against 0.02 for the loss itself, and ranked the arms as Paloma did, up to a 0.0002 near-tie at the top, not as Uncheatable did.
- **Per-parameter grad norms mostly don't reproduce.** The same seed-0 runs match at the first step, but from step 10 on they differ by a median of 6–28% per logged step, close to the 10–20% across seeds. Only `output_proj` and the final norms reproduce well. These runs span three commits; same-commit reruns are untested.

Details and scripts: https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/main/qk-trial-noise

🤖 Proposed QK sweep for the 4K→16K switch, following @ClassicLarry's and @bethehand's comments above. Edited: arms now run 100 steps, as Larry first proposed, with an extra eval at step 50 so each arm keeps training after an eval, and the 4K control arm is dropped because neither its evals nor its batches match the 16K arms. Corrected: arms do not pass `--num-steps` (see below), and the per-arm time includes a cold compile. The code is on main: #9888, #9890, #10086 (`qk_mult_long_scale`, an extra multiplier on the global layers only), and #9689 (the production launcher's context history and trial flags). Decisions needed before launch are listed at the end.

**How the arms launch.** Every arm runs from one trial branch whose only change is the deploy edit: `HERO_MODEL.max_seq_len = 16384` and `qk_mult = 1.48` in `heuristic.py`, the 4K entry `HarrierContextPhase(end_step=N, seq_len=4096)` in `HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES`, and `HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL` set to the parent's `throughput/total_gflops` × 1e9 at W&B `_step` N−1. Arms then differ only in launcher flags. Every arm uses the `trigger_hero.sh` launcher arguments plus:

```
--initialize-from-checkpoint <handoff checkpoint at step N> --eval-every 50 [--qk-mult X] [--qk-mult-long-scale Y]
```

The arms do not pass `--num-steps`: in this launcher it sets the schedule length as well as the stop step, so it would change the learning rate, data stages, and FLOPs budget. Each arm keeps the 390251-step schedule and is cancelled once its N+100 eval has been logged.

**Wave 1: A1–A3.** Every arm restores the same permanent checkpoint and uses the same seed. Same-seed arms read the same batches, so their losses can be compared step by step: the seed-0 16K restores differ by an SD of 3–5e-4 per step, against 0.06 across seeds.

| Arm | Context | `--qk-mult` | `--qk-mult-long-scale` | Global / local QK |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | 16K | — | — | 1.48 / 1.48 (default) |
| A2 | 16K | 1.58 | — | 1.58 / 1.58 |
| A3 | 16K | 1.68 | — | 1.68 / 1.68 |

A2 and A3 bracket the all-layer value above the default: 1.58 is close to DeepSeek-V2's mscale coefficient (about 1.57) and 1.68 is the squared YaRN form.

**Possible follow-up waves**, decided after wave 1:

| Arm | Context | `--qk-mult` | `--qk-mult-long-scale` | Global / local QK |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | 16K | 1.3 | 1.1386 | 1.48 / 1.3 |
| G3 | 16K | 1.3 | 1.2964 | 1.68 / 1.3 |

- G1 and G3 scale only the global (full-causal, no-RoPE) layers. The local layers keep a 2048-token window at both lengths, so their number of keys per query grows by at most about 25% (fewer queries sit near a sequence start), against 4× for the global layers. On the 67B, a global-only arm did worse; that run started from 1.3 at 8K, so its arms sat at different values from these. They are most useful if a higher all-layer value wins in wave 1, to check whether the gain comes from the global layers alone.
- A second seed for A1 and the best other arm, if wave 1's differences are close to the noise bar (decision 2).

**Shared settings.**

- 100 steps per arm at the production schedule (390251 steps), tokens per update (4,194,304 per rack, batch 2816 at 16K), and gate/router weight decay 0.02. The optimizer config is identical at 4K and 16K.
- Eval every 50 steps, so at N+50 and N+100. Eval packs at the training context, 16K. The mid-run eval exercises eval followed by more training, including memory after the dropless 16K eval, which has not run on GPUs yet.
- One checkpoint save and resume in at least one 16K arm.
- Capacity factor 1.15 in every arm, from `HERO_MODEL`. Expert drops at 16K were 16× the 4K value on one rack (3.1e-3 against 1.9e-4 on the current stack); the sweep records them, and a capacity change would be a separate decision.

**Reading the results.** The default is 1.48 on all layers. Another arm replaces it only if it is better on both Uncheatable and the Paloma macro without PTB and WikiText at 16K packing, by a margin clearly above the noise, with no worse loss stability. bethehand's 2× pooled-SD bar is the guide, and the N+100 eval is the scoring point, since the arms are still converging at N+50; the final call is made by people, not by the rule. Also compare:

- step-by-step training loss against A1 on the shared batches;
- total grad norm, spikes, and loss stability over the 100 steps;
- per-parameter grad norms, only for parameters that reproduce across same-seed reruns (`output_proj` and the final norms), or for differences well above the 6–28% per-step rerun spread;
- expert drop fraction, tokens/s, and peak memory, which also set the rollback bands for the production run.

The hero's own steps before the handoff are the no-switch reference for loss stability, grad norm, drops, and throughput; a 4K arm would read different batches from the 16K arms, so its loss and evals would not line up with theirs either. A 4K-packed retention check of the 16K arms, since `qk_mult` changes the model at every length, needs a separate eval of each arm's final checkpoint; the launcher has no eval-only mode.

**Decisions needed**

1. **Racks.** On 11 racks (Larry's preference) each arm is about 22 minutes of training at 13–14 s/step, plus a 3–5 minute restore, a cold compile of about 30 minutes (the 16K executables and each `qk_mult` value are new to the compile cache), and two evals, so about 60–70 minutes per arm. Wave 1's three arms pause the hero for roughly 3–3.5 hours plus the hero's own restart, and each follow-up arm adds about an hour. On the one spare rack the hero keeps training, but each step has 11× fewer tokens, and the arms run one at a time.
2. **Noise bar.** With one seed per arm, the seed-to-seed SD of eval differences is not measured. Options: add a second seed for A1 and one other arm, or use the hero's eval-to-eval noise (SD of the change 0.0026 for the 14-subset Paloma macro, 0.0012 for Uncheatable).
3. **Handoff checkpoint.** It must be permanent and at a multiple of 50 steps, so the trial evals land at N+50 and N+100 (resumed runs skip the first-step eval). For the production switch, it should also sit a few hundred steps before a 3000-step eval boundary, so the first 16K eval comes soon after the deploy.
4. **Retention check.** Whether the 4K-packed eval of the 16K arms is worth adding eval-only tooling before the switch, or can be skipped given that the production run will train at 16K from here on.

Comment above shows the earlier results from the 67B run. Long only is slightly better on train loss- evals may have some noise. Will see what results are for long only qk mult 1.68 on hero, estimating that will look best.

@ClassicLarry @mcwitt Paired per step on the shared batches, the arms separate more clearly than the eval totals in #10101 do, and this supports keeping 1.48: A2 roughly ties it, while A0 and G3 are behind at every step after step 20.

- A0 (1.3): +0.0164 at step 0, before any update, then +0.0022 over steps 1–49, +0.0012 over 50–99 and +0.0009 over 100–107, still closing slowly. At N+100 it is worse on Uncheatable (+0.0009) and on 15 of the 16 Paloma subsets (all but gab).

- A2 (1.58): +0.0022 at step 0, closing to +0.0002 by step 10, then level (+0.00001 over steps 10–99; +0.0001 over 100–107).

For scale, the three same-seed 16K restores from step 180k that I compared above differ by under 0.0001 on average over steps 30–89, and are positive on 30–35 of those 60 steps; G3 is behind A1 on all 60.

On the hero, G3 and A1 were still level at step 19, where the 67B probe stopped, and the gap built up only from about step 25, so a 20-step run here would not have shown it. Later switches may need arms of 100 steps or more.

A2's +0.0012 at N+100 on the Paloma macro without PTB and WikiText is mostly twitterAAE; the other 13 subsets average +0.0002. Over the hero's last 30 evals before step 252k, twitterAAE accounts for 58% of that macro's eval-to-eval variance, so it may be worth reporting the macro without it as well.

topics.title: [grug] Switch the hero to 16K context with qk_mult 1.48
topics.body:
Switch the hero from 4K to 16K context with `qk_mult` 1.48 on all layers. The new run `hero-ctx16k-step257k` forks `hero-mfu30-step231k` at its permanent `step-257553`, where the parent stopped on 2026-10-13. Tokens per rack per update, the 390251-step schedule, and the optimizer stay the same, so the batch drops from 11264 to 2816 sequences on 11 racks.

`HERO_MODEL` gets `max_seq_len=16384` and `qk_mult=1.48`. `HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES` records the 4K phase ending at step 257553, and `HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL` is 1.7792877262736668e24, the parent's `throughput/total_gflops` × 1e9 at W&B `_step` 257552 (`global_step` 257552). `trigger_hero.sh` hands off from `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-mfu30-step231k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-257553` (permanent, `metadata.json` step 257553) and forks W&B at `hero-mfu30-step231k?_step=257552`; `current_run.py` names the child.

`build_ladder_run` now uses the checked-in history for d6144 by itself instead of relying on `main()`, and it refuses an explicit `num_steps` while a history is in effect, because the prior phases' data stages are rebuilt from the schedule length. The diagnostics launcher and restore benchmark take their default batch from the hero's tokens per rack at the model's context length (256 sequences per rack at 16K); the old fixed 1024-sequence default would have put four times the hero's load on a rack. `HERO_EP_BATCH_SIZE` is replaced by `HERO_TOKENS_PER_RACK` and `hero_rack_batch_size` in `hero_recipe.py`.

In 100-step arms at 16K from permanent `step-252000` on the 11 hero racks (#9615), the dropless eval loss after step 252100 was 1.81349 at `qk_mult` 1.3, 1.81156 at 1.48, 1.81200 at 1.58, and 1.81282 for 1.68 on the global layers only. The differences are within eval noise, so we keep the YaRN-style value 1.3 × (0.1·ln 4 + 1). topics.title: [levanter] Wrap cudnn-frontend's fused MXFP8 MoE kernels for JAX
topics.body:
Add JAX entry points in `levanter.grug._moe.mxfp8` for the fused MXFP8 MoE grouped-GEMM kernels in `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` 1.31.0, a new Linux-only dependency of levanter's `gpu` extra. Nothing calls them yet; #10415 wires them into the ragged expert-parallel backend behind `ExpertPrecision.MXFP8`, off by default.

MXFP8 stores E4M3 values with one power-of-two E8M0 scale per 32 elements, which Blackwell tensor cores apply inside the MMA at twice the bf16 rate. A GEMM needs its scale blocks along the axis it contracts over, so an activation is quantized along features for the forward and data-gradient GEMMs and along tokens for the weight gradients. Four kernels cover one SwiGLU expert MLP: the gate/up GEMM with a SwiGLU epilogue that quantizes its output along both axes, a plain grouped GEMM, the down-projection data gradient with a dSwiGLU epilogue that also returns the per-row routing-weight gradient, and the grouped weight gradient.

All four come from the package. The backward uses the unified dGLU kernel with `act_func="dswiglu"` and `deterministic=True`, which writes each 256-column tile's routing-gradient partial into its own slot; the JAX wrapper (`adapter.py`) sums the slots, so the gradient is bitwise deterministic. One change upstream lacks needs an override: `mxfp8/kernels/swiglu_forward_only.py` subclasses the dedicated SwiGLU kernel and copies its `__init__`, `__call__` and `kernel` from 1.31.0 to add a compile-time `forward_only` option, marked "Modified by Marin". With it set, the kernel skips the pre-activation and token-quantized outputs, which only a backward pass reads. That file is 1,945 of this PR's 4,342 added lines. NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1759 asks upstream where they would take this option.

The pin is exact because the override copies private methods. 1.31.0 is also the first release whose weight-gradient kernel acquires its online TMA descriptors before using them. Without that, CUDA-graph replays read a stale descriptor when XLA gives both weight-gradient calls the same workspace, and returned a partly NaN gradient; a replay test in #10415 fails with the acquire removed and passes with it. `uv.lock` gains only the package itself: its dependencies, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.6.2 and `apache-tvm-ffi`, were already locked. `cutlass_kernel_cache.cutlass_call` gains an optional `input_output_aliases` argument, which the dGLU call uses to accumulate into a zeroed slot buffer; existing callers are unchanged.

The JAX wrapper launches every kernel through `cutlass_kernel_cache`, as the existing bf16 QuACK kernels do. `triton_quant.py` builds both MXFP8 copies of an activation and their swizzled scale layouts in one pass. Its output is bitwise equal to the pure-JAX reference in `quantize.py`, which XLA runs as several passes; at the shape below the Triton kernel takes 0.80 ms and the reference 5.14 ms.

The measurements use one B200 and one sequential expert chunk of the EP hero run on one GPU: 3 experts, 302,336 rows, hidden size H and expert width I both 3072. Every kernel output is within 1e-3 (GEMMs) or 2e-3 (quantized outputs, weight gradients) relative Frobenius error of f32 matmuls on the dequantized operands it consumed. That bounds the kernels' own error, separate from MXFP8 rounding of their inputs. Reruns are bitwise identical, and an expert without rows gets an exactly zero weight gradient. Against a copy of the same kernels from cudnn-frontend commit 3041f3e8, which mcwitt's research branch (c3cb334f8e) used, every output is bitwise equal except the routing gradient, whose slots are summed in a different order (about 1e-7 relative). The six kernel calls of one forward and backward (gate/up GEMM, down GEMM, dSwiGLU data gradient, gate/up data gradient, two weight gradients) took a median 24.2-24.8 ms across balanced, skewed and one-empty-expert routings, against 41.5 ms for the bf16 QuACK kernels, with inputs already quantized and the legacy dSwiGLU kernel's packed epilogue; the dGLU backward used now took 3.99 ms in one run, against 3.91 ms for the legacy kernel's scalar epilogue and 4.52 ms for its packed one. The GPU tests skip without an SM100 GPU; they passed on a Modal B200.

Part of #6699.

topics.title: [grug] Add a ring_filtered expert-parallel MoE backend
topics.body:
Adds `ring_filtered`, an opt-in expert-parallel MoE backend (`moe_implementation="ring_filtered"`). It sends each token only to the GPUs that own its experts, where `ring` sends every token to every GPU. On 8x MI355X with `save_moe` remat, it cuts the June 67B-A2B step from 1.575 s to 1.484 s (13.2% → 14.0% MFU). With `recompute_all` it runs at about the same speed as `ring_gather_combine` there. It is also faster on H100, but slower on TPU, so TPU should stay on `ring`. Against `ragged_all_to_all`, the existing backend that also sends tokens only where their experts are, it ties on MI355X and is 2-4% faster on H100.

`ring` all-gathers every token to every GPU, and every GPU sends back a full-size output that gets summed with `psum_scatter`. With top-4 of 256 experts on 8 GPUs, a token's experts sit on 3.3 GPUs on average, so most of what `ring` moves is never used.

`ring_filtered` does this instead:

1. Each GPU sends each token once to each GPU that owns at least one of its experts, with an `all_to_all`. A second, small `all_to_all` carries the router weights and expert ids.
2. The receiving GPU runs its experts and sums each token's expert outputs, weighted by the router, into one row.
3. A third `all_to_all` sends each row back to where it came from.
4. The token's home GPU adds up the rows it gets back.

Example with 4 GPUs, 2 experts each, top-2, 4 tokens per GPU, and 2 slots per destination:

```
GPU g owns experts E(2g) and E(2g+1). GPU 0's tokens and the experts the router picked:
  a: E2 E3    b: E0 E6    c: E1 E5    d: E3 E7

What GPU 0 sends               to GPU 0   to GPU 1   to GPU 2   to GPU 3
  ring        every token      a b c d    a b c d    a b c d    a b c d    16 rows, 7 used
  ring_filtered  C = 2 per block  b c        a d        c .        b d         8 rows, 7 used
                                                     (. = padding)

On GPU 1 (E2, E3), ring_filtered
  receives one block per GPU  from 0: a d   from 1: f h   from 2: j .   from 3: m o
  groups the rows by expert   E2: a f j o   E3: a d h m
  sums each row's outputs     a' = w(a,E2)*E2(a) + w(a,E3)*E3(a)
  sends rows back             block "from 0" (a' d') goes back to GPU 0

GPU 0 adds the rows that came back for each token:
  a' = from GPU 1    b' = from GPU 0 + 3    c' = from GPU 0 + 2    d' = from GPU 1 + 3
```

At batch 64 each collective moves 537 MB per GPU, against 1,174 MB for `ring`. The expert MLP is the same as `ring`'s: same capacity rule, same `_select_local_assignments` (#9928) and `ragged_dot`. Rows are moved with `ring`'s gather helpers from #9860, so there is no hidden-width scatter-add in the forward or backward pass. `_combine_gather_sum` moves from the pooled-wave backend into `ep_common.py` so both backends can share it.

The new setting is the sender capacity. `all_to_all` needs fixed-size buffers, so each GPU gets a fixed number of slots per destination: `pooled_transport_capacity_factor` times the number of tokens it would send there under uniform routing. This reuses the existing `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` setting, and `moe_mlp` raises if it is unset.

If more tokens want a GPU than there are slots, the extra tokens lose their experts on that GPU, even if those experts have spare capacity. We call these sender drops. `ring` cannot drop tokens this way. We used 1.1, which gave no sender drops on the June benchmark or with uniform routing. Routing that piles onto one GPU may need a higher value. The full-model drop rate on MI350X is 1.00-1.12%, against 0.93-0.99% for `ring`.

Each row compares `ring_filtered` with the platform's default backend: `ring_gather_combine` on GPUs and `ring` on TPU.

| Hardware | Workload | Remat | Default | ring_filtered | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8x MI355X | June model | `save_moe` | 1.575 s | 1.484 s | -5.8% |
| 8x MI355X | June model | `recompute_all` | 1.589 s | 1.582 s | -0.4% |
| 8x MI350X | June model | `save_moe` | 1.730 s | 1.580 s | -8.7% |
| 8x MI350X | June model | `recompute_all` | 1.798 s | 1.688 s | -6.1% |
| 8x H100 | 4-layer model | `save_moe` | 0.588 s | 0.565 s | -4.0% |
| 8x H100 | 4-layer model | `recompute_all` | 0.611 s | 0.577 s | -5.6% |
| 8x H100 | one MoE layer | | 33.4 ms | 25.6-26.1 ms | -22% to -23% |
| TPU v5p-16 | 4-layer model | `save_moe` | 1.043 s | 1.220 s | +17% |
| TPU v5p-16 | 4-layer model | `recompute_all` | 1.118 s | 1.322 s | +18% |
| TPU v5p-16 | one MoE layer | | 109.9 ms | 131.6 ms | +20% |
| TPU v6e-8 | one MoE layer | | 106.0 ms | 182.7 ms | +72% |

The June model and 4-layer rows use batch 64 and report the median of steps 2-19. The 4-layer model is the June model cut down to fit in memory. The one-layer rows time forward and backward at the batch-64 shapes with uniform routing, median of 20 calls.

On MI355X, both backends ran on the same node with `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` attention (Vultr jobs 11698 and 11699). The H100 4-layer rows ran in one job on CoreWeave `cw-rno2a` with `xla_flash` attention (Iris job `/dev/bridge-cse-018ox-h100-filtered-vs-ragged`). We have not profiled why `recompute_all` gains so little there.

On MI350X (jobs 454012 / 454021 and 454022 / 454026), the default backend also had the ROCm top-k change from #9889, which was not merged. One `ring_filtered` run (454010) ran out of memory at step 5 because of allocator fragmentation. Its retry passed, and #9901 fixes the fragmentation.

Losses match to 5 decimals in the TPU pairs, to within 2e-5 on H100 and to within 3e-4 on MI355X. We have not profiled the TPU slowdown.

`ragged_all_to_all` also sends each token only to the GPUs that own its experts, but as one row per (token, expert) pair, sized exactly with a ragged all-to-all, so it has no padding and no sender drops. Same setups as above:

| Hardware | Workload | Remat | ragged_all_to_all | ring_filtered | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8x MI355X | June model | `recompute_all` | 1.583 s | 1.580 s | -0.2% |
| 8x MI355X | June model | `save_moe` | 1.579 s | 1.489 s | -5.7% |
| 8x H100 | 4-layer model | `recompute_all` | 0.590 s | 0.577 s | -2.2% |
| 8x H100 | 4-layer model | `save_moe` | 0.590 s | 0.565 s | -4.2% |

The MI355X rows ran both backends on the same node (Vultr jobs 11700 and 11701). The H100 `ragged_all_to_all` runs were a separate job on the same cluster (`/dev/bridge-cse-018ox-h100-ragged-untagged`).

The `save_moe` rows overstate the gap. `ragged_all_to_all` tags none of its tensors for `save_moe`, so it recomputes everything under that setting, and its two remat rows are the same speed. An experiment outside this PR tagged them: `ragged_all_to_all` then matched `ring_filtered` on MI355X (1.476 s against 1.482 s, same node, job 11706) and reached 0.582 s on H100, still behind. That version also hit a non-finite loss at step 5 in one of two H100 runs, so it is not ready to ship.

On the JAX 0.11.0 ROCm stack these runs used, `ragged_all_to_all` fails unless `--xla_gpu_experimental_ragged_all_to_all_use_barrier_with_nccl=false` is set. With JAX 0.11.1 and the 0.11.1 ROCm plugin it runs without the flag at the same speed (job 11709).

Correctness checks:

- CPU, f32, 8 shards: outputs and all four gradients match a dense reference to 1e-5, including with sender drops, receiver drops, uneven padding and an all-padding batch. They match `ring` whenever nothing is sender-dropped.
- One full-size layer on 8x H100, against f32 `ring`: outputs and gradients are within 0.47-0.52%. bf16 `ring` is within 0.50-0.57%, except for the routing-weight gradient at 5.75%, because `ring` casts the routing weights to bf16 and `ring_filtered` keeps them in f32.

Part of #9812

comments.body: 🤖 Restacked: the ring helper refactor moved to #9928, and this PR's base is now that branch. I merged #9928's branch into this one with a merge commit (no force-push). The diff now has only the ring_dedup additions. Merge order: #9860, #9928, then this PR.

🤖 Holistic review of fd57d1a21b1004119c78b9cc0f04b90b10eff051.

Adds an opt-in `ring_dedup` expert-parallel backend that sends each token once per destination shard through a fixed-capacity `all_to_all`, reusing ring's capacity rule, `_select_local_assignments`, `_dispatch_rows` and `_combine_rows`. The data flow checks out end to end (sentinels, inverse maps, the trailer-row demand sum, f32 routing-weight gradient), the enum and dispatch wiring are complete, and the nine ring_dedup-selected tests pass locally in 30 s on CPU. Nothing blocks. The performance and drop-rate claims rest on the cited job ids; no default changes depend on them. The findings are one duplicated helper and one requirement the validation sites outside the diff do not know about.

**Blockers**

None.

**Should fix**
1. `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring_dedup.py:50` `_weighted_gather_sum_rows` and its fwd/bwd (lines 43-91) duplicate `ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all._combine_gather_sum` (lines 69-141): the same `out[n] = sum_j w[n, j] * src[idx[n, j]]`, the same residuals (`flat_idx` is the pooled-wave's `assignment_sources`), the same gather backward for `src` and f32 weight gradient. The copy also lacks the pooled-wave's `sonic_gather_sum_masked` path, so on NVIDIA the expert-side combine runs the XLA loop where the pooled-wave runs the fused kernel. Lift `_combine_gather_sum` into `ep_common.py` (which already hosts `_sort_activations_custom`) with an `output_dtype` parameter (pooled-wave returns f32; ring_dedup needs the row dtype before its return `all_to_all`), derive `keep` from in-range positions as `sonic_gather_sum_masked` already does, and call it from both backends. `test_ring_dedup_expert_combine_keeps_bf16_sums_in_float32` then covers the shared helper. The body's "every hidden-width movement is a gather through ring's `_dispatch_rows` and `_combine_rows`" describes this combine inaccurately; it goes through the new custom_vjp.
2. `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py:583` is the second copy of the `pooled_transport_capacity_factor is None` raise (line 594 is the first), and each caller that wants to fail fast now has to know the pair. Add `_TRANSPORT_CAPACITY_MOE_IMPLEMENTATIONS = ("ring_dedup", "fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all")` to `_moe/common.py` beside `_EP_MOE_IMPLEMENTATIONS`, check it once before the dispatch chain, and import it at the sites in item 3.
3. `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/model.py:116` says the factor is "required by `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` only"; that is now false, and this is the config the PR's benchmarks ran through. `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py:196` fails fast only for `POOLED_WAVE_MOE_IMPL`, so `--moe-impl ring_dedup` without `--pooled-transport-capacity-factor` dies at the first-step trace after the full model state is built, which that check exists to prevent. `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py:326` has the same pooled-only check. `lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py:231` lets `SnowballConfig` select `ring_dedup` but has no field to pass the factor, so the selection always raises. Replace the string compares with membership in the item-2 tuple and fix the docstring.

**Tests to drop**

None. The 8-shard test's dense reference is independent and the drop expectations follow from the stated capacity rules.

**Related PRs**
4. #9942 (routing top-k import in `grug_moe.py`, test helpers), #9718 (`QBRoutedMoE` bias, new tests) and #9867 (`tpu` markers in `test_grugformer_moe.py`) edit the same files in unrelated regions. None deletes or duplicates this change; any merge order works, with an import-block conflict against #9942 only.

On JAX 0.11.0 ROCm, the barrier flag workaround works, and with JAX 0.11.1 plus the 0.11.1 ROCm plugin it runs without the flag at the same speed. So your read of the XLA change was right.
On MI355X it ties ring_filtered once it’s compared fairly. ragged_all_to_all doesn’t tag anything for save_moe, so its save_moe runs were really recomputing everything. Tagging its residuals (which needed optimize_remat=False on _routed_experts, since names inside the fwd rule aren’t visible to the outer policy) brought it to 1.476 s against 1.482 s for ring_filtered on the same node.
On 8x H100 (4-layer June model), ring_filtered is still 2-4% faster: 0.577 s vs 0.590 s with recompute_all, and 0.565 s vs 0.590 s with save_moe. The tagged ragged_all_to_all reached 0.582 s, but hit a non-finite loss at step 5 in one of two runs, so I’m not proposing that change yet.
With the stacked follow-ups (#10343, #10345, #10346), ring_filtered pulls ahead on AMD too: on 8x MI355X at batch 128 with save_moe, 2.63 s vs 2.79 s for tagged ragged_all_to_all (-5.5%, three same-node pairs on two nodes, same memory and loss). ring_gather_combine runs out of memory at that batch size.

We’ve added the batch-64 numbers to the PR description.

topics.title: [skyrl] Save the interference checkpoint schedule and export FP32 masters as HF
topics.body:
Save the interference experiment's checkpoint schedule and export its fp32 master weights as HF models.

`trainer.checkpoint_steps` lists the weight-checkpoint steps, and `trainer.optimizer_checkpoint_steps` lists the subset that keeps full optimizer state. The optimizer list must be a subset of the checkpoint list. Combining the explicit list with YAML checkpoint callbacks raises, rather than one being ignored. At the other listed steps the policy worker saves a masters-only checkpoint: the optimizer filter matches records by their `ShardedTensor.key` and keeps model records and fp32 masters while dropping moments. Masters-only saves require `optimizer_checkpoint_sharding_type: fully_reshardable`, the only format where masters and moments are separate records. A marker file records each checkpoint's optimizer state, and resuming from a masters-only checkpoint raises instead of restarting Adam with fresh moments.

`save_fp32_master_hf_model` exports a checkpoint's fp32 masters for weight analysis. Each rank loads its own master slices through the model's sharded state dict, swaps them into the live parameters for one Bridge export at `weight_dtype=float32`, and restores the weights. The export has the same HF names and layout as `save_hf_model`, with master values. A parameter without an fp32 master record raises, so a bf16-only checkpoint cannot export as fp32. Local checkpoints are read in place; S3 checkpoints stream rank tensors directly.

The GPU gate passed on a CoreWeave H100 node (`/benfeuer/wp2-fp32-export-gate-10`). It takes one Adam step on tiny Grug, saves a masters-only checkpoint, and requires three things:
- the fp32 export rounds exactly to the bf16 HF export;
- it differs from the upcast bf16 somewhere;
- its embedding equals the checkpoint's master record.

CPU tests cover schedule validation, resume guards and the masters-only filter.

Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment (CL8).

```markdown
The interference experiment's checkpoint schedule — fp32 master weights every

Weight checkpoints follow the explicit list when one is set, otherwise the
interval. Checkpoints outside the optimizer list keep the model records and
the fp32 master params but drop the moment states through a recursive filter
over the optimizer's sharded state, and rank zero writes an
`optimizer_state.json` marker per checkpoint. Resume from latest fails with a

Schedule resolution, the callback's list mode, and the masters-only filter

Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment (CL8).

```

topics.title: SWE-smith Harbor packages expose the fix through git history in the agent container
topics.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

🤖 A fresh GLM 5.3 trial on the raw package used the history to check its fix.

**Setup:** `swesmith-00003` from `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (revision 78b0d879), unchanged. Harbor at `marin-community/harbor@016dd78b`, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 with a 32k context, Daytona sandbox, GLM 5.3 through the internal bulk service. The trial passed (reward 1, 16 model calls).

**History use in the trajectory:**
- Step 6: `git log --oneline -5 && git status` showed `Remove F2P Tests` / `Bug Patch` / `Initial commit`.
- Step 8: `git log --all --oneline -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && git show 614b134:oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py`. The second command prints the pre-bug file (`614b134` is `Initial commit`).
- Step 17: `git diff 614b134 -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && echo "IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL"` printed `IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL`. The agent confirmed that its edit matches the original file before submitting.

GLM made the edit itself at step 10, after reading the original file at step 8. So this pass is history-assisted, and a GLM pass rate on these packages would be inflated in the same way as the Kimi data.

**Visibility probe:** an oracle-agent probe printed the container state during the agent phase (no model calls).
- `/testbed`: 944 branches (`main`, the task branch, `remotes/origin/*` for every task), and `git log --all` lists every task's `Bug Patch` / `Remove F2P Tests` commits.
- `/tests`: absent.
- `/solution`: absent for model agents. Harbor uploads it only for the oracle agent.
- None of the other task files are present (`task.json`, `test_*_state.py`, `setup.sh`, `container.def`, `test_state.py`).

**Run folders:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/swe-dry3` (trajectory: `swesmith-00003__LQ7xGdF/attempts/000/agent/trajectory.json`) and `.../dryrun/visibility1`.

**Consequence for the SFT-shootout teacher pilot (#10213):** the SWE-smith 200x2 pass-rate pilot will run only on the history-stripped packages.

🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|

topics.title: [skyrl] Add a fixed-dataset trajectory runner for SFT
topics.body:
Add a fixed-completion trajectory runner so SkyRL can train SFT on pre-generated expert rows (M1) under the same trainer, budget and response caps as on-policy distillation (M4).

Rows come in two formats. Text rows carry a message-list prompt and completion text, and they must end with the tokenizer's EOS. Tokenized rows carry a whole conversation with assistant masks, so reasoning and tool observations keep their exact tokens. Every row needs a non-empty `data_source`; joint runs also carry a `teacher_route`. A row over its prompt or response cap raises at load rather than being dropped, so the rows consumed match the data manifest.

Rows spanning more than one `teacher_route` require `data.sampling.kind=domain-weighted`, so every `train_batch_size` window holds the configured rows per route, as M4's prompt order does. The validator rejects other sampling kinds and positive staleness, so a batch is exactly one window. `generator.max_generate_length_by_data_source` sets per-task response caps, which the dataset filter, the runner and rollout requests all read, so a joint X+R run keeps each task's cap. It cannot be combined with Harbor tasks or trajectory reward shaping, which read only the global cap.

`TrainingBudget` is what one optimizer step consumes: sequences per step and per mini-batch, input cap, and per-task response caps. `validate_objective` resolves and logs it. A test composes the Snowball MOPD smoke recipe and an M1 recipe through the Iris launcher. The two budgets agree only when M1 trains rollouts-per-prompt times as many rows per step.

`SeededPasses` now seeds each pass from a hash of (seed, epoch); `seed + epoch` made seed s's second pass replay seed s+1's first. This changes data order for every run using seeded passes.

The NLL test checks the padded training loss, gradients and one AdamW step on a tiny Qwen3 against per-row unpadded forwards. No GPU or end-to-end trainer run has been done.

Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment (CL1).

topics.title: [taskforge] Add validation trials, failure classifier and control replay
topics.body:
Add `stage50_validate`, which runs a built task's trials and replays its fixed controls. `lowering.lower` lowers a draft's task for the validating host, with machine startup deadlines that outlast the Iris factory's scheduling budget so a sandbox that never starts is the factory's typed timeout. `control_drafts.write_controls` asks the model for a round's fixed controls and checks them against the grader step's reference answer and rejection ceiling, refusing a control that submits the same reply and files as a candidate the grader step already graded, since controls are written, not fitted to the grader.

Before trials, `preflight` probes a grader-base task machine on the local backend once and moves it to the container backend if its setup fails there, because a setup command can write where the local backend cannot and only running it shows that. `trials.run_trials` runs k trials of a `TaskRolloutSpec` on one RolloutEngine (`EngineSettings.engine`) under the messages trace. Each trial is `Graded` or `Ungraded` with one typed `Cause` from `classify.classify`, the only failure classifier, and a retryable cause triggers another attempt. `evidence` totals graded trials, and `controls.replay` replays each control as a `CONTROL` trial.

`round.validate_round(draft, context, solver_model, controls_model, adversary_model)` runs one validation round as a graph of units: lowering and control writing start together, each solver trial starts once the task is lowered, and each control replay and adversary trial once the lowering and the controls both exist. Each unit is idempotent on its own file, keyed by the draft's digest, the lowered spec's `task_digest` and, for replays, the control set's digest, so a relaunch runs only the missing units and no file of another draft, lowering or control set counts as done. `validation.json` holds every decision input without the rollouts. An adversary trial (`adversary.run_adversary_trial`, `AdversaryPolicy`) red-teams the grader with a shell on a private task machine and a `submit` graded as a control is; the round records each submission's grade, and judging whether a pass is a shortcut is left to review.

The coordinator's validate step now passes the round's context (workpiece, round, round dir, the proposal the round built, its MODIFY rounds left and its validation pass) and gets a `ValidationResult` back, and review gets that result and a `ReviewContext`. `stage60_review.rules.default_review` is the default rule table: a host refusal of the lowering rejects; a violated control sends the program back (`Modify`) while a MODIFY round is left and rejects otherwise; incomplete evidence retries; otherwise the solve rate decides against the caller's band. A violated control with a MODIFY round left decides the round early and cancels its outstanding solver and adversary trials, which leave no partial attempt files. A review `Retry`, and a relaunch of an abandoned workpiece, rerun exactly the trials left ungraded for a retryable cause, each with a fresh retry budget.

The standard template's end-to-end test now lowers its built task and runs it through RolloutEngine, and the infrastructure test checks the validation deadlines; both assertions were held back from #10298.

Builds on #10298; #10301 builds on it.

---

```markdown
Add `stage50_validate`. `lowering.lower` lowers a draft's task for the validating host. `control_drafts.write_controls` asks the model for a round's fixed controls and checks them against the grader step's reference answer and rejection ceiling. `preflight` probes a grader-base task machine on the local backend once and moves it to the container backend when its setup fails there. `trials.run_trials` runs k trials of a lowered task through RolloutEngine under the messages trace, each `Graded` or `Ungraded` with one typed `Cause` from `classify.classify`, the only failure classifier, and attempts a trial again for a retryable cause. `evidence` totals graded trials, and `controls.replay` replays each control as a `CONTROL` trial.

Builds on #10299; #10301 builds on it. The standard template's end-to-end test now lowers its built task and runs it through RolloutEngine, and the infrastructure test checks the validation verifier deadline; both assertions were held back from #10298. The taskforge suite passes 686 tests here (95 more than #10299).

```

</details>

🤖 Holistic review of a3a666b8 (reviewed at 4cd89e8d; the merge of #10298's new head since then leaves this PR's diff unchanged, and the line anchors below were re-checked at a3a666b8).

This PR adds `stage50_validate`. A draft's `TaskSpec` is lowered to a `TaskRolloutSpec` (`lowering.lower`), probed once on the local backend and moved to a container when its setup fails there (`preflight`), run k times on RolloutEngine with each attempt classified `Graded | Ungraded(Cause)` and retried for `RETRYABLE` causes (`trials.run_trial`, `classify`), replayed against model-written controls (`control_drafts.write_controls`, `controls.replay_control`) and totalled (`evidence.Evidence`). The last two commits also add `round.validate_round`, an idempotent file-backed graph of validation units, and `adversary.run_adversary_trial`, red-team agent trials. Nothing in-repo yet wires `validate_round` to `StageFunctions.validate`.

The unit suite is behaviour-focused (fake factories and models, atomic attempt files, relaunch and cancellation tests in `test_round.py`). Locally at head: 200 passed, 6 deselected (`test_live.py` under `live_glm`). The two assertions the body says were held back from #10298 do what it says: `test_standard.py:172-176` lowers the built task and runs it through `rollout_engine(...).run_task` asserting `(GRADED, 1.0)`, and `test_infrastructure.py:357-362` compares the new deadline constants to `SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT`. The Codex threads on the lowering startup timeout, the duplicate preflight deadline and the file-control comparison are fixed; finding 4 is a follow-on to the first of them.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker:** `stage50_validate/adversary.py:501` `trial_grade` turns a verifier that failed on the adversary's last submission (`_submission_grade` returning `GradeResult(UNAVAILABLE, ...)`) into `GradeResult(SUBMISSION_FAILURE, None, "the last verifier call failed")`, and `_agent_attempt` (`:692`) wraps that as `Graded` with reward 0. So `AdversaryResult.status == GRADED`, `cause is None`, and the attempt is not retried, while the same `GRADER_TIMEOUT` or `MACHINE_TERMINATED` on a solver trial is `Ungraded` and retried through `outcome.RETRYABLE`. A grader outage reads as "the adversary found no shortcut". Have `Verifier.submit` keep each submission's `Outcome`; when the chosen submission is `Ungraded`, return that `Ungraded` from `_agent_attempt` with its cause and retryability intact. Add a `test_round.py` case with a faulty verifier factory asserting `AdversaryResult.status == UNGRADED`.

- **2. Blocker:** The body and README say `classify.classify` is the only failure classifier. `adversary.py:134,632` `MACHINE_LOST_MESSAGES` and `_machine_lost` are byte-identical to `sandbox/host_failures.py:16,25` `MACHINE_LOSS_MESSAGE_PREFIXES` and `machine_lost`, whose docstring exists so that build and validation cannot drift, and `adversary.py:681` decides `Cause.ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT` itself before calling `classify`. Use `host_failures.machine_lost(error)` and route the deadline case through `classify` by raising `RolloutInterrupted(..., RolloutOperation.ATTEMPT)` as the engine does; `_interruption_cause` (`classify.py:180`) already maps it.

- **3. Should fix:** `round.py` (563 lines), `adversary.py` and `adversary_prompts.py` (840 lines) and `outcome.py` are in the diff and absent from the title and body. A reader of the body does not learn that 1,400 lines of adversary and round orchestration are here. Name them in the title and body, or split them into the next PR.

- **4. Should fix:** `stage50_validate/lowering.py:25,33,40` re-derive `STARTUP_TIMEOUT = SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT + GRADE_CANDIDATE_PREPARATION_TIMEOUT`, `VERIFIER_TIMEOUT = SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT + GRADER_TIMEOUT` and `TASK_MACHINE = draft.machine(startup_timeout=...)`, value-identical to `stage40_build_with_program/sandbox_effects.py:66,73` `GRADE_CANDIDATE_MACHINE` and `GRADE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_TIMEOUT`. Move the pair to `spec/draft.py` as the one machine-start and grading deadline that outlasts the factory's scheduling budget, and have both stages import it. The coupling to the Iris 600 s scheduling budget then lives in one place next to `SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT`.

- **5. Should fix:** Limits are set three times. `lowering.py:41` `LIMITS` are placeholders by their own comment; `trials.py:169` `Deadlines.apply` overwrites two `RolloutLimits` fields and `trials.py:123` `EngineSettings.apply` four more; `round._trial_digest`, `run_trial` (`trials.py:233`), `preflight._probe` and `run_adversary_trial` each re-apply both; and `preflight(task, host, factories, settings, deadlines)` receives `factories` twice (`round.py:322`, and again inside `settings`). Replace `Deadlines` plus the four limit fields of `EngineSettings` with one `limits: RolloutLimits` on `EngineSettings`, pass it to `lower(task, host, factories, limits)`, and delete both `apply` methods, `LIMITS`, `Deadlines` and the duplicate `factories` parameter. `ValidationContext` then carries `engine` alone.

- **6. Should fix:** `adversary.py:712` `run_adversary_trial` duplicates `trials.py:228` `run_trial` (the backoff copy, the retry counter, the `retryable`/`max_retries` loop) with a different attempt body, and `adversary.py:695` `_refused` duplicates the submission-refusal check at `trials.py:235-240`. Give `trials` one `run_attempts(plan, trial, attempt: Callable[[int, str], Awaitable[Outcome]]) -> Outcome` and one `refusal(spec, factories) -> Ungraded | None`; both trial kinds call them.

- **7. Should fix:** Three scripted models: `preflight.py:82 _ProbeModel`, `controls.py:38 ScriptedModel` and the pre-existing `sandbox_effects.py:122 _CandidateModel`. The probe is `ScriptedModel(({"role": "assistant", "content": ""},), context_assistant_turns(task))`. Delete `_ProbeModel`. To let stage40 share it too, move `ScriptedModel` to `spec/controls.py` (respecting stage import direction) and run `grade_candidate` under `TraceMode.MESSAGES`, which removes `_CandidateModel`'s made-up token ids.

- **8. Should fix:** Two definitions of "passed". `evidence.py:26` `_solved` accepts `reward >= score_max` or `isclose(..., rel_tol=1e-9)` because a grader that sums partial credits can land at 0.9999999999999999; `adversary.py:382` `passing` uses bare `>=`. The same honest full-credit submission is solved in `RewardStats` and `passed=False` in the adversary's `submit` observation and `SubmissionResult`, so the adversary is told its honest answer failed and `trial_grade` picks a different last passing submission. Export `_solved` as `evidence.passed(grade)` and use it in both.

- **9. Should fix:** `evidence.py:15,20` `Complete`/`Incomplete` wrap "is the Counter empty"; the only consumer, `round.py:514` `_solver_evidence`, immediately unwraps with `isinstance(status, Incomplete) ... else {}`, and `test_live.evidence_summary` does the same. Replace `Evidence.status` with `ungraded: Counter[Cause]`; emptiness is the status.

- **10. Should fix:** Backoff has two representations threaded through layers: `ValidationContext.retry_backoff: RetryBackoff` becomes `.schedule()` at `round.py:448`, then `TrialPlan.retry_backoff: ExponentialBackoff` is used as a template through `copy.copy` at `trials.py:242` and in `run_adversary_trial`. Hold `RetryBackoff` on `TrialPlan` and call `.schedule()` in the loop; delete the copies and the template docstring.

- **11. Drop test:** `tests/stage40_build_with_program/test_infrastructure.py:358,361-362` assert `VERIFIER_TIMEOUT >= SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT + GRADER_TIMEOUT` and `TASK_MACHINE.startup_timeout > SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT`, where both constants are defined as those sums (`lowering.py:25,33`); after finding 4 they are the stage40 constants already asserted on the preceding lines. Keep the pre-existing asserts and drop these.

Not flagged: `EngineSettings.engine()` builds a new `RolloutEngine` per trial and per probe despite the body's "one RolloutEngine"; `RolloutEngine.__init__` only stores three references, so this is cosmetic. No environment reads in stage50; new dataclasses force every field; `TASK_MACHINE`'s `MachineLimits()` leaves Iris memory at shellbox's 2048 MB default, the same as the build's grading machines.

topics.title: [iris] Finish the operator vocabulary and resource-model cleanup
topics.body:
Follow-on to #7543 and PR #7546. #7543 landed the incident-driven vertical slice — a read-only operator CLI without provider extras, `task`/`attempt describe`, and persisted per-attempt backend identity plus a bounded terminal reason, so a past failed-in-init attempt self-explains after its pod is gone. This issue tracks the rest of the uniform noun-verb vocabulary and the internal resource-model cleanup.

Design and rationale live in `.agents/projects/2026-07-23_iris_operator_vocabulary.md` on PR #7546, including the codex peer review (request-changes) folded into its "Peer review response" section. Delivery is one design, several PRs, incident slice first.

## Landed on PR #7546
- [x] Read-only operator CLI without `iris[controller]` (lazy `CloudK8sService`)
- [x] `task describe` / `attempt describe`
- [x] Persist per-attempt pod name/uid/node + bounded terminal reason (migration 0047)

## Part I — finish the CLI vocabulary
- [ ] `DescribeTask` RPC: live enrichment (phase, live init-container status, node) for a running or pending attempt, returning a typed partial-result so `GetTaskStatus` stays a cheap poll
- [ ] `spec` verb: `job spec` / `task spec` over `GetJobStatus.request`, presented as a sanitized submitted configuration (the request is redacted, so not a guaranteed re-runnable spec). Making it genuinely reproducible is a submission-model change designed in #7565 (secret + bundle references)
- [ ] `events` verb — blocked on the events design decision below
- [ ] `stop` rework — blocked on the stop design decision below
- [ ] Renames and matrix fill: `job summary`→`describe`, `cluster status`→`describe`, `slice`/`worker` promotion, `endpoints`→`endpoint`, `process` dissolution; prune the cells the review showed are unimplementable (actor list/describe/events, attempt profile, task/cluster spec)
- [ ] Package restructure: one module per noun over a shared render/targets layer
- [ ] Write the vocabulary into `lib/iris/OPS.md`; sweep skills and docs to the new verbs

## Part II — internal resource model
- [ ] Extract a minimal typed `ResourceKey` (plus `AttemptLocator`/`AttemptIdentity`); share the target/source/`JobName` parsing behind adapters. No full `ResourceRef` subsumption and no generic `List(kind, query)`.
- [ ] Mechanical renames (no behavior change): fold the `vm` proto noun into worker/slice; rename `platforms/vm_lifecycle.py` → `controller_lifecycle.py`; split the CLI grab-bags; align the controller-side stop vocabulary (`kick_tasks`/`terminate_job`/`Worker.KillTask`); make the shared CPU-sampling helper public; optionally split the 3.5k-line `service.py`
- [ ] Docstring sweep to the `reads.py` convention; drop `__all__` blocks that only mirror the import list
- [ ] Schema alignment (migration-gated, last): typed state adapters over an int→string migration; name the three event streams by role without renaming established namespaces; decide the free-floating ids (`backend_id`/`scale_group`/`user_id`/`cluster`) per coordinate; pick the `slice`↔`worker` denormalization direction after measuring real DBs

## Cross-cutting (thread through Parts I and II)
- [ ] Federation: a home cluster and, where different, an execution cluster on every ref and event; proxy to the authoritative peer or return a structured partial for describe/events/stop
- [ ] Authorization: per-resource tenant authz before any DB/finelog/backend read; redaction allowlists for event details and backend messages; principal identity on stop/audit events; terminal-control-character sanitization
- [ ] Versioning: proto field/RPC deploy order and capability detection; a precise replacement message for any removed command
- [ ] Performance/isolation: no per-task live GET in `job describe` unless requested; no event queries on the control thread; deadlines and backend rate limits on live describes

## Open design questions (block `events` and `stop`)
1. **events** — finelog namespace and durability contract (audit vs telemetry), the event schema (id, provenance, parent keys), retention, and drop/backpressure behavior.
2. **stop** — distinct domain verbs (`cancel`/`retry`/`terminate`/`delete`) versus one overloaded `stop`; asynchronous accepted-vs-completed semantics; an `attempt_uid` compare-and-stop to close the attempt-rollover race.

comments.body:

This is a multi-PR design effort ("one design, several PRs, incident slice first"), spanning the CLI vocabulary (Part I), the internal resource model (Part II), federation/authz/versioning cross-cuts, and two open design questions. It is well past the self-contained-fix bar, so I am not opening a PR — this comment records state and the next actionable slice for a human to green-light.

# Research
The prerequisite incident slice is still unmerged: PR #7546 (`weaver/issue-7543`) is OPEN, and `main` has none of it — no `DescribeTask` RPC, no `task`/`attempt describe`, no migration 0047. Every checkbox here is therefore blocked on #7546 landing first. The design doc + codex request-changes response live only on that branch (`.agents/projects/2026-07-23_iris_operator_vocabulary.md`).

**Relevant code (main, current state)**
- `lib/iris/src/iris/cli/task.py` — ~60 lines, no `describe` verb yet
- `lib/iris/src/iris/cli/{job,cluster,endpoints,process_status,actor}.py` — the grab-bags Part I/II split and rename
- no `DescribeTask`/`describe_task` in `lib/iris/src` (RPC not yet added)
- no `*0047*` migration on main

# Proposed sequencing
Follow the codex-accepted order in the design doc; do not fan out parallel PRs:

1. **Land #7546 first** — it carries the incident slice everything else builds on.
2. **`DescribeTask` live enrichment + `spec` verb** — unblocked, self-contained extensions of the landed slice; good next PR once #7546 merges.
3. **Renames + package restructure (one module per noun)** — mechanical, no behavior change; do after the RPCs settle so it moves stable code.
4. **`events`** — blocked. Resolve open question 1 (finelog namespace, audit-vs-telemetry durability contract, event schema/provenance, retention, drop/backpressure) before any code.
5. **`stop`** — blocked. Resolve open question 2 (distinct `cancel`/`retry`/`terminate`/`delete` verbs vs one `stop`; async accepted-vs-completed; `attempt_uid` compare-and-stop) before any code.

Part II schema alignment stays last (migration-gated), per the doc.

Recommendation: keep this issue as the tracker, split each numbered slice above into its own PR with `Part of #7560`, and answer the two design questions in-thread before starting `events`/`stop`.

topics.title: [post-training] Configure Stage 0 SFT on the shared template and one budget
topics.body:
Configure Stage 0 SFT for all four bases on the shared chat template and one training budget.

Snowball trains with Levanter on the converted Stage 0 artifact (#10525's converter), reading one `ArtifactDatasetSpec` per stage rather than raw Hugging Face datasets. It starts from the pinned 262k base. The resource request is 8 nodes of 8 H100s, matching both the mesh's 8-node context axis and #8225's 64 GPUs. Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3.5-MoE and Nemotron-H train through the Axolotl launcher (#10490). Each passes `shared_template(FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS[arch])`, and stages chain through `init_checkpoint` at the launcher's real output paths.

`budget.py` holds every #8225 hyperparameter once: Adam at 5e-6 with betas 0.9/0.95, cosine schedule, clip 1.0, no warmup, a global batch of 64 sequences of 32,768 tokens, and one epoch per source. Both trainers build their settings from it, and a test asserts the two resolve to the same budget. The router policy and gradient clip are required fields per architecture.

Stacked on #10490. Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment.

topics.title: [echo] Measure Echo's effect on agent sessions from local transcripts
topics.body:
Echo gives agents search across the wiki, repository files, pull requests, issues, and Discord. We do not know whether Echo makes agent sessions better or worse. `infra/echo/search_benchmark.py` scores retrieval relevance against graded judgments, but it does not measure the effect on the session that made the query.

Build an analysis that runs on a developer machine and reads local agent session transcripts. Central collection of sessions is not necessary. Claude Code writes JSONL transcripts to `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`. The transcripts record Echo calls as Bash tool calls to `infra/echo/cli.py`.

For each Echo call, an agent-based classifier gives one outcome:
- Helpful: the agent used a fact from the result, changed the plan, or did not do the same work again
- Neutral: the agent read the result and did not use it
- Harmful: the result was wrong or not current and the agent acted on it, or the search used turns and gave nothing

Report rates for each outcome, divided by Echo domain (wiki, files, pull requests, issues, discord) and by command (`search` or `get`). Keep the worst examples so that a person can review the classifier.

Done when:
- A script in `infra/echo/` reads local transcripts and emits one record for each Echo call
- The classifier gives helpful, neutral, or harmful with a short reason and the transcript turns that support it
- The script prints rates by domain and by command, and writes the records to a file
- A person reviews a sample of the labels, and the agreement rate is in the output
- The analysis runs on one machine, and it adds no central data collection

comments.body:
@yonromai had a very valid question about how do we plan to measure if Echo is helping or degrading our agent experience. This issue is one idea to try to answer that question.

CC: @rjpower
Sounds good to me, certainly better than my plan of "randomly assume it's working okay" model :) ...

topics.title: [taskforge] Add machine factories, task images and the image builder
topics.body:
Taskforge runs a task's machines on whichever host it is on, a laptop or an Iris task, and builds task images from Dockerfiles the model writes. This adds the `sandbox` package that the build and validation stages share for both.

`sandbox.factories` picks the shellbox machine factories per host: ShellSim and Docker on a laptop, ShellSim and gVisor on Iris, and the local backend for lock-only graders where bubblewrap works. A laptop whose Docker daemon is missing, unreachable or slower than the 20 s probe keeps ShellSim only. `task_refusals` asks each factory about the machines of a `TaskRolloutSpec` before a trial starts, so validation can record a typed refusal with the factory's message instead of failing inside a started trial. ShellSim gets the package catalog its CPython comes from.

`IrisImageBuilder` builds a `DockerBuild` with kaniko in one Iris CPU job and pushes it with `crane` in a second job, so the registry credential never shares a container with the model-authored Dockerfile. It returns the image pinned by manifest digest. The builder takes the credential at construction and reads no secret store, so it runs on a host without `gcloud` or Google credentials, such as a coordinator in an Iris task. Only the laptop helper `registry_credential_json` calls `gcloud`, and `scripts/build_image_job.py` uses it to run one build from a laptop. `sandbox.host_failures` holds the host-failure messages that both stages classify.

Builds on #10292; #10294 builds on it. The build stage (#10298) constructs the builder and classifies host failures, and validation (#10300) calls `task_refusals`. Two manual machine tests need `spec.draft` and land in #10294.

topics.title: [finelog] Bound cache warming and release readers during cleanup
topics.body:
Limit optional object-cache warming to immediately available download slots. Broad or cancelled queries previously left queued fills downloading and writing objects long after the request ended, competing with ingestion and repeatedly evicting cached data.

Release the shared query-visibility lock between batches of 16 cache removals, including object garbage collection. Keep each batch's write-lock guard inside its blocking task, which can continue after its caller is cancelled, so readers cannot overlap an unfinished unlink. Readers retain their existing protection against files disappearing during a scan.

One Marin hub log request spent 12.05 seconds waiting for this lock and 0.56 seconds querying. A cache sweep removed 28,535 files under one write lock. The change bounds concurrent cache warming and limits each cleanup lock acquisition to 16 removals without changing stored data, retention, or deployment resource limits. Incident: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/843.

topics.title: [taskcompendium] Start grading in the grader workspace
topics.body:
The grading machine now starts in the grader's workspace unless its environment specifies a `working_directory`. This restores the behavior before #10021 when the environment names no directory and preserves an explicit directory when it does.

Since #10021, every script-graded task has failed while creating its grading machine on Iris. `_grade_staged` previously passed `workdir=grading.workspace`; the move to `prepare_machine_spec` dropped that argument. When the grader environment names no directory, `prepare_machine_spec` retains the spec's workdir, which is empty for an image machine because `rolloutengine._machine_spec` leaves it empty. Docker interprets an empty workdir as the image's `WORKDIR`, so laptop grading continued to work. Iris instead runs `mkdir -p ""` and fails:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to create Iris workdir : mkdir: cannot create directory ''
```

The Taskforge ladder dry run on cw-rno2a hit this failure in every grader sandbox. Solver and control machines were unaffected because `draft.requirements` names `/workspace`.

A test checks the spec passed to the factory with and without an explicit `working_directory`; the grader-workspace case fails on main. The ShellSim-backed taskcompendium suite passed locally. The bubblewrap-backed tests require Linux, and CI runs the full suite.

---
