topics.title: [post-training] Offline binned sequence-KL estimator
topics.body:
The interference experiment needs an offline KL estimator. Every checkpoint of a run is scored teacher-forced on fixed token sequences against a reference model, using the reference's top-256 tokens at each position and a tail bin. The training-side teacher objectives contain this math behind distillation evidence plumbing that an offline analysis job reading stored scoring rows cannot construct.

Add `sequence_kl.py` to compute binned forward and reverse KL (KL(reference ‖ candidate) and KL(candidate ‖ reference), the design's two fidelity-loss forms) over stored top-K support and a tail bin. Apply the training-side tail-mass floor to both models' tails so forward KL stays finite when the candidate's tail rounds to zero. The estimator also provides exact full-vocabulary KL for the seeded subsample that bounds the estimator, the subsample mask, and a columnar row schema with sequence ID, position, token ID, both logprobs, KL, exact KL, and the WP8 token-type and position tag columns.

CPU checks show that identical models score zero in both directions, support spanning the vocabulary matches exact KL, the binned gap shrinks monotonically as K grows and falls below 1e-6 at K = V, and the tail floor keeps extreme cases finite.

The scoring passes that produce these rows run through mismatch_probe's frozen-sequence path on the Megatron/vLLM stack and belong to the GPU lane. They include the reference pass (top-K IDs, logprobs, tail mass, and per-(token, layer) routing capture), the candidate pass, and forced routing through the replay controller. The long-context limit measurement is also GPU-lane work. Those passes and the measurement are outside this PR; this estimator defines the contract for their rows.

Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment (CL14 estimator core; CL6/CL15 scoring passes follow on the GPU lane).

---

```markdown
forms) over a stored top-K support plus tail bin, with the training-side
tail-mass floor applied to both models' tails so the forward form cannot go
infinite when the candidate's tail rounds to zero; exact full-vocabulary KL
for the seeded subsample that bounds the estimator; the subsample mask; and
the columnar row schema (sequence id, position, token id, both logprobs,

gap shrinks monotonically as K grows and falls below 1e-6 at K = V, and the
tail floor keeps extreme cases finite.

Scoping note: the scoring passes that produce the rows — the reference pass
(top-K ids, logprobs, tail mass, per-(token, layer) routing capture), the
candidate pass, and forced routing through the replay controller — run
through mismatch_probe's frozen-sequence path on the Megatron/vLLM stack and
are GPU-lane work, as is the long-context limit measurement. They are not in
this PR. The estimator here is the contract those passes write against.

Part of the Phase 0/1a work for the OPD-SFT controls experiment (CL14
estimator core; CL6/CL15 scoring passes follow on the GPU lane).

```

</details>

🤖 Applied the WP4 review (e39a1f166b).

**Blocker — direction removed.** `binned_kl(support_logprobs, scored_support_logprobs)` takes one model's stored top-K as the support and the other model's logprobs gathered on those ids. Forward KL(reference ‖ candidate) passes the reference's rows; the reverse form is the role swap — the candidate's top-K and tail are the support and the reference is gathered on those ids. **No tail is floored anywhere**: the old reverse form scored a support tail floored at 1e-12, so a candidate tail of 0.01 added ~0.23 nats set by the floor.

**Required items.**
- Both retained log masses derive on device from the stored top-K logprobs (float64 `logsumexp`), never passed separately, so a tail cannot disagree with its support; a peaked model keeps its true near-zero tail instead of fp32 `1 - sum(exp)` noise. Inputs summing past one raise.
- `exact_kl` is split from `binned_kl` and asserts a normalized full vocabulary; `binned_kl` owns the tail bin.
- `SequenceKLRow` gains `candidate_step`, `reference_id`, `probe_hash`, `top_k`, `reference_tail_mass`, `candidate_tail_mass`, and `form` (a `KLForm` StrEnum); the WP8 tags are required — `token_type_tag` is typed by a `ProbeBucket` StrEnum mirroring WP8's `probe_sets/buckets.py` values (`reasoning`, `tool_name`, `tool_arguments`, `final_message`, from the WP8 branch since #10511 isn't mergeable here), and `position_tag` is WP8's turn index.
- The subsample mask covers scored positions only, drops the biasing at-least-one backfill (an empty draw is a valid, unbiased outcome), and its seed comes from `request_seed(master_seed, f"{probe_hash}:exact-subsample", 0)`.
- The engine/dtype/kernel-matching and pre-registered B-vs-B rescoring-floor requirement is recorded as the row contract in the module docstring; the scoring passes themselves remain GPU-lane work as the PR describes.

**Location note.** The estimator moved from `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/sequence_kl.py` to `experiments/post_training/mismatch_probe/sequence_kl.py` (tests alongside): it is offline analysis for rows the Marin tree owns, the vendored fork is excluded from Marin lint/types, `skyrl_train` is not importable from the Marin environment, and vendor code could never import the WP8 enum the tags require. `request_seed` is mirrored byte-identically in `experiments/post_training/mismatch_probe/protocol.py` with a comment naming the vendored `mismatch_probe/protocol.py` as canonical — flagging that in case the stacking pass wants a single definition.

**Tests** (`experiments/post_training/mismatch_probe/test_sequence_kl.py`, CPU, 13 passing): identical models score zero; a support spanning the vocabulary matches exact KL on exactly-representable (powers-of-two) vectors; forward and reverse gaps shrink monotonically against exact computations and each binned value is a lower bound on its exact divergence; a 1e-13 tail keeps its own mass with no floor; a peaked scored model gets an honest infinite forward KL and finite role-swapped KL; sum-past-one inputs raise; the subsample equals its raw seeded draws. The two slop tests and the never-activating floor test are gone; mutation-checking the suite against a re-introduced 1e-12 floor fails 3 tests, so the no-floor behavior is actually pinned. WP4's DESIGN.md/decision-log entries are left to the spec-docs pass.

topics.title: Record and display resource usage
topics.body:
For research / sharing purposes (e.g. how much does it cost to train? What do you really need for each stage?) and to help us steward our limited and disparate resource, it would be valuable if we could monitor the resources we use in the course of our training and evaluation. 

Notably, this would be cluster resources (compute, network, storage, etc), container (e.g. Daytona),  and even API (e.g. Together). 

Baseline assumption is that we'd use FineLog to record, and build a simple dashboard for (admin) users to track. Integration with Discord / Slack for alerting and reporting would be additionally helpful. 

# Definition of done
This requires some more thinking, but roughly:
* An API for recording resource usage (for any given resource), assigned to jobs and users
* Indefinite persistence of these logs (perhaps compacted)
* A dashboard to see this usage (likely auth-gated)
* Stretch: some connection to post to Discord and/or Slack

# Related issues
- If Together had a billing API… https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6581

topics.title: [tpu] Step12 TPU serving diverges from H100 past the 2048-token sliding window
topics.body:
On TPU, Snowball Step12 assigns different next-token log probabilities than H100 from token position 2048 onward. Up to position 2047 the two platforms agree to within TPU run-to-run noise. Step12 uses `sliding_window = 2048` with `global_every = 4`, so three of every four attention layers attend only to the last 2048 tokens. The divergence starts at that window size.

Impact: MATH500 on the same model, revision and Evalchemy commit scores 0.944 and 0.950 on H100 and 0.878, 0.882 (v6e-8, TP8) and 0.884 (v5p-8, TP4) on TPU. 39 items are correct on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU; 22 of them are long answers that drift to a different question.

Measurement: teacher-forced log probabilities of the same 10 texts on each platform (rendered Step12 chat prefix plus an H100-generated, H100-correct MATH500 completion; vLLM `/v1/completions` with `echo`, `logprobs=1`, `max_tokens=0`, concurrency 1). 35,801 scored positions; token ids are identical on both platforms.

| Positions | H100 vs TPU mean \|Δlogprob\| | top-1 token differs | TPU concurrency 1 vs 10 mean \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.010–0.019 | 0.8–1.0% | 0.012–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.026 | 1.6% | – |
| 2368–2559 | 0.066 | 3.1–3.3% | – |
| 2048–3071 | 0.063 | 3.6% | 0.014 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.142 | 6.8% | 0.018 |

Pooled over all positions: mean \|Δ\| 0.056 (TPU self-noise 0.014), maximum 12.3 (TPU self-noise 1.1), top-1 differs at 2.8% of positions (TPU self-noise 0.86%). TPU's mean per-token negative log likelihood is higher on all 10 items.

The per-element window mask agrees across the three stacks. Each keeps the last W tokens including the query token:
- training: [`levanter/grug/attention/_core.py` L126](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py#L123-L126), `k >= q - (W - 1)`;
- H100 vLLM fork: [`grugmoe.py` L957-L964](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py#L957-L964) passes `per_layer_sliding_window=2048` on local layers;
- TPU: [`grugmoe.py` L786](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L776-L787) passes the window as `attention_chunk_size`, which [`attention_interface.py` L496](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L494-L498) forwards as `sliding_window`; the RPA v3 kernel masks with [`q < k + W` at L494](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494).

The cause is not confirmed. Two unverified suspects on the TPU path:
- the RPA v3 sliding-window block skipping, which computes the first KV block to read from `kv_q_gap - sliding_window` ([kernel.py L388-L399](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399), [L916-L942](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942));
- KV-cache handling for the sliding-window layers.

Reproduce:
1. Serve `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` at revision `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`, bf16. TPU: v6e-8, TP8, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d`, vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`. H100: H100x8, DP8 with expert parallelism, Marin vLLM fork build `01911be34fac`.
2. Run `python teacher_forced_logprobs.py --endpoint URL --model open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 --items teacher_forced_items.json --output DIR --concurrency 1` against each server. The client and items (sha256 `9d4779361b79259d36dcd2402d6fe686c81884d111cab550bb6c7fff158cdc4d`) are in `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/inputs/`.
3. Compare with `python compare_tf.py H100_DIR/results.json TPU_DIR/results.json` from the same folder, and bin `|Δlogprob|` by position.

Expected: TPU per-position log probabilities stay within TPU run-to-run noise of H100 at every position, including beyond 2048.

Next step: rerun the TPU side with `grugmoe_attention_mode` set to the dense reference path (`_dense_reference_attention` in `grugmoe.py`, which applies the window as an explicit mask). If dense-mode TPU matches H100 past position 2048, the defect is in the production RPA path.

Caveats: the H100 completions were re-tokenized from text because the eval record has no sampled token ids, and vLLM omits special tokens such as the leading `<|start_think|>` from returned text. Both platforms scored the same bytes, so the comparison is valid, but the first completion positions are not a replay of the original sampled trajectory.

Data:
- H100: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-h100x8/concurrency-1/`
- TPU v6e-8: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-v6e8/concurrency-{1,10}/`
- H100 MATH500 per-item and three-way tables: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task224-math500/`

- The served vLLM build (`fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`) never reads `grugmoe_attention_mode`; its Grug model always uses the `Attention` layer (`vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py` L958-L964). Passing the field through `hf_overrides` changes nothing.

The replacement control is a kernel-level test: run tpu-inference's ragged paged attention tests with Step12's shapes (sliding window 2048, page size 16, 32 query / 8 KV heads after padding) against the reference implementation on a v6e-4.

The 2048-token onset implicates local attention, but matching elementwise mask inequalities do not establish that TPU RPA visits the right KV blocks or reads intact cache pages. `GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` selects a dense path that computes from the full input without updating KV cache, or a production path that calls RPA v3. - [`kernel.py#L493-L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494) — elementwise window mask

`GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` → `shared_attention()` → RPA v3 is the production call chain. The failing step within that chain is not established, so use the frozen Step12 inputs to isolate it:

1. Replay the issue's 10 teacher-forced inputs on the reported TPU revisions with `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` and `production`; force one complete prefill per request because dense has no historical KV-cache reads, verify identical token IDs, and compare bins around position 2048 with the existing H100 results.

topics.title: [skyrl] Emit worker-labeled training and inference metrics to Finelog
topics.body:
SkyRL training, rollout generation, and inference workers do not emit one durable operational metric stream keyed by the Marin root run. W&B can track experiment metrics and vLLM can expose Prometheus metrics, but an operator cannot query the state and performance of every worker through the same Finelog and Grafana path used by Iris and Levanter.

Done when:

- Training and inference metrics carry root run, Iris job, task, worker, role, rank, and restart-attempt labels.
- Training workers report step, phase, loss or reward, batch counts, rollout latency, and optimization latency at a documented cadence.
- Inference workers report request throughput, time to first token, time per output token, queue depth, and KV-cache use when the backend exposes them.
- Worker start, readiness, restart, failure, and terminal state are queryable alongside numeric metrics.
- Metrics remain available after the job exits and repeated delivery does not create ambiguous duplicate series.
- A bounded RL run can be diagnosed from Finelog and the run-scoped Grafana dashboard without opening worker-local logs.
- W&B remains available for experiment tracking; the Finelog contract does not require W&B to diagnose a live or failed worker.

Part of #7804 under #5198. Supports #7098 and #6598.

comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — large task, no PR.** This is a multi-module integration (training + rollout + inference workers, orchestration, dashboards, docs), so per the fix-issue workflow I'm posting root cause and a proposed approach for review rather than opening a PR.

## Research

The Finelog forwarding path the issue asks for **already exists and is used by Levanter and native-`vllm serve`; the RL/SkyRL workers just never opt into it.** They report only to W&B. So this is an integration task, not a new telemetry system.

- `rigging.telltale` — Prometheus-style `gauge()`/`histogram()` + `set_global_labels()` + a forwarder. [`telltale.py#L94-L149`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telltale.py#L94-L149)
- `iris.runtime.telltale.start()` — idempotent; serves the registry and forwards to Finelog, **stamping `job_id`/`task_index`/`attempt`/`worker`/`region`/`process_index` on every row**, durable after exit. [`telltale.py#L31-L131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/runtime/telltale.py#L31-L131)
- Iris already writes worker start/readiness/restart/failure/terminal to the `iris.task_event` namespace keyed by task — worker lifecycle is **already queryable**.
- `marin.inference.vllm_metrics` — mirrors a native `vllm serve` `/metrics` into telltale (`source=vllm`). Does **not** apply to the RL path: RL runs vLLM in-process/offline (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, no HTTP `/metrics`). [`vllm_metrics.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_metrics.py)

**Gap (RL workers emit nothing to Finelog):**
- Training: metrics computed in `_training_step_timing_metrics` go only to `trainer.tracker.log()` (W&B). [`train_worker.py#L116-L534`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/train_worker.py#L116-L534)
- Rollout: standalone `RolloutTracker` wraps `wandb.init` directly (avoids Levanter's tracker to not deadlock vLLM); phases logged as plain log lines. [`rollout_worker.py#L179-L198`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_worker.py#L179-L198)
- Neither worker calls `runtime_telltale.start()` or `set_global_labels(source=, run=)`; no `run`/`role`/`rank` labels. Root run id exists as `RLJobConfig.run_id` but is only threaded into W&B/actor names.

## Proposed approach

Reuse the existing telltale→Finelog path; add a thin RL metrics emitter. No new transport.

1. **Boot + labels (all roles).** On each worker entry (`_train_worker_entry`, `_rollout_worker_entry`, inference ctx init) call `runtime_telltale.start()` and `telltale.set_global_labels(source="skyrl", run=<root run_id>, role=<train|rollout|inference>, rank=<worker_index/process rank>)`. Iris already supplies job/task/worker/attempt/process_index, so `run`+`role`+`rank` complete the label set. `attempt` is the restart-attempt label; per-attempt+process_index series avoid ambiguous duplicates.
2. **Training metrics.** Add a small telltale bridge that mirrors the existing metrics dict (step, phase, loss/reward, batch counts, rollout-wait vs forward/backward latency) into `gauge()`/`histogram()` alongside the current `tracker.log()` — do not replace W&B. A documented cadence = the existing `every=1` hook.
3. **Rollout metrics.** Same bridge over `_log_rollout_metrics` (throughput, success_rate/avg_reward, weight-transfer counters); turn the `PHASE:` log lines into a phase gauge.
4. **Inference metrics.** Offline vLLM has no HTTP `/metrics`, but the V1 engine's Prometheus `StatLogger` registers `vllm:` families into the **same process** registry when stats aren't disabled. Enable stat logging on the offline `LLM`/`AsyncLLM` engine and forward the in-process `vllm:` families directly (reuse the `_VllmMetricsProxy` collect logic without the HTTP poller) to get TTFT/TPOT/queue-depth/KV-cache. Confirm the Marin vLLM fork's `kv_cache_metrics` arg feeds this. **This is the one genuinely new piece** and the main open risk.
5. **Lifecycle.** Rely on Iris `iris.task_event`; document the `run`→Iris-job mapping so an operator can join lifecycle events to the numeric series.
6. **Dashboard + docs.** Add a run-scoped Grafana dashboard filtered on `run`/`role` (extend `infra/grafana/dashboards/training.json` pattern) and document the RL Finelog contract. W&B stays as-is for experiment tracking.

**Open questions for a human before implementation:**
- Label vocabulary: `source="skyrl"` vs `source="marin-rl"`? Explicit `role`/`rank` columns vs deriving from the Iris job path?
- Offline-vLLM stats: acceptable to enable the V1 `PrometheusStatLogger` in-process (small overhead), and does the fork's `kv_cache_metrics` populate the standard `vllm:` families or a custom one?
- Scope of an initial PR — suggest landing steps 1–3 (train+rollout, low risk) first, then inference (step 4) and the dashboard separately.

Blocked on the label/scope decisions above before writing code.

topics.title: [grug] Early hero checkpoints store router bias equal to their pending QB update
topics.body:
Checkpoints from the original hero run `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` store a router bias that already equals the bias derived from their own `pending_qb_betas`. A consistent step-N checkpoint cannot do that, so these checkpoints may mix state from two training steps.

The hero train step (`_make_train_step` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py`, same order at 12d8b6f0) overwrites the router bias with centered(−`pending_qb_betas`), runs the forward, backward, and optimizer update, then stores the step's new quantile-balancing betas as `pending_qb_betas`. The router bias has no gradient (`stop_gradient`), no weight decay, and all-zero Adam moments, so a step-N checkpoint should hold bias = centered(−β_{N−1}) and pending = β_N. Each β is a fresh per-step quantile estimate, so the two should differ.

Every checkpoint from step 114000 onward behaves as expected. On 9 permanent checkpoints from step 114000 to 264000, mean |stored bias − centered(−pending)| is 0.017–0.034 and the max is 1–7 logit units.

The six `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` checkpoints do not. At steps 6000, 12000, 24000, 36000, 48000, and 54000 under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-12d8b6f0-dee637/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/`, `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` equals centered(−`pending_qb_betas`) to at most 4.8e-7, which is fp32 rounding. The bf16 `params` bias equals bf16 of the master bias. That would require β_N = β_{N−1} + a per-layer constant at every save. This run used fp32 pinned-host master params (`MasterParamMode.FP32_PINNED_HOST`). The later runs keep fp32 `params` and no master.

Two explanations fit: the saved weights come from one step later than the saved `pending_qb_betas`, or the saved `pending_qb_betas` is one step stale. In both cases the checkpoint would combine two steps' state, possibly through the async save path and the donated train-state buffers in pinned-host master mode. None of this is verified.

Reproduce: read `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` and `pending_qb_betas` from one of the checkpoints above with tensorstore (`{"driver": "zarr3", "kvstore": {"driver": "ocdbt", "base": build_kvstore_spec(ckpt), "path": key + "/"}}`). Compare `bias` with `b - b.mean(-1, keepdims=True)` where `b = -pending`. Both arrays are [48, 384] float32.

Done when the cause is identified, and if it is a save-path bug, the affected checkpoint modes and steps are listed and the current save path is shown to be unaffected or fixed.

topics.title: Clear masked shared-memory tiles in segmented FA4 backward
topics.body:
Clear masked shared-memory entries before the existing segmented FA4 backward kernel copies queries, keys, values, and output gradients. Its synchronous copies leave masked destinations unchanged, but matrix operations still read those entries. Stale NaNs can therefore propagate through products with zero.

Add a GB200 test that repeatedly compares partial-tile outputs and gradients against the float32 reference.

Extracted from #9228. This fixes the existing segmented kernel independently of native SM100 kernel selection.

The [GB200 regression](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-scope-port-20260922b) passes. The run used CPU Torch 2.11.0 to avoid main’s unrelated `libcufile.so.0` import failure. Seven affected safe tests pass locally; lint and type checks pass.

topics.title: Levanter ignores dtype_override when reading BF16 safetensors
topics.body:
`read_safetensors_fsspec(..., dtype_override=jnp.float32)` returns BF16 arrays for BF16 tensors. This also affects `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=jnp.float32)` and can make a supposed FP32 reference forward compute in BF16.

In `lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py`, the conversion guard uses `np.issubdtype(tensor_np.dtype, np.floating)`. The predicate repro is:

```python
import ml_dtypes
import numpy as np
assert not np.issubdtype(np.dtype(ml_dtypes.bfloat16), np.floating)
```

Reproduce the loader behavior on CPU:

```python
import asyncio
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from safetensors.numpy import save_file
from levanter.compat.fsspec_safetensor import read_safetensors_fsspec

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "weights.safetensors"
    save_file({"weight": np.ones((2, 2), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)}, path)
    tensors = asyncio.run(read_safetensors_fsspec(
        f"file://{path}", dtype_override=jnp.float32, sharding_fn=lambda _: None,
    ))
    assert tensors["weight"].dtype == jnp.float32  # Fails: bfloat16
```

Expected: BF16 tensors honor the requested floating dtype; integer tensors remain integers. A regression in `lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py::test_dtype_override` fails before changing the guard to `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` and passes after, including exact widened values and unchanged integer tensors.

Found during #10213. The affected Qwen diagnostic `task231-qwen-fp32-diagnostic-20261019-r2` used Levanter BF16 against HF FP32, not FP32 on both sides. Its FP32-vs-FP32 interpretation is withdrawn; the original measurements remain as cross-dtype evidence.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`read_safetensors_fsspec()` checks floating input with NumPy, which does not classify BF16 as floating. As a result, the loader skips `dtype_override` for BF16; `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=...)` passes its request through this loader.

**Relevant code**
- [`fsspec_safetensor.py#L270`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py#L270) — conversion guard
- [`hf_checkpoints.py#L404`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L404) — converter passes dtype
- [`test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93) — existing override coverage

# Proposed Fix

`load_pretrained()` passes `dtype` to `read_safetensors_fsspec()`, whose NumPy guard skips BF16 before conversion. Extend `test_dtype_override` with BF16 input, exact FP32 widened values, and unchanged integer tensors; then use `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` in the guard.

🤖 [PR #10267](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10267) applies `dtype_override` to BF16 safetensors and preserves integer dtypes. The regression failed before the guard change and passes after. The safe Levanter suite passed in four fresh-process batches (1,316 passed, 55 skipped); a monolithic run exhausted local memory. All-files lint and the local lint review passed.

🤖 [PR #10267](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10267) is mergeable and CI passed, including Levanter unit tests and Marin lint. The BF16 regression also passes against the merged `main`. The PR is awaiting human review.

topics.title: Weight-merging RSI loop on spare TPU compute: tracking issue
topics.body:
## Goal

Run a weight-merging loop on spare Marin compute: merge Snowball checkpoints on CPU (reserved v4 hosts in us-central2-b), screen the merges cheaply with TPU vLLM on preemptible single-host slices, and promote winners to the H100 policy evaluation. This issue tracks the project end to end.

## Pins

- Marin base `24ce375f06`
- vLLM fork `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d` (head of marin-community/tpu-inference#27, stacked on #29 and #28), applied job-locally
- Evalchemy `3bb8278`, MATH500 full set, harness seed 19311
- S = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` @ `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`

## Status

| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Inventory, feasibility, campaign matrix | done 2026-10-15 |
| Parents S, C, A5, M staged and sha256-verified in `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/parents/` | done 2026-10-16 |
| Merge toolkit: allowlisted BF16 to F32 widening for M's router biases (branch `task/197`) | done, no PR yet |
| TPU scoring smoke test | done: TPU scores 6-7 points below H100 |
| Matched H100 control | done 2026-10-17: 0.944 |
| Quantized serving on v5e | blocked: the pinned fork rejects every quant config for GrugMoE |
| Localize the TPU gap | in progress (#10250) |
| Iteration-one merges (3 recipes) | not started, waiting on the scoring path |

## MATH500 scores for S, same model revision, same Evalchemy pin, same effective sampling

| Server | Score |
|---|---|
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-03 record | 0.950 |
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-17 | 0.944 |
| TPU v6e-8 TP8 bf16 (two runs) | 0.878, 0.882 |
| TPU v5p-8 TP4 bf16 | 0.884 |

Per item: 421 right everywhere, 39 right on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU, 12 wrong everywhere. The 39 are long solutions; 22 of them drift onto a different problem mid-solution.

## The TPU gap (#10250)

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 items match the H100 within noise up to token 2047 and diverge from exactly token 2048, which is S's `sliding_window` (`global_every` 4). The gap grows to about 0.14 nat mean absolute logprob difference by 3-4k tokens.

Ruled out: truncation, thinking mode, sampling (Evalchemy strips temperature and seed, both servers run vLLM defaults), batch dependence, sharding degree and chip generation (v5p-8 TP4 scores the same), cross-request contamination, mask off-by-one (training, FA3 and the TPU kernel all keep the last W tokens including self), KV block eviction (the TPU runner keeps one full-attention cache group), per-layer window plumbing (reaches the TPU kernel unchanged; global layers get no window), KV cache dtype (bf16 on both).

Not valid controls at this pin: `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` (never read by the vLLM model), a GPU TP8 run (GPU GrugMoE requires TP=1), the experimental batched RPA kernel (fails to compile: its SMEM schedule is sized from a reported capacity above the compiler's 1 MiB limit).

A standalone probe of the pinned ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel against its dense reference with random inputs passes 22 cases around the window boundary (error flat at bf16 noise). Random inputs spread attention over about 2048 keys, so that probe cannot see an edge or sink effect. Running now: a kernel probe with peaky scores, a BOS-like sink key and position-bucket values, and a TPU serving control with the window disabled.

Consequence for the loop: TPU vLLM cannot rank merges until this is fixed. One H100x8 MATH500 run costs about 14 minutes of box time per candidate.

## Related

- #10250 TPU sliding-window divergence
- #9400 tpu-inference pin bump and hardware checks
- #8323 Snowball TPU serving
- #7555 earlier long-context divergence on TPU
- marin-community/tpu-inference#28 custom router selections, #29 host storage release, #27 TP8 head padding (the stack every TPU run here used)
- Two Evalchemy integration gotchas found on the way: the pinned Evalchemy strips `temperature` and `seed` from requests, so the server's defaults apply; and marin's FineStore result reader expects native results JSON while Evalchemy `3bb8278` writes parquet tables, so the parent eval job reports FAILED although the child succeeded and the score is in `data/evalchemy_results/`.

## Open decisions

1. Score iteration-one merges on H100 now, or wait for the TPU fix.
2. Open a PR for the merge-toolkit change on `task/197`.
3. File the Iris autoscaler tier-blocking issue (a v6e-4 group in backoff blocks v6e-8 demand in the same zone).

The pinned Evalchemy writes parquet tables while Marin's result reader looks only for `results_*.json`, so a successful child can leave the parent failed. ## Localization update: the TPU/H100 gap is the sliding window, and the TPU side matches training

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 MATH500 prompts (Snowball S, `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02@50fe2f48`), now in five configurations: H100 and TPU v6e-8 each with the model's 2048 sliding window and each with the window disabled (`--hf-overrides '{"sliding_window": 262144}'`), plus an H100 repeat for run-to-run noise. Mean |Δ logprob| per position bin:

| positions | H100 vs TPU, window off on both | H100 vs TPU, window on | H100: window on vs off | TPU: window on vs off | H100 repeat noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.014–0.016 | 0.015–0.017 | 0.013–0.015 | 0.000 | 0.013–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.012 | 0.026 | 0.013 | 0.025 | 0.012 |
| 2112–2303 | 0.012–0.014 | 0.037–0.039 | 0.018–0.024 | 0.038–0.041 | 0.011–0.014 |
| 2304–2431 | 0.011–0.017 | 0.040–0.066 | 0.037–0.084 | 0.058–0.114 | 0.010–0.014 |
| 2432–3071 | 0.014–0.015 | 0.066–0.079 | 0.124–0.186 | 0.143–0.211 | 0.012–0.015 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.021 | 0.142 | 0.703 | 0.700 | 0.013 |
| 4096–8000 | 0.033 | 0.133 | 1.123 | 1.096 | 0.010 |

1. With the window off on both platforms, H100 and TPU agree at every position to within 0.03 nats. The whole divergence is in how the 2048 window is applied.
2. On TPU (tpu-inference `ae387b8`, ragged paged attention v3) the window takes effect at token 2049 on every long item. Three standalone kernel probes (random, peaky/sink, and serving's per-shard head geometry and request classes) put exactly zero attention mass outside the window. This matches levanter's training mask (`splash_attention_mask.LocalMask(window_size=(W-1, None))` AND causal, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/kernels/pallas/splash_attention.py`).
3. On H100 (vLLM fork `01911be`, FlashAttention 3) the window's effect stays at noise until about token 2150, is about half the TPU's around token 2340, and equals the TPU's from about 2460 on. Past 3072 the two effects are the same size, so every local layer is windowed on both platforms; the H100 differs only in the first few hundred tokens past the boundary, i.e. it keeps seeing some early tokens that the exact window drops.
4. Ruled out on the TPU side: the kernel, the batched kernel (does not compile at this pin), KV block eviction (one cache group on TPU), KV dtype, per-layer window plumbing, RoPE, prefill chunk size (knee stays at 2048 with 1536-token chunks).

Open: which code path in the FA3 backend produces the loose boundary (an FA2 run is in flight), and why the looser window scores higher on MATH500 (0.944 H100 vs 0.878–0.884 TPU). ## TPU serving defect localized: global attention layers get the sliding window

Follow-up to the seven-way comparison above. The TPU-side defect is now named and fixed by a config override; the proper fix is in tpu-inference.

**What happens.** tpu-inference registers a vLLM general plugin (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/__init__.py`, `register_layers` -> `_register_grugmoe`). Whenever the TPU stack is present it sets `_CONFIG_REGISTRY["grug_moe"] = GrugMoeHfConfig`, replacing the vLLM fork's `GrugMoeConfig`. `GrugMoeHfConfig` (`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py`) is a plain `PretrainedConfig` with name aliases; it never sets `layer_types`. The fork's `GrugMoeConfig` sets `layer_types` from `grug_moe_layer_types(num_layers, global_every)`. Plugins load in `EngineArgs.__post_init__`, before the model config is built, so on TPU `hf_text_config.layer_types` is `None`. vLLM then sets `cache_config.sliding_window = 2048` (arg_utils: "only set CacheConfig.sliding_window if the model is all sliding window"), and the fork's GrugMoE model, which passes `per_layer_sliding_window=None` for its 7 global layers (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25 of 26), gets 2048 for them through the `Attention.__init__` fallback. A static trace of the TPU engine shows all 26 layers at `sliding_window=2048`. On H100 the plugin is absent, the fork config is used, and the engine builds 4 KV cache groups with the global layers unwindowed. The fork model derives its own layer pattern from `global_every`, so nothing crashes; the window is just applied to the wrong layers.

**Verification.** Passing `--hf-overrides '{"layer_types": [...]}'` (the fork's list: `full_attention` at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25, `sliding_attention` elsewhere) changes the trace to 7 layers at `None` and 19 at 2048, with 4 KV cache groups. Teacher-forced probe (same 10 MATH500 items, 35,801 positions) against the exact-window eager reference, mean |delta logprob|:

| positions | TPU, override | TPU, default | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2048 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 2048-2304 | 0.013-0.016 | 0.023-0.038 | 0.012-0.014 |
| 2304-3072 | 0.015-0.017 | 0.054-0.080 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 3072+ | 0.012-0.015 | 0.132-0.142 | 0.011-0.014 |

TPU with the override vs H100 directly: 0.011-0.017 at every position. MATH500 with the override (Evalchemy 3bb8278, seed 19311, same settings as the TPU runs above): **0.940** (470/500, 500 generated and scored, 1421 s), against 0.878-0.884 for TPU without it and 0.944 / 0.950 for the two H100 runs. The gap is closed.

**Fix.** Proper fix is in tpu-inference: `GrugMoeHfConfig` should set `layer_types` the same way the fork does, or the plugin should not replace a registry entry the fork already provides. tpu-inference `main` at 340444337772 (2026-10-19) still has the overwrite. Until then, TPU serving of any GrugMoE checkpoint whose `config.json` lacks `layer_types` needs the override above. Pins: vLLM fork fb02daf, tpu-inference ae387b8, Step12 @50fe2f488aee.

topics.title: [rolloutengine] Start command and verifier deadlines with the work
topics.body:
A local command's timeout now starts when the sandboxed program starts. The command's process writes a start byte on the launcher's status pipe just before `exec`, and `Command.timeout` runs from then. Spawning the launcher and entering the sandbox have their own 60-second limit; a command that misses it raises the new `shellbox.machine.CommandStartTimeout`, a `RuntimeError`, and the machine stays usable. SkyRL wraps it in `TaskMachineError`, which it masks as infrastructure.

The verifier deadline now stops while the verifier machine is prepared (`prepare_machine_spec`, including building a lock runtime) and created. `grade_in_sandbox` takes the caller's deadline and pauses it around that step, which the machine's `startup_timeout` bounds instead. A verifier machine that misses its startup deadline fails grading with a `TimeoutError` and no `GradingFailure.TIMEOUT`. SkyRL's task worker maps that case to `EnvironmentStartTimeoutError`, an infrastructure error, instead of `VerifierTimeoutError`; an expired verifier deadline still maps to `VerifierTimeoutError` through the grade.

In the Taskforge RL run, host-side queueing made both deadlines expire: tool calls failed as `AgentTimeoutError` and were charged to the policy, and graders failed as `VerifierTimeoutError`. With #10506, a local command starts in about 25 ms at 96 concurrent machines, and a stalled host now surfaces as an infrastructure error.

The tool-turn deadline is unchanged and still includes command start time. It spans several commands and host tools, and excluding start time would need every backend to report when its commands start. After #10506 that time is milliseconds, and a start that stalls longer than 60 seconds raises `CommandStartTimeout` well inside the RL configuration's 240-second turn deadline.

Stacked on #10506.

topics.title: [grug] Honor dynamic attention bounds in reference backends
topics.body:
Honor the per-query bounds that the hero layer scan uses to select local attention windows in the reference and XLA attention backends. These backends previously ignored the bounds and silently evaluated local layers with full-causal attention.

Zero outputs for fully masked padding queries and reject precomputed bounds in Splash, which does not support them. Scan regressions compare outputs and Q/K/V gradients across local windows, packed segments, and padding. The XLA fallback materializes a dense mask; the active FA4 kernels are unchanged.

topics.title: [post-training] Shared chat template and the Stage 0 protocol converter
topics.body:
The shared chat template in `experiments/post_training/chat_template.py` and the converter in `stage0/convert.py` provide the first part of the review's changelist that downstream work reads from for the OPD-SFT controls experiment's Phase 0/1a work. They supersede the template and converter parts of #10505; that PR will be retargeted onto the reworked WP5 with only its configs.

One Jinja skeleton now defines the structural behavior for all four model families. Reasoning renders from `reasoning_content` on every assistant turn, tool calls serialize identically, and tool responses use bare `<tool_response>`. Each family supplies delimiters through a `ChatTokens` map: Grug uses `<|start_header_id|>`, `<|eot_id|>`, and `<|start_think|>`; Qwen3, Qwen3.5, and Nemotron-H use `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, and `<think>`. Each map validates that its delimiters are single tokens under the pinned tokenizer. The delimiters become Jinja string literals, making the template self-contained for tokenizer configs. This replaces the published-template patches and Nemotron template source from #10505.

The converter strips both source think-marker styles into `reasoning_content` and raises on unclosed blocks. It selects one row-id set by requiring a maximum rendered length of 32,768 tokens across all four pinned tokenizers, and records dropped IDs in the manifest. All four architectures therefore train on the same rows.

The 28 tests validate token maps against the real pinned tokenizers, render 100 rows per source for each family, and check token-level spans: reasoning appears between single think tokens, no spurious empty think appears, and every turn closes. They also cover the length filter and manifest, and check at the Jinja level that the Qwen and Nemotron instances differ only in BOS.

topics.title: [evals] Trigger configured evals when checkpoints become eligible
topics.body:
The shared evaluation launcher accepts a model and eval subset, but every run is still started manually. #6503 requires an eligible checkpoint to trigger its configured evaluations and publish results without an operator invoking the CLI.

Done when:

- A checkpoint has an explicit, reviewable evaluation policy: eligibility, model configuration, eval subset, and retry behavior.
- An idempotent trigger launches the existing evaluation pipeline when an eligible checkpoint becomes available.
- Repeated events do not create duplicate runs for the same checkpoint, evaluation, and version.
- Trigger state and terminal run records are inspectable, and failures can be retried without editing database state by hand.
- A canary demonstrates checkpoint availability through indexed evaldash results with no manual launch step.

Part of #6503.

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read AGENTS.md, fix-issue, commit skills
- [x] Actionability check (clear "Done when" → actionable)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PR/issue)
- [x] Research existing eval infra
- [x] Post Research + proposed approach
- [ ] Awaiting human review before implementation (scope > PR threshold)

# Research

Scope is a new event-driven subsystem (trigger + policy + idempotent state + retry + canary), not a self-contained bug fix, so this is an analysis for review rather than a PR. The pieces to build on already exist:

- **Launcher** `experiments/evaluation/launch.py:98-154` — `build_evaluation_batch()` / `launch_group()` take a model + eval keys and submit one Iris orchestrator. This is the "existing evaluation pipeline" the trigger must call.
- **Record store** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py:114-159` — `EvalRunRecord` is the source of truth; `record_path()` is `{prefix}/{run_id}/record.json`. evaldash indexes these.
- **evaldash ingest** `infra/evaldash/src/server.py:289-370` — poll-based ingest (300s) of terminal records into Postgres; this is where the canary must show results with no manual launch.
- **Checkpoint discovery** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/utils.py:9-21` (`discover_hf_checkpoints`) and `experiments/grug/checkpointing.py:40-76` (`metadata.json` → `step`, `timestamp`) — on-demand only; nothing watches for readiness.

**Idempotency blocker:** `launch.py:72-74` `_run_id()` = timestamp + `uuid4()`, so it is non-deterministic. Replaying the same checkpoint event today produces a *new* `run_id` and a duplicate run. The DoD "repeated events do not create duplicate runs for the same checkpoint, evaluation, and version" therefore requires a deterministic idempotency key; it cannot be met by reusing `_run_id` as-is.

Nothing exists for: checkpoint eligibility policy, an event/trigger, trigger state, or checkpoint→run linkage.

# Proposed approach (for review)

Smallest design that satisfies each DoD bullet. Reuse the launcher unchanged except for the run-id path.

**1. Eligibility + policy (reviewable config).** A dataclass `CheckpointEvalPolicy` in `experiments/evaluation/` declaring: eligibility predicate (`step % N == 0`, or min-step, or an explicit allowlist), `model` config template, `evals` subset (reuse `EVALS`/`SUITES` keys), and `max_retries`. Policies live in-repo next to `models.py`/`evals.py` so they diff in PRs. No per-checkpoint DB config.

**2. Deterministic run id → idempotency.** Add `eval_run_id(checkpoint_id, eval_key, version)` returning a stable hash-suffixed id (drop the timestamp+uuid for triggered runs). Idempotency then falls out of the existing object layout: a run exists iff `record.json` is present at its deterministic `record_path`. The trigger skips any eval whose record already exists in a terminal-success state; retry re-launches only records that are absent or `INFRA_FAILED`/`FAILED` under `max_retries`. `RunStatus` (`records.py:32-42`) already separates infra vs eval failure, which is exactly the retry signal.

**3. Trigger.** Prefer a **poll-reconcile loop** over a push event bus (matches the codebase's existing 300s evaldash ingest and avoids new infra): list eligible checkpoints, join against existing records, launch the missing/retryable ones via `launch_group()`. Reconciliation is idempotent by construction, so "repeated events" is a non-issue. Open question for reviewers: run it as an Iris cron job, or fold into an existing daemon? (see #6503 "Trigger definition" — still TBD there.)

**4. State + inspectability.** No new database — the record store *is* the state. Trigger decisions are derivable from records + policy; add a small `record.json` field linking the source `checkpoint_id` (currently absent — records have no checkpoint ref) so eval results are traceable back to the checkpoint and evaldash can surface it. Retry = ignore the failed record and let reconcile re-launch; no hand-editing DB state.

**5. Canary.** A test that stages a synthetic eligible checkpoint, runs one reconcile pass, and asserts a terminal record lands at the deterministic path and is picked up by ingest — end to end, no manual `cli.py launch`.

Two decisions I need before implementing:
- **Trigger host**: Iris cron vs. extend evaldash ingest vs. a new daemon?
- **Eligibility source**: HF exports (`discover_hf_checkpoints`) vs. training `metadata.json` (`step`) — which is the canonical "checkpoint became available" signal for the first cut?

This is design-review work under #6503; I have not opened a PR.

topics.title: [levanter] Vectorize FA4 SM100 segment mask and zero accumulators in prep
topics.body:
This PR changes two parts of the SM100 FA4 kernels. The forward evaluates the document segment mask 32 columns at a time. The backward zeroes its fp32 accumulators the same way as upstream FA4 and no longer launches scalar zero-fill kernels. Before this change, the forward for document-masked local attention at hero shapes was about 1.7x slower than upstream FA4 varlen. Now the forward is within 5% of upstream.

The vectorized mask_mod builds keep-bitmasks with `r2p_bitmask_below` and `r2p_bitmask_above`. Its output is bitwise equal to the output of the scalar mask. In the backward, the preprocess kernel clears the dQ accumulator while it computes the row dot products. dK and dV start from an XLA zeros buffer that the kernel receives through `input_output_aliases`. Callers give the aliases to `cutlass_call` as a tuple of pairs, because the kernel cache key must be hashable. `cutlass_call` converts them to the dict that `cutlass.jax` expects. SM90 and SM120 keep the current zero-fill path.

Kernel measurements on one GB200 at hero shapes (median 16K rows):

| Metric | Before | After | Upstream varlen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local-layer forward | 3.16 ms | 1.96 ms | 1.87 ms |
| Local-layer fwd+bwd | 10.23 ms | 8.97 ms | |
| Projected attention cost | 0.777 s/step | 0.672 s/step | |

Output, dq, dk and dv match an fp32 reference with the same relative error as before. That error is 2.0e-3 to 2.6e-3, which is the bf16 rounding floor. The FA4 test file passes on GPU.

The end-to-end test ran on one GB200 NVL72 rack, restored from hero step 240000. At 16K context, the step time goes from 13.055 to 12.956 s/step (+0.76% tokens/s). The loss stays inside same-code noise, and the drop fraction does not change. A rank-0 trace shows that the attention kernels are 0.23 s/step faster. Peak memory increases by 0.5 GB because of the aliased dK/dV buffers.

The remaining gap to upstream is about 0.035 s/step, and it is in the backward. This backward uses 1-CTA with the scalar mask. The upstream backward uses 2-CTA.

topics.title: [SkyRL] Share BF16 checkpoint records with FP32 master weights
topics.body:
Deduplicate BF16 model weights against their synchronized FP32 optimizer masters in Megatron S3 checkpoints. Both logical names reference one stored FP32 record. Full training restores load masters and moments once, then cast masters into BF16 model buffers and synchronize distributed parameter shards. Model-only restores read the shared records and cast them to BF16.

Buffers and weights without matching model-space masters retain separate records. For matching BF16 parameters with FP32 masters and Adam moments, tensor storage and full-restore reads fall from 14 to 12 bytes per parameter: about 14%, or 134 GB for a 939 GB checkpoint with this layout. Model-only loads read FP32 records, twice the weight bytes of a BF16-only copy.

topics.title: [datakit] Release the shared Zephyr pool after its last stage
topics.body:
Release the shared Zephyr pool when its last stage succeeds, so idle shared workers stop holding hosts needed by dedicated pools. `run_reference_steps` runs normalization before starting the shared pool; a watcher thread calls `ZephyrContext.shutdown()` after every step in `DatakitSteps.shared_pool_steps` succeeds. `ZephyrDatakitSteps` and `DecontaminationSteps` each list the stages that receive the shared context. If the watcher's status check raises, the run fails with that error. All three ferries use this path through `run_reference_ferry`, as does `reference_pipeline.py --target all`. The shared pool uses `_IdleWorkerPolicy.RETAIN`, so it previously kept every acquired worker until the DAG ended: up to 512 workers (2 CPU / 16 GiB each) on v5e hosts, while the embed, quality, fuzzy-cluster, and store pools waited for hosts.

Reduce the tier-1 store worker from 4 CPU / 32 GiB RAM / 64 GiB disk to 2 CPU / 8 GiB RAM / 16 GiB disk. A store task with one normalized shard peaks below 2 GiB RAM and spills below 1 GiB. On 2026-10-12, the old shape received 1 of 106 workers; the new shape received 12 workers in 1 minute.

On the fixed code, tier 1 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153556`) succeeded in 56 minutes. Tier 3 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153605`) succeeded, and its shared pool stopped at 19:30 UTC after fuzzy dedup. Tier 3 took 5h47m, exceeding the 20,700-second CI wait. On a busy cluster, the shared pool received only 275 of its 512 workers, and tokenization took 2h37m, compared with 37 minutes on 2026-10-05.

The tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers drop from 16 CPU / 128 GiB / 64 GiB disk to 8 CPU / 64 GiB / 32 GiB, with 64 instead of 32 workers, so the task count stays at 512. Only one of the larger workers fits on a v5e host. On 2026-10-13 the verify workers waited 3h46m for hosts, and the tier-3 ferry took 7h30m. At 16 tasks per worker, cluster text peaked at 66 GiB and verify at 26 GiB.

The three tiers passed in CI on this branch. Tier 1 took 56 minutes, and tier 2 took 1h51m. Tier 3 (`/runner/iris-run-job-20261013-165715`) took 2h25m, with 36 minutes for fuzzy verification. This is much less than the 20,700-second CI wait.

The tier concurrency groups now include `github.ref`, so a run started on a branch and the scheduled run on main do not cancel each other.

Fixes https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10047. Part of https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10059.

The PR starts the shared Zephyr pool after the normalize steps and stops it once every shared-pool stage succeeds. It also shrinks the tier-1 store and tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers and scopes the canary concurrency groups by ref. The design fits the existing `ZephyrContext` lifecycle: `shutdown()` is idempotent, and a later `execute()` raises `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`. `test_shared_pool_is_held_only_between_normalize_and_its_last_stage` passes locally and checks the ordering this PR depends on. **Should fix**
1. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1147` `shared_pool_steps` is a second, hand-written list of the steps that `zephyr_datakit_steps` and `decontamination_steps` built with `zephyr_context`. The list is complete today. A future stage that gets `zephyr_context=zephyr_context` but is left off this list will run after the release and fail with `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`, hours into a tier-3 ferry. Fix: have each builder return its own list, for example a `shared_pool_steps` property on `ZephyrDatakitSteps` (exact_dedup, tokenize, minhash, fuzzy_dedup) and on `DecontaminationSteps` (bloom, drop_sets, marks), and set `shared_pool_steps=zephyr_steps.shared_pool_steps + decontamination.shared_pool_steps`. The membership then lives next to the code that passes in the context.
2. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1210` If `step_is_built` raises inside `_release_shared_pool`, for example on a transient object-store error reading a `StatusFile`, the daemon thread exits. `threading.excepthook` prints the traceback to stderr, `watcher.join()` returns normally, and the pool keeps its workers until the DAG ends. That is the #10047 behavior again, and no failure is reported. Fix: submit the watcher through a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` and call `future.result()` after `stop.set()`, so the exception reaches the caller. Alternatively, catch the error, log it, and retry on the next poll.

A busy cluster can still push the tier-3 ferry past 20,700 s, because the shared pool still requests 512 workers. Fix: change the body to "Part of #10059", or cite a second tier-3 pass under load before closing the issue.

4. #10108 also edits `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py`, but only the embed and centroid `pip_dependency_groups`. It is independent of this change, and the two can merge in either order.

topics.title: [datakit] Backtranslate instructions for scientific-software repos in Stack v3
topics.body:
Instruction backtranslation over Stack v3 repositories that use scientific software: the repository is the response, and GLM-5.2 writes the brief a scientist would hand a language model to build it from scratch, making explicit what the code leaves implicit (the scientific question, why each tool fits, the parameters that encode domain judgement, expected outputs).

Detection and prompt extraction exist but are uncommitted: `experiments/datakit/scientific_software.py`, `experiments/datakit/repo_backtranslation.py`, and two scripts under `experiments/datakit/scripts/`. They call a `raw_stack_v3_step()` extraction in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/stack_v3.py` that was reverted out of #7788 and has to land with them.

Detection covers 44 tools across materials and chemistry, bioinformatics, imaging, and workflow engines. It keys on structured signals — Python imports, R `library()`, dependency manifests, command invocations in shell/Nextflow/Snakemake, bioconda channel references, and signature filenames such as `INCAR`/`POSCAR` — because most of the tool names are ordinary English words and substring matching is useless on them. Over the full corpus 146,661 of 172,898,790 repositories match, of which 9,089 have at least 10 stars. Prompt corpus at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/analysis/stack-v3-backtranslation-prompts_4141dfc2` and scan manifest at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/analysis/stack-v3-scientific-software_686e7bbe`; both were written by the current rules, and neither row count has been verified since the last rules change.

GLM-5.2-FP8 serving is not built. It needs 8 GB200s across two nodes with Ray and tensor parallel 8, which does not fit the single-Iris-task constraint in `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:330`, so it means porting the hand-rolled serve from `experiments/kernelgym/collect_glm52_rollouts.py`.

Repository selection is unresolved. 2,670 of the 9,089 match a single tool through a single evidence file, the profile of an incidental hit: `github-linguist/linguist` matches 11 tools from `samples/`, `XAMPPRocky/tokei` matches 5 from `tests/data/`. A test-path blacklist would be wrong, since `google-deepmind/alphafold`'s evidence includes `relax/utils_test.py`. Requiring corroboration — two evidence kinds, or import/dependency evidence rather than a lone command match — is the likelier lever.

Done when:
- Detection and prompt extraction are committed with tests, including the `raw_stack_v3_step()` extraction they depend on.
- The prompt corpus row count is verified against the starred population.
- A repository-selection rule is chosen and applied.
- GLM-5.2 has generated briefs for the selected repositories into a Parquet artifact carrying repo_path, matched tools, and token counts per row.

The marin-loom stack now declares the remote MCP connector's OAuth clients under `oauthClients`. Activation passes them to Loom's `deployment.reconcile` as `oauth_clients`, so nobody has to run `loom oauth-client add` by hand.

- `claude-ai` accepts claude.ai's callback on both `claude.ai` and `claude.com`.
- `claude-code` accepts Claude Code's loopback callback on any port.

Both are public clients that prove themselves with PKCE, so the stack carries no secret. In claude.ai the connector takes client ID `claude-ai` with a blank secret. claude.ai cannot change a connector's OAuth settings after it is added, so these ids must never be renamed. Because the stack prunes, removing a client from it revokes every token the client was issued. The README's connector section describes this instead of manual registration.

Depends on marin-community/loom#405. Loom builds without that change ignore `oauth_clients`, so this config deploys cleanly before it lands but registers nothing until Loom has the support.

topics.title: [iris] Add revocable task credentials and a CW OpenBao mock
topics.body:
Give CoreWeave Kubernetes tasks renewable controller and S3 credentials bound to their verified submitter and exact task attempt. Add an OpenBao deployment and policy mock for a CW-hosted credential authority shared by the CW and GCP execution clusters.

The rollout order is: deploy an isolated development vault, qualify its identity and recovery paths, integrate Iris as a delegation client, then enable a small workload cohort. Developing the Iris client can proceed in parallel; production workloads must not depend on it before those gates pass. No infrastructure, cloud grants, DNS records or live controller configurations are changed by this branch.

## Implemented and proposed behavior

| Area | State in this branch |
| --- | --- |
| CW task/controller authentication | Implemented: 15-minute task JWTs, attempt-bound refresh capability, authenticated submitter provenance, rollover and disable enforcement in Python and the native proxy |
| CW object-storage credentials | Implemented: controller-held API or OIDC authority exchanges for temporary S3 credentials; task SDKs refresh through AWS `credential_process` |
| OpenBao servers and delegation policies | Mock: offline resource/policy rendering and a Pulumi application project; no initialization, auth bindings, policy application or secret population |
| Iris-to-OpenBao runtime client | Proposed: approved secret references, admission, child-token issuance, helper reads, durable accessor revocation and GCP worker delivery still require implementation |
| CW primary / GCP federation | Proposed configuration and cutover procedure; current submission endpoints and peer configurations remain unchanged |

OpenBao becomes the shared credential issuer and policy enforcement service. Iris remains responsible for the authenticated submitter, job admission and live-attempt authorization. OpenBao service tokens do not automatically authenticate Iris RPCs or replace human login.

## One main service, separate development service

The target topology uses one main OpenBao data set and Raft quorum in `cw-us-east-02a`. Other Kubernetes clusters and the GCP controller are clients of that service. They do not run Raft members or require a vault per cluster. A Bao namespace per execution cluster separates its controller login, permitted profiles and token revocations; namespaces share administrators and availability.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    User[Authenticated submitter] --> Primary[CW primary Iris: cw-us-east-02a]
    Primary --> CW[Other CW execution controllers]
    Primary --> GCP[GCP marin: federated execution peer]
    subgraph Authority[Main authority in one CW Kubernetes cluster]
        Bao[Main OpenBao API: bao.oa.dev]
        Raft[Target: five voters on five reserved CPU hosts]
        Bao --- Raft
    end
    Primary -->|Own Bao namespace| Bao
    CW -->|Own Bao namespaces| Bao
    GCP -->|Own Bao namespace| Bao
    Raft --> Backup[Encrypted snapshots outside the host cluster]
    Dev[CW and GCP development clients] --> DevBao[Separate dev Bao on cw-us-west-04a]
```

Main and development have separate data, CAs and unseal shares. Both checked-in stacks bootstrap with one sealed server and internal exposure. The qualified targets are five main voters and three development voters. This capacity is not provisioned: the current east02 configuration lists four CPU nodes. Reserved hosts, admission restrictions and primary-controller placement remain prerequisites.

Keep Raft within its host cluster. Losing that cluster stops new vault credential acquisition for all main consumers, including GCP. There is no cross-cloud quorum, automatic fallback or assumed replication to the development service. A second production service would require separately managed data, trust and recovery.

## Current CW credential path

This path is implemented independently of OpenBao. Each attempt receives a private refresh capability in a Pod-owned Secret. The helper exchanges it for a task JWT; the SDK credential process uses that JWT to request temporary storage credentials.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Iris as CW execution controller
    participant Helper as Task credential helper
    participant SDK as Task AWS SDK
    participant CW as CoreWeave credential API
    participant S3 as Object storage
    Iris->>Helper: Mount exact-attempt capability in private Secret
    Helper->>Iris: RenewTaskSession over verified TLS
    Iris->>Iris: Check submitter, live attempt and session generation
    Iris-->>Helper: 15-minute task JWT
    SDK->>Helper: AWS credential_process request
    Helper->>Iris: GetTaskCredentials for granted storage profile
    Iris->>CW: Exchange controller-held API or OIDC authority
    CW-->>Iris: Temporary S3 keys, session token and expiry
    Iris->>Iris: Recheck session before returning credentials
    Iris-->>Helper: Temporary credentials, normally 30 minutes
    Helper-->>SDK: Credential-process response
    SDK->>S3: Signed requests, refresh before expiry
```

The task JWT permits task operations within its root job; it does not inherit the submitter's administrator role. Python and the native proxy check current session state even when a JWT signature is cached. Endpoint tokens and active proxy streams follow rollover and disable decisions. Already issued S3 credentials retain their provider lifetime. API-token exchange uses the configured CoreWeave service principal; actual bucket permissions must be provisioned at the provider.

Broker activation requires matching controller/task code, RBAC and cert-manager resources. VM workers retain their current authentication model. The broker's minting credentials are projected into controller-only private files.

## Proposed OpenBao secret path

Start with a synthetic third-party token profile. An operator-owned credential profile maps to fixed vault permissions; a logical reference selects an allowed object for delivery. For example, `model-reader-pilot` permits the cataloged `research/pilot-model-token` KV object. A task cannot supply a vault path, token role, entity alias or policy. Selecting fewer references or a KV version does not narrow a broader profile's vault permissions.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as Authenticated submitter
    participant Primary as CW primary Iris
    participant Exec as Execution controller: CW or GCP
    participant Helper as Attempt-local helper
    participant Bao as Main OpenBao on CW
    participant App as Task process
    User->>Primary: Submit profile and logical references
    Primary->>Primary: Authorize and persist approved grant
    Primary->>Exec: Place root job with verified provenance and grant
    Exec->>Exec: Apply local admission and narrow child grants
    Exec->>Helper: Start exact-attempt helper with private runtime files
    Helper->>Exec: Prove active attempt over verified TLS
    Exec->>Exec: Recheck attempt, grant and catalog revision
    Exec->>Bao: Platform JWT login in execution-cluster namespace
    Bao-->>Exec: Restricted parent token: 20-minute ceiling
    Exec->>Bao: Create fixed-profile child using required entity alias
    Bao-->>Exec: Nonrenewable child token: at most 10 minutes, plus accessor
    Exec->>Exec: Persist accessor and effective expiry, recheck attempt
    Exec-->>Helper: Child bearer via private runtime delivery
    Helper->>Bao: Read requested objects with child token
    Bao-->>Helper: Secret values
    Helper->>App: Requested private credential files
```

For a job executed on the primary, `Primary` and `Exec` are the same controller. For a federated job, the receiving execution controller owns scheduling, retries, task sessions and credential delivery. Federation carries authenticated provenance and approved grants; it does not forward task bearers or secret values.

CW controllers authenticate to Bao using projected Kubernetes identity with the exact issuer, ServiceAccount subject and audience. GCP uses a Google-issued identity token bound to its controller service account's numeric subject and a dedicated audience. Those real bindings remain to be configured. Each controller can create only named profile tokens and revoke accessors in its namespace. Its login grants no KV reads, policy administration or root-namespace access.

Parent logins have a 20-minute ceiling; the client obtains a replacement about every five minutes. Before creating a ten-minute child, it requires more than ten minutes plus clock allowance remaining on the parent. Effective child expiry is the earlier parent or child expiry. Old parents remain until their children expire.

The helper reads vault values directly and exposes only requested files to the task. Submitted specs, controller persistence, rendered Pod manifests, bundles and Pulumi state contain references or authorization records, not vault values. Existing `EnvironmentSpec.secrets` file delivery can carry application material; it does not itself implement reference authorization. GCP needs worker-supervised private runtime files and an exact-assignment proof. Privileged TPU tasks require suitably isolated worker pools. `SANDBOX` receives no vault helper or identity.

## Refresh, cancellation and failure

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Helper as Attempt-local helper
    participant Iris as Execution controller
    participant Bao as OpenBao
    participant Operator as User or operator
    Helper->>Iris: Request replacement before effective expiry
    Iris->>Iris: Recheck live attempt and current entitlement
    Iris->>Bao: Mint bounded child under sufficiently live parent
    Bao-->>Iris: Replacement token and accessor
    Iris-->>Helper: Deliver replacement and atomically replace private file
    Operator->>Iris: Cancel job or remove entitlement
    Iris->>Iris: Commit disabled state and durable revocation work
    Iris->>Bao: Revoke accessors with retries after outages or restart
    Bao-->>Iris: Acknowledge revocation
    Helper->>Iris: Later refresh request
    Iris-->>Helper: Denied
```

Tasks reauthenticate through Iris instead of renewing Bao tokens themselves. If Bao or Iris is unavailable, acquisition retries are bounded and no shared-key fallback occurs. Existing credentials keep their actual validity; an application environment or SDK cache needs an explicit reload or refresh mechanism. Bao token revocation blocks further vault reads. A copied static API key still requires rotation at its origin, and cloud credentials require provider revocation or expiry. Durable revocation reconciliation is part of the proposed runtime client, not implemented by the mock.

## Deployment stages and IaC ownership

1. Provision development prerequisites. Reserve CW CPU capacity; enforce the host boundary; qualify the `block` StorageClass, CNI/DNS, cert-manager and Traefik. The new `infra/openbao` application project owns server resources, TLS declarations, network policy and optional TLS-passthrough routing. Canonical `infra/pulumi` stacks retain ownership of CW capacity and all GCP IAM, workload-federation and infrastructure grants. Existing DNS ownership remains unchanged.
2. Bootstrap the isolated vault. Apply the reviewed development resources, initialize one server, and use five Shamir shares with a three-share threshold held outside CW by separate custodians. Enable two independently monitored audit destinations and protected administrator login, then revoke the initialization root token. A protected Bao reconciler/operator owns namespaces, auth bindings, policies and entities. Secret owners populate synthetic values out of band. Pulumi does not initialize, unseal or configure the vault.
3. Qualify the service before Iris adoption. Check real CW/GCP identity bindings, fixed-profile denials, parent/child expiry, TLS trust and renewal, disk recovery, sequential Raft joins, leader loss, audit failure and network partition. After initialization, audit and local denial checks, enable reviewed DNS/TLS-passthrough routing and distribute the public CA bundle for cross-cluster probes. Implement an external privileged snapshot job and demonstrate isolated restore and Bao token revocation through direct API probes. Five-minute RPO and four-hour RTO are targets pending measured recovery. Pulumi skips readiness waiting for the intentionally sealed bootstrap, so a successful update does not establish service health.
4. Implement and pilot the Iris client. Add reference admission, persisted grants, exact-attempt helper delivery, accessor tracking and restart reconciliation. Run one non-production workload on each backend across multiple token lifetimes, retry, cancellation and controller restart; demonstrate that persisted revocation work survives restart and vault restore. Check synthetic-secret exposure in specs, state, manifests, bundles and logs. Keep the CW storage broker initially. Its OIDC option already supports controller-mediated exchange; further storage work would qualify CW projected Pod identity or GCP profile-scoped service-account impersonation, plus long-lived SDK refresh. The private Bao CA endpoint alone is insufficient for a public OIDC issuer.
5. Qualify main and change submission routing. Grow the main service to its reviewed five-host layout. Establish verified human login at the CW primary and a noninteractive CW-to-GCP machine route. GCP's IAP edge needs an identity in addition to the Iris federation bearer. Configure receiver peer keys, allowed submitters and local admission; remove obsolete parent routes that would create cycles. Switch new submissions first. Existing multi-week jobs keep their owning controller, state, keys, endpoints and refresh access until they finish.

CW hosts the proposed runtime authority. The mock uses manual Shamir unseal, avoiding a GCP KMS dependency for Bao startup. Pulumi deployment tooling still uses the repository's GCS backend and KMS secrets provider. Existing CW Iris signing-key and principal-directory sources still point to GCP Secret Manager; controller-only CW bootstrap files must be provisioned before claiming a full trust-root cutover.

The current Iris controller can create and exec Pods across namespaces, so a controller in Bao's host cluster is inside its trust boundary. Reserved nodes and namespaces alone do not remove that authority. Use a dedicated management cluster if controller compromise must not permit control of vault Pods. Production adoption also requires named operators, unseal custodians, recovery ownership and a migration plan before the free CW allocation expires.

Detailed configuration and operating procedures: [task credential broker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-on-demand-credentials/lib/iris/docs/credentials.md), [CW OpenBao mock and recovery](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-on-demand-credentials/infra/openbao/README.md), [Iris federation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-on-demand-credentials/lib/iris/docs/federation.md).

topics.title: [eval] Track publication policy metric names
topics.body:
Track source metrics, canonical FineStore keys, and publication statistics for all 26 benchmarks in the October 2026 policy suite (#10197). CRUXEval publishes `output_pass@1` while its primary record key is `pass_at_1`. SOTOPIA publishes the cohort-derived `length_controlled_overall` statistic from Harbor rewards. PIQA publishes `acc_norm` while Evalchemy selects `acc` as its primary metric, recorded as `accuracy`.

The campaign-local checker resolves each Evalchemy task against vendored benchmarks or pinned lm-eval definitions, checks Harbor reward metadata, and compares config coverage and canonical keys for each benchmark. It runs in the Evalchemy unit job on relevant pull requests and the existing daily schedule. The graded-count fix reported in #9538 is already on main; this change guards the policy metric names requested in its follow-up comment.
