topics.title: [datakit] Render exactly one reasoning span per assistant turn under /think
topics.body:
Part of #10400. The Marin chat format allows zero, one or several reasoning spans in an assistant turn. A grader therefore cannot treat a second span as an error, and training rows can teach any of these shapes.

Under `Reasoning: /think`, two paths produce turns that do not start with exactly one span:

- [`_inference_messages`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L69-L79) joins the analysis messages of a turn into `content`, each wrapped in its own `<|start_think|>…<|end_think|>` by [`_assistant_content`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L41). A turn with two analysis messages renders two spans. The 10.05 SFT mix has 23 turns with two spans, all back-to-back pairs in `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v2` ([scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6326229373)).
- [`MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L114) renders a span only when `reasoning_content` is non-empty. [`chat_normalize`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L276-L278) turns on `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant message has analysis, so a call-only turn in that conversation renders with no span.

Target format: under `/think`, every assistant turn starts with exactly one span, which is empty when the turn has no reasoning. Under `/nothink`, no turn has a span. An undefined reasoning mode keeps the current behavior. Each checkpoint serves the chat template stored in its own repository, so existing checkpoints keep the current template.

Done when:
- `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` is the only code that emits think tokens, and SFT rendering and serving both produce the target format.
- `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` is bumped from `marin-v3`.
- Parity cases in `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` cover an empty span, a turn with two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a conversation that mixes them.
- A new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision carries the template.
- An audit of the rerendered SFT stores finds no `/think` assistant turn with zero spans or more than one.
- `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` describes the format.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`_inference_messages()` folds adjacent assistant messages into one turn, while `_assistant_content()` wraps each analysis message separately. `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` emits a span only for nonempty `reasoning_content`; `chat_normalize` sets `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant turn has analysis. The existing parity table already compares Datakit text with tokenizer output, but it does not cover multiple analysis messages or an empty span. No open PR directly addresses #10519; #10520 covers the separate RL grader.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_render.py#L33-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L79) — analysis wrapping and turn folding
- [`chat_template.py#L106-L115`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L115) — conditional span emission
- [`chat_normalize.py#L275-L278`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L275-L278) — conversation-level mode
- [`test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433) — renderer/tokenizer parity

# Reasoning span format

A `/think` assistant turn will start with one `<|start_think|>...<|end_think|>` pair, including an empty pair for turns without analysis. `/nothink` will emit no pair. An omitted mode and other custom mode strings will retain the current conditional behavior.

## Challenges and risks

Consecutive analysis messages need one `reasoning_content` value. Moving analysis before commentary also changes relative order if a source interleaves those channels; the rerender audit should count such records separately. A template change invalidates rendered SFT artifacts and must reach the tokenizer artifact used by new training and serving. Existing checkpoint repositories carry their own templates and keep their current behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. In `chat_render.py`, collect analysis text from each assistant turn into `reasoning_content`, leave commentary/final text in `content`, and remove think-token constants and wrapping from the adapter. Join adjacent analysis messages with one newline so their sentences do not run together. Keep tool-call order and the single end-of-turn token.
2. In `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, emit one span at the start of every `/think` assistant turn, even when `reasoning_content` is empty; emit none for `/nothink`. Preserve the current nonempty-only rule when the mode is absent or custom. A `/nothink` call with supplied reasoning should omit that reasoning; Datakit normalization only selects `/nothink` when no analysis exists.
3. Bump `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` to `marin-v4`. Update `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` with the new contract and the tokenizer revision. Export and publish a new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision from the same `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, then pin that revision for new SFT and serving artifacts that use this format.
4. Rerender the SFT sources used by the target mix in their storage region. Audit every rendered assistant turn by its conversation mode, reporting per-store turn counts, zero-span and multi-span counts under `/think`, spans under `/nothink`, and any interleaved analysis/commentary source records. Require zero format violations before using the stores for training.

## Verification

Extend `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` parity cases for an empty `/think` span, two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a mixed multi-turn conversation. Compare rendered text and token IDs through the same template used in the exported tokenizer; retain the existing tool-call, assistant-mask, and generation-prompt checks. Run the Datakit rendering tests and repository lint before publishing the tokenizer revision and audit results.

## Open question

For analysis after commentary within one assistant turn, is moving the analysis into the initial span acceptable? The proposed audit will measure whether this occurs before any source-specific repair is chosen.

topics.title: [iris] Expose admitted topology labels for placement audits
topics.body:
## Status

This is a non-blocking observability enhancement, not a reproduced placement-correctness blocker. PR #7225 requests required and sliced topology from Kueue at admission. Recent B200 research has not shown an admitted gang violating those constraints or drifting after startup.

The reproduced gap is narrower: Iris status includes pod-to-node assignments but omits the configured topology-domain values needed to independently verify the realized placement. The probe on branch `agent/b200-repro-placement-audit` therefore returned `UNOBSERVABLE`, not `VIOLATION`.

Kueue remains the enforcement authority. This work should provide provider-independent readback and diagnostics, not act as a second scheduler or make jobs query provider APIs.

## Reproduction

Run against any admitted topology-constrained Iris gang:

    iris rpc controller get-kubernetes-cluster-status | python -m iris.cluster.topology_audit --task-prefix TASK_PREFIX --topology-key TOPOLOGY_KEY --expectation single-domain -

Current result: `UNOBSERVABLE` when the requested topology key is absent from the admitted node records.

Expected result: Iris exposes the configured topology values for admitted nodes, allowing the audit to return `MATCH`, `VIOLATION`, or `UNOBSERVABLE` for genuinely incomplete data.

## Recommended progression

### 1. Expose allowlisted realized topology

- Add a topology-label map to `NodeStatus`.
- Populate only label keys referenced by configured Kueue topology levels; do not expose every Kubernetes node label.
- Add provider-independent tests for present, missing, and partially populated labels.

This is the smallest useful increment and should be kept separate from remediation policy.

### 2. Make requested-versus-realized placement first-class

- Surface the requested topology mode, topology key, and slice size alongside the realized pod-to-node placement.
- Audit required single-domain and exact sliced placement without caller-supplied provider details.
- Return explicit `MATCH`, `VIOLATION`, or `UNOBSERVABLE` results, including enough context to diagnose a mismatch.
- Handle partial admission, retries, and missing or deleted node records without reporting false violations.

### 3. Add operational presentation if useful

- Surface the audit in the CLI or dashboard and optionally emit alerts.
- Validate it during scheduler upgrades or configuration changes.
- Consider automatic abort or retry only if violations are actually observed and an explicit policy is agreed. Automatic remediation is not part of this issue.

## Non-goals

- Replacing Kueue's admission-time enforcement.
- Hardcoding provider-specific topology labels or querying provider APIs from training jobs.
- Exposing arbitrary node labels.
- Automatically aborting jobs based on the initial audit implementation.

## Done when

Required single-domain and balanced sliced placement can be audited after admission without provider-specific API access, with requested intent and realized placement clearly distinguished.

Source: #7225
Repro branch: `agent/b200-repro-placement-audit`
Non-blocking follow-up to #6710

topics.title: [storage] Route shared CoreWeave scratch to US-EAST-08A

Route temporary writes from every CoreWeave cluster to the separate `s3://marin-us-east-08a` scratch bucket. Keep permanent output roots in `marin-us-east-02a` and `marin-us-west-04a`. The d6144 hero explicitly keeps rolling checkpoint writes and resume searches in `hero-checkpoints`.

Resolve scratch storage by backend on launch hosts and workers, preserving explicit per-job overrides. CoreWeave resume searches include permanent storage, the new scratch destination, and former scratch roots in the output bucket and `hero-checkpoints`, so resubmitted runs can find their newest complete checkpoint. Explicit restore paths remain authoritative.

Remove R2 from shared job storage configuration, CoreWeave CI fixtures, and Datakit sync routing. Use the bucket registry for Datakit sync credentials, endpoint, and signing region. Keep the existing R2 bucket and lifecycle resources declared independently in the bucket stack. Finelog archive and Ducky query configuration are outside this change.

Manage the scratch bucket's nine TTL prefixes (1–7, 14, and 30 days) and seven-day multipart cleanup through `marin-buckets`. The live bucket, lifecycle configuration, and organization access policy are adopted with deletion protection. Existing jobs retain their launch environment; controller defaults take effect after deployment. After releases of `marin-rigging` and `marin-core` containing the routing, configuration, and checkpoint discovery changes, update the affected dependency locks in MarinSkyRL, Harbor, and Evalchemy.

topics.title: [grug] Add the quality-classifier fast track
topics.body:
* add the quality-classifier fast track: for each rung budget `B`, score the first `10·B` tokens of a fixed raw pool, keep the top whole documents until they fill `B`, and train the fast-track ladder on them
  * this PR holds only the quality track from #9371 [^1]
* `corpus_sample_cli` builds a `RawCorpusPool` from the registered DataKit sources in proportion to corpus size with `corpus-id-interval-v1`: one seeded cyclic interval in the 128-bit document-ID space for each source. it skips a row group only when its ID statistics show no overlap
  * `--label-exclusion-manifest` is required, so the pool contains no labelled duplicate group
  * one map task reads 64 normalized shards, with 128 workers. a 291-source pool has 149,717 shards. one task for each shard with 8 workers did about 100 shards a minute, and each reducer had to merge one scatter output per shard. the 10.7B-token pool now takes 25 min
* `quality_labels_cli` freezes the GLM-5.2 labels and fits a ridge head on cached Harrier features (target `(quality - 1) / 4`, 80/10/10 split by duplicate group)
* `quality_cli --stage features|score|select|train` scores the pool one time at the largest rung, then selects and trains each rung from the same `ScoredPool`
  * `--selection-method candidate|incumbent|random`. `random` ranks the same `10·B` prefix by a seeded hash and is the matched control
  * a custom scorer is a `module:factory` that returns a `DocumentQualityScorer`, with a JSON `--classifier-identity`
  * the selected documents keep the raw-pool order, so scores do not change the training order
  * the feature stage joins the complete Harrier pins (`hero_data.pinned_map("harrier")`, not the `hero_data.harrier` `StepSpec`) and converts only the selected rows of each row group [^2]
* gate the quality track on downstream capability, not on Paloma macro loss [^4]
  * `downstream_eval` scores a saved dense checkpoint on one H100: 13 OLMES-style cloze tasks (per-choice log-likelihood, acc, acc_norm, correct-answer BPB), gold-answer BPB on GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, and MBPP, and Paloma/Uncheatable loss by token class, by context length, and on fixed targets at 128–3968 tokens of context. the tasks are a frozen copy (`downstream-cloze-v3`, 20,472 cloze examples)
  * the code and math gold answers have no format tokens: MBPP code has `\n` line ends and no spaces at line ends (same Python AST for 500 of 500), and GSM8K has no `<<48/2=24>>` calculator annotations [^5]
  * `quality_judge` compares a candidate with its matched random control on English knowledge, English commonsense, code, math, and long context, with Welch t intervals: the seed variance of the per-run gains of each arm plus a bootstrap over paired examples [^6]. better = weighted gain of English, code, math above 0 at the lower bound and no group below its harm limit (1% per English group, 2% for the others)
  * `quality_cli --save-checkpoints` keeps the final checkpoint for the scorer. the model ladder keeps Paloma macro
* loss-validity study: 99 dense runs, 14 probe selections (`probe_scorers.py` plus a local production fusion-score probe), d512/d768 with 3 seeds, d1280 with random ×3 and four selections ×2, judge frozen on d512 before d768/d1280 ([report](https://claude.ai/artifact/46KvN5W9qp7rMnMPCdcNc9)). all numbers use the v3 tasks
  * Paloma macro ordered selection pairs like the capability target on 32% (d512), 40% (d768), and 11% (d1280) of pairs, 23% and 32% at d512/d768 without the longest-documents probe. Uncheatable macro: 84%, 76%, 44%. no single held-out loss passed at every rung
  * with all 138 runs, the positive controls included: Paloma macro 28%, 35%, 16% (25 pairs at d1280), Uncheatable macro 84%, 78%, 68%
  * dirty web (Nemotron-CC medium tiers + HPLT) at d1280: Paloma −1.5%, c4_en −6.2%, but cloze BPB +2.5%, acc_norm −0.6 pt, code gold BPB +181%
  * shortest documents at d1280: acc_norm +2.0 pt, but Paloma +10.9%, because on fixed targets its loss at 3968 tokens of context is 58% worse than random
  * quality classifiers (GLM ridge head, production fusion score) trade commonsense for knowledge: fusion within source quotas at d1280 gains 2.0% on knowledge BPB but loses 8.9% on commonsense and 4.7% on math; ridge at d1280 gains ARC-Easy +2.0 pt and loses HellaSwag −2.4 pt and LAMBADA −11.4 pt. no probe beat random
  * whitespace-heavy selection lowers the whitespace part of the Paloma loss, but not Paloma macro, so format gives no false gain when the track only filters documents
  * held-out losses have 0.2–0.3% seed SD (d512/d768), cloze BPB 1.2–1.5%. the decisions transfer: the three d1280 selections get the d512 and d768 decision
* positive control: `probe_scorers:dclm_fasttext_web` ranks the raw web documents by the public DCLM fastText classifier and takes 60% of the web tokens, against a random 60% (`web_only`)
  * 12 seeds per arm at d512: `better`, G +2.2% [+1.7, +2.7], knowledge, commonsense, code, and math up. Paloma macro is 0.2% worse and c4_en 1.1% worse, so a Paloma gate rejects a published good classifier
  * 3 seeds: G +2.0% (d512), +4.0% [+2.6, +5.4] (d768), +4.1% (d1280), all `inconclusive`, because a knowledge or commonsense interval is wider than its 1% harm limit
  * a local FineWeb-Edu classifier probe with 12 seeds at d512 gives G +1.5% [+0.9, +2.1] but commonsense −2.1% [−3.0, −1.2], so the judge says `worse`, and a rule on G alone accepts it. SmolLM2 also reports this commonsense loss. with 3 seeds at d768: G +3.4%, commonsense −1.0% [−1.7, −0.3], Paloma macro 1.4% worse
  * in the full pool web is 17% of the tokens, and the same classifier on the web sources gives G +0.3% (d512), +0.4% (d768), and +0.4% [−0.9, +1.8] (d1280), which three seeds cannot resolve
* seed test, planned before the runs: 9 more seeds (27 runs) for `web_only`, `dclm_web`, and `fineweb_edu_web` at d512, so 12 per arm
  * A/A on the 12 `web_only` runs: the percentile bootstrap that the judge used before said `better` for 5.5% of 3-seed pairs, and each bound missed 0 in about 10% (target 2.5%). the Welch t judge: 0.6% `better` at 3 seeds, 1.4% at 6, bounds miss 0.4–3.2%. a 10,000-experiment simulation agrees
  * the knowledge seed SD of one run is 2.3%, against a 1% harm limit, so knowledge sets the seed count. the README gives `16 s² / (g + h)²` seeds per arm for 80% power: 24 for a 0.9% knowledge gain, 86 for none. a simulation of the complete judge with the real seed covariance gives 78% and 80% power at these counts. use 3 seeds only to rank search candidates. the count is fixed before the runs, and `inconclusive` does not accept
  * with the Welch t judge, 4 of 38 decisions against random move from `worse` to `inconclusive`: a harm near its limit, or 2 seeds at d1280. the large harms stay `worse`
* fresh-seed replication, planned before the runs: 12 new seeds of `dclm_web` and `fineweb_edu_web` and 24 new `web_only` at d512, on the rebased code
  * FineWeb-Edu: `worse` again, commonsense −1.9% [−2.7, −1.1]. against all 24 new controls −1.6% [−2.3, −0.9], so `inconclusive`
  * DCLM: G +2.0% [+1.5, +2.6], but knowledge +0.2% [−1.5, +1.8], so `inconclusive` against the predicted `better`. against all 24 new controls `better`. 12 seeds is below the knowledge power rule
  * A/A on the 24 new controls: `better` for 2.0% of 12-seed pairs. their knowledge SD is 1.6%, and the README keeps 2.3% for the seed count
  * inverse-variance knowledge weights, frozen before the runs, cut the knowledge SD by 22% [15, 29] and give DCLM `better` with 12 seeds. they are in #10424, not in this PR
* add `fast-track-long-string-v1` for raw-corpus tokenization: split at the first whitespace at or after 10,000 characters, and reject a document above 64 MiB with its source and ID
  * bound native tokenizer batches by bytes, from #10419. a local 32 MiB probe kept all 19,532,169 token IDs, and peak RSS went from 4.60 GiB to 2.85 GiB
* `launch.py` resolves the rung budget in `resolve_h100_ladder_budget` and takes a `TrainingSource`, so the quality track uses the same training wiring as `fast-track`
  * add `--seed` and `--data-seed`. `--submit` forwards `WANDB_MODE` and accepts `WANDB_MODE=disabled` without `WANDB_API_KEY`
  * the quality CLIs default to MoE and `d512`, and derive `--data-seed` from `--seed`
* the library fixes of the validation runs are in their own PRs: #10416 (fray actor concurrency), #10417 (levanter eval telemetry), #10418 (artifact load paths), #10419 (tokenizer batches and `tokenizer_content_hash`), #10420 (iris CUDA files and coordinator names), #10421 (datakit CPU group)
  * this PR keeps the #10418 and #10419 changes until they merge, because the quality track loads nested artifacts and imports `tokenizer_content_hash`. the files are the same as in those PRs
  * grug dispatch forwards `WANDB_MODE`
* validation on `cw-us-east-02a`: one 10,695,475,362-token pool from the 291 sources other than `stack-v3`, scored one time at d768, dense models, final eval loss from the training logs [^3]

  | run | selection | Paloma macro | Uncheatable macro |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | d512 control, tie seed 0 / tie seed 1 / model seed 1 | random | 3.704 / 3.699 / 3.682 | 3.264 / 3.264 / 3.245 |
  | d512 ridge head | top `B` | 4.017 (+8.7%) | 3.353 (+2.9%) |
  | d512 inverted ridge head | top `B` of `-score` | 3.706 (+0.3%) | 3.513 (+7.8%) |
  | d512 longest documents | top `B` by UTF-8 bytes | 4.262 (+15.3%) | 3.871 (+18.8%) |
  | d512 shortest documents | bottom `B` by UTF-8 bytes | 3.781 (+2.3%) | 3.248 (−0.3%) |
  | d768 control | random | 3.296 | 2.791 |
  | d768 ridge head | top `B` | 3.597 (+9.1%) | 2.868 (+2.8%) |

  * changes are against the mean of the three d512 controls, or against the d768 control. a new random selection moved Paloma loss by 0.005, and a new model seed by 0.022. the d512 control is near the Hero-cache baseline (3.676)
  * each rung prefix is 10.00·B, each selection is at most one document above `B`, and the random selections have the source mix and mean ridge score of their prefix (0.6097 against 0.6095)
  * the ridge head is a domain filter: its selection has a mean score of 0.818, moves tokens from `finetranslations` and medium-quality web to PDFs, books, and synthetic QA, and improves s2orc (−7.0%) and arXiv physics (−7.6%) but not social text (Twitter +19.0%). the inverted head gives the opposite change on each of these datasets
  * the longest selection is 862 documents (mean 420k tokens, SEC filings, books, PDFs). the shortest selection is 1,223,195 documents (mean 296 tokens)
* known limits
  * `stack-v3` has documents of 79–213 MB, above the 64 MiB limit, so a pool from all 292 sources stops with an error. select the other sources with `--source` until a policy exists
  * the feature stage reads almost all Harrier data, because one Harrier row group holds about 127k rows and a pool samples each one
  * the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer

[^1]: #9371 keeps the Hero-mix track and the `max_train_sequences` rename. it can rebase on this PR after merge.
[^2]: the complete pins from #8270 agree with the normalized shards in shard names, row counts, and ID order. the join compares each ID and stops on a difference.
[^3]: the inverted-head and length probes in this table are in `probe_scorers.py`. W&B ran offline.
[^4]: a selection moves the training mix, and Paloma has its own fixed mix (web-heavy, long documents), so a selection can move Paloma without moving downstream capability. the GLM ridge head and the fusion score are still worse than random or inconclusive under the judge at every rung.
[^5]: 499 of 500 MBPP gold solutions use `\r\n`. in web-only models `\r` tokens carried 25–56% of the MBPP bits, and at d1280 they made the DCLM selection look 22% worse on code and gave `worse` (G −5.8%), while HumanEval had DCLM 7% better. MBPP and GSM8K were scored again on 133 checkpoints with the judge and its limits unchanged: one of 18 judge decisions changed, the d1280 pair above. one merged checkpoint matched a fresh full evaluation exactly.
[^6]: with three runs per arm, the percentile bootstrap over runs and examples covered about 80% at a nominal 95%. the Welch degrees of freedom come from the seed part only.

  * a custom scorer is a `module:factory` that returns a `DocumentQualityScorer`, with a JSON `--classifier-identity`
  * the selected documents keep the raw-pool order, so scores do not change the training order
* add `fast-track-long-string-v1` for raw-corpus tokenization: split at the first whitespace at or after 10,000 characters, and reject a document above 64 MiB with its source and ID
  * bound native tokenizer batches by bytes. a local 32 MiB probe kept all 19,532,169 token IDs, and peak RSS went from 4.60 GiB to 2.85 GiB
* `launch.py` resolves the rung budget in `resolve_h100_ladder_budget` and takes a `TrainingSource`, so the quality track uses the same training wiring as `fast-track`
  * add `--seed` and `--data-seed`. `--submit` forwards `WANDB_MODE` and accepts `WANDB_MODE=disabled` without `WANDB_API_KEY`
  * the quality CLIs default to MoE and `d512`, and derive `--data-seed` from `--seed`
* run fixes
  * iris: repair missing CUDA toolchain files. put the child job and attempt in JAX coordinator names, because sibling training jobs connected to the coordinator of a different job
  * fray: pass actor concurrency to Iris RPC servers, because the 32-thread default let long waits block worker heartbeats. the inference broker sets its concurrency explicitly
  * datakit CPU drivers install the `cpu` group with `datakit`, so that they do not resolve the CUDA Torch wheel
  * artifact loading keeps absolute bucket paths, grug dispatch forwards `WANDB_MODE`, and levanter keeps eval metrics between detail intervals
* known limits
  * `stack-v3` has documents of 79–213 MB, above the 64 MiB limit, so a pool from all 292 sources stops with an error. select the other sources with `--source` until a policy exists
  * the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer

[^1]: #9371 keeps the Hero-mix track and the `max_train_sequences` rename. it can rebase on this PR after merge.

```

</details>

🤖 Thank you. The two concerns had different results:

- `hero_data.harrier` returns a `StepSpec`: this is correct, and it is a real bug on current main. Commit 7b3728aa2 joins the relative path from `hero_data.pinned_map("harrier")` to `hero_data.MANIFEST_PREFIX`, the same rule that the raw pool uses for normalized paths. A new test checks the resolved paths. Commit db6cb6e18 corrects the scoring test, because it replaced `hero_data.harrier` with a string path and hid the bug.
- Row offsets after a dedup filter: this does not apply to the pinned features. The pins point to the complete `datakit/embed/harrier-all/...` outputs from #8270, not to the deduplicated `datakit/embed/harrier/...` outputs. #8270 records that the complete outputs agree with the normalized shards in shard names, row counts, and sampled ID order. The join also compares each Harrier ID with the normalized ID and raises an error if they differ, so a different pin stops the run before it can select wrong data.

🤖 Holistic review of 1b566cc4a80a8ed63ab995cdf68777c59d286284.

> **In short:** The diff adds a quality-classifier track to fast-track: it samples a raw pool, scores it, selects the top `B` tokens, and trains a rung. It also carries seven independent fixes in iris, fray, levanter, and marin. Item 1 recommends moving those fixes to their own PRs. The track works as stated, but its pool skips decontamination and dedup (item 3).

### System
```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph dk["DataKit pins"]
    N["normalized shards (hero_data_paths.json)"]
    HR["Harrier embeddings (pinned_map)"]
  end
  subgraph ft["experiments/grug/fast_track"]
    CS["corpus_sample_cli → RawCorpusPool"]:::added
    QL["quality_labels_cli → ridge head + label_exclusion"]:::added
    QF["quality_features"]:::added
    QP["quality_pipeline: score → select → token cache"]:::added
    L["launch.py: TrainingSource"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph libs["shared libraries"]
    TK["levanter.tokenizers"]:::changed
    FR["fray / iris actor server"]:::changed
    JX["iris.jax.init"]:::changed
  end
  N -->|"ID-interval sample"| CS
  QL -->|"exclusion manifest"| CS
  CS -->|"10·B prefix"| QP
  HR --> QF --> QP
  QP -->|"QualityTrainingSource"| L
  CS --> TK
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

### Why
The fast-track ladder could only measure model changes on a frozen Hero cache. This PR adds a track that holds the model fixed and changes the document scorer, so a classifier is judged by final Paloma macro loss. It splits the quality half out of #9371, and it builds on the complete Harrier pins from #8270.

### Current state
Before the change, `launch.py` was the only entry point. It trained a dense or MoE H100 rung (d512 to d1280) on one frozen Hero v16384 flat cache through `_flat_cache_data_config`. `--match data|compute` set the budget, the seed was fixed at 0, and `--submit` re-ran the command as an Iris job with `--reserve H100`. Nothing in fast-track selected data. DataKit already pins per-source `decontam`, `exact_dups`, `verified_fuzzy_dups`, and `fusion_scores` attributes (`experiments/datakit/hero_data.py:70-75,136-141`), and the DataKit store removes the flagged documents. Iris actor servers always ran 32 method threads, whatever `ActorConfig.max_concurrency` said.

### How
**The pool is a seeded interval of the 128-bit document-ID space, per source, so source shares follow token mass without a full scan.** Row groups are skipped only when their ID statistics exclude the interval (`corpus_sample.py:187-196`). Each map task reads 64 shards.

**Each rung scores the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents up to `B`, in raw-pool order.** `random` ranks the same prefix by a seeded hash, so it is the matched control. A selection holds at most one document above `B` (`ranked_pool.py:142-150`).

**A scorer is a worker-loaded `module:factory` with a JSON identity, and one `ScoredPool` at the largest rung serves every rung.**
```python
# experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py
identity = {
    "raw_pool": raw_pool.name,
    "classifier_identity": candidate.identity,
    "label_exclusion": label_exclusion.identity(),
    "token_budget": token_budget,
    ...
}
step_name = content_step_name("scored-pool", identity, version)
```

**Labels are frozen, and a ridge head is fit on cached Harrier features with an 80/10/10 split by duplicate group.** The pool build requires the label-exclusion manifest at the CLI.

The fixes that ride along: actor concurrency passthrough, JAX coordinator names, CUDA `ptxas` repair, tokenizer batch limits and a content hash, eval-metric sampling in telemetry, `raw_load` context, and the DataKit CPU group. The fast-track tests (54) and the affected iris, fray, levanter, and dispatch unit tests pass locally at head. The PR states the validation table from runs on `cw-us-east-02a`.

### Limitations
- **`stack-v3`:** its 79–213 MB documents exceed the 64 MiB limit, so a pool from all 292 sources fails. Each run must list the other sources with `--source`.
- **Validation evidence:** the probe scorers and the selection report are scratch code, and W&B ran offline, so nothing in the repository reproduces the table.
- **Domain, not quality:** the PR states that the ridge head acts as a domain filter (PDFs and books up, social text down). A Paloma gain can therefore come from domain shift.
- **Incumbent labels:** the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer.
- **Harrier reads:** the feature stage reads almost all Harrier data, because one row group holds about 127k rows.

### Review

**Should fix**
1. `lib/fray/src/fray/iris_backend.py:333` The diff carries seven library fixes that do not depend on the quality track: actor concurrency (fray/iris), `iris/jax/init.py:275` coordinator names, `iris/cluster/setup_scripts.py:173-188` CUDA repair, `levanter/tokenizers.py:644-681` batch limits, `levanter/tracker/telemetry.py:199-206`, `marin/execution/artifact.py:148`, and `marin/datakit/__init__.py:12`. Their owners cannot review them inside a 6k-line experiments PR, and #9371 carries byte-identical copies. Move each fix to its own PR, and keep only the fast-track code here.
2. `lib/fray/src/fray/iris_backend.py:333,742` `ActorConfig.max_concurrency` defaults to 1 (`fray/types.py:578`). Iris used to ignore it, so every actor that uses the default config goes from 32 threads to 1, which can deadlock an actor that calls itself. `LocalClient` still ignores the value, so the two backends now differ. The in-repo callers (Zephyr 100, inference broker 32) set it explicitly. Change the `ActorConfig` default to the old 32, or pass it through only when the caller sets it. Add a fray test that checks the value reaches `ActorServer`. The current test stubs the server with `lambda **_kwargs`.
3. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample.py:349-353` The pool globs the normalized shards with no `decontam`, `exact_dups`, or `verified_fuzzy_dups` filter, while the Hero cache it is compared against applies them. A scorer can then select Paloma-overlapping documents, or many copies of one high-scoring document, at a different rate than the random control. Filter `_sample_records` with the pinned attributes from `hero_data`, and add those pins to `_spec_identity`.
4. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py:778-790` The scored-pool identity hashes the user-supplied `--classifier-identity` but not the `--scorer-factory` path. Two different factories with the same identity JSON silently share one cached `ScoredPool`. Put the factory path into `ScorerSpec` and into the identity.
5. `experiments/grug/fast_track/ranked_pool.py:49-64` `write_parquet_tables` duplicates `zephyr.writers.write_parquet_file` (`lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/writers.py:378`) through a Python `StoragePath.open("wb")` sink. The zephyr writer's own comment (`writers.py:338-346`) says this sink copies whole pages and has pushed workers over their memory limit. The token cache rows here carry `input_ids` for documents of up to 64 MiB. Use `write_parquet_file` at the five call sites.
6. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_pipeline.py:483-648` Rank keys are unique (source and ID), so "top `B` whole documents" is "every row with key ≤ k\*", where k\* is the key at which the cumulative tokens first reach `B`. Sort the `(key, token_count)` pairs, find k\*, and filter the raw prefix in one pass in raw order. This deletes `_summarize_scores`, `_score_range`/`_random_range`, and the second group-by.
7. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample.py:272` The normalized ID is `xxh3_128(text)` (`marin/datakit/normalize.py:125`), so the `sha256(text)` `duplicate_group` marks the same documents as the ID, and the ID check at `corpus_sample.py:268` already excludes them. Key the exclusion and `label_split` on the normalized ID, and drop the column and the per-document SHA-256 (`label_exclusion.py:21`, `quality_labels.py:207`).
8. `lib/levanter/src/levanter/tokenizers.py:781` `tokenizer_content_hash` hashes the whole staged directory. A leftover `.tmp`, or a mirror staging that copies more files than the HF allow-patterns, changes the hash, and `require_tokenizer_content` (`contracts.py:76`) then fails the run. An HF cache snapshot with symlinks raises. Its only callers are in fast-track. Move it to `experiments/grug/fast_track/contracts.py`, and hash only the `tokenizer*.json` files.
9. `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_labels.py:34-37` The default label inputs are in personal scratch prefixes (`marin/user/rav/...`, `marin/user/muchanem/...`). The frozen-label artifact then depends on files that their owners can delete. Copy them under `datakit/`, and pin that path.
10. `experiments/grug/fast_track/corpus_sample_cli.py:25` `--max-training-tokens` defaults to 17,478,713,344, which requests a 175B-token raw pool. That is 16× the 10.7B pool that was validated, which took 25 minutes. Also, `CorpusSampleSpec.label_exclusion` defaults to `None` (`corpus_sample.py:77`), so the exclusion is required only at the CLI. Make both explicit.

**Tests to drop**
11. `test_pinned_feature_sources_resolve_complete_harrier_paths` (`test_quality_features.py:123`): it rebuilds the path with `pinned_map` in the expectation, which copies the implementation.
12. `test_corpus_sample_low_probability_preserves_global_rank_order_and_prefix` and `test_corpus_sample_grows_integer_cutoff_until_pool_is_large_enough` (`test_corpus_sample.py:207,362`): they recompute the expectation with the private `_sampling_cutoff` and `_rank_salt`, which copies the implementation.
13. The asserts on `num_train_steps == 16669` and `training_tokens == 17478713344` in `test_quality_cli_reuses_scored_pool_for_moe_rung` (`test_quality_pipeline.py:261-262`): they project the ladder table, not quality-track behavior.
14. `test_text_scorer_selects_only_after_the_deterministic_raw_prefix`, `test_larger_training_budget_expands_the_raw_candidate_prefix`, and `test_max_scored_pool_matches_exact_rung_pools_through_raw_cache` (`test_quality_scoring.py:63,249,292`) all check prefix-then-select, and `:209` and `:389` both check the constant-score error. Replace them with two parametrized tests.

**Related PRs**
15. #9371: it has byte-identical copies of 30 of these files, including every library fix, and differs only by its Hero-mix track and older versions of four pool files. Merge this PR first, then rebase #9371 to keep only the Hero-mix files, as its footnote says. If item 1 moves the library fixes out, remove them from #9371 too.
16. #9718 (draft) conflicts in `experiments/grug/dispatch.py` in either merge order. The other overlapping PRs (#10074, #9863, #10067, #9495, #9706, #9799, #9502, #10169, #8567) merge without a conflict.

Since the earlier review at `1b566cc4`, the PR also changes how the track decides whether a selection is better. It no longer uses Paloma macro loss. It scores saved dense checkpoints on downstream tasks (`downstream_eval`) and compares candidate and control runs by capability group with a bootstrap (`quality_judge`). The track hangs together, but two of its inputs need attention before it serves as a decision gate. The pool skips the DataKit decontamination and dedup attributes, which matters more now that GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP and MMLU decide the outcome. The judge also turns a missing or mismatched input into `inconclusive` instead of an error.

  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px

Each rung ranks the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents up to `B`, in raw order. `random` ranks the same prefix by hash and serves as the matched control. The judge reads `downstream_records.parquet` and the `text` block of `metrics.json`. It takes the correct-choice BPB for English cloze, gold-solution BPB for code and math, and the fixed-target loss at 3968 tokens of context. It draws one paired example index per task and resamples the runs. A candidate is `better` when the 95% lower bound of the E/C/M mean is above zero and no group passes its harm limit.

**Evidence and limits.** The fast-track tests and `tests/test_grug_dispatch.py` pass locally at head (63 passed). Filter `_sample_records` with the pinned attributes from `hero_data` (`decontaminated`, `exact_dups`, `VERIFIED_FUZZY_DUPS_PATH`), and add those pins to `_spec_identity` (`corpus_sample.py:444`).
- **2. Should fix:** `experiments/grug/fast_track/quality_judge.py:78-92` accepts inputs it cannot compare. A checkpoint scored with `downstream_eval --skip-text` writes `"text": {}`, so `np.mean([])` makes `L` NaN. Every comparison involving `L` is then false, and the judge prints `inconclusive` instead of failing. It also ignores the `tasks_version` and `scorer_version` that `metrics.json` records (`downstream_eval.py:379-380`; the scorer is already at `v4`). It takes `example_counts` from `control[0]` alone, so runs from different task copies are paired by position or raise an `IndexError`. In `read_run_scores`, raise when no set has `fixed_target_documents >= 5`. In `judge`, require equal versions and equal `example_id` arrays for each task across all runs.

Should fix:** `experiments/grug/fast_track/downstream_tasks.py:270` stores the frozen `downstream-cloze-v2` tasks under a personal prefix (`marin/user/rav/...`), and the module's `__main__` rewrites that same root in place. topics.title: [taskforge] Keep unit tests independent of the ports catalog
topics.body:
Run Taskforge's agentic unit tests with shell-only ledger tasks. Their solvers return scripted answers, so downloading CPython adds a network dependency without exercising those behaviors. A fixture rejects catalog and runtime downloads while the existing grading, evidence, budget and review assertions run on real ShellSim machines.

Remove the guest-Python acceptance test and its dedicated solver helper. The repository's testing policy assigns interpreter and ports acceptance coverage to ShellSim.

ShellSim's public catalog returns HTTP 403, causing 11 failures on unchanged main and blocking [the Taskforge check on #10556](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39909748946/job/120269935016). This change isolates unit coverage; it does not restore the external runtime service. [Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/849).

topics.title: [harbor] Run installed agents with only explicitly approved service access
topics.body:
Run installed Harbor agents without public internet access during task execution. Permit only a scoped model gateway and explicitly declared task services. A broad local-network allowance is insufficient: local addresses can expose controllers, other jobs, storage and metadata services.

Done when:

- Separate dependency preparation from execution. Receive the task Dockerfile/build context or immutable image reference, prepare compatible pinned agent dependencies in an isolated build stage, and retain verified build and package provenance. Execution must not resolve or download packages at startup. This does not require one universal image for all tasks.
- Enforce default-deny egress on the processes running installed-agent code and their tool sandboxes, covering IPv4 and IPv6. Allow only the approved model gateway and declared task-service endpoints/ports. Define necessary DNS access explicitly and prevent it from becoming unrestricted external access.
- Block public internet, unrelated jobs, the Iris controller, production storage services, host/provider metadata endpoints and undeclared private or carrier-grade NAT addresses. A dedicated service provisioned for the task may be allowlisted, including a task-local database or object-store fixture; declaring it must not grant access to production services or credentials. Enforce this below the agent process; environment flags or agent instructions are insufficient. Redirects, proxy settings and DNS changes must not bypass the policy.
- The model gateway authenticates a narrowly scoped trial capability and cannot act as an arbitrary network proxy. Model-provider credentials stay outside the agent environment. A separate trusted collector uploads artifacts without giving the agent storage credentials.
- Tasks that genuinely need external access declare that requirement and use a separately approved, auditable exception policy. No silent fallback to unrestricted networking. Document the installed-agent startup behavior that is supported offline.
- Run representative tasks for every retained agent from the initial Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE audit successfully with public internet blocked. Verify permitted model/task-service requests succeed and controlled attempts to reach public, private, metadata and undeclared endpoints fail. Confirm failed downloads or update checks produce actionable redacted logs and do not weaken the policy.

The companion launch-path issue owns the runnable Iris recipe; the companion security audit reviews the retained agents. Reuse #9816 and #10486 for isolation and credential boundaries, #10481 for build/runtime evidence, and #10485 for approval of elevated infrastructure privileges. Network exceptions require their own explicit approval scope.

Companion issues: #10487, #10488.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The current Iris sandbox profile withholds cluster credentials, but its only usable network choices are no egress and broad public IPv4 egress. Kubernetes permits DNS plus public destinations for the latter; it has no per-trial list of model and task services. Marin's trusted Harbor driver receives storage credentials, so installed-agent code needs a distinct trust and network boundary. This spans Iris networking, Harbor's runtime, and #10487, #10481, #10486 and #10488; the duplicate-work search found no open PR for #10489.

**Relevant code**
- [`sandbox.py#L59-L120`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/sandbox.py#L59-L120) — three egress modes; sandbox defaults to INTERNET.
- [`controller.py#L465-L493`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L465-L493) — DNS and public IPv4 allowance.
- [`tasks.py#L837-L860`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L837-L860) — pod isolation selected at dispatch.
- [`driver_config.py#L203-L208`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d9d49f2c656cbb72af3148de09a90b27af2dfc3b/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L203-L208) — trusted driver inherits storage credentials.

# Proposed Fix

## Design

1. Add a trusted, per-trial service-access contract at Harbor preflight and Iris submission: one model gateway identity and endpoint, plus explicit task-service identities, addresses and ports. The default is empty. Resolve service names in the trusted control plane, reject wildcards, broad CIDRs, controller/storage/metadata targets and undeclared destinations, and bind the validated policy to the job attempt. A task file or agent process cannot extend it. External-access tasks require a separate, reviewed exception record with destination, purpose and expiry; an unsupported policy fails before execution.
2. Move task image and agent dependency preparation to an isolated build phase. Accept a task Dockerfile/context or immutable image reference; resolve and pin the retained agent's complete dependencies there, retain artifact hashes and build provenance, and hand execution an immutable image digest. Do not run package managers or update checks at agent startup. Require the post-install, per-attempt evidence from #10481 before the first agent action. Keep build network permissions separate from execution permissions.
3. Run installed-agent code and its tool commands inside the same restricted execution boundary, separate from the trusted Harbor driver and uploader. Build on `CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX`: no host network, service-account token, controller token, cluster Secret, shared cache, runtime socket or privileged mount. Enforce default-deny ingress and egress for IPv4 and IPv6 below the agent process, with only the gateway and declared service addresses/ports admitted. Allow DNS only through a restricted resolver for declared names, or omit it for fixed endpoints. Add node-level enforcement for host and metadata traffic, and verify the actual CNI before enabling a backend: [Kubernetes NetworkPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/) alone does not guarantee same-node isolation, and its IP-block behavior can vary around service address translation. If the backend cannot enforce the contract, reject the trial.
4. Give the agent a trial-scoped model capability accepted only for the selected model's inference API. The gateway must reject arbitrary URLs, CONNECT and forwarding to other services; provider keys remain in the trusted gateway. Put artifact collection in a separate trusted process and network namespace that reads only the trial's output, uploads with its own storage credentials, and cannot pass those credentials into the agent. Coordinate effective env and mount validation with #10486 and the runnable Iris recipe with #10487. #10488 determines which pinned agents may use the path.

## Validation and rollout

First test policy validation and generated pod/network manifests. Then use an isolated test cluster to prove permitted model calls and a declared local database/object-store fixture work, while public internet, controller, unrelated job, production storage, metadata, undeclared private/CGNAT, IPv6, alternate DNS, redirect and injected proxy probes fail from both agent and tool processes. Repeat after a failed setup and a retry; confirm redacted diagnostics and no silent fallback. Finally run representative coding and trace tasks for each agent retained by #10488 with public internet blocked, and publish the tested backend/CNI and offline startup contract in #10487. No production rollout until the live enforcement probes pass.

## Costs / risks

Per-trial policy and a restricted resolver/gateway add infrastructure and operational work. Standard NetworkPolicy can miss node-local traffic; a passing manifest test cannot establish isolation. Keep unsupported backends disabled until their enforcement is measured.

## Open questions

- Which Iris backend and cluster will #10487 certify first, and what node-level enforcement can it provide for pod-to-host traffic and IPv6?
- How should short-lived task-service addresses be bound to a trial without admitting other pods or services at the same IP/port?

topics.title: [datakit] Repair orphan reasoning close tags
topics.body:
Replace unmatched `</thinking>` and `</think>` tags in assistant-message content from SWE-ZERO-12M and daVinci-Dev env-native with paragraph breaks. The repair preserves balanced tags, keeps adjacent reasoning sentences separate, and counts removed tags. User messages and tool results bypass the repair.

SWE-ZERO chat conversion now repairs extracted reasoning before enclosing it in `<think>...</think>`. Chat source validation rejects either `<thinking>` tag so this markup cannot pass into Harmony records. In one normalized shard per source, 15 of 1,944 SWE-ZERO documents and 16 of 528 daVinci documents contained the reported pattern. Version bumps create new cache paths for the affected steps. Historical Hero data accessors retain their materialized v1 paths; the new outputs have not yet been built or selected for a cooldown.

Part of #10518

topics.title: Add Skill2Env to RL Data Atlas
topics.body:
Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, conversion, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

Current status (2026-10-22): catalog registration (#10120) and Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198) are merged. QUICK conversion in #10154 is ready for human review at `4b45b34ebf`. The full-release run confirmed 7,452 converted tasks and 44 exclusions. Runnable SAMPLE/FULL campaigns remain unfinished; live Atlas publication has not been verified. The earlier #9632 implementation is superseded.

The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to release version 1.0.1 / revision 2 with 7,496 tasks, digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`.

Completed validation:

- The full-release QUICK driver at `4b45b34ebf`, recipe revision 10, processed cached packages in 75 batches: 7,452 converted, 42 `native_outputs` exclusions, and 2 `native_workspace` exclusions. There were no unexpected failures. Every converted TaskSpec was read back and every uploaded batch archive was checksum-verified.
- Native and converted grading matched across 146 controls for all 29 digest-pinned capture exceptions. Controls cover initial state, reference solutions, corrupted state, deleted state, and empty submissions, plus one symlink control. Both reward components and scalar means matched. One native reference solution scored 0.98; conversion reproduced that value. Matching rewards do not establish grader correctness.
- All 22 focused tests and mechanical lint pass. CI at `4b45b34ebf` has 18 successful checks and 20 skipped, with none failed or pending. The latest independent review of that exact commit found no actionable code defects. Its PR-description cleanup is applied.

The 44 exclusions remain explicit because the current runtime cannot preserve their execution contracts or validation found a mismatch. They include filesystem metadata, live-process and startup requirements, inaccessible state, and incomplete Git metadata in a cached export. Seven candidates failed symlink/executable-state comparisons. The Go-based `yeet` task scored 1.0 natively and 0.0 after conversion and stays excluded. The cached `lsp-edit-symbol` failure has not been established as an upstream dataset defect. The adapter introduces no new service fixture or privileged capture mechanism.

Remaining work:

- [ ] Human review and merge of #10154.
- [ ] Resolve and pin actor/verifier images, configure native resource limits, and validate the runnable campaign path. QUICK still retains unresolved build contexts.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign to assess execution, grading, task quality, and model difficulty. Full-corpus conversion and the selected Docker controls do not complete this assessment.
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign and verify the live Atlas source entry. This can proceed independently of runnable integration.

<details>
<summary>Historical investigation and superseded implementation plan (before #10120)</summary>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.

```python

topics.title: [post-training] Run the Baby RSI loop as streams over real boxes
topics.body:
* part of #9638
* replace the stub feedback graph with the rsi loop of [Post-training: Boxes/Systems](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qRs0UIuYIzMOdIchHy6OItT2VUKJVQFK4nJ0L2zinZ4) over real boxes, written as async streams, so the data drives the loop and there is no `while` [^1]
  ```python
  rollouts = Broadcast[TaskRollouts]()
  failures = failed_runs(rollouts.listen(), config.max_pass_rate)
  ideas = boxes.analyze_failed_runs(batched(failures, config.failures_per_analysis))
  tasks = mix(Source(seed_tasks, 1 - share), Source(boxes.generate_tasks(ideas), share), seed=config.seed)
  return rollouts.publish(boxes.train(tasks))
  ```
* seed: `TaskPool` streams the Smartie RL pool of Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1 (69,487 tasks, pinned hf revision) in an order whose every prefix keeps the strata weights (structural 82.6%, competitive coding 10.9%, reasoning gym 2.8%, stem mcqa 2.7%, calendar 1.1%)
  * in the trained groups of all 4 final runs, the seed strata shares are within 0.0004 of these weights
  * structural rows convert with `structure_closure_task`; script graders run in bubblewrap with the host python instead of the daytona image
* train: `train(runner, server, learner, tasks)` is on-policy grpo with a lora adapter beside a `vllm serve` with runtime lora loading; `VllmPolicy` is an exact-token `rolloutengine` model (local chat template, completions with token ids and logprobs, continuation splicing)
* analyze: `analyze_failed_runs` (#10265) on batches of one failed attempt per task that the policy passes at most 25% of the time
* generate: one agentic taskforge session per idea, with the served policy as the gate's solver; the build program of each accepted task makes training instances and held-out probes
* `taskforge.agentic` (#10444): `submit` also takes the build program and, after the other checks and before the review, checks that it writes the task again and that 8 other ids give runnable tasks whose reference answers vary [^2]; `task_instances` runs the program again on the workspace snapshot
* a preempted run continues from its last uploaded adapter and optimizer state, skips the pool tasks it trained, and gives back the synthesized instances it did not train on
* `run.py evaluate` and `report.py`: base (twice), control and rsi adapters on held-out pool tasks and probes, paired bootstrap over tasks; `audit.py` has deepseek v4.1 flash audit the accepted tasks
* drop the `curriculum_sft` → `baby_rsi` rename and the taskcompendium rollout engine of the old stack, which main's `rolloutengine` replaced
* result, qwen3-4b-instruct-2507, lora r32, 120 steps × 32 tasks × 8 attempts, rsi vs a control that trains on pool tasks only, two seeds pooled:

  | held-out set | tasks | base | control | rsi | rsi − control (95% ci) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | probes of the synthesized families | 358 | 0.390 | 0.278 | 0.455 | +0.177 [+0.134, +0.218] |
  | smartie validation tasks | 800 | 0.232 | 0.393 | 0.375 | −0.018 [−0.036, +0.000] |

  * of the 104 probes that the base never passes in 8 attempts, rsi passes 49% at least once, control 21%, a second base evaluation 24%
  * seed 0 was best at step 60 (+0.162 over control) and lost some of it by step 120 as both arms answered shorter; seed 1 gained after step 60 (+0.251 at step 120)
  * deepseek found no problem in 11 of 25 and 8 of 20 accepted tasks, all of which the glm reviewer accepted
  * synthesized tasks entered training at 11 (seed 0) and 14 (seed 1) different steps between step 28 and step 119, while training continued, and made 17% and 21% of the trained groups
  * outputs in `s3://marin-us-east-02a/user/rav/projects/baby-rsi/run-{4,5}/`

[^1]: `job.sh` maps the pod's assigned gpu (from `/var/run/nvidia-container-devices`) to `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and vllm binds a free port: a privileged coreweave task sees all 8 gpus of its node and shares the host network, and the first runs collided on gpu 0 and port 8011
[^2]: with qwen3-1.7b one accepted family had the reference answers 3, 4 or 5, and the policy learned to answer a guess without the work (0.06 against 0.51 for the control on that family's probes)

🤖 Holistic review of `3e27e12d5e87f7770fdcbd4d5dbad11d6c361739`. I would address the resume and evaluation findings before merging.

The change replaces the earlier stub graph with a live training loop. A stratified Smartie pool feeds GRPO; each step runs graded attempts with the current LoRA adapter, then loads the next adapter into vLLM. Failed attempts become capability ideas through the existing analysis pipeline. Taskforge uses those ideas and the served policy to accept new task families. Their generated training instances reenter the task stream; probes go to a separate evaluation. The control arm runs the same trainer on pool tasks alone.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  pool["TaskPool: Smartie train"] --> mix["mix: pool + synthesized tasks"]
  mix --> train["train: graded attempts + GRPO/LoRA"]
  server["vLLM / VllmPolicy"] --> train
  train -->|"load adapter"| server
  train -->|"TaskRollouts"| broadcast["Broadcast"]
  broadcast --> records["Group records + checkpoints"]
  broadcast --> failures["failed_runs + batches"]
  failures --> analysis["GLM / Zephyr analysis"]
  analysis -->|"CapabilityIdea"| forge["Taskforge agent + gate + build program"]
  server -->|"gate solver"| forge
  forge -->|"training instances"| mix
  forge -->|"held-out probes"| eval["evaluate base / control / RSI"]
  validation["Smartie validation"] --> eval
  records -->|"adapters"| eval
```

The reported two-seed result is +0.177 [0.134, 0.218] RSI minus control on 358 probes from synthesized families, and −0.018 [−0.036, 0.000] on 800 held-out pool tasks. This supports improvement on the generated families; the pool result does not show a broader gain. The separate DeepSeek audit found no problem in 19 of 45 accepted tasks, which limits how confidently the probe gain can be read. I ran the local Baby RSI and Taskforge agent tests in the Taskforge environment: 6 passed. I did not rerun the GPU experiment.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix — checkpoint identity:** [`run.py:299`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e27e12d5e87f7770fdcbd4d5dbad11d6c361739/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/run.py#L299-L326) loads the last adapter from `--output-dir` before checking the model, seed, pool revision, or training settings that produced it. The pool is pinned, but the base model is passed as a Hugging Face name without a revision to vLLM, the tokenizer, and the learner. A relaunch with changed settings can continue the old optimizer on a different task order or model while retaining one run identity. Store a run manifest with the resolved model revision and training settings, and reject a resume that disagrees with it.

- **2. Should fix — failed synthesis becomes permanently known:** [`feedback.py:137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e27e12d5e87f7770fdcbd4d5dbad11d6c361739/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/feedback.py#L137-L146) writes `idea.json` even when an agent result has `failure` and zero tasks; [`known_ideas`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e27e12d5e87f7770fdcbd4d5dbad11d6c361739/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/resume.py#L88-L93) then suppresses that capability on every resume. Analysis and session exceptions are also logged and skipped, so an RSI run can finish as a pool-only run after an outage. Record failed outcomes separately, retry incomplete ideas, and surface the number of successful synthesized tasks in the run result.

- **3. Should fix — duplicate probes count as independent tasks:** [`held_out`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e27e12d5e87f7770fdcbd4d5dbad11d6c361739/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/feedback.py#L182-L188) checks probes against the accepted task and training instances, but never adds a kept probe to `seen`. Deduplicate probe content across each evaluation's roots before scoring and report the unique count.

- **4. Related PR — coordinate the Taskforge stack:** This diff includes the agentic Taskforge implementation also under [#10439](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10439) and the split [#10444](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10444) → [#10445](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10445) → [#10446](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10446) stack. Land the chosen Taskforge stack first, then rebase this PR so its RSI changes have one dependency and one review surface.

topics.title: [Epic] Post-training Data manager
topics.body:
🤖 *Public definition of the **Post-training Data** role — what it owns, the boundary with the supervisor, its current near-term work, and its compute envelope. (The reporting line and any evaluative / "is the overhead worth it" notes are tracked privately.)*

## Role shape

**Post-training Data manager** is tasked with maintaining and freshening the library data Marin uses for post-training. Two halves: **(1) synthesis** — building brand-new, high-quality datasets to fill the gaps uncovered through experiments; and **(2) inspection & analysis** — reading RL rollout traces and samples from existing SFT and RL tasks to surface hidden data issues. Keeps the data landscape organized (formatting + ETL), runs eval-set decontamination in collaboration with the Evals manager, and marshals volunteer effort + purchased data to support. This is the data-quality backbone for post-training — *not* accountability for the training runs the data feeds.

**Scope split:**
- ✅ **The contributor owns:** dataset synthesis; trace/sample inspection + analysis (RL rollouts, SFT/RL task samples) to find hidden issues; data inventory + organization (formatting, ETL); eval-set decontamination / leakage checks; coordinating volunteers and purchased data; and small, compute-limited supplementary experiments to support data-centric decisions.
- 🚫 **The supervisor owns:** high-level data strategy / prioritization (which gaps matter), budget approval for purchased data and for larger compute, and accountability for data decisions bubbling into the actual **hero runs**.

**Decision rights (what "owns" means concretely):** autonomous inside the owned box — synthesis, inspection/analysis, ETL, decontamination, and **compute-limited** experiments run without sign-off. Outside the box — **a larger experiment, or any purchased-data / large-compute spend** — the contributor files an issue and tags the supervisor, who decides. A boundary of authority, not a seniority statement.

## Scope — next 2–4 weeks

Near-term only; further work is added as it becomes concrete (no long-range forecast). Each item becomes its own child issue as it's scoped:

- [ ] First trace/sample audit — *to be scoped* (e.g. inspect a sample of current RL-rollout traces + SFT-task samples to surface hidden issues)
- [ ] First decontamination pass — *to be scoped* (eval-set leakage check on a current post-training dataset)
- [ ] First synthesized dataset / ETL task — *to be scoped* (fill a specific gap uncovered by experiments; land it formatted + organized)

## Compute estimate

Deliberately **compute-limited** by design (larger runs are gated via issue + supervisor, per decision rights above):

- Limited scale, primarily pre-emptible TPU and laptop
- $5,000/month frontier-API credits (or equivalent hosted-compute calls)
- 500 containers, steady state

topics.title: [inference] Launch multi-host TPU serving within one Iris slice
topics.body:
Allow `marin-serve iris` and the evaluation launcher to serve one model across a multi-host TPU slice. A `v4-32` request now submits four replicas coscheduled by `tpu-name`, starts a Ray head on rank zero and workers on the other hosts, and publishes the serving endpoint only from rank zero. Single-host serving keeps its existing path; multi-host serving requires the isolated TPU vLLM backend, one serving instance spanning the host replicas, and streaming weights shared by all hosts.

Ray runs inside the same isolated environment as vLLM. Iris supplies the GCS, Ray Client, dashboard and dashboard-agent ports; worker ports are kernel-selected. Ray log deduplication is disabled on every host. Startup reports the Ray process log on failure, and shutdown stops only the job's own processes. Explicit multi-host evaluation overrides use direct serving rather than the single-host request broker; automatic hardware selection is unchanged.

The [four-host smoke test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10270#issuecomment-6350331747) established the launch recipe on v4-32 with `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` in BF16, TP16/PP1: generation succeeded and one 5,279-token teacher-forced item matched the H100 reference at mean absolute logprob difference 0.0153. topics.title: Harbor eval record fails as infra_failed when one trial raises unclassified DaytonaError
topics.body:
A single plain `DaytonaError` causes a Harbor eval record to be marked `infra_failed` with empty `metrics`. Harbor's error taxonomy (`harbor_config/errors.py`) lists `DaytonaProcessError`, `DaytonaDockerSetupError`, and `DaytonaSandboxStopError`, but omits the base `DaytonaError` raised by the Daytona SDK when session creation fails. The runner records the trial as `unknown:DaytonaError`, so `_evaluation_outcome` (`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py`) rejects the whole run as taxonomy drift.

The affected TBLite-100 run used Harbor 38742b0f. Its [record](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261020-233725-v7-plain-low-v01-20261020-openthoughts-tblite-100-66da/record.json) reports `EvaluationError: Harbor eval encountered error names absent from its taxonomy under '…/results': unknown:DaytonaError=1`. Trial `harbor_openthoughts-tblite_8b8e96c3cc54/cpp-daemon-sighup-segfault__2uaQ4iL/attempts/000` has `exception_type: DaytonaError` and message `Failed to create session:` with empty detail. The same run's `results/harbor_result.json` already contains a complete aggregate: 100 attempted, 93 scored, 12 solved, mean reward 0.146, and errors `AgentTimeoutError 42, ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure 4, TmuxBatchProtocolError 3, TmuxSessionEndedError 2, TmuxCommandError 1, unknown:DaytonaError 1`.

About 2 h of an 8×H100 serve produced a usable score that the record discards. The same error can affect any Daytona-backed Harbor eval.

A session-create failure should count as an infrastructure error because the model never ran. For this run, the record should report 12 solved of 93 scored, mean reward 0.146, and completion 93/100 = 0.93, above the default 0.9 gate (`DEFAULT_MIN_COMPLETION_RATE`). It should list these seven unscored trials and their error types:

| Task | Error |
|---|---|
| basic-message-queue | TmuxBatchProtocolError |
| grid-pathfinding | TmuxBatchProtocolError |
| iot-device-registration-server | TmuxBatchProtocolError |
| maven-slf4j-conflict | TmuxSessionEndedError |
| sign-vector-game | TmuxSessionEndedError |
| image-tile-identification | TmuxCommandError |
| cpp-daemon-sighup-segfault | DaytonaError |

Classify `DaytonaError` as `ErrorCategory.INFRASTRUCTURE` in `src/harbor_config/errors.py` in marin-community/harbor (missing at 38742b0f and on main), then bump the Harbor pin. The drift check works as designed; the missing name causes the rejection.
