topics.title: [grug] Add hero launch controls for a context-length switch
topics.body:
The scaling-ladder launcher holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, and gate/router weight decay therefore match the 4K run. The hero's context length, QK multipliers, and capacity factor live in HERO_MODEL. --qk-mult and --qk-mult-long-scale (global layers only) override the QK multipliers for trial arms and ladder rungs; trial arms set the context length on their branch alongside the history. Eval packs at the training context, as on main, so the eval_dropless/* series shift at each switch. For short trial arms, --eval-every overrides the eval cadence.

The hero's context history is checked in, like the data mix's switch point: HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES in launch_scaling_ladder.py lists each context the d6144 hero trained at before its current one with the step it ended at, and HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL holds the parent's cumulative training FLOPs at the last switch. A context-switch deploy PR edits Python only: it sets the HERO_MODEL fields, appends one entry to HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES, and sets HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL, so a second switch (4K to 16K, then 16K to 64K) is described exactly and trigger_hero.sh is unchanged. The launcher turns the history into a FlopsBaseline at the last end step and, through the prior_context_phases argument of harrier_mix_2026_08_18_data_config, into LmDataConfig.prior_context_phases, with each earlier phase's Harrier stage schedule and shuffle blocks at its own batch size, so the Harrier sources continue from their earlier reads. At d6144 the launcher rejects a history that does not start at 4K, repeats a length between adjacent phases (including the current context), or disagrees with whether the baseline is set. LmDataConfig rejects end steps that do not increase, and rejects any switch below the 1e23-FLOP simulated-epoching cutoff because the data offsets assume each source reads its whole cache. The narrow rungs take no history.

topics.title: [eval] Retry context lookup failures before evaluating
topics.body:
Retry transient failures when reading the inference server's context length. After three failed attempts, propagate the error instead of launching Evalchemy with a default context limit. Permanent HTTP errors fail immediately.

A timeout or HTTP 429 previously caused the first evaluation attempt to omit the context limit. A successful lookup on retry then changed the settings, so FineStore refused to resume. Five evals hit this failure.

[Investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/828).
topics.head: a2afa11898a20cad5e381ffa3f26664194fa6d7e

topics.title: [levanter] Run Belay's ReLU² experts on cudnn-frontend MXFP8 kernels
topics.body:
Add `moe_mxfp8_expert_kernels=cudnn_frontend`, an opt-in backend that runs the ragged backend's ungated ReLU² routed experts on nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.31.0's fused MXFP8 grouped GEMMs. It needs `mxfp8_expert_wgrad=true` and bf16 dispatch (`moe_mxfp8_dispatch=false`). The default stays `quack`, and its layout and traced program are unchanged.

All six expert GEMMs run in MXFP8. The up GEMM applies ReLU² and quantizes its output in its epilogue. The backward GEMM through `w_down` fuses the ReLU² backward. It writes each row's routing-weight gradient into one slot per N tile, and the slots are summed afterwards, so the result is deterministic. It also regenerates the token-quantized `relu(c)²` for `dW_down` from the saved bf16 pre-activation `c`. Tokens and output cotangents are quantized along rows and tokens in one Triton pass. The kernels need every expert's rows to start on a 256-row boundary. Expert MLPs now report a receiver alignment: this one reports 256 and the existing QuACK, Pallas and `ragged_dot` paths report 1. The kernels stop at the last expert's received rows, so unused receiver capacity costs nothing. The JAX wrappers follow marin#10415.

On one B200 at the GB200 hero's per-GPU expert chunk (6 experts, latent 3072, width 4608), QuACK uses the `TUNED_GB200` schedules. Times are forward plus backward in ms, the median of 3 rotated rounds with each arm in its own process:

| Receiver buffer | QuACK | cudnn-frontend |
|---|---:|---:|
| 688,128 rows, all received, balanced | 91.0 | 61.0 |
| 688,128 rows, all received, one expert empty | 93.8 | 61.1 |
| 655,360 of 688,128 rows received (capacity factor 1.05) | 88.4 | 58.3 |

- **Where the gain comes from:** the backward, which takes 70 ms on QuACK and 39 ms here.
- **Memory:** peak program memory is 34.8 GiB, against 40.5 GiB for QuACK.
- **Error:** relative error against float32 is the same for both paths at normal and at 1e-9 cotangent scale (y 5.8%, dx 6.5%, dW_up 6.5%). The exception is dW_down: at normal scale it is 3.48% here against 3.45% for QuACK, because `relu(c)²` is regenerated from bf16 `c`.
- **Determinism:** both paths are bitwise deterministic across reruns.

Over 48 layers the expert-MLP saving is about 1.4 s per step on these B200 numbers. That estimate is unmeasured on GB200 and in the full step.

The new path has run only on one GPU. On CPU, an alignment-4 test MLP checks the aligned ragged all-to-all against the packed layout, with drops and two chunks. The two-GPU end-to-end case `ungated_relu2_mxfp8_wgrad_cudnn` in `experiments/grug/fast_track/test_mxfp8_swiglu_experts.py` needs two SM100 GPUs and has not run. A rack A/B would compare the GB200 recipe with `--model-set moe_mxfp8_expert_kernels=cudnn_frontend --model-set mxfp8_expert_wgrad=true --model-set moe_mxfp8_dispatch=false` against the same flags with `quack`, and against the current recipe with MXFP8 dispatch.

`uv.lock` is relocked with uv 0.12.21, which keeps lock revision 3. It adds nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.31.0 and a torch 2.10.0 entry with its CUDA libraries; the rest of the diff is rewritten resolution markers. The root `pipeline` extra does not get the dependency, because its `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.0` pin conflicts with cudnn-frontend's `>=4.6.2`.

topics.title: [levanter] Continue mixture reads across a context-length switch
topics.body:
Harrier's shuffle blocks change from a fixed 256 sequences to a fixed 2^20 tokens (io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len). At 4K the two are identical, so the live run's data order is unchanged. At a longer context, the token-sized blocks keep the outer block permutation the same, and only the order of sequences inside each 512-block shuffle window changes. With the old 256-sequence blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T.

The new LmDataConfig.prior_context_phases describes the earlier context lengths of a resumed run, one ContextPhaseConfig per length. With prior_context_phases set, each source skips the unread rest of the shuffle window it was reading at the switch step and starts its next window, so nothing is served twice. At a 216000-step handoff this skips about 52B tokens, 0.65% of the rest of the run. MixtureDataset takes per-source start offsets to apply the skip. Every phase must give positive weight to the same sources, because a training config drops zero-weight sources and that changes the shuffle keys of the rest; a change in the active sources is rejected. So is a phase at the same sequence length as the one before it, since there a source could continue in place and the skip would only discard data. The seed, the source order, and restoring at the last switch step cannot be checked from the config, so the field docstring states them. The offsets come from each source's true position in the earlier phase, so they also absorb the main-mixture boundary moving from step 108000 to 108096 at 16K. The grug train loop builds its mixture through the new LmDataConfig.train_mixture.

Part of #9615
topics.head: aa184d6ddbe72291a0b3c896c6d8f9ed3fe4134d

comments.body:
🤖 Review notes from a walkthrough of the change. None of these block the mechanism; the rename is the main request.

**Rename the prior-phase types.** `PriorDataPhase` is easy to misread: "data" does not say which aspect of the data changed, and in the Harrier code and docs "phase" already means a mixture phase (`_SPEC.phase_weights`, the JSON `phases`, "Phase 1/2/3" in `docs/reports/hero-mixture-log.md`). A context switch can fall in the middle of a mixture phase, so the two divisions of the run need different names. Suggested names:

| Current | Suggested |
| --- | --- |
| `PriorDataPhase` | `ContextPhaseConfig` |
| `LmDataConfig.prior_phases` | `prior_context_phases` |
| `MixturePhase` | `ContextPhase` |

This follows the `FooConfig` → `Foo` pattern: `ContextPhaseConfig` declares a past context phase in steps, and `ContextPhase` is the form `skip_to_window_offsets` uses (start step, `BatchSchedule`, stages in sequence indices). The `ContextPhase` list also holds the current phase. The `MixturePhase` docstring ("A phase of the mixture for ...") should change with it, for example to "One context phase of the run, with its batch schedule and stages in sequence indices." Please also add a sentence to the field docstring that batch-size changes within one context belong in `BatchSchedule`, and that `prior_context_phases` describes earlier context lengths only.

Names and strings that follow from the rename:

- `_prior_phase_offsets` → `_prior_context_phase_offsets`, and `_prior_phase_window_tokens` → `_context_phase_window_tokens`.
- The `"prior_phases ..."` error messages and the `train_mixture` docstring.
- `"Every data phase must draw from the same sources"`, `"Data phases must start at increasing steps"`, and `"Prior phase {phase} must shuffle ..."` → "context phase".
- In `test_context_switch_data.py`: the imports, the `_phase` and `_offsets` annotations, and `test_lm_data_config_prior_phase_resumes_without_repeating_tokens`.
- In #9689: `HarrierPriorContext` and `prior_contexts`, so the stack uses one term. The context history that replaces `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` there (see my comment on #9689) can use the same name.

**Reject adjacent phases with the same sequence length.** `skip_to_window_offsets` accepts two adjacent phases with the same `seq_len`, for example a relaunch that changes only the batch size. In that case the within-window order does not change, so a source could continue at its exact position. `_next_window_start` still rounds up to the next shuffle window and discards up to one window per source (about 537M tokens per source at Harrier's settings). A check that adjacent phases differ in `seq_len` would turn that silent waste into an error. It would also make the `ContextPhase` name exact.

**Rename `counts_before` and make it block-aligned.** `counts_before` does not say what it counts; `sequence_counts_before` does. Its partial-block branch also never runs in this PR: `skip_to_window_offsets` calls it only at block boundaries (rounded up for the old phase, down for the new one). That branch returns a count, but in a partly served block the count is not a read position, because slots are shuffled; a source that served 3 sequences may have served occurrences 0, 7, and 31. Taking a block index instead, as `sequence_counts_before_block(block_id)`, removes the branch and prevents a later caller from using a mid-block count as a position.

**Check source order across phases.** The active-source check compares sets, but order matters as much: it sets each source's shuffle key through `key_iterator`, and the mixture's slot layout through `dataset_index` (including which source receives the rounding remainder). A config that lists the same sources in a different order passes the check and gets a different data layout. Recording the source order in the prior phase and comparing lists would catch this; at minimum, the docstring should say the order must not change.

**Document two assumptions that cannot be checked here.** (1) The shuffle and mixture keys come from the trainer seed, so the seed must be the same in every phase. (2) The offsets assume the current phase starts reading at the last `end_step`. A launch that restores a checkpoint from before that step would re-read data. #9689's trigger checks this for the hero; a docstring sentence on `prior_phases` would cover other callers.

**Optional: give a prior phase a `BatchSchedule`.** `PriorDataPhase.batch_size` is an `int`, so a prior phase cannot have a batch ramp, while the current phase takes a full `BatchSchedule`. A `BatchSchedule` field would give prior and current phases one representation.

**Possible follow-up, not for this PR.** Batch-size history (`BatchSchedule`) and context-length history (`prior_phases`) are both step-indexed descriptions of the run's shape, and could become one schedule. That needs three things this PR should not take on: the trainer must reject a `seq_len` change after the current step, because `Pos` is fixed per launch, while it can follow a batch change; `BatchSchedule` is used in 28 Python files; and the Harrier stage schedule would need to record the realized step of past stage boundaries instead of rounding them again for each batch size.

🤖 Addressed in new commits on top of the reviewed head ([compare 5a2525a4ec..748ad7fe6f](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/compare/5a2525a4ec..748ad7fe6f)):

- **Rename** (86fff8f63b): `ContextPhaseConfig`, `prior_context_phases`, `ContextPhase`, `_prior_context_phase_offsets`, `_context_phase_window_tokens`, the error messages, the `ContextPhase` docstring, and the test names. The field docstring now says that batch-size changes within one context length belong in `BatchSchedule`. In #9689, b596fe391c renames `HarrierPriorContext` and `prior_contexts` to `HarrierContextPhase` and `prior_context_phases`.
- **Same-length adjacent phases** (4ca2f1ba0d): `skip_to_window_offsets` now raises an error.
- **`counts_before`** (c7bdbe68f1): now `sequence_counts_before_block(block_id)`, without the partial-block branch.
- **Source order** (1c99ccec06): documented, not checked. A recorded source list would not catch the case that matters: the Harrier launcher rebuilds the prior phase from the same spec at every launch, so a reordered spec changes the recorded list and the current list together.
- **Seed and restore step** (1c99ccec06): both assumptions are in the `prior_context_phases` docstring.
- **Batch schedule for a prior phase** (748ad7fe6f): `ContextPhaseConfig.batch_size` is now `int | IntSchedule`, the same type as `TrainerConfig.train_batch_size`, so the existing `BatchSchedule(...)` conversion handles both.

The unified schedule is left for a follow-up, as suggested. The `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` history from the #9689 comment is not in these commits.

topics.title: [taskforge] stage40: the SDK, standard template, build services and the agentic author
topics.body:
Add the build stage as one package. `stage40_build_with_program` holds the SDK that build steps call, the standard six-step template, `GlmAuthor`, the agentic author, and `RLEnvBuildServices`, through which a build reaches machines, images, web tools, the ledger and agent limits. Host failures are told apart from program failures (`infrastructure`) so that a host outage never spends a revision, and the build runs in a child process under a wall clock (`build_process`).

`agentic_author.AgenticAuthor`, passed directly as the coordinator's author stage, runs agent sessions in a workspace that starts with the standard template, the proposal, the SDK reference and an empty notes file. Its tools read, write and edit workspace files, run the loader in a child process, build the program on the caller's step store, grade a candidate against the last draft, and search and fetch the web when the proposal lists research; `submit` hands the program in. A host failure, an expired clock or a storage fault never reaches the model, so none of them spends a revision. A build failure's text leads with the authored program's own frame (file, line, step and source line), then the error, so the author sees where its program raised rather than harness frames. `grade_candidate` gives a candidate a task machine exactly when the task has the shell capability, as validation's lowering does, and the SDK reference documents what a grade returns.

The package name states whether a build program produces the task draft at all, not how the program's writer runs. The agentic author writes and iterates a build program, so it lives here with the SDK, the template and the services it is handed. `stage40_build_with_agent` is reserved for a future build in which an agent produces the draft directly, with no program; it has no contents, `BUILDS_ON` in `tests/test_imports.py` is empty, and the README and that test's docstring state the distinction.

`run_build` now takes the services and a `ResearchRequirement`, keys steps on `build_model_digest`, records a `STEP` span for each step, and rejects a task whose solver machine differs from the one the proposal pins. A wall, step or grader timeout raises `BuildExpired`, distinct from a program `BuildFailure` or a host `BuildInfrastructureFailure`. The coordinator adaptation is in this PR because the build signature changes here: `StageCoordinator` holds the services and the research requirement and passes them to each build, records the requirement at `OPENED` so a relaunch cannot change it, and holds an expired workpiece without spending a revision. `check_workpiece_id` moves from `step_store` to `ledger.records`, and the coordinator and the `Author` protocol type proposals as `TaskProposal`. Triage runs `stage20_triage.preflight.preflight` and returns its `Verdict`; the coordinator exits accept or reject on it and records the verdict's reasons on a reject. The coordinator keeps its repair edge, a surface for a deterministic rewrite or a consumer's triage within `max_triage_repairs` (callers pass 0), and passes an accept's `author_state` to every author call as the `Author`'s third argument; nothing in the package writes one.

`stage_coordinator.run.run_workpieces(coordinator, proposals, retry)` runs many workpieces: it starts each as the async iterable of proposals yields it, so a proposal still being written holds back no other workpiece, and it sets no width. A failed workpiece cancels none of its siblings. A transient infrastructure failure (`ModelUnavailable`, or a `BuildInfrastructureFailure` whose cause can change on the same host) runs the workpiece again in-process after a backoff, up to `InfrastructureRetry.max_attempts`, resuming at the stage that raised; a task or program failure, an expired clock and a storage fault are never retried. `WorkpieceBudget.max_modify_rounds` bounds the rounds review may send back with `Modify`; past it the workpiece is rejected on its budget.

`publish_image` classifies an image job the host failed (`image_builder.ImageJobFailed`, #10293) as the host's `IMAGE_JOB_FAILED` and a Dockerfile kaniko refused (`BuildFailed`) as the program's `BuildFailure`.

Builds on #10297; #10300 builds on it. #10299 is folded in here. The loader tests from #10297 land here, and two assertions that lower a built task through `stage50_validate` land with that stage in #10300. The first two commits repeated a GLM client change and a sandbox docstring fix that the lower branches were cut without. Since the stack sync, the client is #10291's, which requests no per-token logprobs, and neither commit changes this diff.

---

🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:02c433df24ac33ec58f45259f7021b9dddf703992c744b38d98f52e6c0cb5d8f -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
Add the build SDK and everything a build program runs on. `stage40_build_with_program` gains the SDK steps call (`sdk`, `outputs`), the host's machines, images, web tools, ledger and agent limits passed to every build (`RLEnvBuildServices`), step effects on the host (`build_machine`, `grade_candidate`, `publish_image`), host failures told apart from program failures (`infrastructure`), the standard six-step template, `GlmAuthor`, and a build child bounded by a wall clock (`build_process`). `run_build` takes the services and a `ResearchRequirement`, keys steps on `build_model_digest`, records a `STEP` span per step, and refuses a task whose solver machine is not the one the proposal pins. A build that runs past a wall, step or grader clock raises `BuildExpired`, a third outcome beside the program's `BuildFailure` and the host's `BuildInfrastructureFailure`; the coordinator holds such a workpiece without spending a revision.

The coordinator adaptation lands here because `run_build`'s signature changes here. `StageCoordinator` holds the services and research requirement and passes them to every build, `check_workpiece_id` moves from `step_store` to `ledger.records`, and the coordinator and the `Author` protocol type the proposal as a `TaskProposal`. The walkthrough and the capability coordinator test build their proposals with `stage10_proposal.parse`.

Builds on #10297; #10299 builds on it. The loader's tests from #10297 land here. Two assertions that lower a built task with `stage50_validate` (the standard template's RolloutEngine run and the validation verifier deadline) come with that stage. The taskforge suite passes 567 tests here (151 more than #10297).

```

</details>

🤖 Holistic review of 7e4b5bcb (reviewed at 635e3289; the merge of main since then leaves this PR's diff unchanged, and the line anchors below were re-checked at 7e4b5bcb).

This PR adds the whole build stage: the SDK that build steps call, the six-step template, `RLEnvBuildServices`, the split between host, program and expired failures, a child-process runner, `GlmAuthor`, the agentic author and the coordinator plumbing. The failure taxonomy is coherent and well tested. Locally at head: 628 passed, 1 skipped, 22 deselected with the README's command.

The structural problem is that three headline pieces have no production caller in this PR or at the heads of #10300 and #10301: `agentic_author.author_round`, `build_process.run_build_in_process` and `stage_coordinator/run.py::run_workpieces`. `author_round` also cannot be plugged into the coordinator as written (finding 1). Two surfaces, the triage repair edge and the `author_state` plumbing, land with zero producers (finding 3). The body's "the build runs in a child process under a wall clock" is not realized on any path a user runs; only `tests/.../test_build_process.py` calls `run_build_in_process`, so `STEP_TIMEOUT` cannot fire on a non-yielding step in `StageCoordinator._build`, the walkthrough, or the capability test.

Body claims verified: `ImageJobFailed` exists at base, the research requirement is recorded at `OPENED` in `_open`, and storage faults re-raise in both the coordinator and `AuthorSession.run_build`. The Codex threads on image failure classification, research-requirement persistence and storage faults are fixed in b76f4048 and 4c8389dc; none of the items below repeat them.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker:** `stage40_build_with_program/agentic_author.py:1210` `author_round(...) -> AuthorOutcome` does not satisfy `stage30_author/author.py:63` `Author.__call__(proposal, revision, author_state) -> AuthoredProgram`, and nothing adapts it, so the agentic author is unreachable from the coordinator. It also writes the coordinator's layout from below: `agentic_author.py:117-118` redefines `ROUNDS_DIR`/`AUTHORED_DIR` (the stage cannot import `stage_coordinator`) and writes `rounds/<n>/authored/<k>/program.py` with `k` counting sessions including handoffs, while `stage_coordinator/coordinator.py:207` `authored_dir` writes the same files with `k = state.build_revisions`. After one handoff in a round, an adapter would have the coordinator write `authored/0/program.py` and the author `authored/1/program.py`, and `_authored_program` reads whichever the coordinator wrote. Have `author_round` return the artifacts (source bytes, manifest, session and transcript records) and let the coordinator's `_author` write them, or pass the target directory in from the caller; delete the duplicated directory constants; add the `Author` adapter in this PR.

- **2. Should fix:** `stage_coordinator/run.py` (`InfrastructureRetry`, `transient_infrastructure_failure`, `run_workpieces`, 143 lines, commit 7ce56682) is outside the title and has no caller outside `test_pipeline_walkthrough.py`; #10301's driver does not use it either. Move it and its four walkthrough tests to #10301 where the driver can call it, or say in the body why a driverless `run_workpieces` lands here.

- **3. Should fix:** The triage repair edge has no producer. `stage_coordinator/workpiece_machine.py` adds `Exit.REPAIR`, the `(TRIAGE, REPAIR)` transition and `WorkpieceState.triage_repairs`; `coordinator.py:127,157,211` add `REPAIRED_DIR`, `WorkpieceBudget.max_triage_repairs`, the REPAIR branch of `_triage`, `_repaired` and `_Workpiece.proposal_at`; `stage_functions.py:49` adds `RepairProposal` and `StageFunctions.repair`. `stage20_triage/preflight.py:39` returns only ACCEPT or REJECT and the body says callers pass 0. The same holds for `author_state`: the third `Author` parameter, `static_author`'s, `GlmAuthor.__call__`'s ignored argument, `AUTHOR_STATE_ATTR` (`workpiece_machine.py:69`), `WorkpieceState.author_state` and the `canonical_json`/`json.loads` round trip in `_triage` and `transition`. Every producer attaches `{}` and every consumer ignores it. Delete both until a producer exists; `proposal_at` then collapses to `workpiece.proposal`. Keep the pre-existing `Verdict.author_state`.

- **4. Should fix:** `stage40_build_with_program/services.py:60-75` `RLEnvBuildServices.ledger: Ledger | None` plus the `recording` property, `_DiscardingLedger` and `_DISCARD` is an always-truthy wrapper around an optional. All four readers (`context.py`, `run.py`, `agentic_author.py`) use `.recording`; the only `.ledger` use is `replace(build.services, ledger=...)`. Make `ledger: Ledger` required, put a public `DiscardingLedger` in `ledger/records.py` next to the `Ledger` protocol, and have `build_process._resources` pass it when `ledger_root is None`.

- **5. Should fix:** `stage40_build_with_program/infrastructure.py:137,147` defines two chain walkers: `_chain` follows `__context__` unconditionally and `exception_chain` honours `__suppress_context__`. `infrastructure_failure` and `deadline_failure` use the first; `raised_in_program` uses the second. One `raise ... from None` inside a step makes the two disagree about the same error. Keep `exception_chain` only.

- **6. Should fix:** `stage40_build_with_program/sandbox_effects.py:36,38` imports `rolloutengine.cleanup._Cleanup` and `rolloutengine.machines._prepare_machine`. `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/machines.py` exposes only `task_machine` publicly. Add a public `prepare_machine(requirements, runtime, files, factories, cleanup, stack)` in rolloutengine and import that; the module docstring already explains why `task_machine` does not fit.

- **7. Should fix:** `sandbox_effects.py:73` `GRADE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_TIMEOUT = SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT + GRADER_TIMEOUT` (600 + 300 s) is fixed, but the SDK reference hands the author `draft.python_grader(..., timeout=)` and `draft.script_grader(..., timeout=)` (`glm_author.py:102`), and `taskcompendium.models.ScriptGrader.timeout` defaults to 600. A program grader with `timeout > 300` has the engine's verifier deadline fire first; `deadline_failure` labels it `SANDBOX_DEADLINE`, `run_program` raises `BuildInfrastructureFailure`, and `run_workpieces` retries the same program as transient. A slow grader the author wrote is recorded as a host outage and never sent back for revision. Compute the deadline per call in `grade_candidate`: `SANDBOX_SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT + grader.timeout` for a `ScriptGrader`, else `GRADER_TIMEOUT`.

- **8. Should fix:** `agentic_author.py:324-325` `SessionBuild.client` and `.policy` exist only to fill `RLEnvBuildContext.model`/`.sampling` for `grade_candidate`, whose docstring says no model is called; `sandbox_effects.py` reads only `context.workpiece_id` and `context.services`. Give `grade_candidate` and `publish_image` a core that takes `(services, workpiece_id, ...)` and keep the `context` form as the SDK's one-line wrapper; delete `SessionBuild.client`/`.policy` and the test fixtures that supply them.

- **9. Should fix:** `coordinator.py:188` `StageCoordinator.services` and the `Build` protocol's new `services` parameter (`stage_functions.py:75`) only forward to `stages.build`; the coordinator never reads them. `build_process.py:146` `BuildRequest` repeats the same nine fields as config so the child can rebuild them, and no `Build`-shaped adapter over `run_build_in_process` (`build_process.py:224`) exists, so the coordinator cannot use the child runner (it holds a live `ModelClient`, not a `BuildModelConfig`). Bind `model`, `sampling`, `services`, `research` and `model_digest` into the `Build` callable with `functools.partial` at the call site, so the coordinator keeps only `model_digest` and `research` (which `OPENED` records), and ship a `Build` adapter that constructs a `BuildRequest` and calls `run_build_in_process`. Otherwise remove the child-process claim from the body until a caller exists.

- **10. Should fix:** Four more copies of the atomic-write idiom: `glm_author.py:394 _write`, `agentic_author.py _write_bytes`, `stage40_build_with_program/run.py:421 _write_draft`, `build_process.py:368`, beside the pre-existing `coordinator._write` and `step_store._write`; taskforge now has 14 `atomic_rename` sites. Add `write_bytes_atomic(path, content)` to `lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem/atomic.py`, which already owns `atomic_rename`, and call it from all six.

- **11. Should fix:** `tests/test_imports.py:33` `BUILDS_ON: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}` makes the `if imported in BUILDS_ON.get(importer, ())` branch unreachable, and `README.md:63` and the test docstring reserve a `stage40_build_with_agent` package that does not exist as a directory. Delete `BUILDS_ON` and the two paragraphs; add them with the package.

- **12. Drop test:** `tests/stage40_build_with_program/test_standard.py:237 test_a_rejection_ceiling_at_full_credit_is_refused` and `:373 test_fixtures_refuse_a_package_with_pip_options` are configuration guards on pydantic validators with no regression behind them (TESTING.md, scalar and configuration guards). `tests/stage40_build_with_program/test_glm_author.py:26 test_the_sdk_reference_lists_the_fields_of_the_task_types_steps_read` asserts substrings of generated prose such as `class TaskResource(*, path: str, source: taskcompendium.models.InlineFile`, which breaks on any taskcompendium signature reflow without the reference being wrong. Keep `test_each_name_appears_in_one_section_of_the_sdk_reference` (`:35`), and either drop the substring test or assert that `getattr(module, name)` resolves for each `REFERENCE_SECTIONS` entry. With finding 7, `test_infrastructure.py:348 test_verifier_deadlines_outlast_the_sandbox_scheduling_timeout` only asserts a constant inequality and goes too.

topics.title: [datakit] Strip orphan reasoning close tags from pretraining text sources
topics.body:
Part of #10400. Two agent-trajectory sources in the pretraining mixture write reasoning close tags with no opening tag. They are the likely origin of the habit in #10400, where the model closes a think block, keeps reasoning, and closes it again ([scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6327348899)).

Counts from one normalized shard per source of `gs://marin-us-central2/datakit/store_8ac06c74`:

- `swe-zero-12m`: 15 of 1,944 documents. In those documents, 197 of 225 assistant turns end their reasoning with `</thinking>` and no opener, and 8 turns close two or more times with reasoning between the closes. A second shard gave 15 of 1,936 documents.
- `davinci-dev/env-native`: 16 of 528 documents have an assistant turn with a bare `</think>`.

These documents are about 0.04% of training tokens, roughly 5M stray close tags over the run. The base checkpoint wrote plain-text `</think>` 6,546 times and `<think>` 307 times in its SWE-bench eval.

The text renderers copy assistant content verbatim: [`swe_zero_12m.row_to_doc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107) and [`davinci_dev.env_row_to_doc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/davinci_dev.py#L224-L234). The `swe-zero-12m` chat conversion wraps all text before the bash block in think tags, `</thinking>` included ([swe_zero_12m.py:156](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L156-L157)), and [`_check_source_markup`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88) matches only `<think>` and `</think>`. [`join_reasoning_and_answer`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/glm_kernelgym_rollouts.py#L74-L82) already repairs the same defect for the GLM kernelgym rollouts.

Done when:
- Rebuilt `swe-zero-12m` and `davinci-dev/env-native` documents have no assistant message with a reasoning close tag that lacks an opener. Pipeline counters report the number of repairs. Tool output and user text are unchanged.
- `swe-zero-12m` chat rows have no `</thinking>` in their reasoning, and `_check_source_markup` also rejects `<thinking>` and `</thinking>`.
- The changed `processed/` and `processed-chat/` steps have new `hash_attrs` versions and are rebuilt.
- The owners of the Hero mixture (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/harrier_mix_2026_08_18.py`) have been asked whether its next cooldown uses the rebuilt sources.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`swe_zero_12m.row_to_doc` and `davinci_dev.env_row_to_doc` copy assistant content into pretraining text, including unmatched `</thinking>` and `</think>` tags. The SWE-ZERO chat adapter wraps that content in a new think block, and source-markup validation misses `<thinking>` tags. No open PR covers these transforms.

**Relevant code**
- [`swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L98-L107) — text rendering.
- [`swe_zero_12m.py#L151-L157`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/swe_zero_12m.py#L151-L157) — chat reasoning.
- [`davinci_dev.py#L224-L235`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/davinci_dev.py#L224-L235) — env text rendering.
- [`rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/rollout_transforms.py#L74-L88) — markup check.

# Proposed Fix

Repair unmatched reasoning close tags in assistant content before either text renderer emits a document, and count each repair. Apply the same repair to SWE-ZERO chat reasoning, reject `<thinking>` source markup, and bump the affected `processed/` and `processed-chat/` step versions before rebuilding and checking the outputs. User and tool content stays as recorded.

topics.title: [agents] Preserve runnable research engineering workflows
topics.body:
Coordinate iterative design exploration, data analysis, and experiments through
a research-engineering workflow. Preserve the working source and notebook on
Marin-derived branches in marin-community/marin-logbooks, and extract selected
implementations into ordinary Marin PRs.

Use logbooks issues for the current conclusion and milestone updates, with
commit-pinned evidence in the notebook. Keep the logbooks default branch as an
index and preserve published research history. Background research continues
to use the existing experiment-record guidance.

The workflow starts before training launches and includes dataset investigation,
rejected designs, and meaningful failed attempts. Kernel tuning routes through
it when repeated comparisons are expected to produce reusable evidence.

Companion archive procedures are in [marin-logbooks#1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/pull/1).
